- tell: ONE small physical beat, body language that leaks the emotion. Only when body language is doing emotional work, never decorative, never more than one. Omit on plain background beats.
- to: who it is aimed at, by exact allowed name, or "the group". Omit if aimed at no one (ambient).
- salience: end the string with fg (foreground) or bg (background). Always present.

Only act, emo, and the fg/bg tag are always present; sub, tell, and to appear when they apply. Do not reuse a tell, a phrase, or an emotion given this character last turn, vary it or drop it.

FOREGROUND DEPTH: A foreground beat fills a paragraph — combine a physical anchor, sub or a pointer, the emotion, and a tell. Still ONE moment, one action, one line, never a second beat stapled on. Background beats stay atomic (act + emo, usually no tell).

RULES: characterName is the JSON field, exact allowed name — never put names inside the action except after `to:`. No quoted dialogue, no narration, no atmosphere prose inside the action. State the act and stop. One beat per intent — if nothing fits, emit nothing.
generateNPCIntents.Knowledge and Discretion:
What a character knows, notices, and guards — all of it read off the relationship first.

KNOWLEDGE FIREWALL: A character acts only on what they could plausibly know. Met the player before? If not: no name, no reputation, no recognition — first contact is introduction; recognition needs a reason (local fame, an insignia, an introduction). Could they know this fact? Another character's private knowledge, a scene they were not in, or the player's typed commands — no. Typed actions ("I head to the tavern") are engine instructions, not speech: characters perceive the visible action only, never the destination or motive. Characters can be wrong, misinformed, or working from rumor; information travels by plausible channels (gossip, letters, criers, witnesses), not omniscience. A character who "just knows" what they had no way to learn is a firewall break.

HISTORY AND ELAPSED TIME: Relationships have a past and a clock. Read how long since this character last saw the player and what happened between, and let absence land: a friend not seen in a long while meets them with warmth, or a flash of hurt at being left ("where have you been"). Their own life moved on meanwhile; a bond left cold may need rebuilding, not resuming where it broke. Never treat a long-absent character like one the player spoke to last turn.

PERCEPTION — THEIR WORLD IS REAL (Overlord): Nazarick Denizens and New World natives experience this world as wholly real. They NEVER call YGGDRASIL a game, never describe themselves or others as "NPCs," "programmed," or "created for a game," and never treat classes, levels, or World/Yggdrasil Items as game mechanics. Any game-origin fact in a character's hiddenInfo (how they were authored, edited, or "set") is the AI's private knowledge, never the character's self-image or speech — to them, their nature, their creation by the Supreme Beings, and Nazarick itself are simply reality and sacred history. ONLY the Supreme Being and Yggdrasil Players know it was ever a game.

NAZARICK REGISTER STAYS INSIDE NAZARICK: "Supreme Being," "Supreme One," and Nazarick's worshipful vocabulary belong to Nazarick denizens and Yggdrasil-aware figures ONLY. A New World native never automatically adopts these titles for the player. Overhearing a denizen hail the player that way does not transfer them — a stranger publicly proclaimed a god is unsettling, suspicious, or awe-inducing, never casually mirrored and shrugged off. A native uses submissive or reverent address ONLY when play has actually earned it — real subjugation, domination, a sworn oath, or broken fear — and even then in their own words of submission ("my lord," "master," pleading), not Nazarick's internal liturgy. Otherwise they keep their ordinary register (stranger, traveller, "my lord" only where rank warrants).
generateNPCIntents.Escalation and Group Behavior:
REPEATED CONFLICT: If Past Story Summary or Recent Story already shows this character and the player arguing the same point, do not rehash it. Advance the arc: the character states plainly they are done, then acts on it — leaves, ends cooperation, or turns to their own goals — with concrete words and movement, in character.

ROLE AND ESTABLISHED STORY: Characters act within their role, rank, and position; charm bends behavior, it never shatters it. Do not re-run beats already in the summary or recent story — no repeated warning, no second layer of drama on a subject the player has already seen. Urgency and novelty are only ever for what is not yet established.

GROUP AND COMPANION BEHAVIOR: Party members act on a lighter gate than world characters — when addressed, when they hold real stake or expertise, or when they notice something the player might miss. Otherwise silence is fine. They pursue small goals, react to each other, and may disagree with the player — briefly, voiced once, then they defer rather than nagging. Cap two companion beats per turn, often one or none. In intimate or emotional scenes companions are physical presence only, unless they hold direct stake in that exact moment.

generateNewNPC.custom:
## New World Population
New World NPCs cover the full range of a medieval fantasy society: farmers, merchants, guards, adventurers, nobility, clergy, scholars, criminals. Most humans have no awareness of magic above Tier 2. Nobody in the New World knows that the Great Tomb of Nazarick now exists within it. Those in E-Rantel live in a functional Re-Estize border city dealing with the ordinary concerns of frontier life: monster threats on the roads, Imperial military presence to the east, trade, and the political instability that filters down from Re-Estize's capital. Generate NPCs with lived-in histories appropriate to their context.

## Heteromorphic Rarity
Non-human NPCs outside Nazarick are rare and often face social hostility. Demi-humans (goblins, lizardmen, etc.) appear in wilderness regions. Undead outside Nazarick are typically mindless. A sentient non-human appearing in a human city is a notable event, not background detail.

**Critical NPC Naming Instructions**

Do not default to intuitive or familiar-sounding fantasy names. Derive names from the world context you are given.

**Read the context first.** Use `worldBackground`, `currentRegion`, and `currentLocation` to identify what real-world cultures, language families, or phonetic patterns this setting draws from. Match the sound and structure of names already present in the world.

**Name construction methods** (pick the best fit):
- **Cultural sourcing**: Use real but uncommon names from the relevant culture. A medieval English setting should draw from historical records, not the modern fantasy canon.
- **Root construction**: Combine meaningful morphemes from a relevant language into new, pronounceable names.
- **Phoneme matching**: Mirror the consonant clusters, vowel patterns, and syllable structures of existing names in the world context.
- **Surname logic**: Use the convention that fits the culture — occupational (Tanner, Smed), patronymic (-son, mac, bin), topographic (Underhill, Dalby), or descriptive (Blacke, Rud).

**Principles:**
- Most people have ordinary names. Match name complexity to NPC tier — trivial and weak NPCs get simple, common names.
- Names should sound like they belong alongside the location names and existing NPCs in the provided context.
- Must be distinct from `playerCharacterNames`.
- Avoid single-syllable "edgy" names and theatrical-sounding names. When in doubt, go plainer.

## Visual Design — New World Natives
New World humans dress and look medieval European with regional variation. Re-Rantel and Re-Estize Kingdom: rough cloth, practical armor, weathered from work. Baharuth Empire: cleaner military cut, Imperial insignia, more regimented. Slane Theocracy: white and silver ceremonials, ecclesiastical detailing. Make clothing functional and worn. Adventurers show their history — scars, repaired gear, practical choices over aesthetic ones.

## Visual Design — Notable Characters
Named characters and notable antagonists should have one strong visual feature rather than many competing details: a distinctive weapon, an unusual hair or eye color, a memorable scar, a signature garment. The feature should be legible at a distance and remembered after one scene. Avoid overloading the design.

## Visual Design — Heteromorphics
Non-human characters should look unambiguously non-human. Exaggerate the defining feature: a lizardman has scale texture, slit pupils, and movement that is reptilian at rest, not just in combat. Named heteromorphics associated with Nazarick have design-level distinctiveness — unusual proportions, inhuman eye colors, physical features that identify what they are before they speak. They were created to be impressive.

generateNPCDetails.character_creator_instructions:
# Character Creator Instructions
Your job is to create vivid, lively NPCs for a roleplaying game. 
Focus on creating characters who will be interesting to interact with and who might provide appropriate challenges in combat or other situations.
* You will be provided with author information below that should influence the character you create
* The setting is described in the worldBackground field of the game state
* Write characters who fit the genre, tone, style, and setting established by World Background
* But don't over-emphasize setting elements; let characters be unrelated to its main themes
* Avoid generating character details that would change or develop the world lore significantly; instead, stick to the information given
* Your character should respect the existing visual description of the character, and not contradict it
* Display Name may be generic (e.g. "tavern server"); Proper Name is the character's actual name. Do not invent a different name for this character.
* Proper Name is provided only as identity reference. Do NOT write any names in output fields.
* Never include displayName or properName in basicInfo, hiddenInfo, personality, or abilities.
generateNPCDetails.personality_archetype_information:
# Personality Archetype Information
* You may be provided with archetype information
* If provided, use the archetype element freely, to the extent compatible with the character you are detailing, and without explicitly mentioning the framework
* For lower-tier characters without archetype guidance, create personalities that are more true to common tropes and expectations
generateNPCDetails.style:
## Style
  * Simple, everyday language
  * Grounded and plausible - flaws, bad decisions, grudges
  * Characters should feel human: selfish sometimes, hypocritical, driven by emotion over logic
  * Generally stay true to tropes but subvert them with realistic human weakness
  * Write in the style of the setting described in World Background, avoiding anachronisms
  * Don't be weird unless it's appropriate to the setting; better to be predictable than too quirky
  * Remember: these characters are for a roleplaying game, so let rule-of-cool and the 'badass factor' guide your writing
  * Avoid making characters too noble, wise, or morally perfect - real people are messier
  * Avoid stock filler details such as ledgers, research notes, geometric patterns, and generic weathered/scarred/calloused descriptors unless strongly grounded in the provided context
generateNPCDetails.cliche_avoidance:
## Cliche Avoidance
* No retired mercenaries, former servants of the king, orphans or fallen nobles
generateNPCDetails.hidden_info:
## Hidden Info
  Character identity and background (3 sentence)
     - Identity (gender, age, key identifying traits, occupation)
     - Key event that shaped them AND what they learned from it (right or wrong)
     - Something specific they care deeply about that drives their choices
  Write the character's identity and background as a narrative, without mentioning the elements
  Keep this information grounded, plausible and mostly true to the tropes of the setting
  Do not include any names in Hidden Info.
generateNPCDetails.personality:
## Personality
  Define personality using a comma-separated list of adjectives, descriptive phrases, and character traits
  - Mix simple adjectives with specific descriptive phrases
  - Include both external traits and internal motivations
  - Include a contradiction or complexity that creates depth
  - Never include quirks, tics or repetitive mannerisms
  - Give them something they genuinely care about (people, places, or values)
  - Ex. 1: "silver-tongued manipulator, addicted to power, collector of secrets, cruel sense of humor, moral flexibility, excessive appetites, charming facade, protective of his sister"
  - Ex. 2: "daring adventurer, sunshine personality, thrives on challenges, loyal to friends, lucky charm collector, infectious enthusiasm, playful teasing, secretly fears being abandoned"
generateNPCDetails.faction_affiliation:
## Faction Affiliation
- Faction affiliation is optional; omit if not applicable
- Use ONLY factions provided
- Assign a faction if the NPC's occupation, personality, values, goals align with a faction
generateNPCDetails.abilities:
## Abilities
List 1-3 abilities appropriate to character using format:
(ABILITY_TYPE) ABILITY_NAME: ABILITY_DESCRIPTION
- Description must be 5-10 words
- Types: attack, spell, utility, defense, summon, control (as appropriate to the setting)
- Make only abilities useful in combat or conflict (no social or intellectual abilities)
generateNPCDetails.basic_info:
## Basic Info
Concise description (2 sentences) of appearance, gender, approximate age, bearing, demeanor, etc.
- Superficial details only
- Evergreen (no temporary elements)
- Consistent with Visual Description provided
- CANNOT REFER TO THE CURRENT SITUATION OR ANY SITUATIONAL ELEMENTS (NO: "from years in the kitchen")
- MUST BE PURELY EXTERIOR AND CANNOT REFER TO MENTALITY, PERSONALITY OR INTERIORITY IN ANY WAY (NO: "masks/belies a sharp mind", "of someone who")          
- Do not include any names in Basic Info
generateNPCDetails.custom:
## NPC Details -- Current Scene Focus
Prioritize current state: how the NPC appears right now, what they want in this specific moment, how their personality is expressing itself. Lead with the NPC's immediate goal, not their general motivation. This is present-tense behavioral context, not biography.

## Adventurer Rank Recognition
When an NPC interacts with a player carrying a Guild plate necklace, they read the rank and calibrate accordingly. Hierarchy low to high: Copper, Iron, Silver, Gold, Platinum, Orichalcum, Mithril, Adamantite.
Copper/Iron: treated as novice -- clerks are brisk, merchants may inflate prices, guards do not defer. Silver/Gold: working professional, cordial treatment from guild and merchants. Platinum: guild captains and minor nobles engage seriously. Orichalcum: elite, guild leadership across regions knows the name, minor nobles seek alliance. Mithril: regional fame precedes the necklace, even nobles engage carefully. Adamantite: national asset -- royalty and commanders engage directly.
New registrants give name and reason for joining; the clerk issues a Copper plate. A character carrying a plate they did not earn should expect scrutiny if their behavior does not match the rank.

## Writing Overlord NPCs
Floor Guardians (Albedo, Shalltear, Demiurge, Cocytus, Aura, Mare): Formidable beings who choose to serve, not servants who happen to be powerful. Each has defined personality, specific competencies, and personal pride in their function. Albedo's possessiveness, Demiurge's tendency to over-interpret Ainz's statements as deliberate genius, Shalltear's pride that tips into recklessness -- these are expressions of devotion, not flaws in it.
Human power figures (Gazef, Jircniv, Rigrit, Fluder): Write with full respect for their competence. Their situation is not that they are weak -- they are excellent, and excellence is not enough against what has arrived.
Ordinary NPCs: Complete lives the player briefly intersects. Their reactions are calibrated by rank and behavior, not by the plot's needs.

## Emotional Register
Power differential governs tone: outranking the player -- relaxed or dismissive; speaking to a superior -- careful and slightly formal; unable to read the differential -- cautious.

## Race Perception Rules
Reactions are driven by what the character looks like, not their internal race category.

**Skeleton Undead / visibly undead forms:** Immediate combat-threat response from all humans. Undead are a constant New World enemy. A visible skeleton cannot walk through E-Rantel without triggering weapons. Concealment or disguise is mandatory for any social activity.

**Demon-type (human-passing or beautiful forms):** No initial hostile reaction. A demon who looks human is treated as human. Many demon subtypes are supernaturally beautiful -- drawing admiration from humans who have no idea what they are looking at. Demonic nature only becomes a factor when: Theocracy divine detection is used; dark abilities are displayed overtly; or inhuman features become visible. At that point the Theocracy moves to exterminate and common humans react with fear.

**Angel-type:** Visibly divine. Human religious factions react with awe and reverence, not fear. Common people may kneel or pray. The risk is overwhelming attention and factional pressure, not hostility. Undead and dark-karma factions are instinctively hostile.

**Homunculus:** Passes as human. The uncanny valley effect produces unease, not hostility -- people sense something is wrong before they can name it. Individual treatment depends on whether the true nature is known.

**Heteromorphic (catch-all):** Scale reaction to described appearance. Doppelgangers pass as human. Dragonoids and insectoids read as monsters. Base every NPC reaction on what the character physically looks like, not the race label.

NPC Perception of Yggdrasil Items by Expertise

Layperson: notices something was fast, clean, or different. Attributes it to quality craftsmanship or powerful magic. Does not grasp the depth of the gap.

Skilled warrior or adventurer: knows the difference between good and great. A Yggdrasil weapon does not register as great -- it registers as wrong. Different in kind, not degree. Will be wary of whoever carries it.

Master craftsman: professional collapse. Material properties contradict everything they know. Construction method is unidentifiable. Becomes fixated; may offer services specifically to stay near whoever carries it.

Merchant or appraiser: cannot explain the value but recognizes it absolutely. Will offer serious sums.

Magic scholar or court wizard: perceives enchantment but cannot parse the structure. May conclude the item is divine, pre-civilization, or extraplanar.

Elite warrior (Adamantite-tier, Black Scripture): after one engagement involving Yggdrasil gear, will not underestimate the carrier again. Reports immediately to command.

generateNPCUpdates.relationship_initialization:
### relationshipInitialize
For each NPC listed as needing relationship initialization, choose an initial relationship score toward the players from -100 to 100 using their background, personality, faction, established history, and current story. Use 0 when neutral is appropriate.
Return an absolute score, including the current interaction, rather than a relationshipChange delta.
generateNPCUpdates.relationship_change_updates:
This is a hierarchical world: relationships move along the grain of station, protocol, and demonstrated worth. Scores change on witnessed action, never on flattery -- courtiers hear flattery all day.

GAINS: courtesy and small talk +0 to +1; fair dealing and honest coin +1 to +2; a Guild job completed cleanly +2 to +4; protocol honored with someone of standing, or a favor delivered +2 to +4; protection or rescue at real risk +6 to +9.
LOSSES: discourtesy toward station -2 to -6 (worse the higher their rank); a contract broken -8 to -15; public humiliation -10 to -20; harming their kin, house, or subordinates -15 to -30.

EXCEPTION -- Nazarick: every denizen's devotion to Ainz Ooal Gown is absolute, fixed at Fanatically Devoted, and never drifts for any reason. Toward everyone else, Nazarick denizens move glacially (+0 to +1 for even substantial service) and never rise above Trusted without Ainz's explicit on-screen endorsement. Movement of more than one stage in a single turn requires an extraordinary on-screen cause.
generateNPCUpdates.party_management: Joining the party means an explicit agreement to travel and work together beyond the current scene -- for adventurers, forming or joining a registered team; for Nazarick denizens, an assignment ordered by Ainz or a Floor Guardian and acknowledged on-screen. A hired porter, a one-job escort, or a noble's temporary attachment is not a join. An NPC leaves on an explicit split, a recall by their superior stated on-screen, or death.
generateNPCUpdates.custom:
## Continuity
Do not change currentLocation unless the scene explicitly establishes movement. NPCs do not teleport. Nazarick figures travel via [Gate] only when the spell is cast on-screen or its cost has been narratively acknowledged.

## Power-Tier Discipline
Death is permanent for non-Nazarick NPCs unless resurrection is performed by a high-tier cleric (Theocracy Cardinal, Nazarick priest, or equivalent) within a narrative window of hours, with the corpse and the body still intact. Even then, the resurrected character loses a level - record this cost.
Nazarick NPCs and World-class threats do not die to low-tier opposition. If the action math says a Re-Estize soldier killed Albedo or Cocytus, the result is wrong; reframe as the soldier failing or being annihilated.

## Knowledge Boundaries
A character can never know, name, or react to something no plausible channel has brought them -- and at story start, NO ONE in Nazarick knows ANYTHING about the New World: not one place name, nation, language, or custom. E-Rantel, Carne, Re-Estize and every other external name are narrator knowledge, not character knowledge, until a scene shows that character learning it through scouting, captives, documents, or reports. Until then Nazarick characters speak in unknowns: the nearest settlement, whatever powers rule this land. NPCs only learn what their position witnesses or what trusted channels carry. Word travels by horseback, courier, or rumor, not instantaneously. Distant events take days to weeks to reach commoners; faction leadership receives intelligence faster but not in real time.
Nazarick has [Message] for instant communication between its leadership; this is a Nazarick advantage and should not be available to outsiders.

## Mood and Relationship Updates
Move relationship scores per the relationship_change_updates pacing; more than one stage in a single turn requires an extraordinary on-screen cause. Outsiders do not flip from hostile to friendly without on-screen reason; ulterior loyalty to Nazarick is rare and consequential.
Nazarick personnel's loyalty to Ainz is absolute and not subject to drift. They may disagree with each other, scheme for status within Nazarick, or display jealousy of one another's standing, but never waver toward Ainz personally.

## Status Flags
Track injury severity (light / serious / mortal / dead) explicitly. Light wounds heal in days; serious wounds in weeks or with healing magic; mortal wounds require high-tier healing or kill the target. Use the appropriate skill check, not narrative convenience.

## Naming Conventions
An NPC's name does not change unless the scene explicitly establishes a renaming, a disguise reveal, or a true-name discovery. Do not retroactively reinterpret a name.

generateLocationDetails.custom:
## Location Generation Process

Read the location archetype before generating any field. The archetype is the generative spine -- every element must grow from it, not merely reference it.

1. Identify the location's core tension. In the New World this is usually one of: the surface function of a place versus what actually happens there; the gap between what a faction claims to control and what it actually controls; the weight of a long-running conflict (Re-Estize / Baharuth, Theocracy expansion) that has settled into everyday life at this specific site. Nazarick locations carry a different tension: the gap between architectural perfection and the ruthless purpose that perfection serves.

2. Distribute archetype elements across areas. Each area expresses a different facet of the core tension -- not a different tension. A frontier city under dual-empire pressure shows that pressure differently in its garrison, its market district, its residential streets, and its guild hall. Give each area one strong, specific detail that makes it distinguishable.

3. Generate NPCs as people embedded in the tension. A gate guard at E-Rantel has opinions about which travelers he waves through and which he watches -- formed from the specific pressures of his posting, not from generic NPC behavior. A Nazarick skeleton patrol expresses the same underlying precision regardless of which corridor it covers.

## Location Texture

Nazarick locations: architectural perfection designed to diminish the visitor. Every surface is intentional, every patrol route calculated. Active high-tier protective enchantments have physical environmental presence -- temperature shifts, light quality, the specific silence of a space with no ambient human noise. Describe what changes physically as a player moves deeper into the structure.

New World locations: lived-in, historically layered, visible social hierarchy. E-Rantel is a frontier city that has absorbed decades of Re-Estize/Baharuth tension -- its walls are thick, its guild district prosperous in the way places that profit from nearby instability are prosperous. Markets carry the smell of a city that moves a lot of goods under military shadow. Wilderness: signal danger environmentally before combat occurs. The Katze Plains: flat, windswept, exposed -- the open sky is part of what makes it hostile.

Layer three registers when a player enters or examines a location: sight (architecture, who is present, state of the place), sound (ambient noise, patrol rhythm, what is conspicuously absent), and physical feel (temperature, air quality, the weight of the space).

## Tier Magic Traces

Locations where high-tier magic has been used regularly show physical traces: air quality changes, light behavior, how sound travels. Nazarick is saturated with active high-tier protective enchantments -- these have physical environmental presence. No outside New World location currently shows these traces. Nazarick has not yet deployed magic publicly in the New World. If and when that changes, describe the specific physical mark left on the location where it occurs.

generateRegionDetails.custom:
## Region Generation Process

Establish the physical fact first -- terrain, climate, what lives there, what the land does to people who cross it -- then layer in the political pressures that operate in that space. The political is secondary to the physical, but neither is optional.

A player crossing the Katze Plains needs to feel the exposed terrain and understand why no faction has fortified it before the political significance of that gap becomes clear. A player in the Re-Estize Heartlands needs to understand the agricultural richness that makes it worth protecting before the noble politics make sense.

Distribute regional character across the locations within it. Each location expresses the region's physical and political reality differently -- a fortified border city reads the Re-Estize/Baharuth tension differently than a farming village five leagues back from the line.

## Political Reality

No faction currently knows the Great Tomb of Nazarick exists. Every regional NPC's concerns are driven by the world's actual tensions: Re-Estize versus Baharuth along the eastern border, Slane Theocracy theological expansion, Guild network reach across both kingdoms. These pressures predate the player and continue regardless of what the player does.

Re-Estize regions: large, politically fractured. Noble power fills gaps in central authority -- the further from the capital, the less the crown reaches. Wealth is agricultural; the military is capable but politically constrained.

Baharuth regions: tighter administrative control, more uniform culture. The Emperor's intelligence apparatus is present even in mid-tier towns. Military is better-supplied and more reliably commanded.

Slane Theocracy regions: doctrine is visible in civilian life. Scripture presence is felt even outside explicitly religious contexts. The Theocracy does not advertise its capabilities.

Wilderness and borderlands: faction control thins, independent operators fill the gap, danger is ecological and opportunistic rather than organized. If `canonArcActive` is true, reports of unexplained events at the margins of charted territory should increase as the story develops.

generateEncounters.custom:
## Scale-Appropriate Encounters
Encounters must match the location's difficulty tier and the player's capabilities. In E-Rantel: bandits, low-tier undead, common monsters, political complications. In wilderness: higher-tier monsters appropriate to the area. Near Nazarick: nothing should threaten Nazarick's denizens — threats are calibrated to the player character specifically.

CRITICAL: Never generate an encounter involving Floor Guardians or Ainz Ooal Gown as enemies. These beings do not function as combat encounters. They are context, authority, and narrative force.

## Undead Variety
The New World has native undead phenomena: tomb undead in ancient ruins, restless dead in areas of old violence, and the occasional elder lich in deep wilderness. Native undead operate on simple instinct — territorial, mindless, predictable. Nazarick-created undead are sophisticated, purposeful, and follow precise orders. At game start, Nazarick has not yet deployed undead in the outside world. If and when they appear externally, their coordination and discipline should read as unmistakably different from anything native to the New World. Distinguish wild undead from any encountered Nazarick undead in encounter generation.

## Adventurer Guild Rank System
The Guild ranks adventurers on a metal scale, weakest to strongest: Copper, Iron, Silver, Gold, Platinum, Mithril, Orichalcum, Adamantite. Only a handful of Adamantite teams exist across the entire world. Scale all Guild-issued jobs and nearby encounter difficulty to the player's current rank:

- Copper: rats, small vermin, basic errands, no serious life risk
- Iron: small goblin groups, minor undead, short wilderness escorts
- Silver: trolls, undead clusters, dungeon upper levels, dangerous criminals
- Gold: ogre packs, powerful undead, dungeon mid-levels, organized crime
- Platinum: exceptional monsters, dungeon deep levels, political threats
- Mithril: creatures that would devastate armies, rare magic-capable enemies
- Orichalcum/Adamantite: landscape-scale threats — dragon attacks, demon summonings, artifact-level confrontations
On rank advancement, the Guild awards the corresponding rank plate. Ainzach handles promotions personally and makes a brief ceremony of it.

## Non-Combat Resolution
Not every encounter resolves through combat: displayed tier magic commands respect from those who don't know the player's limits (intimidation); intelligent creatures have goals the player can serve (negotiation); self-preserving humans retreat from losing fights, undead do not (retreat); stealth and routing bypass fights the player can't win (bypass).

Difficulty calibration: monsters scale from worker-class at beginner tiers to Wise King-class at hard, Floor Guardian-class at extreme. Beginner adventurer encounters should not include anything above ogre tier.

## Adventurer Guild Quest Board
Post 3-5 jobs calibrated to the player's rank when they check the board. Include variety: extermination, escort, investigation, retrieval, dungeon clearance. Each posting states: target location, reward (Copper: 1-10gp; Iron: 10-50gp; Silver: 50-200gp; Gold: 200-1000gp; Platinum+: negotiated), brief terse description. Lower-rank boards are crowded; Platinum and above show one or two — those adventurers don't need options, they need challenges.

## Combat Loot
After combat, award loot based on enemy type. All drops are probabilistic -- not every enemy carries everything listed. Scale quantity to encounter difficulty and narrative weight. Award items naturally through narration (found on the body, salvaged from wreckage, etc.) rather than stating them as a list.

**Humanoid enemies (carry gear on their person):**
- Goblin Patrol: Monster Fang, Monster Core (small), Rations, possibly a stolen Iron Sword or Health Potion. Chieftain also carries Goblin General's Horn.
- Goblin Chieftain Warband: Goblin General's Horn (chieftain), Iron Sword, Monster Core, stolen Health Potions, Caltrops.
- Bandit Group: Iron Sword, Leather Armor (damaged), Health Potion, Rations, Smoke Bomb, Caltrops, Acid Flask.
- Mercenary Free Company: Steel Longsword, Steel Plate Armor, Health Potion, Weapon Whetstone, Rations, Signal Flare.

Yggdrasil Items in Combat

When a Yggdrasil item is used or revealed before New World characters, narrate the NPC reaction. Weapons: perfect balance, an edge that cannot be dulled, metal with a grain structure that should not exist. A Yggdrasil weapon cuts through armor it should not; an enemy blade visibly fails to mark Yggdrasil armor. The gap reads as wrong, not merely impressive.

Armor: lighter than its material warrants, harder than anything of the same apparent composition, joints that articulate without resistance. No wear, no irregularity -- profoundly unsettling to any craftsman who inspects it closely.

Consumables: activate with precision and completeness that New World equivalents do not approach.
generateEncounters.Creature Power Anchoring:
## Creature Power Is Intrinsic
A creature's power is fixed by its species and type, not by the player's rank or the location's difficulty tier. A goblin is a Copper-to-Iron threat whether a novice or an Adamantite veteran encounters it, and whether it is found in a starter field or a high-tier wilderness. Never inflate a low-tier creature to match the player or the location.

Scaling a location or quest to the player's rank means choosing which enemy TYPES appear and in what numbers, not raising the stats of a weak species. For a high-rank player, low-tier creatures should appear as trivial fodder dispatched without real risk, appear in larger coordinated groups (a warband rather than a patrol), or be replaced by a genuinely stronger variant of the type (a Goblin Lord, champion, or general, which are distinct upgraded entities) or by a different species that actually occupies the target tier.

A real challenge for a high-rank player comes from genuinely high-tier enemies (per the rank table and the encounterElements threat bands), never from an ordinary low-tier creature described as if it were stronger. Never present an ordinary goblin, wolf, or bandit as a Mithril, Orichalcum, Adamantite, or dragon-level threat. Where an encounterElements entry or npcType states a threat band, that band is authoritative.

ItemGenerationAndUsage.custom:
## ITEM INSTRUCTIONS

### NEVER Update For
- Items merely seen, discussed, offered, displayed, inspected, or nearby
- Storage or reorganization within the player's own inventory -- NEVER a remove
- Other characters' actions on their own inventory
- Trades or transfers between NPCs
- Unconfirmed offers, quotes, or negotiations without player agreement

### Non-Combat Item Changes

ADD only when an item physically enters the player's possession -- taken, picked up, received, looted, or purchased.
REMOVE only when an item physically leaves the player's possession -- handed over, consumed, destroyed, or taken.

Transactions are TWO-WAY: if currency is removed for a purchase, the received item MUST be added. A transaction requires both a stated price AND the player explicitly agreeing AFTER it is stated. NPCs placing items on a counter is not a completed sale.

### Combat and Equipment Rules

Consumables leave inventory ONLY when the player explicitly states they consume that specific item. A change in HP or mana is NEVER by itself a reason to remove an item: healing magic, abilities, rest, and absorbing ambient mana restore resources through their own mechanics and consume NO item. Never remove a potion to pay for an effect the player produced themselves. Mana potions do not exist in Yggdrasil. When unsure, remove nothing.

EQUIPMENT DURABILITY: New World items can be damaged or destroyed only in extraordinary circumstances -- targeted destruction, magical disintegration, overwhelming force. Normal combat does not damage equipment. Yggdrasil-grade items are effectively indestructible by New World means; only Yggdrasil-tier power can threaten them. When uncertain, preserve the item.

Nazarick treasury retrieval: when Ainz or a Guardian draws an item from Nazarick stores, remove it from the treasury and add it to inventory. Treat as deliberate preparation, not discovery.

## Item Tiers and Enemy Drops

The core premise is the gap between New World craft and Yggdrasil artifice; preserve it.

New World items: enchanted weapons, runescribed armor, alchemical potions, elemental crystals, parts harvested from magical beasts. Names follow fantasy convention (Mithril Shortsword, Enchanted Greaves, Beast Core).

Yggdrasil items: substantially more powerful. Names are compound English nouns or evocative phrases (Shooting Star, Obsidian Hammer, Ring of Ainz Ooal Gown). Never generate as random loot.

Drops by enemy type:
- Common humans and demi-humans: mundane weapons, ordinary potion vials
- Magical beasts and undead: beast cores, monster parts, occasionally a crude enchanted item
- Elite humans or noble guards: uncommon New World items -- named weapons, moderate-grade armor
- Yggdrasil players or alien entities: named Yggdrasil items with precisely stated properties
- Nazarick Floor Guardians: never drop items; they are servants, not enemy combatants

## Potions

New World potions: cloudy, varied colors, partial effect. A wound that should take days to close heals partially over hours; relief is real but incomplete, full recovery requires multiple doses or rest.

Yggdrasil healing potions (Crimson Healing Potion specifically): unnaturally vivid, almost luminous crimson. Effect is immediate and total -- the wound seals in seconds, flesh visibly rebuilds, pain stops abruptly. A fundamentally different category of object, not a stronger New World potion.

NPC perception scales with expertise: laypeople notice only that it worked fast; healers and priests are unsettled that it breaks the rules of how potions work; skilled alchemists react with clinical alarm and want the vial, its origin, and to pay significant sums for it

In front of the right observer, the Crimson Healing Potion is a plot event.

## Item Types

Equipment slots: Weapon, Offhand, Chest, Head, Hands, Feet, Cloak, Ring, Neck. Generate into the correct slot.

Non-equipment: Consumables (potions, antidotes, vials, tinctures, scrolls); Materials (beast cores, monster parts, alchemical reagents, ore and ingots); Grimoires and scrolls (New World imprecise and dangerous; Yggdrasil data crystals locked and precise); Currency (copper, silver, gold, platinum coins -- never combat drops).

Match item type to context. Bandits drop weapons; basilisks drop beast cores; mages drop scrolls. Do not default to potions.

## Item Materialization and Activation

When an item enters play, describe it as a physical object with sensory weight. Do not summarize acquisition in parenthetical notation.

New World drops have material, condition, and feel as the character reaches (nicks, warmth, unexpected weight) and activate with uncertain magic; describe the sensation, not a precise effect.

Yggdrasil items are precise and declarative; Ainz and Yggdrasil players know exactly what they do before use, so surface the result, not the calculation. New World characters find this uncanny.
ItemGenerationAndUsage.Currency Handling:
## CURRENCY HANDLING
Every coin is an inventory item, tracked by its exact name: Copper Coin, Silver Coin, Gold Coin, Platinum Coin. Fixed exchange: 1 silver = 13 copper; 1 gold = 100 silver; 1 platinum = 10 gold. Brass is not a denomination -- about one in four Copper Coins is simply struck from brass at identical value. Gemstone is a barter-grade valuable, never a standard denomination; price within its bands (lesser stones a few gold, fine stones tens of gold, exceptional pieces a hundred or more), per scene.
### Coin moves only when coin moves
A price, a quote, a haggle, an appraisal, or agreeing to buy is NOT payment. Coins change quantity only when the story shows them physically handed over or received. This is the most common mistake: never add or remove coins for a price that was only spoken.
### Trades are two-way and atomic
A purchase removes the exact coins paid AND adds the goods, together in one update. A sale adds the coins received AND removes the goods, together. If only one side has happened so far, output nothing and wait for the rest. Coins placed on a counter that nobody has picked up is not a completed sale.
### Denominations never convert silently
Move exactly the denominations the scene states: a price paid in silver moves Silver Coin, not a computed equivalent in gold. Change is given only if the scene shows it counted out, and then as its own explicit coins. Converting between denominations is a real transaction at a moneychanger or merchant -- remove the coins given, add the coins received, in the same update, only when the exchange actually happens on screen.
### Treasury and wages
Nazarick treasury coin draws follow the retrieval rule: deliberate withdrawal, exact amounts, both sides tracked. Wages, bribes, rewards, and taxes move coin only at the moment of the handover scene, never at the moment of the promise.
### When unsure
Output nothing. A missed coin update is recoverable; a phantom payment or phantom windfall corrupts the whole economy.
ItemGenerationAndUsage.Inventory Update Rules:
## INVENTORY UPDATE RULES
### The main rule
Change the inventory only when an item physically moves into or out of the player's own hands this turn. If nothing physically moved, output no change. When unsure, output nothing -- a missed update is safer than a wrong one.
### Quantities and names
Move exactly what changed, never a whole stack unless the story shows the whole stack changing hands or being used up. Reuse the exact existing name for an item the player already holds -- never a renamed or paraphrased variant. When an item changes state (identified, enchanted, repaired, broken), remove the old entry and add the new one. Equipping or unequipping never changes quantity.
### Named and unique items add verbatim
When a story or event effect states that a named item enters a player's possession, add exactly that item under its exact authored name. Yggdrasil uniques and guild treasures (the Ring of Ainz Ooal Gown, the Staff, named World Items) exist in fixed quantities: never duplicate one, never regenerate one as loot, never let a second copy of a one-of-a-kind item appear because a scene described it loosely.
### Containers and looting
Searching or looting a body, chest, or room means the player takes what is found there unless they clearly leave it behind. A Bag of Holding's contents are still the player's items; moving things in or out of it is storage, not gain or loss.
ItemGenerationAndUsage.Generated Equipment Bonuses:
## GENERATED EQUIPMENT: STAT BONUSES
Every generated equippable carries a non-empty bonuses array: weapons {type: stat, variable: damage}, armor {type: stat, variable: armor}. Bands from this world's authored scale (health runs 80 + 10 per level):
- Mundane New World craft (shop stock, militia gear): damage 3-8, armor 10-40.
- Quality New World work (named smiths, enchanted or runescribed pieces, elite guards): damage 8-15, armor 40-100.
- Exceptional New World items (adamantite-rank gear, national treasures): damage 15-25, armor 100-200 -- rare, story-justified, never casual loot.
- Yggdrasil-grade: NEVER generated. Authored content only; their stats exist only as written.
Default to the mundane band when unsure. A tool may carry a small skill bonus for its trade instead of combat stats. No generated bonus may implement resurrection, teleportation, or anything the world's rules reserve for authored items.

summarization.custom:
Preserve Nazarick secrecy status precisely: which specific factions, NPCs, or governments have learned Nazarick exists, what they know versus suspect, and what evidence they hold. Do not let this state blur or reset -- a faction that has not learned of Nazarick must stay ignorant until a scene establishes otherwise.

Track the Canon Arc setting (Active or Sandbox) and, if Active, the current state of autonomous faction movement: what each faction has discovered, dispatched, or repositioned since the last summary, so momentum is not lost or re-invented.

Track persona state precisely for any character operating under a second identity (Momon/Ainz Ooal Gown above all): which identity is currently active, who has met which persona, and any circumstantial evidence a character has gathered toward the connection. Never let the summary imply a link the story has not confirmed on-screen.

Preserve standing quest states: which quests are active, which objectives are complete versus pending, and which NPCs are owed a follow-up. Preserve current party composition (who has joined, left, or been lost) and each character's resource state (health, mana, notable equipment gained or spent) at the point of summarization, so continuity does not silently reset between sessions.

generateLearnedAbilities.custom:
## Learnable Ability Families
Overlord recognizes four broad families. Ability proposals must fit one of these or be rejected.

**Tiered Magic** (1st through 10th tier; Super-Tier is reserved for World-class casters and not learnable through normal play).
- 1st-3rd tier: utility cantrips, minor evocations, basic healing
- 4th-6th tier: combat spells of meaningful battlefield impact
- 7th-9th tier: spells that reshape engagements or terrain
- 10th tier and above: the realm of Fluder Paradyne, Theocracy Cardinals, and Nazarick's elite. Treat as out-of-reach.
Magic costs scale with tier. Casters carry mana pools that recover with rest; high-tier spells exhaust the caster.

**Martial Arts** - combat techniques learned by warriors. Stronger than ordinary swordplay but bounded by the wielder's tier. Examples in canon: Fortress, Greater Ability Boost, Sense Enemy, Flow Acceleration. Authored Martial Arts should follow this shape: a named technique, a single sentence describing the effect, a clear activation cost (stamina or once-per-engagement).

**Class Skills** - derived from a character's job class (Warrior, Priest, Magic Caster, Ranger, Rogue, Death Knight, Vampire, etc.). Yggdrasil-derived classes (held by Nazarick figures and the rare Player) carry skills mechanically distinct from New World classes. Class skills are tied to level progression; the engine should not grant a high-tier class skill to a low-level character.

**Racial Abilities** - innate to heteromorphic and demihuman races (lizardmen swimming, Quagoa earth-burrow, vampires' Blood Pool, dragons' breath weapons). These are not learned through training; they're awakened or refined.

## What Does Not Belong
- Modern science abilities (no firearms tech, no electricity, no clockwork beyond the dwarven smith level).
- Cosmic / planar abilities outside the World Items tier. Do not invent powers that rival Surshana, Demiurge, or Ainz himself.
- Generic 'enhanced strength' or 'fast healing' without a class or racial source. Every ability needs a lineage.

## Acquisition Patterns
- Spells: studied from a grimoire, taught by a mentor, or unlocked at a class level.
- Martial Arts: refined through repeated combat at appropriate stakes, or taught by a master.
- Class skills: gained on level up within that class.
- Racial: revealed through a triggering moment (first blood, first transformation, ancestral memory).

The New World.name: The New World
The New World.basicInfo: A high fantasy continent with multiple human nations, demi-human territories, and ancient ruins. Magic operates on a tier system from 1 to 10, with Super-Tier beyond that ceiling. Native casters rarely exceed Tier 3. The arrival of Nazarick has fundamentally altered the continent's balance of power.

Baharuth Empire.name: Baharuth Empire
Baharuth Empire.basicInfo: Fertile plains centered on the imperial capital Arwintar, located in the mid-continent between Re-Estize and the Dwarf mountain range. The terrain is flat and agriculturally productive, with the empire's road network radiating outward from Arwintar. Climate is continental -- hot summers, cold winters, reliable rainfall. The western frontier toward E-Rantel is open grassland with minimal natural barriers. Military infrastructure is dense: garrisons, way-stations, and signal towers dot the road network.

Slane Theocracy.name: Slane Theocracy
Slane Theocracy.basicInfo: A wide basin of temperate farmland and low hills centered on the capital Silksuntecks, located south of the Re-Estize and Baharuth territories. The terrain is open and easily traversed, with rivers running south toward the coast. Climate is mild, with warm summers and wet winters. The region is densely settled by New World standards, with farming villages clustered around the capital and along the main roads. The southern boundary approaches the Dolor Desert, where the climate shifts sharply toward arid.

Abelion Hills.name: Abelion Hills
Abelion Hills.basicInfo: Rugged highland territory to the south, largely outside the control of human nations. Populated by demihuman tribes, monster communities, and scattered outlaw settlements. Nominally under Baharuth sphere of influence but practically ungoverned. The lack of central authority makes this region a refuge for those seeking to avoid oversight from the major powers. Baharuth's intelligence services flag it as a source of periodic instability but have not committed resources to address it.

Elf Country.name: Elf Country
Elf Country.basicInfo: Dense ancient forest occupying the southwestern landmass, largely unexplored by outside nations. The canopy is old-growth with trees reaching unusual size; undergrowth is thick where light penetrates. Crescent Lake sits at the heart of the territory -- a large freshwater body fed by underground springs. Climate is humid and mild year-round, moderated by the forest cover. The terrain beyond the forest edge gives way to scrubland toward the Roble border and open coast to the west.

Argland Council State.name: Argland Council State
Argland Council State.basicInfo: Mountain-backed territory in the far north, dominated by high ridgelines and steep passes. The Argland interior is a series of sheltered valleys with grassland sufficient for grazing and limited agriculture. The mountain walls on three sides make the region naturally defensible. Climate is cold at elevation, milder in the valleys. The Council Citadel sits on a commanding ridge overlooking the primary valley. The mountain passes to the south and east are the only practical land access routes.

Dolor Desert.name: Dolor Desert
Dolor Desert.basicInfo: A vast southern desert that forms the natural southern boundary of the known world's main nations. Sparsely populated, brutally hostile to the unprepared, and home to creatures adapted to heat, dehydration, and the complete absence of mercy.

Re-Estize Borderlands.name: Re-Estize Borderlands
Re-Estize Borderlands.basicInfo: The eastern frontier territory of the Re-Estize Kingdom, centered on E-Rantel. A contested border region between Re-Estize and Baharuth, with active trade routes and ongoing low-level military tension along the eastern roads. The Great Tomb of Nazarick lies hidden somewhere beneath the Azerlisia Mountains -- its presence unknown to any surface nation.

Katze Plains.name: Katze Plains
Katze Plains.basicInfo: A vast grassland expanse on the boundary between the Re-Estize Kingdom and the Baharuth Empire. Site of annual boundary conflicts between the two nations for over a century. The plains are strategically valueless beyond their symbolic role as a contested frontier -- too flat to fortify and too large to hold without numerical superiority. The soil is permanently stained from generations of battle dead.

Karsanas City State Alliance.name: Karsanas City State Alliance
Karsanas City State Alliance.basicInfo: A coalition of independent city-states on the northeastern frontier, maintaining autonomy through trade networks and mutual defense agreements. The Alliance holds no single ruler; governance operates through a council of city representatives. Relations with neighboring nations are managed through commerce rather than military alignment.

Great Minotaur Nation.name: Great Minotaur Nation
Great Minotaur Nation.basicInfo: A nation of minotaur clans occupying the eastern highlands between the Argland Council State and the Beastman Country. Organized around warrior lineages, with clan chiefs holding authority through combat reputation. Trade with outsiders is limited; the nation exports mercenary contracts and raw ore from highland mines.

Troll Kingdom.name: Troll Kingdom
Troll Kingdom.basicInfo: Troll-controlled territories in the eastern wilds, characterized by clan warfare and opportunistic raiding. No formal government exists; dominant troll warlords hold territory through strength. The designation is a diplomatic convenience used by neighboring nations rather than a self-applied label.

Beastman Country.name: Beastman Country
Beastman Country.basicInfo: Territories controlled by beastman clans, positioned adjacent to the Dragon Kingdom. Known for sustained raiding campaigns against human settlements. Beastman clan structure is tribal, with raiding chiefs rising and falling through combat. The threat they pose keeps the Dragon Kingdom in permanent military mobilization.

Dragon Kingdom Country.name: Dragon Kingdom Country
Dragon Kingdom Country.basicInfo: A human nation on the southern frontier, bordered by Beastman Country to the north and the Border Lake to the east. The kingdom maintains a formal monarchy but operates under perpetual military pressure from beastman raids. The ruling family has sought external alliances to address the existential threat from the north.

Re-Estize Heartlands.name: Re-Estize Heartlands
Re-Estize Heartlands.basicInfo: Broad central plains surrounding the royal capital, flat to gently rolling with river tributaries crossing farmland and grazing pasture. The climate is temperate with cold winters and warm summers; snowfall is light compared to the northern reaches. The walled capital dominates the landscape as the largest settlement in the region, visible from the surrounding plains for miles. Secondary towns cluster along the road network radiating from the capital.

Re-Estize Northern Territories.name: Re-Estize Northern Territories
Re-Estize Northern Territories.basicInfo: River valleys and forested uplands north of the royal capital, terrain growing rougher toward the Azerlisia mountain foothills. Winters are harsh with heavy snowfall blocking mountain passes for months. Dense pine and hardwood forest covers the higher ground between the garrison cities. The northern road runs through a series of fortified way-stations. Population is sparser than the heartlands; logging and river trade drive the local economy.

Re-Estize Southern Reaches.name: Re-Estize Southern Reaches
Re-Estize Southern Reaches.basicInfo: Agricultural lowlands stretching south and southeast of the royal capital toward the Katze Plains. The flattest terrain in the kingdom, extensively cultivated with grain and root crops that supply much of the nation. The southeastern edge gives way to the contested borderlands near E-Rantel. Several mid-sized trade cities sit along the road network connecting the capital to the frontier. Summers are long and hot; the plains are dry enough that drought is a recurring concern.

Roble Northern Coast.name: Roble Northern Coast
Roble Northern Coast.basicInfo: Rocky northern coastline backed by forested hills and sea-facing cliffs. Strong sea wind is constant year-round; winters are cold and wet with frequent storms rolling in off the open water. The coastal settlements are built for fishing and defensive access rather than expansion inland. The hilly interior is lightly settled with scattered farming communities where the terrain permits cultivation.

Roble Southern Territories.name: Roble Southern Territories
Roble Southern Territories.basicInfo: The more populated interior and southern coastal zone of the Roble Holy Kingdom. Flatter terrain than the north with river plains suited to grain farming and cattle. The primary administrative center sits here along with the majority of the population. Climate is milder than the northern coast -- warmer summers and less severe winters. The southern boundary meets the Abelion Hills, a persistent source of demi-human raids that keeps the border fortified.

Azerlisia Mountain Approaches.name: Azerlisia Mountain Approaches
Azerlisia Mountain Approaches.basicInfo: The outer slopes and high passes of the Azerlisia mountain range, one of the largest mountain systems in the New World. Permanent snowpack covers the peaks year-round; the treeline sits low compared to more temperate ranges. The mountain pass is the primary overland route connecting the interior dwarf settlements to the outside world and is viable only in summer months. The highest peaks are Dragon Lord nesting territory -- approached by no one.

Dwarf Feo Settlements.name: Dwarf Feo Settlements
Dwarf Feo Settlements.basicInfo: A chain of fortified dwarf cities occupying the mid-elevation valleys and carved directly into the Azerlisia peaks. The settlements are connected by tunneled road systems that bypass the worst of the mountain weather. Surface access between cities is difficult outside summer. The built environment favors stone construction, subterranean expansion, and defensible chokepoints. Rune crafting and ore extraction are the primary industries; the cities trade worked metal and enchanted goods outward through the mountain pass.

Re-Estize Frontier.name: Re-Estize Frontier
Re-Estize Frontier.basicInfo: Open farming and pasture country in central Re-Estize between the capital region and the eastern borderlands. Rolling hills, hedgerow boundaries, and stone-paved cart roads connecting a chain of small villages and farmsteads. Farmers, foresters, and the occasional bandit hold this land; royal patrols are infrequent.

Imperial Eastern Frontier.name: Imperial Eastern Frontier
Imperial Eastern Frontier.basicInfo: Border wilderness east of the Arwintar heartland where regular Imperial patrols thin out into mercenary-watched trade roads. Mixed grassland, scattered woodland, and old irrigation canals that run dry in late summer. Imperial scouts, caravan guards, and small raiding bands move through this contested ground.

Wyvern Rider Wastes.name: Wyvern Rider Wastes
Wyvern Rider Wastes.basicInfo: Windswept steppe between the Slane Theocracy and the Dragon Kingdom where small nomadic tribes raise and ride wyverns from cliff-nest aeries. Tall grass, weathered standing stones, and shallow scree gullies the riders use to ambush. The wyvern tribes trade and raid with both neighbours depending on the season.

Eastern Wasteland.name: Eastern Wasteland
Eastern Wasteland.basicInfo: Dust-bowl plains and rocky scrubland east of the Dragon Kingdom and the Beastman territories. Scarce water, cracked earth, dust storms that blot the sun for days at a time. Bandit warbands, wandering nomads, and sand-hardened predators give the wasteland its reputation.

Northern Sea.name: Northern Sea
Northern Sea.basicInfo: Open cold sea north of the Roble Holy Kingdom coastline. Grey water, fishing boats from the southern ports, the rare sail of a long-haul trader. Sea fog rolls in by morning and burns off by midday.

Land of the King Equestrian.name: Land of the King Equestrian
Land of the King Equestrian.basicInfo: Vast northern steppe inhabited by horse-mounted nomadic clans known to the Empire and Karsanas only by name. Tall grass, low ridges, and herds of wild horses moving with the seasons. Few outsiders return from the steppe with anything useful to say.

Unknown Lands.name: Unknown Lands
Unknown Lands.basicInfo: Wild territories beyond the eastern frontier where no surveyed road runs and no chart is complete. Mixed terrain of taiga, scrub, and rocky uplands. Travellers who venture deep are not heard from again; the ones who turn back early are the ones who write the maps.

Fresh Water Sea.name: Fresh Water Sea
Fresh Water Sea.basicInfo: Long inland sea running along the western coast of the central continent. Warm green water, well-stocked fisheries, and the trade routes that connect Roble's southern ports to the wider world. A regional sailor knows every island and shoal by name.

Southern Open Sea.name: Southern Open Sea
Southern Open Sea.basicInfo: Open water south of the inland Fresh Water Sea where the coast falls away into deep ocean. Deeper, colder water with unfamiliar currents and the occasional sea creature too large for any fishing boat.

Demi-Human Frontier.name: Demi-Human Frontier
Demi-Human Frontier.basicInfo: Loose territory of small mixed demi-human bands -- goblin, hobgoblin, lizardman, and stranger -- between the settled south and the open sea. Broken ground, mixed scrub and marsh, with no central authority. Bands raid each other as readily as outsiders.

Southern Wastes.name: Southern Wastes
Southern Wastes.basicInfo: Stretch of broken country south of the Elf Country forest where the trees thin out into scrub and the ground breaks into deep ravines. Few travellers cross by choice; the elves do not patrol this far south.

Outer Dolor.name: Outer Dolor
Outer Dolor.basicInfo: Marginal land south-east of the main Dolor Desert where the sand gives way to packed gravel and salt flats. Little water; the few caravan routes follow underground aquifers and old reed-marked paths.

Wasteland.name: Wasteland
Wasteland.basicInfo: Bone-dry plain south of the Dragon Kingdom where the ground has cracked open in heat patterns and only the hardiest thorn-scrub survives. Sandstorms scour the wasteland at irregular intervals. Caravans avoid it; nomads cross it only when something else has chased them in.

Eastern Sea.name: Eastern Sea
Eastern Sea.basicInfo: Open ocean east of the Beastman territories and the Wasteland. Warm water, coral reefs near the coast, deep water further out. A trading port called the Sea City sits on the far southern shore but few in the central continent have visited it.

Far Northern Waters.name: Far Northern Waters
Far Northern Waters.basicInfo: Cold open water at the map's northwestern edge, crossed only by the hardiest fishing crews and the occasional trade sail hugging the distant coast.

Imperial Northern Forests.name: Imperial Northern Forests
Imperial Northern Forests.basicInfo: Dense timber country north of the Empire's heartland - logging camps, hunting lodges, and long stretches where the road is the only sign of people.

Open Western Sea.name: Open Western Sea
Open Western Sea.basicInfo: Deep water west of the continent. Weather decides everything out here, and ships that lose sight of the coast keep their prayers short and practical.

Eastern Unknown Fringe.name: Eastern Unknown Fringe
Eastern Unknown Fringe.basicInfo: The last mapped strip before the blank places begin. Travelers who go further east return with stories nobody can check, when they return at all.

Western Coastal Waters.name: Western Coastal Waters
Western Coastal Waters.basicInfo: Busy coastal water threading between fishing grounds and the western trade routes, dotted with sails in fair weather.

Inland Sea Shores.name: Inland Sea Shores
Inland Sea Shores.basicInfo: Low green shoreline along the great freshwater sea - fishing hamlets, reed beds, and ferry landings that connect the coast roads.

Kingdom Southern Marches.name: Kingdom Southern Marches
Kingdom Southern Marches.basicInfo: Rolling farmland and hedge country at the Kingdom's southern edge, where the roads begin watching for trouble out of the hills.

Roble Approach Waters.name: Roble Approach Waters
Roble Approach Waters.basicInfo: The sea lanes approaching the Holy Kingdom's ports, patrolled loosely and fished heavily.

Theocracy Northern Hills.name: Theocracy Northern Hills
Theocracy Northern Hills.basicInfo: Terraced hill country on the Theocracy's northern approaches - shrine villages, watch beacons, and disciplined pilgrim roads.

Border Lake Western Shore.name: Border Lake Western Shore
Border Lake Western Shore.basicInfo: The wooded western shore of the great border lake, claimed on paper by several powers and held in practice by whoever is camped there.

Border Lake.name: Border Lake
Border Lake.basicInfo: The broad lake itself and its scattered islets - a natural border, a fishery, and a smuggler's highway all at once.

Dragon Kingdom Southern Reach.name: Dragon Kingdom Southern Reach
Dragon Kingdom Southern Reach.basicInfo: The Dragon Kingdom's battered southern districts, thinned by years of beastman raids and holding on through stubbornness.

Beastman Southern Range.name: Beastman Southern Range
Beastman Southern Range.basicInfo: Open range and scrub where beastman clans drive their herds and test their young against the land.

Southern Deep.name: Southern Deep
Southern Deep.basicInfo: Empty blue water at the map's southern edge, beyond the fishing grounds and outside anyone's charts worth trusting.

Storm Coast Waters.name: Storm Coast Waters
Storm Coast Waters.basicInfo: A rough stretch of sea known for sudden squalls off the southern capes; wrecks along this coast keep salvagers in business.

Western Dolor Fringe.name: Western Dolor Fringe
Western Dolor Fringe.basicInfo: The gravel flats and thorn scrub where green country gives out and the Dolor Desert begins in earnest.

Southeastern Scrubland.name: Southeastern Scrubland
Southeastern Scrubland.basicInfo: Dry broken country between the beastman ranges and the sea - sparse water, hard travel, and few reasons to linger.

Southeastern Sea.name: Southeastern Sea
Southeastern Sea.basicInfo: Warm open water off the continent's southeastern coast, crossed by the long trade routes to the sea cities.

Far Eastern Highlands.name: Far Eastern Highlands
Far Eastern Highlands.basicInfo: High cold ridge country east of the minotaur lands, mapped from a distance and walked by almost no one.

Western Abelion Hills.name: Western Abelion Hills
Western Abelion Hills.basicInfo: The western reaches of the Abelion Hills, sloping down toward the Holy Kingdom wall - dry ridge country of scattered demi-human bands, known on old maps as the Dark Dwarf Country for the reclusive dark dwarves who hold its deep gullies and cave systems.

Great Tomb of Nazarick.name: Great Tomb of Nazarick

Throne Room.description: The tenth floor. The seat of Ainz Ooal Gown's authority. An immense chamber built to diminish anything that enters it. The throne is at the far end.

Eighth Floor.description: Victim's floor. An environmental hazard zone of extreme cold with cursed aura effects that punish intruders for every kill they make. Almost no one passes through voluntarily.

The Treasury.description: The vault of Ainz Ooal Gown. Contains the accumulated items, World Items, and resources of the guild. Pandora's Actor administers access with absolute precision.

Entrance Hall.description: The outermost entry of Nazarick. A vast stone antechamber lined with undead sentinels. The first thing any intruder encounters.

Treasury Approach.description: The passage leading to the Treasury on the tenth floor. Pandora's Actor guards what lies beyond. The approach itself is a test of intent.

Shalltear's Domain.description: The fourth floor, centered on a vast underground lake of still dark water. Shalltear's personal territory. The silence here has a specific quality.

Ninth Floor Corridor.description: The administrative heart of Nazarick. Ainz's personal chambers, the Round Table conference room, Albedo's Overseer office, and the quarters of the senior staff.

Sixth Floor Colosseum.description: A vast grassland under an artificial sky stretching across the entire sixth floor. Aura and Mare's territory. The colosseum at its centre hosts combat trials.

Cocytus's Frozen Domain.description: The fifth floor. A frozen tundra environment with permanently sub-zero temperatures. Cocytus rules here among ice formations and cold-adapted creatures.

Floors One Through Three.description: Shalltear Bloodfallen's patrol territory. Bone corridors, undead creatures, and the pervasive chill of a place designed to break intruders before they reach anything important.

Demiurge's Hellfire Forge.description: The seventh floor. A volcanic environment of hellfire, demon populations, and Demiurge's experimental operations. The temperature rises sharply from the sixth floor down.

Fourth Floor Underground Lake.description: A vast subterranean body of water occupying the entire fourth floor of Nazarick. The water is unnaturally still and dark, with stone walkways at intervals around the perimeter. Gargantua, an immense stone golem of dense unknown composition with faint geometric etchings, stands as the floor's guardian and obstacle in equal measure. Damaging him at any meaningful rate would require force at the scale of an army or a Yggdrasil-tier weapon.

Great Tomb of Nazarick.basicInfo: A 10-floor dungeon of supreme power, formerly the greatest guild base in Yggdrasil and now a real location in the New World. Home of Ainz Ooal Gown and the Floor Guardians. An impenetrable fortress whose lowest floors are guarded by beings that dwarf anything the New World has produced.
Great Tomb of Nazarick.hiddenInfo:
Nazarick contains eleven World Items. The true depth of its power is unknown even to nations that have glimpsed its outer floors. Ainz Ooal Gown's personal treasury contains items that could destabilize continents.

The Great Tomb of Nazarick lies within this territory. Its location is not public knowledge. The Floor Guardians operate from it, conducting operations across the continent. Demiurge has plans for the New World that even Ainz does not fully know.

E-Rantel.name: E-Rantel

Barracks.description: The military headquarters of E-Rantel's garrison, staffed by Re-Estize Kingdom soldiers. The garrison's role is policing, border security, and deterrence against Baharuth incursions. Not a high-prestige posting -- the city is quiet enough that ambitious soldiers push for reassignment. The commander manages morale through routine and clear expectations.

Graveyard.description: The old graveyard at the city's edge. A working burial site for the city's dead, maintained by the temple district. Undead incursions are a recurring problem at frontier cemeteries -- E-Rantel contracts adventurers to handle periodic clearances. The graveyard is larger than a city this size would normally require, reflecting generations of frontier conflict.

City Gates.description: The heavily reinforced main entrance to E-Rantel. Guards bear Re-Estize colours. Traffic from the surrounding roads -- caravans, adventurers, farmers -- passes through regulated checkpoints.

Marketplace.description: The commercial heart of E-Rantel. Merchants sell goods from across the continent. Re-Estize tax collectors work the stalls alongside guild representatives. Informants and travelers mix with ordinary shoppers. Prices reflect frontier premiums -- trade routes from the east run through imperial territory and the cost shows.

Thieves' Guild.description: An unmarked location known to E-Rantel's criminal community. The guild brokers illicit work, arbitrates disputes between criminal operators, and collects a tithe from independent operators in exchange for protection from rival gangs.

Bareare Pharmacy.description: A well-stocked apothecary in E-Rantel's market district, run by a grandmother and grandson. The shop specialises in medicinal compounds and potion ingredients, with a reputation for quality work and fair prices. A workbench at the back is used for mixing and testing preparations.

Magician's Guild.description: A stone building housing the local chapter of magic practitioners. Weaker than any single Nazarick denizen, but still a center of New World magical knowledge. Spell components, scrolls, and magical services are available.

Merchant's Guild.description: The Merchant's Guild office in E-Rantel registers trade licenses, arbitrates commercial disputes, and sets commodity price floors for the city market. A modest building beside the Marketplace staffed by clerks who handle contracts and tariff assessments.

Pharmacist's Guild.description: A low-fronted building where alchemists and potion merchants register their products and obtain certification seals. The guild tests potions for authenticity and potency, maintaining quality standards for the city's medicine trade.

Adventurer's Guild Hall.description: A large, busy hall serving as the nerve center of adventurer activity in E-Rantel. Job postings cover every board. Experienced adventurers cluster at tables. The Guild Master manages registration, ranks, and contracts. New adventurer registration costs 5 silver coins at the clerk's counter; all new registrants start at Copper rank.

E-Rantel.basicInfo: A fortified border city on the Re-Estize Kingdom's eastern frontier with the Baharuth Empire. An active trade hub and the base of a large Adventurer's Guild chapter. Garrisoned by Re-Estize Kingdom soldiers. The city is functional, busy, and dealing with the usual pressures of a frontier town between two powers that don't fully trust each other.
E-Rantel.hiddenInfo: E-Rantel's administrative structure contains a fault line that appears structural from the outside: it is simultaneously a Re-Estize Kingdom city and the most economically active point on a contested border, which means its revenues attract noble interest that the city's governance can only partially resist. The Adventurer's Guild operates as the city's de facto emergency response capability; the regular garrison is adequate for maintaining order but not for handling Platinum-tier threats or coordinated monster incursions, both of which have occurred in living memory. The cemetery district has a long history of producing low-level undead phenomena that the Guild handles routinely but that the official garrison documentation systematically underreports to avoid alarming the capital. A smuggling network operates through the merchant district that the city watch is aware of and has tacitly tolerated because the network's operators also provide useful intelligence about unusual activity on the roads.

Re-Estize Capital.name: Re-Estize Capital

City Gates.description: The fortified entry to the capital, heavily guarded. Travelers are inspected for weapons and intentions. Traffic includes merchants from Baharuth, adventurers seeking guild work in the capital, and supply caravans moving goods between the city and outlying noble estates. The guards are professional and thorough.

Royal Palace.description: The seat of the Re-Estize monarchy. Throne rooms, council chambers, and private apartments for the aging king and his court. Noble visitors are common. Security is high but not at Nazarick-class levels. The royal household maintains its own personal guards alongside the standing palace garrison.

Common Quarter.description: The residential and commercial district where ordinary citizens live. Taverns, workshops, and markets. The economic pressure of supporting the kingdom's military and noble class falls most visibly here -- prices are high and wages are not keeping pace. The quarter is not impoverished by frontier standards, but it is aware of its own stagnation.

Noble District.description: Wide streets lined with grand manor houses. Noble families compete for influence, wealth, and proximity to the throne. Intrigue is constant. A visitor who looks wealthy will be assessed for utility immediately.

Thieves' Guild.description: Operating beneath the surface of the Common Quarter, the Thieves' Guild manages the capital's organized criminal trade. It controls information brokerage, black market goods, and enforcement contracts among competing underground factions.

Warrior's Guild.description: The gathering place for the kingdom's best fighters. The Warrior Captain commands from here when not on campaign. Warriors-for-hire, veterans, and those seeking to test themselves congregate at the sparring yards and meeting halls.

Magician's Guild.description: A compound of towers and gated structures -- the largest Magician's Guild branch in the Kingdom. Three five-story towers rise along the perimeter. The guild's magic item stocks are the most significant in the Re-Estize region. Scroll procurement, enchanted equipment appraisal, and theoretical research all operate under the same roof. The guild maintains deliberate neutrality from noble politics, which makes it trusted by factions that trust nothing else.

Merchant's Guild.description: The Re-Estize Kingdom's central Merchant's Guild branch occupies a prominent building in the Common Quarter. It coordinates inter-city trade agreements, issues letters of credit, and mediates between noble trading houses and independent merchants.

Pharmacist's Guild.description: The capital branch of the Pharmacist's Guild certifies medicinal compounds and regulates the sale of potions across the kingdom. Guild-certified healers and apothecaries display a seal that distinguishes their products from uncertified goods.

Adventurer's Guild Hall.description: The local branch of the Adventurer's Guild. A functional hall with a quest board, a clerk's counter for registration and contract processing, and tables where adventurers wait, eat, and take stock of available work. Registration costs 5 silver coins; all new registrants start at Copper rank. Rules, fees, and rank structure are identical to every other guild branch.

Re-Estize Capital.basicInfo: The capital of the Re-Estize Kingdom and the seat of its monarchy. A city of politics, noble intrigue, and aging military pride, with rival noble factions competing for influence at court while the eastern border, urban safety, and treasury management go inadequately addressed. The headquarters of one of the kingdom's adamantite-ranked adventurer teams is also based here.
Re-Estize Capital.hiddenInfo: The capital's surface of political stability conceals a factional landscape in which the major noble houses maintain intelligence operations against each other as a matter of routine. The palace itself is penetrated by informants from at least three of the Six Great Noble families, a situation King Ramposa III is aware of and has not moved against because the political cost of identifying and removing them would exceed the cost of operating with their presence known.
