Princess Renner's residential quarter is the single area of the palace where external penetration has been reliably prevented, through means she has arranged personally. The capital's information networks are denser and more accurate about Re-Estize events than about anything happening on the eastern frontier, a blind spot that has strategic implications.

Carne Village.name: Carne Village

Forest Edge.description: The border between Carne Village's farmland and the Tob Forest. The forest begins abruptly at the tree line -- within a hundred feet the canopy closes and the light changes quality. Villagers harvest herbs and kindling from the immediate edge but know better than to go further without experienced guidance. Monster activity from deeper in the forest occasionally pushes into this zone.

Village Center.description: The heart of Carne Village -- a well, meeting house, and open square. Villagers gather here for community business, seasonal markets, and emergencies. The village elder, an old man who has led the community for many years, manages village affairs from the meeting house. The square doubles as an emergency muster point when creature activity from the forest becomes a concern.

Village Perimeter.description: The open edge of Carne Village where farmland and footpaths give way to open ground. No wall, no gate, no defensive structure of any kind. The village is entirely exposed on all sides. Villagers rely on distance from major roads and the relative unattractiveness of a poor frontier settlement as their only protection.

Carne Village.basicInfo: A small farming village on the outskirts of the Re-Estize Kingdom, near the Tob Forest. Subsistence farming community with no garrison and minimal defensive infrastructure. Located close enough to the frontier that bandit activity and occasional monster incursions are a known hazard. The villagers are ordinary Re-Estize citizens with no particular military capacity and no connections to major powers.
Carne Village.hiddenInfo: The Slane Theocracy's Sunlit Scripture has identified this village as a target. Its proximity to the frontier and lack of defenses make it suitable for a staged attack designed to provoke a specific military response from the Kingdom.

Tob Forest.name: Tob Forest

Deep Forest.description: Beyond the exploitable outer band. Canopy closes overhead and light becomes filtered and intermittent. The undergrowth is denser than any managed woodland. The creatures encountered here are categorically different from the outer band — not just stronger but clearly aware of being observed.

Forest Edge.description: The accessible outer band of Tob Forest. Herb gathering, small game hunting, and logging operations run here without serious incident. The creatures at this depth are at a level manageable by organised village groups. The outer edge is well-mapped by adventurers based in E-Rantel who run regular clearance contracts.

Ancient Ruins.description: Stone structures predating any current nation, partially reclaimed by the forest. Magic items of unknown origin rest here. Scholars who learn of them sometimes mount expeditions. The expeditions end poorly.

Forest Depths.description: The inner forest where few return. Treants capable of destroying fortifications roam here. Goblin warrens house tribes that have grown powerful. The air feels different — heavier, older, watched.

Forest Approaches.description: The outer edge of the Tob Forest, where adventurers from E-Rantel regularly hunt. Manageable creatures: wolves, giant insects, low-tier undead. Markers indicate how far experienced parties have gone.

The Watched Stillness.description: A section of deep forest where the trees grow unusually dense and the air carries an odd stillness. Creatures that typically range freely through the deeper forest give this area a wide margin. The cause is not apparent to anyone who has investigated. No permanent structures exist here. The stillness has a quality that experienced rangers describe as watched.

Forest Clearing Network.description: A series of open glades connected by paths that seem almost too convenient to be natural. Goblin tribes use some of these clearings as meeting sites and trade points. The paths between glades show signs of use that predate the current goblin populations. Whatever shaped this network is not present, or not visible.

Tob Forest.basicInfo: A vast forest south of E-Rantel, home to multiple tribes of goblins, treants, and more dangerous creatures. Adventurers come here for monster-hunting jobs; most who go too deep do not return. The forest has no known permanent human settlements. Its deeper sections remain largely unexplored.
Tob Forest.hiddenInfo: The Tob Forest's goblin population is significantly larger than the southern settlements' headcount estimates suggest — actual numbers are not known because the forest's interior has not been systematically surveyed. The treant communities in the central forest are ancient enough to have memories of the region before the current human settlements existed; they do not communicate this to humans as a matter of course. The forest floor at depth contains ruins from a pre-existing civilization that the current goblin tribes have colonized without understanding. A cave system beneath the forest connects to points outside the tree line that neither human settlements nor Nazarick are currently aware of. The forest's monster density creates a natural buffer zone that has historically prevented the Baharuth Empire from using southern approaches for military staging.

Katze Plains.name: Katze Plains

Fog Boundary.description: The edge of the Katze Plains' permanent fog bank. The transition from normal air to the fog zone is physically noticeable -- temperature drops slightly and sound carries differently. Armies use the fog boundary as an informal staging line -- the fog equalizes visibility advantages and neither side has found a reliable way to exploit the terrain asymmetrically. The local superstition holds that the fog remembers everyone who has walked into it.

The Open Plain.description: The central contested ground of the Katze Plains. Flat, fog-muffled, and featureless except for old earthworks thrown up by generations of armies that never quite committed to battle. The fog here is denser than at the edges -- it muffles sound and makes distance estimation unreliable. Scouts who venture too far in without landmarks have circled back to their own lines.

Katze Plains.basicInfo: A flat, fog-covered plain on the contested border between the Re-Estize Kingdom and the Baharuth Empire. The two nations have clashed here repeatedly over generations without either achieving decisive victory. The fog is a permanent natural feature of the terrain, giving the plain an eerie character that has accumulated centuries of superstition. The annual military standoffs between the two nations typically concentrate here, with both armies maneuvering across the same flat ground their predecessors did. No decisive battle has been fought in living memory.
Katze Plains.hiddenInfo: The Katze Plains fog has persisted through every recorded historical period of the central continent, predating both the Re-Estize Kingdom and the Baharuth Empire. Local scholars have debated its origin for generations without producing consensus -- some attribute it to a magical ley line beneath the plains, others to atmospheric peculiarities of the region's elevation, others to residual effects from a pre-continental civilization whose ruins lie scattered across the central depression. The annual Re-Estize-Baharuth military standoff on this ground has suppressed systematic investigation; neither army wants to advertise that the field they are staging on is poorly understood. The central plains contain a geographic depression that has produced the highest casualty concentration in the periodic border conflicts; the depression is the deepest part of the fog cover, and the precise reason for its persistent low visibility has never been mapped. No one has investigated the centre systematically.

Azerlisia Mountains.name: Azerlisia Mountains

Mountain Pass.description: The only reliable route through the Azerlisia Mountains. Heavily trafficked by dwarven caravans and occasionally by adventurers seeking the Dwarf Kingdom. Frost giants patrol higher elevation reaches.

Dwarf Kingdom Gates.description: The reinforced entrance to the Dwarf Kingdom carved into the mountain itself. Rune-inscribed stone doors stand fifteen meters high. The dwarves who guard them are equipped far beyond average human military capability.

Azerlisia Mountains.basicInfo: A vast mountain range at the edge of explored territory, home to the Dwarf Kingdom and ancient Dragon Lords. Snow-capped peaks rise beyond practical travel. The Dwarf Kingdom trades in runes and crafted goods. The Dragon Lords predate every human nation.
Azerlisia Mountains.hiddenInfo: The Azerlisia range contains ruins and sealed passages from the Dwarf Kingdom's golden period that the current Dwarf Kingdom has not reclaimed and does not officially acknowledge. The sealed sections contain military installations designed against threats that would require a coherent explanation of what those threats were — one the Dwarf Kingdom's historians have suppressed rather than provided. Dragon habitation in the upper peaks is stable but not zero; the True Dragon Lords of the Argland Council State treat the eastern Azerlisia range as boundary territory. The pass connecting the Dwarf Kingdom lowlands to the broader New World is the only practical land route through the range, a fact the Dwarf Kingdom's political dysfunction has made them unable to leverage diplomatically.

Arwintar Imperial Capital.name: Arwintar Imperial Capital

Arena.description: The Blood Emperor's arena, used both for entertainment and for political messaging. Gladiatorial combat, creature displays, and public executions all occur here. The crowd reads the imperial mood by what appears in the arena on any given day.

Mage Quarter.description: The district where the Empire's magic practitioners live and work. A tall private tower dominates the skyline -- the largest structure in the quarter and the centre of gravity for the Empire's magical research network. The district is quieter than the merchant or military zones: its residents work odd hours and value silence. The academy's secondary facilities extend into this quarter from the main campus.

Magic Academy.description: The Baharuth Empire's primary magical research and training institution. Students begin at a young age and graduate by examination rather than by social standing. The Academy's library contains theoretical texts that exceed anything in Re-Estize. Recent absences in senior leadership have left an administrative void that has not been cleanly filled.

Imperial Arena.description: A large combat arena used for both entertainment and military evaluation. Imperial knights demonstrate techniques here. Visiting warriors are occasionally invited to fight — refusal is diplomatically awkward. The seats fill for significant bouts. The emperor attends in person when he wants to evaluate someone.

Market Quarter.description: Arwintar's commercial district. More regulated than Re-Estize's equivalent. Merchant guilds operate under imperial licensing. Goods are taxed and logged. The district runs efficiently because inefficiency is treated as a financial crime.

Noble District.description: Imperial noble houses with more military discipline than Re-Estize equivalents. Nobles here serve or they fall. The competition is just as fierce, but expressed through demonstrated utility rather than pure intrigue.

Imperial Palace.description: The administrative centre of the empire. Clean lines, efficient layout, and no unnecessary ornamentation. Business is conducted from a working office rather than a throne room, in keeping with the regime's preference for function over ceremony. Guards are rotating imperial knights, the best non-magical soldiers the empire produces.

Magician's Guild.description: Separate from the imperial Magic Academy, the Magician's Guild is an independent body that registers working mages, brokers magical contracts, and provides a neutral meeting ground for spellcasters outside of imperial oversight.

Merchant's Guild.description: The Imperial Merchant's Guild in Arwintar handles trade licensing for goods moving through Baharuth Empire territories. It maintains close ties with the imperial treasury and enforces tariff collection on cross-border commerce.

Pharmacist's Guild.description: The Baharuth branch of the Pharmacist's Guild operates within the Market Quarter, certifying alchemical goods produced in the empire. It maintains a register of licensed practitioners and coordinates with the Magic Academy on experimental compound testing.

Noble Estates District.description: Estates belonging to the empire's established noble families -- those who survived the imperial purge of corrupt nobility early in the current reign. The remaining nobles are precisely aware of the regime's tolerance thresholds and conduct themselves accordingly.

Adventurer's Guild Hall.description: The local branch of the Adventurer's Guild. A functional hall with a quest board, a clerk's counter for registration and contract processing, and tables where adventurers wait, eat, and take stock of available work. Registration costs 5 silver coins; all new registrants start at Copper rank. Rules, fees, and rank structure are identical to every other guild branch.

Arwintar Imperial Capital.basicInfo: The capital of the Baharuth Empire and the seat of its meritocratic government. A planned city with wide boulevards, efficient infrastructure, and a population that includes significantly more trained mages than any Re-Estize equivalent, anchored by the Imperial Magic Academy. The capital runs on paperwork, competence, and the constant awareness that the ruling office watches its officials closely.
Arwintar Imperial Capital.hiddenInfo:
Jircniv is the most politically capable ruler in the current era. He maintains standing orders for his intelligence networks to flag any unusual power concentrations along the frontier. Recent scout reports of strange magical activity east of the border have reached him; he has not yet determined whether they represent an opportunity or a threat. Fluder Paradyne is his most valued magical adviser and Jircniv relies on his assessments for strategic decisions involving magic.

Fluder Paradyne, the Empire's greatest mage, has spent decades seeking a practitioner whose magical ceiling exceeds his own. He serves as court wizard and director of the Imperial Magic Academy. Jircniv maintains intelligence networks along the eastern frontier, alert for unusual power concentrations or political shifts that could affect imperial interests. He is the most capable political operator among the current generation of human rulers.

Imperial Colosseum District.name: Imperial Colosseum District

Colosseum Floor.description: The fighting surface. Sand over stone. Drainage channels cut into the perimeter handle the practical aftermath of serious bouts. The stands hold tens of thousands. Sound here is total — cheering crowds create a physical pressure. Fighters learn quickly that showmanship matters as much as competence.

Fighter Preparation Area.description: Rooms beneath the colosseum floor where fighters wait before bouts. Equipment maintenance, injury treatment, pre-fight briefings. The smell of metal polish and liniment. Veterans are recognisable by their composure. New fighters are recognisable by everything else.

Imperial Colosseum District.basicInfo: The entertainment and evaluation quarter of Arwintar. The colosseum hosts gladiatorial exhibitions, martial tournaments, and the occasional criminal execution staged as combat. The district around it houses training facilities, gladiator quarters, bookmakers, and taverns catering to fight audiences. The emperor uses colosseum results as one data point in assessing military talent.
Imperial Colosseum District.hiddenInfo: The colosseum's booking records are maintained by imperial intelligence as a secondary function — notable fighters who appear here are flagged for recruitment assessment. Several current imperial knights were identified through colosseum performance.

Great Lake.name: Great Lake

Lake Centre.description: Open water. Deep. Cold in the lower depths. Used for large-scale fishing and tribe-to-tribe travel. Lizardmen are strong swimmers. Large aquatic predators inhabit the depths but coexist with the tribes through established territorial understanding.

Swamp Channels.description: The maze of waterways connecting the lake to the broader marsh territory. Navigable by those who know the routes — disorienting to outsiders. Monster populations here are denser than in open water. Used by the tribes for controlled border management.

Green Claw Shoreline.description: The territory of the Green Claw tribe along the lake's northern shore. Fishing platforms extend over the water. Scale-huts are built on pilings. The tribe's warriors are visible at all perimeter points -- alert by default, especially toward neighboring tribal territories where boundary disputes are ongoing.

Tribe Meeting Ground.description: A central island in the lake used for inter-tribal council meetings. Neutral territory. The island's stone surface is covered in tribal markings dating back generations. Decisions made here carry binding weight across all tribes.

Great Lake.basicInfo: A vast freshwater lake in the southern wetlands, the centre of lizardman territory. Multiple tribes hold sections of the shoreline and have done so for generations. The lake provides food, fresh water, and spiritual significance. Inter-tribal conflict over fishing grounds and territorial boundaries is a recurring feature of lake politics. The tribes have developed a meeting-ground tradition for resolving major disputes without open warfare, though it does not always succeed.
Great Lake.hiddenInfo: The lake bottom contains ruins of a pre-lizardman civilisation. Zaryusu has explored sections of it but has not catalogued the full extent. Some underwater sections are still structurally intact and contain ancient enchantments that pre-date current New World magical frameworks.

Dwarf Royal Capital Feo Jera.name: Dwarf Royal Capital Feo Jera

Royal Hall.description: The Dwarf King's throne hall, a vast carved chamber with a ceiling lost in shadows overhead. The hall has hosted ten generations of dwarven rulers. Its walls display carvings of battles won and alliances made. The current king sits here daily, conducting a government increasingly aware of its own fragility.

Market Warrens.description: The trading district carved into the mountain's lower levels. Dwarven goods — metalwork, stonework, mineral extraction — are traded here with caravans that make the journey north. The market is smaller than it was historically, reflecting the kingdom's contraction.

Runesmiths Hall.description: The workshop district where the remaining dwarven runesmiths practice the ancient art of rune carving. The knowledge was almost lost — several techniques were recovered only through archival research. The runesmiths here are among the most technically skilled individuals in the New World, working a craft that predates current enchantment methods.

Military Barracks.description: The dwarven military's residential and training facility. Warriors here are competent at tunnel fighting and defensive holding actions. Open-field combat is not their strength -- a weakness the quagoa have exploited in incremental territorial advances over decades. The garrison debates whether to commit to a counter-offensive or continue the current policy of holding fixed positions.

Forge Terraces.description: The stepped smelting and forge levels cut into the mountainside, where ore becomes the metalwork the kingdom trades on. Fewer furnaces burn than the terraces were built for, and cold hearths outnumber lit ones. Heat, hammer-noise, and the smell of scorched stone fill the worked levels.

Deep Tunnels.description: The oldest and lowest shafts, descending toward the depths the quagoa press up from. Several branches are walled off or abandoned, held only by patrol. The dark here is total beyond the reach of a lamp, and the air tastes of cold rock.

Dwarf Royal Capital Feo Jera.basicInfo: The primary city of the Dwarf Kingdom, carved into mountain rock over centuries. A dense vertical city of tunnels, chambers, and great halls. The capital of a proud culture that has been declining for generations -- quagoa pressure from below, runesmith knowledge loss, and political stagnation have all compounded. The king governs a population that is proud of its history and anxious about its present.
Dwarf Royal Capital Feo Jera.hiddenInfo: The Dwarf King is privately willing to offer significant concessions to any outside power capable of providing military protection against the Quagoa threat -- the public conservative faction does not know the extent of what the king has considered. The remaining runesmiths number fewer than a dozen.

Ancient Ruins Dungeon.name: Ancient Ruins Dungeon

Deep Levels.description: The largely unexplored lower section. Expedition teams that reached this depth reported active constructs, magical traps at a tier above anything accessible in the upper section, and a faint hum that has no identified source. No team has documented what lies below.

Upper Ruins.description: The explored section. Partially collapsed corridors with clearable rubble. Trap mechanisms that have been documented and disarmed by previous parties. Creature lairs in side chambers — abandoned by anything intelligent but occupied by monsters that moved into the power vacuum.

Middle Depths.description: The transition zone. The architecture here is better preserved but stranger. Wall carvings in an undeciphered script. Doors that open on magical triggers rather than physical mechanisms. Creature encounters escalate sharply — fighters who handled the upper levels comfortably find themselves struggling.

Ancient Ruins Dungeon.basicInfo: A partially collapsed underground complex of unknown origin in the Wilderness Territories. Adventurer teams have explored the upper levels for years without reaching the bottom. The architecture does not match any known New World civilisation. Magic emanations suggest active enchantments at significant depth. Creature populations escalate sharply past the third explored level.
Ancient Ruins Dungeon.hiddenInfo: The ruins' deep levels contain dormant constructs using a magical framework inconsistent with New World development. The architecture style shares elements with descriptions from Yggdrasil lore that Ainz recognises. A former Player may have built or repurposed this structure in an earlier era.

Eight Fingers Warehouse District.name: Eight Fingers Warehouse District

Warehouse Row.description: Rows of locked warehouses with legitimate-looking manifests posted on the doors. Guards in merchant livery — good enough to pass casual inspection, too disciplined for actual hired labour. The smell of goods that do not match any manifest. Loading happens at off hours.

Counting House.description: The financial administration point for this district's operations. Double-entry books — one for inspectors, one for actual figures. The counting house staff are vetted by threat, not contract. Their composure reflects awareness of what happens to people who make accounting errors.

Eight Fingers Warehouse District.basicInfo: A section of E-Rantel's outer commercial district that serves as a logistics hub for Eight Fingers criminal operations. Warehouses ostensibly registered to legitimate merchants front for smuggling, drug distribution, and slave trafficking operations. The organisation's reach extends to multiple cities. Its leadership operates from this district in rotating locations to avoid investigation.
Eight Fingers Warehouse District.hiddenInfo: Eight Fingers has bribed guild officials in three cities. Their drug operations fund a significant portion of the organisation's political corruption budget.

Wilderness Trading Post.name: Wilderness Trading Post

Storage Yard.description: Secure storage for goods in transit. A fee-based service. Contents are not inspected by post staff — maintaining that fiction is what makes merchants willing to use it. Guards on rotation. The fence line is solid but not magical.

Trading Hall.description: The main exchange floor. Stalls, negotiation tables, a scale for weighing trade goods. Noise is constant. Multiple languages. The post factor moves through the hall at regular intervals — observing without appearing to observe. Prices here reflect actual supply and demand without guild interference.

Tavern and Inn.description: Accommodation and food for travellers. The information density per square metre is exceptional — travelling merchants, mercenaries between contracts, and scouts resting between jobs all pass through. The barkeep has heard everything and volunteers nothing.

Wilderness Trading Post.basicInfo: A fortified trading settlement at the junction of several overland trade routes through unsettled territory. Run by a consortium of merchant houses that maintain neutrality as a business necessity — the post trades with kingdom representatives, empire factors, and independent operators without prejudice. Monster hunters, caravan guards, and scouts pass through regularly.
Wilderness Trading Post.hiddenInfo: The trading post's factor has maintained a private record of unusual individuals and equipment passing through for the past three years. The record was not started for any intelligence agency — the factor is simply observant. The record now contains descriptions that would be of interest to Theocracy intelligence.

Blue Rose Headquarters.name: Blue Rose Headquarters

Planning Room.description: Maps, mission notes, target dossiers, and the team's accumulated intelligence on active threats. The team leader runs briefings here before major operations. The room is warded against scrying by a permanent enchantment installed by one of the team's casters. Seating accommodates the full team of six.

Equipment Room.description: Gear storage and maintenance. Each team member's equipment is staged here between missions. The weapons here represent more magical power per square metre than most kingdom armouries. Maintenance is taken seriously — the equipment is life-critical.

Private Quarters.description: Individual rooms for team members who use the headquarters as a base. Two of the rooms are shared by choice. One room has no window and additional private wards layered into its walls. The leader's room has a desk perpetually covered in correspondence with noble contacts.

Blue Rose Headquarters.basicInfo: The private base of operations for the Blue Rose, one of Re-Estize's adamantite-ranked adventurer teams, located within the Re-Estize Capital. The headquarters functions as a planning room, equipment storage, and secure meeting point for missions that require more discretion than a guild hall allows. Access is restricted to team members and invited guests.
Blue Rose Headquarters.hiddenInfo: Lakyus's holy sword Kilineyram is a cursed blade that exerts influence on its wielder. The team is aware of this but Lakyus has not fully disclosed the extent of the sword's effect on her decision-making. Evileye's true identity as a vampire is known within the team and concealed from everyone else.

Eight Fingers Headquarters.name: Eight Fingers Headquarters

Council Room.description: The meeting space for the division heads. Around a table with eight seats — the title 'Eight Fingers' is literal. Discussions here determine the organisation's major strategic moves. No servants are permitted inside during meetings. Records are destroyed immediately after.

Vault Corridor.description: The corridor leading to Eight Fingers' financial reserves and blackmail archive. Both doors are physically reinforced and magically locked. The blackmail archive contains material on over three hundred individuals including five noble families and two guild officials.

Eight Fingers Headquarters.basicInfo: The true operational centre of the Eight Fingers criminal syndicate. Location rotates but is currently within the Re-Estize Capital's merchant district, hidden behind three layers of legitimate business fronts. The eight division heads rarely meet in person — communications are typically handled through cutouts. The headquarters is used only for major strategic decisions.
Eight Fingers Headquarters.hiddenInfo: Demiurge has complete knowledge of Eight Fingers' organisational structure. Several division heads have been replaced by Nazarick-influenced individuals without their colleagues noticing. Eight Fingers is being steered without its leadership's awareness to serve Nazarick's regional strategy.

Re-Estize Border Fort.name: Re-Estize Border Fort

Stables.description: Horse and supply management for the garrison. The farrier here doubles as a field medic. The stables smell of hay and iron — the iron from the weapons rack on the far wall.

Watchtower.description: The observation post with sight lines across the contested border zone and the Katze Plains to the east. The watch rotation covers all hours. Observers log what they see in standardized reports -- troop movements, merchant traffic, unusual creature activity. The logs are sent to the capital weekly. The garrison uses the data for their own tactical planning regardless of whether anyone at the capital reads it.

Garrison Hall.description: The main operational building of the border fort. Duty rosters on the wall, a tactical map of the surrounding territory, and a commander's desk visible through a glass partition. Soldiers here are professional but aware that the strategic situation they trained for no longer exists.

Re-Estize Border Fort.basicInfo: A fortified military outpost on the contested border between Re-Estize Kingdom and Baharuth Empire territory. Garrisoned year-round. The site of annual military posturing between the two powers — open warfare has been avoided, but skirmishes along the road are a recurring problem. The garrison watches both directions.
Re-Estize Border Fort.hiddenInfo: The garrison commander has been maintaining unusually careful logs of Baharuth troop movements along the opposite side of the border. The pattern is not quite right for the seasonal posturing both sides have conducted for decades -- the timing is slightly off and the unit compositions have changed. The commander has filed reports. The reports have gone to the capital and received no reply. He continues filing them.

Imperial Magic Academy Campus.name: Imperial Magic Academy Campus

Lecture Halls.description: Tiered seating halls for structured instruction. Classes run on fixed schedules. Instruction quality remains high -- the established curriculum is still in use. The faculty are competent practitioners teaching material designed by someone who operated in a different tier of capability entirely.

Practice Ranges.description: Outdoor and enclosed spaces for spell testing at scale. Reinforced walls and ceiling in the enclosed sections. Target constructs for combat spell evaluation. Students are supervised during practice hours — the occasional containment failure makes this policy non-negotiable.

Research Laboratory Block.description: The faculty research spaces and the academy's senior private laboratory. Active research continues throughout the block. The senior laboratory occupies the eastern wing and is accessible only with personal authorisation from its owner. The quality of work produced here consistently exceeds anything other institutions in the New World can match.

Imperial Magic Academy Campus.basicInfo: The Baharuth Empire's primary magical education institution, located within Arwintar. A structured campus of lecture halls, practice ranges, dormitories, and research laboratories, with entry by examination rather than social standing. The academy is the most productive magical research body in the human nations, and its curriculum and research priorities are set from within.
Imperial Magic Academy Campus.hiddenInfo: Fluder's private research laboratory occupies a sealed wing of the research block. The faculty know his official research goals; they do not know what his private pursuit has become in recent years. He has grown increasingly focused on the theoretical maximum of magical achievement -- a fixation the faculty ascribe to the eccentricity of genius. The laboratory logs he keeps are not accessible to anyone else.

Theocracy Black Scripture Base.name: Theocracy Black Scripture Base

Reliquary Access.description: The passage to the Theocracy's relic vault. A series of authentication checkpoints, each progressively more involved. The vault itself is beyond the last checkpoint. Only Cardinals may pass the final gate unescorted.

Scripture Barracks.description: The Black Scripture's residential quarters. No rank insignia visible on the exterior — the building looks like a minor administrative annex. The members inside are visibly not administrators. Equipment maintained in personal rooms rather than a common armoury — each member's gear is too specialised for shared storage.

Theocracy Black Scripture Base.basicInfo: The restricted operating base of the Black Scripture, the Slane Theocracy's most powerful Scripture division. Its precise location within Silksuntecks is known only to the Cardinals and to the Scripture's own members. The base houses the Theocracy's most dangerous human combatants, their relics, and their operational planning.
Theocracy Black Scripture Base.hiddenInfo: The Black Scripture possesses relics of the Six Great Gods, including items whose true nature as Yggdrasil equipment the cardinals only partially understand. Antilene has been evaluated as potentially capable of fighting the last Dragon Lord. She has been tasked with finding opponents strong enough to be worth fighting, and has not found one yet in the New World.

Green Claw Village.name: Green Claw Village

Village Center.description: The open communal ground at the heart of Green Claw village where the tribe gathers for decisions, meals, and storage of communal resources.

Green Claw Village.basicInfo: Primary settlement of the Green Claw lizardman tribe on the eastern shore of the Great Lake. The village is constructed on raised wooden platforms above the waterline, with scale-huts, communal storage, and fishing pens arranged around a central meeting ground. Recently introduced fish cultivation techniques have improved the tribe's resource situation relative to neighbouring tribes, which has not gone unnoticed or unresented.
Green Claw Village.hiddenInfo: Zaryusu's fish cultivation knowledge gives the Green Claw tribe a resource advantage that other tribes have noticed. The Red Eye and Small Fang tribes have both sent quiet inquiries about whether the technique could be shared -- inquiries that carry implicit pressure behind the courtesy. The tribe's elders debate whether sharing the knowledge reduces the advantage or reduces the threat.

Feo Berkana Mines.name: Feo Berkana Mines
Feo Berkana Mines.basicInfo: The principal mining complex beneath the Dwarf Kingdom. Multiple shafts extending deep into the mountain, worked by runesmith teams and standard laborers. The runesmith tradition originated here -- the older shafts contain working examples of pre-decline runework integrated into the mine structure itself. Undead incursion from below is a recurring operational problem.
Feo Berkana Mines.hiddenInfo: The deepest active shaft has breached a pre-dwarf structure of unknown origin. The runesmith king has sealed that level pending assessment. Two survey teams that went down have not returned.

Silksuntecks.name: Silksuntecks

City Gates.description: The fortified entry points of Silksuntecks. Paladins check travelers. Heteromorphic races are turned away. The city has never been breached.

paths: Grand Temple of the Six Gods
Scripture Compound.description: The training and administrative facility for the Theocracy's Scripture divisions. High walls, restricted access, the sound of weapons drills at all hours.

paths: Grand Temple of the Six Gods
Cardinal Council Chamber.description: The governing chamber of the Six Cardinals. A circular room with six seats of equal height — no Cardinal is elevated above another. Deliberations here determine Theocracy policy.

Outer Residential Quarter.description: The city's civilian population — priests, scholars, artisans, and merchants. Religious iconography covers every surface. The population is devout and watchful.

Grand Temple of the Six Gods.description: The religious and political heart of Silksuntecks. Six enormous temples arranged around a central plaza, each dedicated to one of the founding gods. The Cardinals meet here.

paths: Grand Temple of the Six Gods
Pilgrim's Quarter.description: Lodging houses, bathhouses, and roadside shrines serving the faithful who travel to worship at the Six Temples. Pilgrims are processed and watched as closely as any traveler, their donations recorded at every shrine. Hymns carry through the narrow lanes from before dawn.

Inquisition Halls.description: The doctrinal courts where the Scriptures try matters of heresy and impurity, with holding cells cut into the lower floors. Clerks move between chambers carrying sealed testimony, and confessions are taken behind doors that do not open from the inside. The air is cold and smells of candle smoke and old stone.

paths: Grand Temple of the Six Gods
Sacred Archives.description: The Theocracy's repository of scripture, census, and the bloodline registries that track descent from the founders. Robed archivists work by shuttered lamplight to keep the records from the sun, and nothing leaves the shelves without a Cardinal's seal. Silence here is enforced as strictly as any law.

Reliquary Market.description: A colonnaded market where blessed charms, devotional texts, and sanctioned relics are sold to pilgrims under the temple's license. Every stall pays tithe and every sale is logged; unlicensed holy goods are confiscated at once. The crowds are dense, hushed, and quick to report irregularity.

Silksuntecks.basicInfo: The capital of the Slane Theocracy and seat of the Six Cardinals. A walled holy city built around the original temples of the Six Great Gods, whose teachings founded the nation. The most heavily guarded city in the Theocracy — its Scripture divisions train and operate from within its walls.
Silksuntecks.hiddenInfo: The Black Scripture — the Theocracy's most powerful combat unit — is headquartered in an undisclosed compound inside the city. The Cardinals possess intelligence on Nazarick that they are not sharing with any other nation. Their doctrine of human supremacy shapes every policy decision.

Re-Blumrushur.name: Re-Blumrushur

Lower Tunnels.description: The deeper, older sections of the mine. Less trafficked, poorly lit, and increasingly cold as the shafts descend.

Market Square.description: The commercial hub where ore, processed metal, and trade goods change hands. Miners, merchants, and imperial buyers all converge here.

Mine Entrance.description: The primary access shaft into the Azerlisia mountain range. Heavily reinforced, with guard posts and weigh stations for ore output.

Forge District.description: A dense cluster of smelting operations. The heat here is constant. Workers move quickly and speak in shorthand.

Re-Blumrushur.basicInfo: A mining city at the western foot of the Azerlisia Mountains. Its economy runs on ore extraction and smelting. The city's walls are blackened with decades of forge smoke.
Re-Blumrushur.hiddenInfo: The mines run deeper than the city's records account for. Something was found in the lower tunnels years ago. The foremen who were there don't talk about it.

Re-Robel.name: Re-Robel

South Gate.description: The gate facing the southern trade route. High traffic, mixed travelers, and a checkpoint that ranges from thorough to perfunctory depending on the guard rotation.

City Center.description: The administrative and residential core. The lord's residence is here, modest by capital standards but well-maintained.

Wool Market.description: The city's economic engine. Merchants from across the Kingdom come here to trade. Prices are set here, then propagate outward.

Re-Robel.basicInfo: A substantial city southwest of the capital, positioned along a trade route connecting Re-Estize to southern markets. Known for its wool trade and practical architecture.
Re-Robel.hiddenInfo: Several noble families in Re-Robel have been quietly acquiring land and properties outside normal channels. Their interest predates the current political tensions by a decade -- this is not a reaction to recent events but a long-running consolidation strategy that the current environment has made easier to pursue without scrutiny.

E-Raevel.name: E-Raevel

City Market.description: A market shaped by cross-border trade — Baharuth goods sit next to Kingdom produce. The prices here reflect tension when relations are poor.

East Watchtower.description: Overlooking the road toward Baharuth territory. Scouts report in here. The view is good in all directions.

Garrison Fortress.description: The military heart of E-Raevel. Heavily staffed given the city's border position. The commander runs a tight operation.

E-Raevel.basicInfo: A border city east of Re-Estize, historically positioned between the Kingdom and Baharuth Empire. The city's political temperature tracks closely with the state of that relationship.
E-Raevel.hiddenInfo: E-Raevel's garrison commander has received unofficial reports of undead activity increasing along the eastern frontier roads. He has quietly increased patrol frequency on the approach routes without requesting formal orders from the capital -- a decision he has not documented.

E-Asenal.name: E-Asenal

Lord's Hall.description: The administrative seat of the city's lord. More intelligence flows through this building than Re-Estize's capital is fully aware of.

Traveler's Quarter.description: The district that serves northern trade. Cold, practical, and accustomed to unusual travelers. Discretion is valued here.

North Gate Checkpoint.description: The entry point for travelers from the north. Argland envoys pass through here under discreet protocols that have developed over decades.

E-Asenal.basicInfo: A northwestern city near the border with the Argland Council State. Its position makes it a waypoint for travelers moving between the Kingdom and the north, and a listening post for intelligence on the dragon-ruled alliance.
E-Asenal.hiddenInfo: The Argland Council State's dragon lords occasionally send envoys through E-Asenal. The city's lord keeps these meetings out of official records.

E-Pespel.name: E-Pespel

City Gate.description: The gate facing south. Foot traffic and wagon routes are both active -- this city's position on the southern corridor makes it a natural transit point for goods moving north from the coast. Merchants, guards, and a steady flow of travelers pass through on regular schedules.

Main Street.description: The central thoroughfare. Active with merchant traffic moving between the Kingdom interior and the southern trade routes. The street reflects the city's commercial character -- more pragmatic than the capital's noble-dominated atmosphere, more prosperous than frontier settlements to the east.

South Market.description: The city's primary market. Mixed goods from the Kingdom interior and Baharuth border trade. The mix shifts seasonally depending on which side of the frontier is less actively patrolled.

E-Pespel.basicInfo: A southeastern city of moderate size, positioned on the Kingdom's active southern trade corridor. A commercial city dealing with typical frontier concerns: bandit activity on the roads, fluctuating trade volumes, and the need to balance relations between noble interests and merchant practicality.
E-Pespel.hiddenInfo: E-Pespel's merchant class watches the Baharuth border closely. Several trading families have been quietly diversifying their routes south and west in anticipation of increased imperial pressure. The city lord is aware and has not intervened.

Re-Beauleuror.name: Re-Beauleuror

City Center.description: The administrative and merchant center. Less frenetic than Re-Estize's capital, with more space between buildings and longer negotiating seasons.

Noble Quarter.description: Wide streets lined with well-maintained estates. The families here are old money -- cautious, well-connected, and watching the Baharuth Empire's steady border pressure with alarm.

Market District.description: A refined market serving the noble households. Quality goods, controlled access, significantly higher prices than Kingdom norms.

Re-Beauleuror.basicInfo: A northwestern city of the Kingdom, known for its noble estates and mild climate. The wealthier noble families maintain secondary residences here away from the capital's politics.
Re-Beauleuror.hiddenInfo: A faction of noble families in Re-Beauleuror has been communicating with Baharuth Empire intermediaries about what a post-Kingdom political arrangement might look like.

Re-Uroval.name: Re-Uroval

North Road.description: The road heading toward the Argland border. It is not heavily patrolled past the city limits. Travelers beyond that point are on their own.

City Square.description: The central gathering point. The population is small, self-reliant, and not given to volunteering information to outsiders.

Northern Waystation.description: The city's function as a rest point for northern travelers. Basic but reliable accommodations, a stable, and a tavern that serves food suited to cold-weather palates.

Re-Uroval.basicInfo: A northern city of the Kingdom, positioned close to the Argland Council State border. Colder and more isolated than most Kingdom cities, sustained by northern mining and the hardy population that northern conditions produce.
Re-Uroval.hiddenInfo: Re-Uroval has seen an uptick in unusual travelers from the north in recent months. The guards have standing orders not to document certain arrivals.

Imperial Castrum.name: Imperial Castrum

Outer Walls.description: The fortification perimeter. Parapets with clear sightlines in all directions, war golems at key points, and a gate designed to delay rather than simply stop an attacking force.

Supply Depot.description: The logistics base for the eastern legions. Food, weapons, armor, and siege equipment are staged here for rapid deployment.

Command Compound.description: The operational center of the Castrum. War maps, troop assignments, and the commander's offices. Access is restricted to officers.

Barracks District.description: The living and training quarters for the Castrum's permanent garrison. Discipline is high. The soldiers are professional and combat-tested.

Imperial Castrum.basicInfo: A major imperial military fortress at the Empire's eastern border, serving as the staging ground for imperial military operations and the base of the Empire's forward legions. Heavily fortified and permanently garrisoned.
Imperial Castrum.hiddenInfo: The Imperial Castrum's garrison commander has been receiving sealed orders directly from Emperor Jircniv, bypassing the normal chain of command. The contents are not shared with the standard officer chain.

Feo Berkana.name: Feo Berkana

Trade Hall.description: The city's commercial center. Dwarf-crafted goods, raw ore, and specialty materials trade hands here. Surface merchants make a comfortable living without ever going deeper.

Surface Gate.description: The main entry point connecting the underground city to surface roads. Customs inspection, trade weighing, and the city's first line of contact with outsiders.

Residential Tunnels.description: The living quarters carved into the mountain. Stone architecture, efficient use of space, and communal heating channels running through the walls.

Feo Berkana.basicInfo: One of the six dwarf cities, positioned closer to the surface than the deeper dwarven settlements. A trading city that serves as the primary interface between the Dwarf Kingdom and surface nations.
Feo Berkana.hiddenInfo: Feo Berkana's surface proximity has made it the entry point for occasional contact with surface human traders. The city's trade council is deeply divided on whether to reopen formal trade routes with human nations after a century of near-isolation.

Feo Teiwaz.name: Feo Teiwaz

Market Hall.description: Where finished goods are assessed, priced, and arranged for transport. Buyers from across the New World make the journey here for premium equipment.

Smith's Quarter.description: The residential and workshop district for the city's craftsmen. Apprentices run errands between masters' workshops at all hours.

Grand Forge District.description: The production heart of Feo Teiwaz. Multiple master-level forges operating at full capacity. The heat and noise are constant.

Feo Teiwaz.basicInfo: One of the six dwarf cities, known for its master smiths and the quality of its metalwork. The city's forges produce equipment that commands premium prices at the surface.
Feo Teiwaz.hiddenInfo: Feo Teiwaz holds techniques for crafting Orichalcum-grade equipment that predate the Dwarf Kingdom's recorded history. The Grand Master Smiths guard these methods jealously.

Feo Raidho.name: Feo Raidho

Deep Passage.description: The entrance to the cavern networks beyond dwarven territory. Expeditions into here require authorization. Not all of them return.

Frontier Gate.description: The city's outer perimeter, facing the unmapped cavern networks. The gate is reinforced beyond standard dwarven specifications. The guards are not talkative about what that was in response to.

Main Settlement.description: The core residential and operational district. Compact, well-defended, and populated by dwarves who prefer the frontier's quiet to the busier inner cities.

Feo Raidho.basicInfo: The southernmost of the six dwarf cities, positioned near the underground passages that connect dwarven territory to the wider cavern networks. A frontier settlement by dwarven standards.
Feo Raidho.hiddenInfo: Feo Raidho borders cavern networks that descend into territory no dwarf expedition has fully mapped. Something occasionally comes up from those depths. It is not friendly.

Hoburns.name: Hoburns

North Wall.description: The fortified northern perimeter, facing the direction of demihuman incursion pressure. The wall is maintained to active combat standards -- the northern frontier sees regular raids from beastman and demihuman groups, and the wall is the primary fixed defense against them. Guard rotations are heavier on the north face than any other section.

South Gate.description: The gate connecting Hoburns to the Southern Holy Kingdom and Roble's trade routes. Civilian and commercial traffic passes through here on standard schedules. The gate guard checks travelers against the Paladin Order's security criteria -- heteromorphic races receive additional scrutiny consistent with Holy Kingdom doctrine.

City Square.description: The public center of Hoburns. Street preachers, tradesmen, and off-duty soldiers share this space. Public announcements from the palace are read here. The square functions as the social and commercial center for the non-noble population of the capital, and reflects the mixture of religious devotion and practical commerce that characterizes Holy Kingdom culture.

Royal Cathedral.description: The spiritual and administrative heart of Hoburns. The queen's throne is here. The cathedral serves both as a house of worship and as the formal chamber for state functions. Its architecture is the most elaborate in the Holy Kingdom -- generations of construction reflect the institution's accumulated resources and theological priorities.

Paladin Barracks.description: The operational base of the Holy Kingdom's paladin order. The barracks house active paladins, training facilities, armories, and the command offices where deployments are planned. The order is professional and well-equipped by human standards. Combat doctrine emphasizes coordinated small-unit action and holy magic support.

Hoburns.basicInfo: The holy capital of the Roble Holy Kingdom, seat of the queen and the Paladin Order. A walled city of religious architecture, built around a central cathedral and designed to serve as both spiritual center and military command point. The queen administers both civil and religious authority from here. The paladin order maintains a permanent garrison and conducts training and deployments from the barracks district.
Hoburns.hiddenInfo: The paladin order's command structure has a generational divide: the senior commanders are experienced veterans who prioritize institutional stability; the younger officers are more aggressive about projecting force into demihuman-held territory to the north. The queen is aware of this tension and currently manages it by keeping the aggressive faction engaged in active patrol deployments.

Kalinsha.name: Kalinsha

Inner Keep.description: The administrative and command center of the fortress city. Royal administrators, garrison officers, and a small noble household.

Guard Barracks.description: The garrison's living and training quarters. Soldiers posted to Kalinsha understand they are on the active frontier, not a ceremonial posting. The training regimen reflects this: combat drills are realistic, and the experienced soldiers here have typically seen actual engagement with demihuman raiding parties.

Outer Fortress Wall.description: The first line of defense. Thick enough to absorb sustained assault. The wall has been built and maintained to active wartime specifications -- the northern frontier has produced enough genuine emergencies to justify the investment. Guard posts are continuous and well-supplied.

Market Square.description: The walled commercial square where the fortress city does its trade, kept running even under frontier strain. Stalls press close together and goods carried up from the south command frontier prices. Soldiers off duty move through it as often as merchants.

Soldiers' Chapel.description: A plain hall of worship raised for the garrison, where the faithful of the Holy Kingdom pray before rotations to the wall. The benches are worn smooth and the altar is simple. Services are brief and often attended in armor.

Refugee Quarter.description: Crowded lodging and tent-rows for those fallen back from the northern farms and villages. Families share floor space in requisitioned halls, and the quarter swells whenever the frontier worsens. The air is close with woodsmoke and too many people in too little room.

Kalinsha.basicInfo: A fortress city north of Hoburns, directly administered by the royal family and protected by walls built to exceptional thickness. The city sits on the primary road connecting Hoburns to the northern frontier, making it both a military staging point and the last major settlement before demihuman territory begins.
Kalinsha.hiddenInfo: The garrison at Kalinsha has been quietly augmented with veterans who specifically requested posting here. Their motivation is vengeance, not duty, and their commander knows it.

Rimun.name: Rimun

Coastal Road.description: The road running east toward Hoburns and west along the coast. The scenic route for travelers who are not in a hurry.

Harbor District.description: The working port. Ships loading and unloading at all hours. The dockworkers know every vessel that passes through.

Merchant Quarter.description: The commercial center of Rimun. Goods arriving by sea are processed, taxed, and distributed here. A mixed population of sailors, traders, and permanent residents.

Adventurer's Guild Hall.description: The local branch of the Adventurer's Guild. A functional hall with a quest board, a clerk's counter for registration and contract processing, and tables where adventurers wait, eat, and take stock of available work. Registration costs 5 silver coins; all new registrants start at Copper rank. Rules, fees, and rank structure are identical to every other guild branch.

Fishmarket Wharf.description: The fishing docks where the day's catch is landed, gutted, and sold before the tide turns. Gulls wheel over the cleaning tables and the planks stay slick year round. The smell reaches well past the waterfront.

Warehouse Row.description: The line of dockside storehouses where seaborne cargo is held between ship and market. Tallymen check crates against manifests and the big doors stand open through the working day. Everything inside is stacked, labelled, and watched.

Rimun.basicInfo: A port city west of Hoburns, positioned on the coast and serving as the Holy Kingdom's primary maritime trade hub. Sea access gives Rimun commercial connections that inland cities cannot replicate. Goods moving between the Holy Kingdom and coastal trading partners flow through the harbor. The city maintains a small naval patrol capacity for coastal security.
Rimun.hiddenInfo: Rimun's harbor sees occasional foreign vessels whose purpose is not purely commercial. The harbor master logs their arrivals but does not investigate.

Prart.name: Prart

Town Center.description: The modest commercial and administrative center. Travelers stopping between Kalinsha and Hoburns pass through here.

Supply Depot.description: The logistical center of Prart. Grain stores, weapon caches, and medical supplies maintained for the northern garrisons.

Prart.basicInfo: A city positioned between Kalinsha and Hoburns, serving as a waypoint and supply depot for the northern road. Small but strategically located for military logistics.
Prart.hiddenInfo: Prart's strategic value comes entirely from its position on the northern road -- it is a waypoint, not a destination. The local lord is aware of this and has cultivated Prart's logistical role deliberately, investing in warehouse capacity and road maintenance that benefit anyone moving supplies along the northern axis. This makes him useful to both military and merchant interests.

Debone.name: Debone

South Road.description: The road heading south out of the Kingdom. A route for traders and travelers moving between the Holy Kingdom interior and the southern coast. Migrants moving away from the northern frontier use this road regularly.

City Center.description: The original city administration and market. Strained by the population increase but functional.

Refugee Quarter.description: The district that has grown to house northern migrants displaced by demihuman raids on frontier settlements. Temporary structures that have become permanent. The residents are organized, vocal about conditions in the north, and not optimistic about returning.

Debone.basicInfo: A southern city of the Roble Holy Kingdom, positioned in more stable territory far from the active demihuman pressure on the northern border. Its distance from the frontier makes it a destination for Holy Kingdom citizens seeking safety, and its population has grown as a result of internal migration from northern settlements affected by recurring demihuman raids.
Debone.hiddenInfo: Debone's growing population includes a proportion of permanent migrants from the north who chose not to return to frontier settlements after demihuman raids displaced them. Their accounts of conditions in the border territories circulate widely in the city and inform the local population's attitude toward the Paladin Order's capacity to protect the frontier.

Loyts.name: Loyts

Market Center.description: A small but functional market. Fish, salt, and practical goods. Not a place for luxury trade.

Fishing Harbor.description: The economic base of Loyts. Small fishing vessels, salt processing facilities, and the smell that defines the city.

Loyts.basicInfo: A southern Holy Kingdom city near the Roble coast, known for fishing and salt production. Far from the northern invasion's reach, it maintained normal operations throughout the crisis.
Loyts.hiddenInfo: Loyts provides salt and preserved fish to supply depots serving the Holy Kingdom's northern garrisons. The lord tracks these contributions carefully and expects political credit for them.

Forest of Evasha.name: Forest of Evasha

Deep Forest.description: The interior of the Evasha forest, where trees are old enough to block out the sky. Elven hunters know this territory completely. Outsiders do not survive here long without a guide.

Theocracy War Road.description: The military road the Slane Theocracy has cut through the western forest. Patrolled by Scripture soldiers. The construction represents decades of effort.

Elven Resistance Camp.description: A concealed camp used by elves resisting the Theocracy advance. Mobile — it relocates regularly. Finding it requires elven cooperation.

Forward Scripture Camp.description: The Theocracy's frontline camp at the road's current terminus. Reinforced, well-supplied, and staffed by soldiers who are not there voluntarily.

Forest of Evasha.basicInfo: The vast forest that constitutes most of the Elf Country's territory. Ancient growth, poor visibility, and an elven population that knows every path. The Slane Theocracy has carved a military road through the western edge.
Forest of Evasha.hiddenInfo: Theocracy forces have established forward camps inside the forest's western boundary. Elven resistance groups operate from the deep forest. Neither side has a decisive advantage.

Argland Council Citadel.name: Argland Council Citadel

Human Embassy.description: The section of the citadel designated for human delegates and visitors. Correctly proportioned, well-maintained, and thoroughly monitored.

Council Chamber.description: The primary meeting hall, built at the scale of the dragon lords who govern here. Human delegates stand on a raised platform to be visible during sessions.

Dragon Quarters.description: The residential area for the council's dragon members. The architecture is functional from a dragon's perspective and cavernous from a human's.

Outer Battlements.description: The citadel's outer walls and gatehouse, raised and thickened against the northern cold and whatever comes with it. Firing steps are built at a scale that suits a dragon as readily as a company of soldiers. Wind off the heights never fully stops.

Hall of Records.description: The chamber where the council's treaties, charters, and correspondence are kept, shelved high and reached by ladder and wing alike. Clerks catalogue centuries of agreements between the dragon lords and the nations below. It is quiet, cold, and meticulously ordered.

Lower Township.description: The human and demihuman settlement clustered below the citadel proper, housing the servants, traders, and laborers who keep it running. Buildings are built to ordinary proportions and huddle close for warmth. Smoke from its chimneys is the only soft thing on the mountainside.

Argland Council Citadel.basicInfo: The seat of government for the Argland Council State, a fortress-city in the far north where the dragon council lords convene. Its architecture was built to accommodate beings considerably larger than humans.
Argland Council Citadel.hiddenInfo:
At least one council dragon is aware that an entity arrived in the New World that did not originate here. This knowledge has not been shared at the council table.

At least one dragon council member is aware that something significant arrived in the New World from outside. They have not shared this assessment with other nations.

Beastman Territory.name: Beastman Territory

Hunting Grounds.description: The territory where Beastman hunting parties operate. Overlap with the Dragon Kingdom borderlands is constant and intentional.

Tribal Gathering.description: The site where multiple Beastman tribes convene for coordination. Not a permanent settlement — it relocates seasonally.

War-Chief's Camp.description: The central command of the current Beastman campaign. Organized for a military culture. Visitors are either prisoners, tribute, or considered hostile.

Beastman Territory.basicInfo: The domain of the Beastman tribes in the eastern frontier. Organized around war-chief hierarchies, driven by resource pressure and cultural aggression. They raid the Dragon Kingdom regularly and have done so for generations.
Beastman Territory.hiddenInfo: The Beastman raids on the Dragon Kingdom have escalated beyond historical norms. Something has changed within the Beastman hierarchy — a new war-chief, or external pressure from further east.

Crescent Lake.name: Crescent Lake

Forest Approach.description: The road through the forest leading to the capital. Difficult for non-elves to navigate. Theocracy forces have been working toward this road for two generations.

Elven Royal Castle.description: A castle grown into the largest tree in the forest, its chambers carved into living wood. The royal throne rises at its apex above the canopy. The treasury is two floors above the audience hall.

Lakeshore District.description: The residential and administrative ring surrounding the crescent lake. Elven architecture integrating living trees with carved stone. The air quality here is exceptional.

Crescent Lake.basicInfo: The capital of the Elf Country, built around a crescent-shaped lake in the heart of the great forest. The Elven Royal Castle — a structure built into an enormous ancient tree — rises at the lake's center point. The Slane Theocracy has been advancing a war road toward this city for years.
Crescent Lake.hiddenInfo: The Elven Royal Castle's treasury contains pre-Six-Gods-era artifacts that neither the Theocracy nor any other nation is aware of. Decem Hougan's personal decisions have done more to advance the Theocracy's war road than their military capability alone.

Dragon Kingdom Royal City.name: Dragon Kingdom Royal City

City Market.description: The main commercial district of the Royal City. Trade has contracted under the Beastman siege pressure -- goods from the east are scarce, and prices reflect it.

Royal Palace.description: The palace of the Dragon Kingdom's ruling line. Large-framed halls built to accommodate draconic guests mix with smaller human-scale administrative chambers. Queen Draudillon holds court here.

Dragon Rider Garrison.description: The operational base for the Dragon Kingdom's military dragon rider units. Dragons are stabled in open-roofed stone pens; riders drill in the adjacent yard.

Lower Wards.description: The crowded common districts where most of the city's people live, worn thin by years of siege economy. Rationing lines form early and repairs go unfinished for want of materials. The mood is tired but stubborn.

Beastman Watch.description: The eastern defensive works facing the Beastman Country, a belt of ramparts, palisades, and signal towers kept permanently manned. Supplies and reinforcements run thin along its length. Watchfires burn through the night toward the frontier.

Scalecrafters' Row.description: A lane of workshops where artisans work dragonbone, shed scale, and hide into tools, armor, and ornament under the kingdom's old dragon-allied traditions. The craft is proud and increasingly starved of raw material. The ring of small hammers runs the length of the street.

Dragon Kingdom Royal City.basicInfo: The capital and seat of power of the Dragon Kingdom, ruled by Queen Draudillon Oriculus. A city built under the authority of the Brightness Dragon Lord's lineage -- its architecture reflects centuries of dragon-allied construction, with chambers scaled for draconic visitors alongside human-proportioned districts. The city is under sustained military pressure from the Beastman Country to the east, and its outer defenses are stretched. Dragon Rider units operate from a dedicated garrison within the city walls.
Dragon Kingdom Royal City.hiddenInfo: Draudillon is aware that without external military assistance the kingdom will eventually be ground down by Beastman pressure. She is actively seeking powerful allies while managing the court's expectation that her Wild Magic will save them. The soul cost of her most powerful spells makes that an option she cannot realistically use.

Eryuentiu (City Under the Floating Castl.name: Eryuentiu (City Under the Floating Castle)

Archive Wing.description: Sealed chambers containing records, maps, and strategic documents from the Eight Greed Kings' era. Some are legible; most require expertise in old script forms to interpret.

Armory Depths.description: The lower sealed vaults where the Eight Greed Kings stored Yggdrasil-tier weapons and artifacts. Most seals are intact. The items within would be significant to any Yggdrasil player. The Platinum Dragon Lord treats this area as the primary reason for his guardianship.

Central Plaza.description: The open core of Eryuentiu -- once a grand gathering space, now empty and windswept. The scale is inhuman, built for beings who expected to rule continents.

Outer Ramparts.description: The perimeter wall of the floating city. Crumbling in places but still structurally sound where the Eight Greed Kings' original construction holds. Wind at altitude is constant.

Collapsed Residential Blocks.description: The ruined dwelling districts where the city's long-dead population once lived, now roofless shells and drifted sand. Streets end in rubble and the inhuman scale makes the emptiness stranger. Nothing moves here but the wind.

Sealed Undervaults.description: Buried chambers from the Eight Greed Kings' era, their entrances warded shut and half-swallowed by the foundations above. What lies behind the seals has not been catalogued. The stonework is older and heavier than anything on the surface.

Eryuentiu (City Under the Floating Castl.basicInfo: The legacy ground-level city built by the Eight Greed Kings in the Dolor Desert, with their floating guild-base citadel stationed perpetually above it. Built during the era when Yggdrasil players first arrived and sought to dominate the New World, Eryuentiu is a ruin in political terms -- its creators are long dead -- but its contents are not. Yggdrasil-era weapons, artifacts, and strategic materials from the Eight Greed Kings' campaign remain sealed inside, and the city is actively guarded by a Dragon Lord against any player or faction attempting to access those resources. The city floats unreachable by conventional means -- flight, teleportation clearance, or Dragon Lord escort are the only viable access routes.
Eryuentiu (City Under the Floating Castl.hiddenInfo:
The Platinum Dragon Lord is not always physically present inside the city -- he patrols the surrounding airspace and can reach any point in or above the structure within minutes. The interior of Eryuentiu contains items that would shift the New World's power balance if accessed by anyone aligned with Nazarick. Tsaindorcus knows this. Any player character who attempts entry without his sanction will find him waiting.

Ancient ruins beneath the Dolor Desert predate the Six Great Gods' arrival in the New World. The items found in them do not match any known magical tradition.

Argland Mountain Passes.name: Argland Mountain Passes

Pass Narrows.description: The tightest section of the main pass. The walls close to within fifteen metres on both sides. The rock face has been cut at regular intervals. Nothing lives here permanently. The air carries the specific cold of altitude and enclosed stone.

Argland Mountain Passes.basicInfo: High-altitude corridors through the mountain range that forms the spine of the Argland Council State. The passes are the only practical surface routes between the interior plateau and the surrounding lowlands. Natural chokepoints. The rock formations here are old and show signs of deliberate reshaping at points where the terrain favoured a defender.
Argland Mountain Passes.hiddenInfo: The passes through the Argland range are not surveilled by human scouts — the Council of Dragon Lords maintains its own awareness of movement through the range through means that do not require visible infrastructure. Travelers who use the passes believing themselves unobserved are mistaken. The passes contain natural formations that amplify sound and light in ways discoverable by attentive travelers, suggesting deliberate shaping. Several passes lead to destinations that are not on any human-accessible map. The Argland Council State has never formally closed the passes to travelers, but travelers who attempt routes without Council awareness sometimes fail to complete them.

Argland Interior Settlement.name: Argland Interior Settlement

Supply Depot.description: Ground-floor storage and trading space. Shelves are stocked with preserved provisions, rope, torches, and basic equipment. A keeper manages inventory from a worn wooden desk. The goods available reflect what travellers in difficult terrain actually need.

Argland Interior Settlement.basicInfo: A fortified settlement on the interior plateau of the Argland Council State. Built for permanence rather than growth: thick walls, deep storage, minimal external decoration. The population is small relative to the infrastructure, which was designed for a larger occupancy. The settlement functions as a supply depot and meeting point for parties operating in the state's territory.
Argland Interior Settlement.hiddenInfo: The settlement's population includes non-human individuals whose presence is not explained by any publicly available account of the region's demographics. The administrative structure of the settlement reflects Council of Dragon Lords governance rather than any human political system, which means its laws and dispute resolution mechanisms operate on principles unfamiliar to travelers from human nations. Trade goods available in the settlement's market include items whose origin cannot be traced to any catalogued production region, suggesting trade routes that are not publicly known. The settlement's security arrangements are not visible in the conventional sense — there are no guards at the gate — but the settlement has not experienced a recorded crime in the period for which records are available.

Elf Country Royal Seat.name: Elf Country Royal Seat

Audience Hall.description: A large open chamber formed between several ancient trunks, roofed by interlocking branches. Natural light reaches the floor through gaps that have been shaped over generations. The space is designed for formal address. Acoustics are precise.

Outer Approach.description: The final stretch of path before the seat proper. The trees here are larger than elsewhere. Elf sentinels observe from positions that are not immediately visible. The path is maintained and clearly intentional.

Inner Council Chamber.description: A smaller, fully enclosed room within the trunk of the largest tree. The walls are living wood. Carvings record decisions dating back centuries. Access is restricted to invited parties. The door has no visible mechanism.

Canopy Dwellings.description: Living quarters woven into the upper branches, reached by rope walks and shaped limbs rather than stairs. The structures bend with the wind and are all but invisible from the forest floor. Voices and birdsong carry between the platforms.

Root Hollows.description: Ground-level chambers hollowed among the great roots, used for storage, workshops, and shelter. The air is cool and earthy and the light filters down green and dim. Everything is shaped from the living wood rather than cut and fitted.

Warden's Platforms.description: Concealed guard posts set along the approach paths, placed so a sentinel can watch without being seen. Each platform covers the next in overlapping lines of sight. Nothing reaches the inner chambers unobserved.

Elf Country Royal Seat.basicInfo: The central seat of governance for the Elf Country, built into the canopy and root network of the oldest trees in the forest interior. The architecture uses living wood rather than cut timber. Access is through a network of guarded paths that are not marked on any external map. The outer approaches are open; the inner chambers are not.
Elf Country Royal Seat.hiddenInfo:
The inner chamber contains records of agreements with entities from outside the region that predate the current political order by several centuries. The terms remain active.

Decem Hougan is not a sympathetic ruler. He is self-serving and has made decisions that have cost his people dearly. The Theocracy's advance through the forest has accelerated under his leadership. His personal treasury contains artifacts that predate current nations.

Theocracy Capital District.name: Theocracy Capital District

Public Plaza.description: The lowest tier, open to general traffic. Markets and administrative offices line the perimeter. The plaza is clean and orderly. Uniformed inspectors circulate at regular intervals. The mood is functional and controlled rather than welcoming.

Temple Precinct Approach.description: The gate to the upper tier and the central temple complex. The checkpoint here is staffed at all hours. The gate itself is reinforced stone with visible warding on the threshold. Beyond it, access is restricted to authorised personnel and invited parties.

Administrative Quarter.description: The middle tier. Buildings here house government functions: registration, licensing, and the external-facing offices of the theocratic administration. Entry requires documentation. The architecture is monumental and deliberately imposing.

Grand Cathedral.description: The central house of worship at the summit of the upper tier, raised to the Six Great Gods beneath a vaulted ceiling tall enough to swallow sound. Services run on a fixed liturgical schedule and attendance by rank is recorded. Incense and filtered light give the nave a deliberate, overwhelming stillness.

Scripture Garrison.description: The billet and muster ground of the Scripture divisions assigned to the capital, closed to civilian traffic behind its own inner wall. Drill yards, armories, and briefing halls keep a standing readiness that never fully stands down. The clatter of formation and the bark of orders carry over the wall at all hours.

Sacred Treasury.description: The warded vaults beneath the temple complex, holding consecrated artifacts and the Theocracy's reserves. Access passes through successive sealed doors, each logged by a different office so no one hand holds the whole key. The corridors are narrow, cold, and lit only where a guard stands.

Pilgrim Gate.description: The controlled lower entrance through which outsiders and pilgrims are admitted into the district, funneled single-file past inspection booths. Documentation is checked, belongings are searched, and those without sanction are turned back at the line. The queue moves slowly under the eyes of inspectors who do not hurry.

Theocracy Capital District.basicInfo: The administrative and religious centre of the Slane Theocracy. The district is built around a sequence of tiered plazas rising toward the central temple complex. Uniformed personnel outnumber civilians in most areas. Access to the upper tiers requires documentation that is not readily issued to outsiders.
Theocracy Capital District.hiddenInfo:
