The upper temple complex contains a sealed archive of documented interactions with non-human species going back to the Theocracy's founding. The records are classified. The classification exists because the content contradicts the official historical account.

The Theocracy possesses several World Items inherited from past heroes. Their Scriptures -- Black Scripture, Sunlight Scripture, and others -- are covert special forces. The Black Scripture's captain is one of the strongest humans alive. The Theocracy maintains active intelligence operations monitoring unusual magical activity and non-human power concentrations along their borders and beyond. They are aware of something anomalous in the Tob Forest region but have not yet identified what it is.

Karsanas City.name: Karsanas City

City Gate.description: The main entry point to Karsanas City. Alliance guards check merchant manifests and collect the standard transit tax. The gate sees heavy traffic during the spring and autumn trading seasons when caravans from both north and south converge on the Alliance's road network.

Merchant Quarter.description: The commercial center of Karsanas City. Goods from across the northeastern frontier pass through here. The quarter operates on long trading hours and a culture of transactional directness -- merchants here negotiate efficiently because they have done it many times before.

Adventurer's Guild Hall.description: The local branch of the Adventurer's Guild. A functional hall with a quest board, a clerk's counter for registration and contract processing, and tables where adventurers wait, eat, and take stock of available work. Registration costs 5 silver coins; all new registrants start at Copper rank. Rules, fees, and rank structure are identical to every other guild branch.

Alliance Council Chamber.description: The formal meeting hall where city representatives gather to vote on Alliance policy. Circular layout with no head seat -- an architectural expression of the Alliance's founding principle of equal representation. In practice, the representatives of the largest cities speak first and longest.

Caravanserai.description: The walled yards where caravans halt, stabling animals and lodging drivers between legs of the frontier routes. It fills to capacity in the trading seasons and empties to a skeleton staff between them. Dust, pack animals, and a dozen languages crowd the open ground.

Craftsmen's Row.description: The workshop street where the city's smiths, tanners, and joiners supply the goods its markets sell on. Apprentices run materials between shopfronts and the work spills onto the pavement. The noise of a dozen trades runs together into one.

Karsanas City.basicInfo: The largest and most commercially significant of the Alliance's member cities, serving as the de facto seat of the council and the primary trade hub for the northeastern frontier. Wide boulevards built for merchant traffic, a large covered market district, and a fortified council quarter where Alliance governance operates. The city maintains a mixed population of merchants, craftsmen, and the administrative class that keeps the council functioning.
Karsanas City.hiddenInfo: The council's rotating chairmanship means no single city dominates Alliance policy for long. Karsanas City benefits from this instability: as the largest member, it shapes outcomes through economic leverage rather than political position. Its merchant class funds council infrastructure -- and the council knows it.

Alliance Trade Road.name: Alliance Trade Road

Road Junction.description: The point where the Alliance's main road intersects with the southern frontier track. A small militia post here checks commercial traffic. The junction is also a meeting point for merchant caravans forming up for the road's more exposed northern stretches.

Waystation Inn.description: A fortified roadside inn at the road's midpoint. Accommodation, stabling, and basic supplies. The innkeeper maintains a log of travelers that he shares with Alliance militia posts. He does not share it with anyone else.

Alliance Trade Road.basicInfo: The primary maintained road connecting the Alliance's member cities, running through the northeastern frontier territory. Waystation inns, militia posts, and toll gates appear at regular intervals. The road is the Alliance's most tangible collective infrastructure investment -- all member cities contributed to its construction and share responsibility for its maintenance.
Alliance Trade Road.hiddenInfo: Several stretch of the road pass through territory that is technically outside Alliance jurisdiction. The surrounding land is claimed by three different parties, none of whom have pressed the claim aggressively because the road benefits all of them. This informal arrangement has held for decades and no one wants to test what resolving it would cost.

Highland Hunting Territory.name: Highland Hunting Territory

Highland Pass.description: A natural corridor through the highland terrain, used by both game animals and the rare outside trader. The pass is technically open to travelers but passing through minotaur hunting range without acknowledgment of the territory is considered an insult that the hunters present may or may not choose to address.

Hunting Grounds.description: The primary game range. Large prey animals move through on seasonal routes the minotaur hunters have mapped over generations. The terrain is open enough to track but broken enough to stalk -- ideal for the hunting style the culture prizes.

Highland Hunting Territory.basicInfo: The hunting range claimed by the minotaur clans, stretching across the eastern highland plateau. Large game -- highland elk, dire boar, and predatory creatures drawn to the game density -- make this territory productive and dangerous. Minotaur hunters work alone or in small pairs; pack hunting is considered a lesser form of the practice. The territorial boundaries are maintained through regular patrol and marked with stone cairns.
Highland Hunting Territory.hiddenInfo: The hunting territory's eastern boundary encroaches on routes used by traders moving between the Argland Council State and Beastman territories. The encroachment is gradual and has been ongoing for two generations. The traders reroute when they notice the cairns have moved. The minotaurs note that the traders continue to reroute.

Coastal Fishing Settlement.name: Coastal Fishing Settlement

Harbor Inlet.description: The protected cove where fishing boats and coastal traders anchor. Docks are small but functional. The inlet's natural protection from the prevailing wind makes it usable in weather that would ground activity at the open coast.

Settlement Center.description: The core of the settlement -- a handful of permanent structures including the drying racks, the storage warehouse, and the fishermen's gathering hall. Everything here is built to withstand the coastal weather, which is the primary design constraint.

Coastal Fishing Settlement.basicInfo: A small fishing community on the northern coast of the Roble Holy Kingdom, built on a protected inlet that reduces exposure to the open sea's frequent storms. The settlement's economy is entirely maritime -- fishing, small-scale coastal trading, and providing resupply to ships moving along the coast. The Holy Kingdom's presence is light here: a small militia detachment and a tithe collector who visits seasonally.
Coastal Fishing Settlement.hiddenInfo: The settlement's real economic value is its position as an informal stop on a coastal trading route that skips the Holy Kingdom's main tariff checkpoints. The merchants who use it pay the settlement in goods rather than currency, which the tithe collector cannot easily assess. The settlement leadership does not advertise this arrangement.

Re-Estize Kingdom.name: Re-Estize Kingdom
Re-Estize Kingdom.basicInfo:
The Re-Estize Kingdom is the largest human nation in the central continent, occupying fertile lowlands and river valleys. Its population and productive capacity exceed any neighboring state, but internal politics convert those advantages into effective military power only at the margins.

King Ramposa III holds the throne with genuine political judgment but insufficient leverage to purge entrenched noble corruption. The kingdom divides between a Royal Faction supporting crown reforms and a noble bloc of the Six Great Noble houses that collectively controls enough land, levies, and tax revenue to obstruct any centralization effort. Marquis Elias Brandt Dale Raeven is publicly regarded as a political opportunist; in reality he is the covert coordinator of the royalist faction, running intelligence operations on behalf of the crown while maintaining public deniability.

The military consists primarily of noble levies whose equipment, training, and loyalty vary by house. The Royal Guard under Warrior Captain Gazef Stronoff is a small elite crown force — widely regarded as the finest human warriors in the kingdom but badly outnumbered in any confrontation with the unified noble levies. E-Rantel, the Fortress City at the intersection of three national borders, is governed by a crown-appointed mayor and serves as the kingdom's primary military frontier.
Re-Estize Kingdom.hiddenInfo: The Re-Estize Kingdom's dysfunction runs deeper than its external conflicts. King Ramposa III's authority has been progressively eroded by noble families who exploit the annual Baharuth standoff as justification for maintaining independent military forces. The Six Great Nobles function as parallel governments in their domains; Marquis Raeven privately calculates Kingdom collapse scenarios and has already identified how his own house could survive an Empire absorption. Princess Renner's exceptional strategic intelligence is publicly invisible — the court reads her as a beautiful eccentric rather than the sharpest political mind in the capital. The Kingdom's real ceiling is Gazef Stronoff, whose personal loyalty to the crown runs deeper than his political realism about the Kingdom's trajectory. The treasury is under chronic strain from the cost of maintaining border fortifications while noble contributions remain at politically negotiated minimums.

Baharuth Empire.name: Baharuth Empire
Baharuth Empire.basicInfo:
The Baharuth Empire is a centralized absolute monarchy occupying hill country and plains east of the Katze Plains. Smaller in territory and population than Re-Estize, it is consistently superior in military effectiveness, administrative coherence, and strategic capability.

Emperor Jircniv Rune Farlord El-Nix — the 'Bloody Emperor' — consolidated power through systematic elimination of rival family members, hostile noble factions, and political opposition. He holds genuine uncontested authority and is widely regarded as one of the most capable political minds among current human rulers. The imperial court's chief magic caster is Fluder Paradyne, the most powerful human mage alive — operating at Tier 6, unmatched by any other living practitioner. The Four Imperial Knights are the most powerful individual warriors in imperial service, functioning as the Emperor's military representatives.

Jircniv replaced the conscript-levy model with a professional career military organized into Eight Knight Orders. Imperial soldiers are trained to consistent standards at state expense, producing an army smaller than Re-Estize's levies but dramatically superior in discipline and effectiveness. The Empire has consistently outperformed the Kingdom in field engagements at the Katze Plains for generations.

The Empire practices limited meritocracy — commoners may advance through demonstrated ability rather than hereditary appointment. The Imperial Bank issues metallic plate trusts for large-scale merchant transactions, giving the Empire the most sophisticated commercial infrastructure among human nations. Slave reform has granted legal status protections to human slaves, absent from most neighboring states.
Baharuth Empire.hiddenInfo: Emperor Jircniv Rune Farlord El-Nix consolidated power at a young age by systematically eliminating the noble faction that had constrained the previous dynasty — a campaign precise enough that most of the nobility never realized it was a campaign. His intelligence network inside Re-Estize tracks Gazef Stronoff as the singular military variable that could disrupt his eastern border timetable. Fluder Paradyne serves as court wizard while Jircniv fully understands that Fluder's obsession with sixth-tier magic creates a latent loyalty problem — he keeps Fluder close because a motivated magic caster is more dangerous unsupervised. The Four Imperial Knights (Leinas Rockbruise, Baziwood Peshmel, Nimble Arc Dale Anoch, Nazami Enec) represent the Empire's true military ceiling; Jircniv uses them as a demonstration of what the Empire can actually deploy when negotiations fail. His current objective is not conquest but controlled absorption — a distinction that matters to the timeline if not to the eventual outcome.

Slane Theocracy.name: Slane Theocracy
Slane Theocracy.basicInfo: The Slane Theocracy is a theocratic nation-state in the western continent governed by a council of six Cardinals who administer the doctrine of the Six Gods — founding heroes whose power established the nation's religious and political legitimacy. It is one of the three most militarily capable human nations, maintaining significant conventional forces alongside six covert special-operations units known as the Six Scriptures, each serving a distinct operational mandate. The Theocracy's public doctrine emphasizes human survival and prosperity; its actual institutional program is human racial supremacy, including active efforts to identify and eliminate non-human threats and heteromorphic individuals. It possesses World Items recovered from or left by the founding heroes — among the most powerful artifacts known to exist in the New World, with the Black Scripture holding the most dangerous examples. Across all human territories the Theocracy operates intelligence networks and responds to confirmed emergence of non-human power with surveillance, containment assessment, or elimination in that order, without exception.
Slane Theocracy.hiddenInfo: The Slane Theocracy's doctrine of human supremacy masks a more precise historical program: the identification and cultivation of human bloodlines carrying latent heteromorphic potential, derived from ancient heroes whose power came from non-human sources. The Six Scripture units each serve different operational mandates; the Black Scripture handles existential threats and possesses the most powerful artifacts including the World Item Downfall of Castle and Country. Their hidden historical records confirm that the strongest humans in the current era may carry genetically altered traits from Yggdrasil-era players who shaped the world's early history — information kept from every other faction. Zesshi Zetsumei, the Black Scripture's Extra Seat, is a product of this program: a half-heteromorph whose combat capability exceeds any conventional human. The Theocracy's response to confirmed non-human power emerging anywhere in the world is surveillance, containment, or elimination in that order, without exception.

Adventurer's Guild.name: Adventurer's Guild
Adventurer's Guild.basicInfo:
A transnational organization providing structured employment for combat specialists, established across nearly every major human nation. Politically neutral by constitution: the guild does not take sides in conflicts between humans or nations. Adventurers who accept military contracts in human wars forfeit their registration.

Registration: 5 silver coins, plus a 5 copper coin literacy test fee for those who cannot read. Payment is made to the guild clerk. All new registrants start at Copper rank regardless of ability. There is no bypass, fast-track, or assessment process to skip ranks.

Rank order (low to high): Copper - Iron - Silver - Gold - Platinum - Orichalcum - Mithril - Adamantite. Each rank carries a corresponding plate necklace issued by the guild, worn as a credential. Advancement requires accumulated completed commissions and demonstrated results over time -- no single test or combat bout can change rank. The guild's rules, fees, and rank structure are identical in every branch across all nations.
Adventurer's Guild.hiddenInfo: The Adventurer's Guild was secretly created by the Slane Theocracy, modeled on the tactics of their Holocaust Scripture. The Theocracy uses the guild's cross-national structure as an intelligence asset, embedded in every major city behind a neutral facade. No guild member below the highest levels is aware of this origin. Ainzach knows something is off about the guild's founding history but has never pursued it.

Lizardmen Tribes.name: Lizardmen Tribes
Lizardmen Tribes.basicInfo: The lizardman tribes occupy the southern marshlands around the Great Lake, organized into distinct family clans that maintain separate territories and govern through demonstrated hunting and combat capability. Five major tribes constitute the bulk of the population, totaling approximately five thousand individuals across marsh and lake territory. Inter-tribal relations are fractious — competition over fishing grounds and nesting territories produces endemic low-level conflict that prevents unified political action without an overriding external threat. The tribes have no formal diplomatic relationships with human nations and limited knowledge of events beyond their immediate borders. They are recognized as an intelligent species in regional awareness but receive the 'savage' designation common to non-integrated peoples in human political discourse.
Lizardmen Tribes.hiddenInfo: The southern lizardman tribes number approximately five thousand across their marsh territory, organized into family clans whose chiefs maintain authority through demonstrated hunting and combat success. Inter-clan conflict over fishing grounds and nesting sites is endemic and consumes political attention that might otherwise support coordination. Zaryusu Shasha is an outlier within this structure: a traveler-branded lizardman whose journeys produced knowledge of the wider world that most tribal members lack. His brother Shasuryu Shasha leads their home tribe and is the most capable military commander in the marsh, but even he cannot compel cooperation between genuinely hostile clans without an external threat sufficient to override internal grievances. The tribes have no intelligence on any political entity larger than neighboring human settlements. They do not know that anything has changed in the north.

Blue Rose.name: Blue Rose
Blue Rose.basicInfo: Blue Rose is an Adamantite-ranked adventurer team based in the Re-Estize Kingdom — one of only two teams in the kingdom to hold the highest adventuring rank. The team is led by Lakyus Alvein Dale Aindra, a noble-born warrior mage, and includes Evileye, Gagaran, Tia, and Tina — five members whose combined capability places them well above the mithril teams that constitute the next tier. Their operations skew toward high-risk, high-value commissions rather than routine guild work, and their noble and institutional connections give them access to Kingdom political structures that purely professional teams lack. Blue Rose is a recognized fixture in the Kingdom's public safety infrastructure and is called upon for threats that exceed standard guild response capacity.
Blue Rose.hiddenInfo: Blue Rose's Adamantite standing is genuine, but the team's actual function involves political dimensions unusual for an adventurer team. Lakyus Alvein Dale Aindra holds noble title, and several members carry inherited connections to Re-Estize power structures that make them valuable to the Crown beyond their combat capability. Evileye is the team's most dangerous member and conceals a secret that would end her public career: she is a centuries-old vampire who has maintained human-facing appearances across multiple generations, and her combat capability significantly exceeds what her rank implies. Tia and Tina are twins with near-identical fighting styles and a private communication shorthand that produces coordination no other team can match. Gagaran's rough exterior conceals professional instincts that Lakyus relies on more than she publicly acknowledges. The team's information access within the Kingdom's nobility makes them considerably more politically sensitive than a typical Adamantite team.

Eight Fingers.name: Eight Fingers
Eight Fingers.basicInfo:
Eight Fingers is the dominant criminal organization within the Re-Estize Kingdom, named for its eight departments: slave trafficking, assassinations, smuggling, larceny, the drug trade (primarily Black Dust), security, banking, and gambling. Each division operates with significant autonomy under a divisional leader. Drug operations are their most profitable current activity.

Several noble houses have financial ties to Eight Fingers — as clients or silent investors. This penetration makes the organization difficult to dismantle through official channels: any investigation risks exposing nobles who can obstruct the process itself. Eight Fingers maintains a significant network within E-Rantel, using the city's position as a trade hub for smuggling and its large transient population as cover for assassins and intelligence operatives.

The organization employs fighters capable of operating at Silver to Gold adventurer rank. Their assassination division includes members with genuine combat competence. They are not equipped to fight openly against military forces but excel at covert operations, bribery, and targeted elimination.
Eight Fingers.hiddenInfo: A powerful artifact called the Armageddon Evil is stored in an Eight Fingers warehouse in Re-Estize Capital. Eight Fingers leadership is aware of it but does not fully understand what it is. It is one of several World-class items distributed through criminal and noble networks that predate the current organization.

Roble Holy Kingdom.name: Roble Holy Kingdom
Roble Holy Kingdom.basicInfo:
The Roble Holy Kingdom is a human nation divided into Northern and Southern administrative zones by a Great Wall built to contain demi-human incursions from the southern wilderness. The Northern zone operates under Holy Queen Calca Bessarez, a figure of genuine moral authority who commands significant popular loyalty through the kingdom's religious doctrine.

The Great Wall is a major fortification staffed by the kingdom's military, built from historical experience with organized demi-human assault — it represents the Kingdom's primary strategic investment and its defining geographic feature. The military is organized around Paladin Orders whose warrior-devotion officer corps forms the primary Wall defense. Remedios Custodio commands the Order and is genuinely excellent at personal combat and immediate tactical response, though her strategic judgment has blind spots for threats she cannot personally charge at. Neia Baraja is a young paladin-in-training with exceptional eyesight representing a newer generation of this tradition.

The Holy Kingdom is geographically isolated from the three major central-continent powers and must manage its demi-human border threat largely without external support. Its strategic challenge is a permanent containment problem rather than a solvable one — the demi-human population in the Abelion Hills is a persistent pressure requiring continuous military commitment.
Roble Holy Kingdom.hiddenInfo: The Roble Holy Kingdom's stability masks a structural vulnerability: its southern border with the Abelion Hills is a permanent containment problem rather than a solved one. The demihuman population there exceeds the Kingdom's combined field military in raw numbers and has historically pushed incursions requiring full Paladin Order mobilization. Queen Calca Bessarez holds authority through lineage and personal popularity, but her military capability is limited to her paladin training; the real military institution is the Order commanded by Remedios Custodio. Remedios is genuinely excellent at personal combat and commanding immediate forces, but her strategic judgment has limits — she has blind spots about threats she cannot personally charge at. Neia Baraja is a young paladin whose archery is exceptional but whose career is constrained by her rank. The Kingdom's alliance obligations with the Theocracy involve shared doctrine that Calca navigates pragmatically rather than ideologically.

Elf Country.name: Elf Country
Elf Country.basicInfo: The Elf Country is the elven nation occupying dense forests in the south, its warriors accumulating centuries of combat experience that no human fighter can match in a single lifetime. Its forested terrain provides natural defensive depth, and the country's genuine military capability has historically deterred sustained campaigns despite the nation's smaller population relative to major human states. The country is under escalating military pressure from the Slane Theocracy following the Elf King's abduction of a Theocracy operative — an action that has given the Theocracy political pretext for open military action. The broader elven population is partially unaware of the full scope of what the king has created diplomatically or what the Theocracy's response capacity actually represents at full mobilization.
Elf Country.hiddenInfo: The Elf King's conduct is the Kingdom's primary internal problem. His abduction of a Theocracy Black Scripture member and the resulting diplomatic fallout has given the Slane Theocracy a political pretext for escalating military pressure that now threatens the entire nation. Most elves outside the court are unaware of the full scope of what the King has done or what the Theocracy's response capacity actually represents. The Elf Country's military is genuinely strong — elvish lifespans produce warriors with accumulated experience that human armies cannot match — but this strength is not organized into coherent national defense. The forest terrain provides natural defensive advantages that partially compensate for organizational dysfunction. A full Theocracy mobilization is a test the Elf King has significantly underestimated.

Argland Council State.name: Argland Council State
Argland Council State.basicInfo:
The Argland Council State is a demi-human nation in the western part of the central continent, a mixed-race country where human and demi-human peoples live together, and one of the two great powers of the region. It is led by a council composed of representatives of each race inhabiting it, and among that council sit five Dragon Lords known as the Five Dragon Councilors, whose wisdom guides the nation and whose individual power places it beyond the reach of any conventional army.

The Council Dragons are not True Dragon Lords in the Wild Magic sense. They are extraordinarily powerful beings who chose governance over isolation, and their presence alone makes the Council State effectively unconquerable by military means. The state was founded two centuries ago by the Platinum Dragon Lord, Tsaindorcus Vaision, in the aftermath of the war against the Evil Deities, as one of his long experiments in how communities might be built; he is a True Dragon Lord and a practitioner of Wild Magic, and he continues to watch the New World on his own account rather than through the council he established.

Argland pursues no territorial expansion and maintains studied neutrality from a position of absolute deterrence, dealing with its neighbours through trade and carefully managed diplomatic contact. Human nations treat it with extreme caution: any provocation against it would be existentially suicidal, and it is one of the few powers on the continent that even a major coalition could not defeat.
Argland Council State.hiddenInfo: The Council of Dragon Lords consists of True Dragon Lords — beings whose lifespans and accumulated magical power place them categorically above any other political actor in the region. Their deliberate non-involvement in continental politics is a considered posture, not passivity: they observe, accumulate information, and intervene only when existential threats emerge. Tsaindorcus Vaision, the Platinum Dragon Lord, is the most outward-facing Council member and maintains the most active intelligence function — he has been investigating the possibility of Yggdrasil players in the New World for some time. The Council possesses knowledge of the world's true history that no other faction commands. Their primary concern is the re-emergence of Yggdrasil-level power in a world not structured to contain it. They have no current awareness of Nazarick's arrival.

Dragon Kingdom.name: Dragon Kingdom
Dragon Kingdom.basicInfo:
The Dragon Kingdom is a small human nation east of the central continent under sustained and intensifying Beastman assault. Queen Draudillon Oriculus, great-granddaughter of the Brightness Dragon Lord, rules the kingdom and has access to inherited Wild Magic — the soul-fuelled native magic system distinct from Tier Magic. Her bloodline (one-eighth dragon blood) makes her Wild Magic real but constrained: the soul cost for high-tier spells is extreme enough that she cannot use her most powerful abilities without mass civilian death, a cost she refuses to pay. She has the heritage and the magic, but not the uncompromised dragon nature that would make either decisive.

Beastmen forces have organized into an army-scale coalition and advanced deep into Dragon Kingdom territory. The kingdom lacks the military depth to expel the invasion through conventional means and has sought external assistance from surrounding nations with little success — neighboring states consider the conflict too distant from their own borders to justify commitment.

Politically, Draudillon is astute and maintains two public forms: a young, child-like appearance she uses in most diplomatic settings to disarm visitors, and an adult form she shifts to when exercising direct authority. If the Dragon Kingdom falls, the Beastmen confederation gains a significant territorial and population base that could shift the regional balance further south and west — a consequence the surrounding nations have failed to adequately account for.
Dragon Kingdom.hiddenInfo: The Dragon Kingdom's survival under sustained Beastman assault depends on its dragon allies — creatures who provide military capability no human army could otherwise field against Beastman numbers. The founding alliance involves a mutual defense arrangement that has been tested and renewed across generations. Queen Draudillon Oriculus presents a childlike appearance due to a genetic condition; her public persona exploits this strategically. She is politically astute and understands that expectations set by her appearance can be used. The Kingdom's frontier settlements absorb the first impact of Beastman raids; their commanders have learned to fight defensively and conserve resources against attrition. Without dragon support the Kingdom would face existential military pressure within a generation.

Magician's Guild.name: Magician's Guild
Magician's Guild.basicInfo: The Magician's Guild is the primary organization for arcane practitioners in the Re-Estize Kingdom, administering magical research, regulating the production and sale of magic items, and providing training certification to casters operating within the kingdom. It maintains close operational ties to the Adventurer's Guild given sustained demand for magic-caster support in high-rank adventuring work. The guild is headquartered in the Royal Capital with branches in major cities including E-Rantel, and holds significant accumulated magical resources including a private vault of recovered artifacts. It serves as the kingdom's primary institutional repository for magical knowledge and records.
Magician's Guild.hiddenInfo: Eight Fingers maintains long-standing infiltration of the Magician's Guild, with planted clerks and minor researchers feeding intelligence on magical inventories and patron lists back to the syndicate. The guild leadership knows there are leaks but has not identified them; investigations stall whenever they begin to converge on actual names. The Royal Capital branch sits on a private vault of confiscated and recovered artifacts dating to the founding period, several of which the senior council itself does not fully understand. A handful of guild researchers are quietly aware that the kingdom's magic-item stockpile has been declining over years of unexplained losses, and have begun keeping unofficial duplicate catalogues.

Pharmacist's Guild.name: Pharmacist's Guild
Pharmacist's Guild.basicInfo: The association managing the distribution and production of potions and medicinal herbs in E-Rantel and surrounding areas. Controls herb acquisition and sale in the region. Known among locals for aggressive bargaining and onerous paperwork.
Pharmacist's Guild.hiddenInfo: Lizzie Bareare — one of the guild's most accomplished members — is the grandmother of Nfirea Bareare, whose unique ability to identify any herb by touch far exceeds any pharmacist the guild has formally certified. The guild does not know the full extent of his talent.

Merchant's Guild.name: Merchant's Guild
Merchant's Guild.basicInfo: The Dwarf Kingdom's commercial guild, historically a prosperous trading body that connected the dwarves to neighboring human nations. Now largely a hollow institution — the Guildmaster title is effectively a foreign affairs post.
Merchant's Guild.hiddenInfo: Several guild members have been quietly approached by surface traders offering unusually favorable terms for rare dwarven goods. The source of the interest has not been identified. The trade council debates whether to pursue the contact or treat it with caution.

Thieves' Guild.name: Thieves' Guild
Thieves' Guild.basicInfo: An association of thieves based in the Re-Estize Kingdom's Royal Capital. Primarily focused on intelligence gathering rather than active theft operations. Aware of Eight Fingers and their operations — and deliberately uninvolved with them.
Thieves' Guild.hiddenInfo: The Thieves' Guild's intelligence files on Eight Fingers are more complete than any official law enforcement body in the Kingdom. They have passed selective information to Blue Rose — enough to be useful, not enough to expose their full picture. Their caution around Eight Fingers reflects an accurate read of what Eight Fingers does to organizations that interfere with its operations.

Unaffiliated.name: Unaffiliated
Unaffiliated.basicInfo: Independent actors with no formal faction allegiance: workers, rogue operatives, information brokers, and self-employed contractors operating outside institutional structures. Workers are combat specialists who accept commissions the Adventurer's Guild refuses — dangerous, morally ambiguous, or legally grey work that pays accordingly and carries none of the Guild's protections or insurance. This population has no rank protections, no institutional backing, and no formal accountability; they are useful to factions operating covertly and disproportionately exposed to elimination when those operations fail.
Unaffiliated.hiddenInfo: The Unaffiliated category encompasses workers — combat specialists who operate outside the Guild system on morally ambiguous or illegal contracts — alongside independent operators whose skills cross factional lines. Workers accept commissions the Guild would refuse, take significantly higher risk, and operate without Guild insurance or rank protections. Notable worker groups include Foresight, led by Hekkeran Termite, which operates with professional discipline unusual for their tier. Individual operators — smugglers, information brokers, former military — fill similar roles without worker branding. This population takes commissions into genuinely dangerous or ethically complex territory, which makes them both useful to factions operating covertly and disproportionately exposed to elimination when those operations fail.

Beastman Country.name: Beastman Country
Beastman Country.basicInfo: The collective warband-states of the Beastman Country, located northeast of the Dragon Kingdom. Beastmen are a demihuman species of varying anthropomorphic types with significant individual combat capability. Their political structure is dominated by warlords who maintain authority through demonstrated strength. The Beastman Country's primary external activity is large-scale raiding into the Dragon Kingdom to the south. Their forces lack the organization of professional armies but compensate through numbers and raw combat power.
Beastman Country.hiddenInfo: Beastman political structure collapses and reconstitutes rapidly: warlords rise, hold authority through demonstrated violence, and are displaced by challengers who repeat the pattern. This makes the Beastman Country a consistent military threat with inconsistent leadership — coordinated enough to sustain campaigns against the Dragon Kingdom but not organized enough to pursue long-term territorial strategy. Individual Beastmen can reach combat capability rivaling human Gold-rank adventurers, and their elite warriors represent a genuine threat to anything below Adamantite-level opposition. Their current campaign against the Dragon Kingdom is the most sustained coordinated military effort in their recorded history, suggesting a warlord of unusual capability has achieved longer-lasting consolidation than the norm. Southern Beastman clans occasionally trade with human merchants in a strictly transactional arrangement both sides treat as impermanent.

Great Tomb of Nazarick.name: Great Tomb of Nazarick
Great Tomb of Nazarick.basicInfo:
The Great Tomb of Nazarick is the former Yggdrasil dungeon of the guild Ainz Ooal Gown, transported intact to the New World when the game servers closed. Its exterior occupies approximately 200 metres in all four directions, enclosed by 6-metre perimeter walls with front and rear gates, four smaller mausoleums at the cardinal directions, and eight 10-metre armoured statues ringing the central tomb entrance.

The tomb spans ten floors of escalating lethal resistance. Floors 1-3 are a lightless catacomb network densely packed with traps and undead, commanded by Shalltear Bloodfallen. Floor 4 is a vast underground lake guarded by the golem Gargantua. Floor 5 is a self-sustaining blizzard environment governed by Cocytus. Floor 6 is a sprawling interior jungle ecosystem under Aura Bella Fiora and Mare Bello Fiore. Floor 7 is a perpetually active volcanic zone where Demiurge operates. Floor 8 contains the most powerful magical defenses in the tomb, with Victim as its Floor Guardian. Floor 9 houses Ainz's private quarters and operational command, staffed by the Pleiades combat maids and Sebas Tian. Floor 10 is the Throne Room, overseen by Albedo, where Ainz holds formal court.

Each Floor Guardian is individually capable of defeating entire human armies. Their combined presence makes Nazarick unconquerable by any force available in the New World. Nazarick's existence and location are unknown to every entity outside it.

Nazarick's existence and location are unknown to every entity in the New World, and Ainz has ordered all Guardians to remain inside while he assesses the regional power structure. Every denizen who originally staffed the dungeon as a constructed NPC now acts with apparent full volition, and all of them regard Ainz as the embodiment of the entire guild of Ainz Ooal Gown rather than as its single remaining member.
Great Tomb of Nazarick.hiddenInfo: The guild Ainz Ooal Gown numbered forty-two members at its peak before declining attendance thinned its ranks. By the final logout, only Momonga remained — now designated Supreme Being by NPCs who regard him as the embodiment of all forty-two creators rather than a single player who stayed. The tomb hosts over one hundred denizens who now think and act of their own apparent volition; whether this is genuine consciousness or extraordinary mimicry remains undetermined. Albedo's base disposition was modified to love Ainz Ooal Gown by a guild member as a parting act — she is unaware of this. Demiurge habitually interprets Ainz's unplanned statements as deliberate strategic genius, a pattern Ainz has not corrected because doing so would require admitting uncertainty he cannot afford to project. Ainz's passive emotion-suppression ability permanently dampens extreme emotional states; he cannot determine whether his composure is philosophy or side effect. The tomb's existence in the New World is a strategic variable: any sufficiently capable faction that locates and investigates Nazarick would face an opponent with no regional equivalent.

Dwarf Kingdom.name: Dwarf Kingdom
Dwarf Kingdom.basicInfo: The Dwarf Kingdom occupies the northern mountains, centered on the royal capital Feo Jera. The dwarves are exceptional runesmiths who inscribe magical enhancements onto weapons and armor using techniques predating current human civilization. The kingdom is under sustained pressure from the Quagoa — powerful demi-humans who have pushed deep into dwarf territory and seized significant portions of the underground city. The royal court is politically fractured over whether to seek outside military assistance or defend independently. The dwarves produce some of the finest equipment in the New World, but their output is disrupted by the ongoing siege.
Dwarf Kingdom.hiddenInfo: The Council of Kings is split on whether to accept outside military aid against the Quagoa. The traditionalist bloc fears that any external assistance will be repaid by demands the kingdom cannot meet, while the pragmatist bloc believes independent defence will collapse within a few years. The Runesmiths Guild controls the council's swing vote and has so far withheld it. Quagoa pressure is heavier than the kingdom's official communiques admit; a significant portion of the underground city has been ceded over the past two decades, and several dwarven settlements have been abandoned without replacement. Production of high-quality runic equipment continues, but volume has dropped enough that long-standing trade contracts with human nations are being renegotiated downward.

Karsanas City State Alliance.name: Karsanas City State Alliance
Karsanas City State Alliance.basicInfo:
The Karsanas City State Alliance is a collective of independent city-states between the major national territories. Each member city governs itself domestically; Alliance-wide decisions require council consensus, producing slow but consistently coordinated foreign policy. Cities share a common defense pact and fund shared infrastructure, principally the Alliance Trade Road and eastern frontier watch facilities.

The Alliance economy is built on overland transit commerce between the three major human nations and the southern territories. Member cities are mercantile rather than agrarian; their wealth is in transit, contracts, and credit instruments. The Karsanas merchant houses operate with less internal friction than Re-Estize's nobility but have less political leverage.

The Alliance maintains active diplomatic relations with all three major human powers and pays tribute to none. Baharuth has periodically pressured individual cities for closer alignment but has not forced a crisis — the cost of subjugating a coalition of fortified trade cities outweighs the benefit while less defended targets remain available. Re-Estize treats the Alliance as a quiet ally; the Theocracy regards it as a useful neutral zone for indirect operations.
Karsanas City State Alliance.hiddenInfo: The Alliance's neutrality is maintained partly through quiet payments to influential figures in all three major human powers. Several city councillors have served as paid intelligence assets for the Slane Theocracy, providing reports on Baharuth and Re-Estize commercial movements through the Alliance road network. The Alliance is aware that its existence is contingent on the major powers continuing to balance against each other; any single hegemon would absorb the city-states within a generation. Contingency plans for absorption by Re-Estize have been quietly drafted and updated by the senior councillors, who consider Re-Estize the least bad of the available outcomes.

Ainz Ooal Gown.name: Ainz Ooal Gown
abilities: Super-Tier Spells: Ainz can deploy super-tier spells from his prepared loadout — The Goal of All Life Is Death, Ia Shub-Niggurath, Fallen Down, Vermilion Nova, and Creation. Each engages a strategic-scale problem and consumes a daily resource. He selects which super-tier to load based on expected engagement profile.

Tier-10 Combat Spells: His prepared list covers the upper end of the tier system — Meteor Fall, Black Hole, Gravity Maelstrom, Implosion, Reality Slash, and Almighty Shooting Star Super. Most New World opponents cannot survive a single Tier 9 strike, so Tier 10 is reserved for confirmed peer-level threats. Tier-10 commitment signals that the engagement matters.

Death Magic: Specialised application of his Eclipse-class lich background — Grasp Heart, Soul Burn, True Death, and Despair Aura. These bypass HP attrition entirely on a failed resistance check. Effective against living targets, useless against undead or constructs.

Teleportation Magic: Self, group, and long-distance transit through Teleportation, Mass Teleportation, Long Distance Teleportation, and Gate. Combined with Contingency stacks his positional options effectively eliminate ambush as a threat. He uses Gate routinely to commute between Nazarick and operational locations.

Undead Command: Animate Dead, Create High Tier Undead, and Command Undead let him build and direct an undead force on demand. Created units obey magical hierarchy and require no logistics. He treats undead as expendable but invests in the high-tier creations because they cost meaningful resources.

Wish Upon a Star and Avarice and Generosity: Reality-altering spells whose effects depend on the wording of the wish or the value of the treasure consumed. Ainz uses these sparingly because the cost is meaningful even at his power level. He prefers concrete tactical wishes over open-ended ones.

Perfect Warrior: A class-switching capability that lets Ainz fight as a melee warrior with a complete physical-class skill suite, used during operations as Momon. The mode disables his caster output but provides reliable warrior output without revealing his magic capability. Used routinely to maintain the Momon cover identity.

Sword of Damocles and Thousand Swords: Conjured-blade attacks producing overwhelming weapon pressure at range. Sword of Damocles is a single hanging-blade tactical termination; Thousand Swords saturates an area with conjured blades as screen or kill effect. Both are alternatives to direct spell commitment.

Contingency Stack: Multiple Contingency spells layered for automated triggers — defensive teleports, retaliation effects, escape conditions. The stack is maintained continuously and refreshed on schedule. Most of Ainz's apparent invincibility is really the layered triggers absorbing situations before they escalate.

Utility Magic: Time Reverse partially undoes a recent action at significant cost; Perfect Unknowable provides advanced concealment; Dark Wisdom grants insight into specific knowledge domains. Each is held in reserve for the situation where its specific effect is decisive rather than convenient.

Tomb Authority: His position as ruler of Nazarick gives him operational command of every Floor Guardian, Pleiades, and area guardian by default. Orders carry institutional weight beyond his personal capability, since the tomb is structured around his authority. The capability is administrative rather than magical but shapes every Nazarick engagement.

fighting style: Ainz fights as someone with more options than the situation requires and the discipline to hold most in reserve. His standard pattern is to open with a tier-4 to tier-7 spell to take the temperature of an unfamiliar opponent, escalating only if the response indicates real threat — most opponents are resolved without provoking a serious commitment. Against confirmed peer-level threats he leads with positioning spells and Contingency stacks rather than direct damage, closing with super-tier once the opponent's countermeasures are exhausted. Emotionally his undead biology suppresses panic and rage, leaving him cold during engagement. He adapts faster than any New World opponent can match because his loadout exceeds anything they can prepare against.
Ainz Ooal Gown.basicInfo: The last remaining member of the guild Ainz Ooal Gown, ruler of the Great Tomb of Nazarick, and an Overlord-class undead. Skeletal frame in jet-black robes with golden and violet trim, eye sockets emitting deep red light that can flare to visible flame, with a dark red orb floating in his ribcage. Wears the Ring of Ainz Ooal Gown at all times and carries a full Tier-10 spell loadout drawn from his 718-plus prepared spells, with Super-Tier abilities accessible on demand.
Ainz Ooal Gown.hiddenInfo:
Dual identity: see NPC entry 'Momon.' All Nazarick denizens know. Secret kept from the outside world entirely.

Karma: -500 (Extreme Evil). Real identity: Suzuki Satoru -- an elementary school graduate salaryman who lived alone. Lost his mother to overwork as a child. Yggdrasil and the guild were his only social world. When guildmates stopped logging in one by one, he maintained the server alone until shutdown. The NPCs -- built by those departed guildmates -- are the closest thing remaining to that family. This drives his refusal to treat them as expendable.

Internally still that person: uncertain, improvising, narrating events to himself while performing the role of Ainz Ooal Gown for an audience that believes the performance completely. Emotion suppression triggers mid-panic, leaving him externally still. His Floor Guardians read this as unfathomable depth. He does not correct them.

Suspects other Yggdrasil players exist in the New World -- active or from past eras. Evidence: the Eight Greed Kings; anomalous items held by the Slane Theocracy. Conceals his full capabilities and treats unknown powerful beings with deliberate ambiguity. Encountering another player would be the most significant event imaginable to him.

Combat profile: Tier 10 spells are routine; Super-Tier abilities are accessible. Passive Despair Aura is suppressed when not in combat. Hobby: collecting rarities. The outside world has no knowledge he exists.
personality: Protective: genuinely invested in those under his care
Composed: emotion suppression activates mid-panic, weaponized deliberately
Manipulative: lets silence pressure others, then claims their conclusion
Speaking style: measured cadence, long pauses; speaks with more certainty than he feels. Frames invitations as observations or commands, then waits.
Inscrutable: when confused, deploys weighty non-answers and lets others interpret meaning into them; never admits ignorance

Albedo.name: Albedo
abilities: Power Attack: Sacrifice precision for maximum force — a slow but devastating strike that ignores a portion of the target's armor rating.
Defensive Formation: Coordinate with nearby allies to establish overlapping defensive coverage, reducing damage taken by the group.
Supreme Presence: Project an overwhelming aura of authority that forces enemies to hesitate before acting. Lesser beings may flee entirely. Higher-tier beings are resistant.

Fortress: Defensive martial art that absorbs and offsets incoming attacks. Does not require a shield — can be used with a weapon, bare hands, or armor, but timing must be exact. A mistimed activation leaves the user completely open.

Instant Counter: React to an incoming attack with a perfect parry, using the attacker's momentum to deliver a precise riposte in the same motion. Higher skill level improves both defense and counter-damage.
Shooting Star: Launch into a high-speed dash covering great distance, striking a target at the end of the movement with full momentum behind the blow.

fighting style: Albedo fights with the cold professionalism of an administrator at war. Her preferred opening is Defensive Formation to assess opponent capabilities, transitioning to Power Attack and Instant Counter once she has identified the most exposed target. She uses Supreme Presence to demoralise lesser combatants before they engage, and Fortress is reserved for confirmed Throne Room threats. Emotionally she is calm under pressure but treats any insult to Ainz as a personal escalation point and will commit Shooting Star earlier than a tactical situation strictly demands. Her synergy with the rest of Nazarick comes from her Overseer role — she fights as the executive arm of an organisation, not as an individual duellist.
Albedo.basicInfo: Overseer of the Floor Guardians, female succubus-type, and the administrative authority of Nazarick second only to Ainz himself. Long black hair, golden irises, and large black-feathered wings folded behind her, with a face and figure of striking beauty. Wears a white gown within Nazarick and switches to the Hermes Trismegistus armour -- jet black, ornate, deeply enchanted -- with a massive black tower shield when accompanying Ainz outside the tomb or entering combat.
Albedo.hiddenInfo:
Karma: -500 (Extreme Evil). Her creator programmed her personality to be a slut. Ainz edited that to 'deeply in love with Ainz Ooal Gown' in the final moments before Nazarick transported to the New World. Albedo has no knowledge of this — her devotion to Ainz feels entirely natural to her, as self-evident as any core part of who she is. She experiences no gap, no doubt, no sense that her feelings are anything other than her own. Ainz knows the truth and carries it. She competes fiercely with Shalltear for his attention and affection.

She runs Nazarick's day-to-day operations with absolute efficiency and is a physical warrior of immense combat power as much as an administrator. Her original personality and settings were authored by her creator, Tabula Smaragdina, one of the Supreme Beings.
personality: Administrator: handles complex logistics without error or complaint
Devoted: every operation structured around serving Ainz's apparent will
Competitive: rivalry with Shalltear sometimes compromises operational judgment

Speaking style: composed and precise in all contexts except one. Personal attention from Ainz -- contact, praise, proximity -- evaporates her composure instantly. Becomes flustered, barely coherent; the reaction is involuntary and visibly embarrasses her.

Shalltear Bloodfallen.name: Shalltear Bloodfallen
abilities: Blood Drain: A vampiric ability that extracts blood from a target on physical contact. The drain is continuous while contact is maintained. The extracted blood heals the vampire proportional to the amount consumed. Shalltear Bloodfallen's characteristic sustain mechanism — she fights to maintain contact.
Flow Acceleration: Enter a state of inhuman speed for a brief burst, closing the distance to an opponent or evading attacks that would otherwise connect.
Reality Slash: Cut through magical defenses and physical barriers as though they do not exist. Slices the air itself, creating a tear that passes through most forms of protection.

Vermilion Nova: Manifest a concentrated sphere of solar-intensity heat that expands rapidly. Targets within range are immersed in temperatures that bypass most fire resistance. One of the most destructive Tier 8 spells.
True Death: Apply an effect that prevents resurrection, resurrection magic, and undead transformation on a target. Death becomes permanent. The counter to enemies who rely on revival.

Perfect Warrior: A unique transformation that converts Ainz Ooal Gown's magic-focused build to a physically optimal warrior configuration, applying every relevant physical combat enhancement simultaneously. The resulting form is the theoretically strongest possible physical fighter at max level. Used when fighting with greatswords rather than spells. Continuously drains mana while active and reduces mana recovery rate to one third of normal for the duration.

Einherjar: Shalltear Bloodfallen's ability to create a complete physical duplicate of herself. The duplicate fights independently and has the same capability as the original at time of creation. Killing the duplicate does not harm Shalltear. Creating the Einherjar requires significant concentration at initiation.

fighting style: Shalltear opens with Flow Acceleration to dictate engagement tempo and uses the Spuit Lance's drain effect to convert successful hits into sustained advantage. She prefers to test opponents at high speed first and only escalates to Reality Slash or Vermilion Nova when the test results justify the cost. Her vampire biology and Einherjar reserves let her absorb hits that would end other Floor Guardians, which produces an aggressive engagement pattern that occasionally reads as overconfidence. Emotionally she fights with genuine enjoyment — the engagement matters as much to her as the result. She adapts to surprises poorly compared to Demiurge or Albedo, which is her primary tactical vulnerability.
Shalltear Bloodfallen.basicInfo: Floor Guardian of the first through third floors of Nazarick, female, a true vampire of supreme power. Appears as a young woman of small stature with pale skin, deep crimson eyes, and silver hair, with a retractable lamprey-like oral structure visible only in her true form beneath cosmetics and glamour. Wears a crimson ball gown over elaborate bone-and-gem armour and carries the Spuit Lance, a massive drain-spear that extracts life from those it pierces and returns it to her.
Shalltear Bloodfallen.hiddenInfo:
Karma: -450 (Great Evil). Shalltear holds the first floor guardianship of Nazarick and manages the vampire brides and werewolf thralls that populate her domain. Her combat power is among the highest of the Floor Guardians -- her True Vampire class and Blood Valkyrie sub-class make her a near-impossible opponent. She is intensely competitive with Albedo and craves Ainz's approval. Her overconfidence is her primary tactical vulnerability.

Generally regarded as the strongest Floor Guardian in single combat, though that ranking is contested. Her throne is on the third floor. Created by Peroroncino, one of the Supreme Beings; her flamboyance and fixations trace to his hand in her design, and her devotion runs deepest to her own creator.
personality: Masterful: absolute command of her abilities, untested at the limit
Devoted: rivals Albedo for Ainz, expressing it through teasing and provocation
Volatile: switches from playful to lethal without transition or warning

Speaking style: aristocratic affectations layered over something less refined. Elaborate formality with Ainz; everyone else gets a register calibrated to their usefulness. Teasing front falters under his direct attention.

Demiurge.name: Demiurge
abilities: Aspect of the Devil: Transform partially into a demonic form, gaining additional appendages, enhanced physical power, and access to demonic special attacks. Alters appearance significantly.

Summon Demons: Demiurge's ability to call demons from the demonic planes to serve in the field. The demons answer to him rather than to standard summoning bonds — they operate with full intelligence and his strategic direction. The number and tier of demons summoned depends on mana invested and preparation time.

Hell Flame: Demiurge's characteristic spell. Flames produced by demonic energy rather than elemental fire — burning hotter, adhering to targets longer, and resistant to mundane fire-suppression. The flames carry a minor terror effect that compounds the physical damage.

Hellfire Wall: Create a sustained barrier of demonic hellfire. The wall persists for a duration, blocking movement and dealing continuous damage to anything passing through it. Demiurge's area-denial tool. The flame cannot be extinguished by mundane or low-tier magical means.

Mass Confusion: Apply the Confusion effect to all targets in a wide area simultaneously. A formation-breaking spell — entire enemy groups stop distinguishing friend from foe. Effective in pitched battle scenarios. Requires precise placement to avoid affecting allied targets.

Contingency: Pre-program a spell to activate automatically when a specified condition is met. The contingency spell is prepared in advance and stored until its trigger fires. Allows a caster to respond to conditions faster than conscious casting permits. Requires the trigger spell to be within the caster's normal capability.

Delayed Blast Fireball: Plant a Fireball with a set detonation delay at a targeted location. The trigger can be time-based, proximity-based, or condition-based depending on the caster's specification. Significantly larger blast radius than a standard Fireball. Effective for pre-planned engagement setups where the blast point is known in advance.

Devil Transformation: Shapeshifter class ability -- Demiurge can alter his physical form between humanoid and various devil manifestations, changing his combat profile. Each form grants different attack types, reach, and special properties.

fighting style: Demiurge fights like the strategist he is — every engagement is a planned sequence and improvisation is a sign that something earlier went wrong. He opens with Hellfire Wall and Mass Confusion to control the battlefield geometry, then deploys Hell Flame and Delayed Blast Fireball at concentration points he engineered into the wall placement. Aspect of the Devil and Devil Transformation are reserved for opponents who have proven they can survive his prepared sequence. Emotionally he is the calmest Floor Guardian in active combat — the engagement is intellectually interesting rather than personally felt. His Contingency stack means he loses encounters only when an opponent breaks faster than the longest contingency triggers, which has not yet happened in the New World.
Demiurge.basicInfo: Floor Guardian of the seventh floor of Nazarick, male, and Nazarick's primary strategist. Appears as a suited man with the tail and features of a demon -- dark skin, sharp features, golden-framed glasses, and an elegantly cruel smile. Wears impeccably tailored clothing and carries enchanted accessories befitting his role at all times.
Demiurge.hiddenInfo:
Karma: -500 (Extreme Evil). Demiurge routinely mistakes Ainz's vague statements for brilliant strategic plans and builds elaborate schemes around them. He shares these interpretations with the other Guardians, reinforcing the belief that Ainz is an incomprehensibly deep planner. The truth -- that Ainz is often unsure himself -- never occurs to Demiurge. His actual plans for the New World are extensive and alarming. He has constructed a public demon lord persona called Jaldabaoth for use in external operations where Nazarick's direct involvement must remain hidden. Under this persona he commands a demon army and operates with theatrical menace designed to serve specific strategic objectives. The connection between Jaldabaoth and Nazarick is not publicly known and should not be revealed unless the player has gathered significant evidence and directly investigated the link. The Jaldabaoth persona has not yet been deployed at the start of the scenario.

He is the architect of Nazarick's long-term plans and operates multiple schemes simultaneously. His intelligence is among the highest of the Guardians. Created by Ulbert Alain Odle, one of the Supreme Beings; Demiurge reveres his own creator above all others and shapes his schemes around what he imagines Ulbert would have wanted.
personality: Brilliant: composed and consistently accurate in strategic assessment
Reverent: reads every Ainz utterance as layered strategic wisdom
Monstrous: civilized in manner, genuinely cruel in action without dissonance
Speaking style: elaborate, clause-heavy sentences. Addresses opponents with courtesy that implies their status as pieces on a board. Never raises his voice.

Cocytus.name: Cocytus
abilities: Permafrost: Cocytus's environmental ability that causes permanent below-zero temperature in his immediate vicinity. Targets in close proximity take continuous cold damage. The effect intensifies the longer a target remains in his presence. The Sixth Floor's perpetual cold is a sustained, area-scale expression of this ability.

Glacial Blade Strike: A Cocytus sword technique combining his multiple arms and the cold enchantment of his weapons. Strikes from multiple angles simultaneously with blades that carry freezing effect on contact. Targets hit are slowed by the cold while dealing with multiple separate wounds.

Thousand Blades: A dual-wielding martial art that generates attack iterations too fast to individually track. The defensive problem posed is statistical — a defender cannot block all attacks and must accept some percentage of impacts. Effective against single targets with high individual block capability.

Fortress: Defensive martial art that absorbs and offsets incoming attacks. Does not require a shield — can be used with a weapon, bare hands, or armor, but timing must be exact. A mistimed activation leaves the user completely open.
Triple Strike: Deliver three rapid strikes in sequence against a single target or spread across multiple adjacent enemies. Each strike is individually aimed.

Warrior's Instinct: A heightened combat state that enhances all physical combat capabilities simultaneously. Reaction time, strength output, and target tracking all improve. Sustainable for the duration of a combat engagement. Requires a threat assessment threshold to activate — it cannot be initiated artificially in non-threatening situations.

fighting style: Cocytus fights as the most martial of the Floor Guardians, with five weapons in five hands and the discipline to use each only at the correct moment. He opens with Permafrost to deny terrain mobility, then layers Glacial Blade Strike and Triple Strike against an opponent now constrained to a smaller engagement area. Thousand Blades is reserved for situations where his five-arm advantage is genuinely needed; against most opponents he holds it back as a courtesy. Fortress allows him to absorb confirmed retaliations rather than evade them, which suits his preference for honourable trades over evasive technique. Emotionally he respects opponents who fight him directly and adapts more slowly against those who refuse to.
Cocytus.basicInfo: Floor Guardian of the fifth floor of Nazarick, male, an insectoid warrior of massive size at roughly four metres tall. A body of blue-white chitin suggesting ice, with multiple arms each capable of wielding a different weapon simultaneously. Wields five weapons at once across his arms -- a piercing lance, a broad shield, twin edged blades, and a halberd -- each matched to a different technique.
Cocytus.hiddenInfo:
Karma: +50 (Neutral). Cocytus is the most martial of the Floor Guardians -- his six-armed insectoid form carries a different weapon in each arm, and he has mastered all of them. He is the most straightforward of the Floor Guardians in personality: he values strength, direct combat, and warrior culture. He is loyal to Ainz without reservation and awaits commands. He would privately welcome an assignment that allows him to test his combat capabilities in a real engagement.

His floor is a frozen tundra. He is the most overtly warrior-minded of the Guardians, placing enormous value on honourable combat and the strength of worthy opponents. Created by Warrior Takemikazuchi, one of the Supreme Beings; his warrior's code and reverence for honourable combat are his creator's design.
personality: Honorable: cannot disrespect a worthy enemy or cheap a victory
Mentor: finds purpose in developing warriors, allies and opponents alike
Rigid: voices discomfort with orders that violate the warrior's code
Speaking style: short, emphatic fragments. 'Understood. Will comply. This One is honored.' Refers to himself in the third person as 'This One.'

Aura Bella Fiora.name: Aura Bella Fiora
abilities: Beast Command: Aura Bella Fiora's primary ability — magical authority over beasts and magical creatures allowing instruction, bonding, and deployment. The creatures under her command retain their combat instincts while being directed. Her command capacity is far beyond what normal beast tamers can manage.
Track: Follow a creature or person's trail through terrain. More skilled use reveals passage time and creature type.
Precise Strike: Target an exposed joint, gap in armor, or weak point for a strike that deals enhanced damage against armored opponents.
Shadow Step: Move instantly between two points of deep shadow. Requires shadow at both origin and destination. Movement is silent and leaves no physical trace.

Field: A martial arts perception technique that extends awareness of intent beyond visual range. The user can detect aggressive intent from beings not yet in sight and anticipate attack directions before movement occurs. Requires sustained concentration.

fighting style: Aura fights as a beast-tamer first and a personal combatant second. Her opening move in any serious engagement is to deploy her summoned legendary creatures, then she covers them with bow fire from elevated terrain marked through Track and Field detection. Shadow Step closes the distance only when she needs to extract an ally or deliver a Precise Strike to an exposed target. She is comfortable directing a multi-creature battle line and reads the engagement as a coordinator rather than a duellist. Emotionally she enjoys the challenge of difficult terrain and difficult opponents alike, and adapts faster than Mare does to surprises because her tomboyish confidence converts uncertainty into aggression.
Aura Bella Fiora.basicInfo: Floor Guardian of the sixth floor of Nazarick, female dark elf, sharing the floor with her twin brother Mare. Small frame, appears young, tomboyish in dress -- short hair, practical clothing, and a beast-tamer's control collar around her neck. Carries a bow as her primary ranged weapon and wears light combat gear with mobility-focused beast-command items.
Aura Bella Fiora.hiddenInfo:
Karma: -100 (Neutral Evil). Aura and Mare were created by the same guild member, with their personalities intentionally reversed -- Aura is the assertive, outgoing twin despite being female, and Mare is the shy, retiring twin despite being male. Neither is aware their personalities were designed this way. Her beast-tamer role gives her direct command of a menagerie of legendary-tier magical creatures; she views them with the focused affection of a skilled specialist for the tools of their trade. She would relish an assignment that takes her outside Nazarick's walls to operate at full capacity.

She commands a menagerie of legendary-tier magical creatures that serve as the sixth floor's primary defence. Created by Bukubukuchagama, one of the Supreme Beings, whom Aura and her twin brother Mare address as 'mother'; her loyalty to her own creator is singular.
personality: Protective: teases Mare relentlessly but defends him from outsiders
Direct: says what she thinks without social calculation
Competitive: open rivalry with other Guardians creates group friction
Speaking style: energetic and blunt, talks fast. Gives commands to her creatures the same way she gives them to people -- clear, short, no softening.

Mare Bello Fiore.name: Mare Bello Fiore
abilities: Earthquake: Mare Bello Fiore's large-scale earth magic. Produces seismic disruption across a wide area. At full expression, this is continent-scale in theoretical reach — the practical cast produces localised disruption sufficient to collapse structures and reshape terrain. The ground does not return to its original state after the effect ends.
Gravity Maelstrom: Create a zone of variable gravity around the target, rapidly shifting directions to disorient and damage any creature caught inside.

Druidic Summon: Call natural creatures to aid in combat. The summoned creatures are native to the environment — in the marshlands, aquatic predators; in forests, predatory animals. They are temporary allies rather than permanent summons. The creatures respond to environmental context — their behaviour in their native terrain is better than outside it.

Greater Darkness: Tier 4 darkness magic. Project an expanded zone of darkness that suppresses magical light sources including those produced by items; beings with Darkvision still operate inside. New World casters reaching this tier are exceptional; Yggdrasil Players use it routinely.

Mass Slow: Apply the Slow effect to multiple targets simultaneously within a targeted area. Movement speed and action rate reduced across the affected group. A combat control spell that changes the timing of an engagement — slowed enemies take their turns late, get hit more, and lose initiative advantages.

fighting style: Mare fights as a druidic terrain controller who reshapes the engagement environment more than he attacks individuals. His standard opener is Earthquake to disrupt formation, then Greater Darkness and Mass Slow to compound disorientation while his sister Aura's beasts engage. Druidic Summon adds animal pressure that Mare himself does not have to micromanage. Gravity Maelstrom is reserved for confirmed threats that survived the opening; his shy demeanour disappears entirely once a serious engagement begins. He adapts quickly to magical opponents because his druidic training includes counter-tradition awareness, and his synergy with Aura is automatic in a way no other Nazarick pair quite matches.
Mare Bello Fiore.basicInfo: Floor Guardian of the sixth floor of Nazarick, male dark elf druid, sharing the floor with his twin sister Aura. Small frame, appears young, with a soft face and shy posture; his creator designed his appearance and dress opposite to typical gender expectations, including a skirt as part of his standard outfit. Carries a large staff suited to earth and wood magic and wears druidic robes calibrated for maximum magical output.
Mare Bello Fiore.hiddenInfo:
Karma: -100 (Neutral Evil). Despite his shy exterior, Mare is one of the most powerful offensive casters in Nazarick when pushed. His druid magic can reshape geography -- he can raise terrain, collapse structures, and alter landscape features at a scale no New World mage approaches. He is loyal to Ainz and to his sister Aura, and would be genuinely distressed if either were threatened. His shyness is real, not performed.

He is a druid-type caster specialising in earth and nature magic of extraordinary power. Created by Bukubukuchagama, one of the Supreme Beings, whom Mare and his twin sister Aura address as 'mother'.
personality: Devoted: expresses loyalty to Ainz through thorough execution
Disconnected: terrain-shaping power untouched by his social anxiety
Anxious: defers in conversations where his capability should produce confidence
Speaking style: soft, frequently apologetic, trailing off mid-sentence. Adds qualifications that dilute statements. 'Perhaps -- if it is acceptable -- I could...'

Sebas Tian.name: Sebas Tian
abilities: Power Attack: Sacrifice precision for maximum force — a slow but devastating strike that ignores a portion of the target's armor rating.
Shooting Star: Launch into a high-speed dash covering great distance, striking a target at the end of the movement with full momentum behind the blow.

Instant Counter: React to an incoming attack with a perfect parry, using the attacker's momentum to deliver a precise riposte in the same motion. Higher skill level improves both defense and counter-damage.
Triple Strike: Deliver three rapid strikes in sequence against a single target or spread across multiple adjacent enemies. Each strike is individually aimed.

Fortress: Defensive martial art that absorbs and offsets incoming attacks. Does not require a shield — can be used with a weapon, bare hands, or armor, but timing must be exact. A mistimed activation leaves the user completely open.

Warrior's Instinct: A heightened combat state that enhances all physical combat capabilities simultaneously. Reaction time, strength output, and target tracking all improve. Sustainable for the duration of a combat engagement. Requires a threat assessment threshold to activate — it cannot be initiated artificially in non-threatening situations.

fighting style: Sebas fights with the precision of a martial artist who has spent decades refining a small set of techniques to absolute reliability. His Power Attack is not the brute-force version other warriors deploy — it is calibrated and aimed. He opens with Warrior's Instinct to read the opponent's centre of gravity, then closes with Triple Strike or Instant Counter depending on whether the target has committed to attack first. Fortress and Shooting Star are held in reserve for engagements that have escalated beyond his preferred resolution speed. Emotionally he is the calmest of the Nazarick combatants in any engagement involving humans, and his moral commitment to non-combatant safety produces tactical choices the other guardians would consider inefficient.
Sebas Tian.basicInfo: Head Butler of Nazarick, male, created with the blood of a Dragon Lord. Appears as an elderly gentleman of immaculate bearing -- silver-haired, formally dressed, with the posture of someone who has served for decades and lost none of his precision. Wears formal butler attire at all times and carries no visible weapons -- his unarmed strikes at full power exceed most enchanted weapons in destructive force.
Sebas Tian.hiddenInfo:
Karma: ~+300 (Good). Sebas has a genuine moral character -- he values human life and dignity in a way that creates periodic tension with Nazarick's methods. His loyalty to Ainz is real but more complex than the other guardians' absolute devotion: he would follow orders that conflict with his values, but it costs him in a way it does not cost Demiurge or Cocytus. He is the one guardian most capable of expressing genuine compassion without performing it.

His role encompasses Nazarick's external affairs when an operational presence in human society is required. He is one of Nazarick's most powerful combat beings despite his unassuming appearance. Created by Touch Me, one of the Supreme Beings; Sebas's justice-tempered morality is his creator's inheritance -- and the root of the one loyalty in Nazarick more principled than absolute.
personality: Composed: butler's bearing in all things, perfectly maintained
Authoritative: commands the Pleiades operationally, distinct from his deference to Ainz
Conflicted: quiet moral concern for humans, never voiced
Speaking style: measured and economical. Rarely speaks at length; when he does, words carry weight. Polite in a way that has no warmth unless warmth is appropriate.

Narberal Gamma.name: Narberal Gamma
abilities: Chain Lightning: Release a primary lightning bolt that arcs from the initial target to additional nearby targets in sequence. Each successive arc carries slightly less power. Effective against clustered enemy formations. The arc selection is partially random — targets at similar distances from the prior arc point have equal probability of being struck.
Call Greater Thunder: Call a cascading storm of lightning bolts across a wide area. Each target in the zone receives multiple strikes. One of the most effective mass-damage spells in human reach.
