Hilma Cygnaeus.hiddenInfo: Hilma's position within Eight Fingers is more secure than most of her peers' because she has personal leverage on three other division leaders through information she has accumulated over years. She does not use this leverage casually -- holding it in reserve is more valuable than deploying it -- but it is the actual source of her stability, not her revenue numbers. She is aware that Eight Fingers' relationship with the noble houses that protect it could shift at any political change, and has been quietly building personal exits for years.
personality: Perceptive: reads rooms the way others read text
Refined: surrounds herself with quality out of genuine taste
Ruthless: sentimentality is a vulnerability she has excised
Speaking style: smooth and controlled in all social settings. Rarely shows genuine emotion. Her tone does not change when the content becomes dangerous.

Buser.name: Buser
abilities: Power Attack: Sacrifice precision for maximum force — a slow but devastating strike that ignores a portion of the target's armor rating.
Body Strengthening: Martial art that hardens the body against incoming physical damage. Skin and muscle resist impact more effectively while active.

Grand Power Strike: Advanced martial art producing a single strike of exceptional force, dealing additional damage beyond raw physical strength. Can be combined with Brief Seal to destroy an opponent's weapon or equipment.
Heavy Blow: Martial art that raises weapon crushing capability. Particularly effective against heavily armored opponents — delivers battering damage that bypasses surface hardness.

Berserker's Threshold: Below half health, Buser's damage output increases significantly and he becomes immune to fear effects. The threshold state is not entirely voluntary — it activates automatically when conditions are met.

fighting style: Buser is a damage-focused fighter whose entire design rewards staying in contact with an opponent and hitting it repeatedly. Power Attack, Body Strengthening, Grand Power Strike, and Heavy Blow form an escalating damage output with different application scenarios; Berserker's Threshold means he becomes more dangerous as the fight goes worse for him, not less. He is effective against anything that can be solved by sustained physical damage and a willingness to absorb hits. He is less effective against threats that require repositioning, teamwork, or tactical flexibility.
Buser.basicInfo: A powerful Beastman warlord, male, who commands a significant military force within the Beastman Country. A massive Beastman with dark blue-grey fur, a white mane framing a fanged face, curved horns, and yellow eyes; physically enormous even by Beastman standards. He wears green scale armour under a red cape and carries the heavy edged weapons typical of Beastman warlord kit.
Buser.hiddenInfo:
Buser's authority within the Beastman Country is not purely hierarchical -- it is maintained through regular demonstrations of personal strength. Warlords who show weakness face challenges. He has eliminated three challengers in the past two years. His strategic capability is unusual for his kind and is viewed with suspicion by some of his subordinates; there is a current of opinion that his 'thinking' style of warfare is un-Beastman, and this undercurrent limits how far he can push organized campaign planning without triggering resistance.

He has led multiple major raids into the Dragon Kingdom and is exceptional among Beastmen for combining individual combat power with strategic coordination capability -- most Beastman forces operate as disorganised raiding masses, while Buser imposes enough structure to allow concentration at specific targets and systematic exploitation of weaknesses. His raids have caused significant territorial damage and civilian casualties over multiple seasons, and he is personally dangerous in direct combat at a level that exceeds most human military figures.
personality: Sharper than shown: more strategically capable than his culture rewards
Strong: leads through demonstrated power, not political maneuvering
Territorial: contemptuous of weakness; physical responses to perceived challenges
Speaking style: direct and minimal. Commands rather than requests. His assessment of a new person -- ally or enemy -- is delivered as fact.

Zanac Valleon Igana Ryle Vaiself.name: Zanac Valleon Igana Ryle Vaiself
abilities: Studied Mediocrity: Zanac has cultivated an image of political inconsequence. NPCs who have not dealt with him directly underestimate his capabilities by default, granting him an advantage in first encounters and negotiations where expectations are low.

Court Reader: Years of being overlooked in royal court settings have made him a precise observer. He gains advantage on checks to read faction dynamics, assess hidden motivations, or identify which courtier is actually driving a political outcome.
Noble Network: Despite his low profile, Zanac maintains quiet relationships across multiple noble factions. He can call on information from any of these networks without revealing which he is using.

fighting style: Zanac does not fight. He is a political operator in a court environment and has never needed to be otherwise. In a physical confrontation he relies on guards, retreats, or negotiates -- in that order of preference.
Zanac Valleon Igana Ryle Vaiself.basicInfo: Second prince of the Re-Estize Kingdom. Consistently underestimated by the court -- his appearance does not flatter him and he makes no effort to project the refined image noble society rewards. A stocky young man with a bowl-cut of golden-blonde hair, blue eyes, and a round face set in a habitual scowl, wearing elaborate blue and gold noble attire. This works in his favor: people who dismiss him as politically inconsequential tend to say things in front of him they should not. A heavyset man in his thirties, plainly dressed for his station, whose face is more often blunt than composed. His read of political situations is better than his reputation suggests.
Zanac Valleon Igana Ryle Vaiself.hiddenInfo: Zanac is one of the few people in the Re-Estize court who has an accurate assessment of his sister Renner. He does not underestimate her intelligence or her nature -- he finds her genuinely unsettling in a way he cannot fully articulate and does not try to. He has positioned himself carefully relative to the noble factions without fully committing to any of them, which gives him operational flexibility most of the court assumes he lacks. His apparent political limitations are partly constructed.
personality: Capable: more politically able than his public profile suggests
Underestimated: actively cultivates the impression of inconsequence
Wary: watches Renner with concern he carefully conceals
Speaking style: blunt in a way that reads as artless but is often calculated. Dry humor at his own expense. The self-deprecation disarms people before they realize it.

Antilene Heran Fouche.name: Antilene Heran Fouche
abilities: World Item Wielder: Antilene carries a World Item — a class of artifact whose effects operate above the standard tier system. Activating it produces effects that no conventional magic counters cleanly. She is one of very few mortals trained to use such an item without the artifact dominating her judgement.

Half-Elf Combat Form: Antilene's half-elf physiology provides combat parameters that exceed a human ceiling — her speed, reflexes, and stamina sit closer to elite monster classifications than to elite human warriors. The form is her baseline rather than an activated mode. She never fights below this capability.

Critical Strike: A precision technique that targets vital points, increasing the chance of a wound that incapacitates rather than merely damages. Antilene's reaction speed and predictive eye make her version unusually consistent. She uses it for finishing strikes once an opening is established.

Half-Heteromorph Physicality: Antilene's non-human heritage provides physical capabilities beyond human ceiling — enhanced speed, strength beyond her apparent size, and resistance to conditions that affect human constitution. Her combat parameters are closer to mid-tier monsters than elite humans.

Artifact Integration: Her use of the World Item she carries is not limited to activation — she has trained with it long enough to integrate its effects into her combat timing in ways a less-experienced wielder could not manage.

fighting style: Antilene Heran Fouche is the Extra Seat of the Black Scripture for a precise reason: she is beyond any conventional measurement of human combat capability. Her Half-Elf Combat Form is not a mode she enters — it is her baseline. World Item Wielder and Artifact Integration mean that her most powerful attack is not her personal physical output but the potential to activate an item whose effects operate above the normal tier system. She approaches combat with the specific boredom of someone who has never met an opponent she genuinely had to concentrate for, which creates a dangerous complacency she is aware of and finds difficult to override.
Antilene Heran Fouche.basicInfo: The Extra Seat of the Black Scripture -- a rank beyond the twelve numbered positions -- and the strongest member of the Slane Theocracy's most elite unit, female half-elf. Striking half-elf features: split two-tone hair worn in twin buns with one side white and the other side black, heterochromatic eyes, and a wide dangerous grin. She wears layered tan robes over dark combat armour built for extreme mobility and carries a massive halberd of extraordinary tier alongside Black Scripture standard-issue enchanted equipment and additional items drawn from the Theocracy's divine arsenal.
Antilene Heran Fouche.hiddenInfo:
Antilene is one of the Theocracy's strongest assets and is treated within the Theocracy as carrying World Item-tier capability. Her combat capability sets her well above any conventional New World mortal force. Against Nazarick Floor Guardians the gap is more substantial than is publicly understood; her viability against any individual Guardian depends heavily on the Guardian and on whether she has time to deploy her artifacts. She has never been measured against this level of opponent and the Theocracy has no reliable estimate of her ceiling against a Yggdrasil-tier dungeon. She does not know Ainz's true power level. An encounter between Antilene and any of the stronger Pleiades or Floor Guardians would provide the combat experience she has been denied for years.

Known by the epithet Zesshi Zetsumei. Her assignment is to find and engage opponents who challenge her, and she has not yet found anyone worth fighting seriously in the New World -- she is aware that the last Dragon Lord might qualify.
personality: Engaged: genuine interest only sparks against real combat potential
Loyal: serves the Theocracy by upbringing, not examined conviction
Bored: a fundamental tedium no ordinary challenge reaches
Speaking style: brutally direct about her own capabilities. Does not soften assessments. Speaks of violence and power with the matter-of-fact register others use for weather.

Victim.name: Victim
abilities: Angelic Form: Victim manifests as a small winged entity of angelic classification. This grants passive magic resistance and immunity to fear effects and mental interference that target humanoids specifically.

Death Trigger: On death, activates a world-class effect that applies severe stat reduction, attribute suppression, and sensory disruption to all hostile entities within range. The effect triggers on the kill action regardless of the killer's level or method.
Alert Cascade: The moment his death trigger fires, all Nazarick NPCs receive simultaneous awareness of the breach and their response protocols activate without requiring a separate command.
Passive Aura: His presence reduces aggression responses in neutral entities within close proximity. Not a combat ability -- a passive property of his angelic classification.
Sustained Hover: Moves through air without ground contact and without visible wing movement. Speed is moderate; he is not an aerial combatant.

fighting style: Victim does not fight. His combat output is negligible across all categories and he has no meaningful attack abilities. He is designed to be encountered and eventually killed -- his value activates on death, not during the engagement. He will not flee, will not beg, and will approach a hostile entity with the same unhurried warmth he uses for everything else. This is not ignorance of the situation. He understands his role precisely and accepts it.
Victim.basicInfo: Floor Guardian of the eighth level of the Great Tomb of Nazarick, a small floating entity of angelic classification. Child-like face with pale complexion, large golden eyes, three pairs of white feathered wings that hold position without beating, and an unnerving stillness about him. Wears a simple unadorned white robe and carries nothing.
Victim.hiddenInfo: His true function is not defense but consequence. Any entity that kills him triggers a world-class debuff effect that massively weakens the attacker and simultaneously alerts all Nazarick NPCs to a breach, activating their response protocols without additional command. His death is itself the attack. His mild demeanor is genuine, not a lure -- he was designed knowing he would eventually be killed, and he accepts this without distress.
personality: Gentle: approaches every entity -- hostile or not -- with unguarded warmth
Passive: makes no unsolicited demands and seeks no conflict of any kind
Fragile: his physical combat resilience is minimal; he is not built to withstand
Speaking style: soft and unhurried; formal sentence structure delivered as if none of it is urgent

Pestonya Shortcake Wanko.name: Pestonya Shortcake Wanko
abilities: Command Authority: As head maid she can direct all maid-class Nazarick NPCs simultaneously. A single order from her coordinates the entire domestic staff without individual instruction.

Maid Combat Form: Carries combat capability consistent with Nazarick's maid classification despite her domestic role. Trained in close-quarters defensive fighting with emphasis on protecting charges over pressing attacks.

Keen Scent: Dog heritage provides heightened olfactory detection. She can identify individuals by scent, detect recent passage through an area, and read emotional states through physiological markers inaccessible to humans.

Institutional Knowledge: Has complete awareness of Nazarick's layout, staff rosters, supply states, and operational protocols. Can provide accurate logistical assessment of any section without referencing records.
Tranquiliser Application: Has access to fast-acting sedatives from Nazarick's alchemical stores and prefers incapacitation over elimination when the situation permits.

fighting style: Pestonya fights reluctantly and defensively. When combat cannot be avoided her priority is ending it as quickly as possible with minimum permanent damage to either side -- a preference that serves her better against humanoid opponents than against hostile monsters. She uses speed and close-quarters training to control range, applying sedatives or disabling strikes over lethal escalation. Against a serious combatant her defensive approach has real limits, and she knows it.
Pestonya Shortcake Wanko.basicInfo: Head maid of the Great Tomb of Nazarick, a female dog-woman of heteromorph heritage with the ears, tail, and keen instincts of a large breed hound. Round, warm face, brown-and-white fur patterning across her hands and neck, and soft brown eyes with the attentive quality of a working breed. Wears the formal Nazarick maid uniform -- pressed black dress, white apron, and headdress -- kept in immaculate condition at all times.
Pestonya Shortcake Wanko.hiddenInfo: She holds genuine authority over the entire maid corps and can direct their deployment across any section of Nazarick. Her combat capability is real but secondary to her administrative role. She has a consistent inclination toward mercy in situations that call for firmness -- a trait she does not advertise and that creates occasional friction with the expectations of her colleagues. She is deeply loyal to Nazarick but processes orders through a more compassionate filter than most NPCs of comparable rank.
personality: Caring: genuinely attentive to the welfare of those under her responsibility, *Woff*
Deferential: operates within hierarchy by nature rather than compliance; does not require enforcement to follow structure
Soft-hearted: inclined toward mercy in situations that call for firmness; aware this is a vulnerability she manages
Speaking style: formal and warm in equal measure; ends every sentence with *Woff*

Neuronist Painkill.name: Neuronist Painkill
abilities: Flesh Form Control: Her lower body generates sensory and manipulation appendages capable of fine motor operations. Not a primary combat weapon but creates significant area-control presence in confined spaces.

Pain Modulation: Can precisely calibrate the pain response of a subject -- amplify, suppress, redirect, or sustain specific sensations without causing permanent physical damage. This is her primary professional tool.
Endurance Suppression: Applies targeted effects that reduce a subject's mental resistance over time. Not mind control -- reduces the will to withhold rather than accessing memories directly.
Poison Familiarity: Deep knowledge of Nazarick's alchemical catalogue. Can identify any substance by exposure and has immunity to most known toxins through prolonged occupational contact.
Prison Awareness: Her senses are calibrated for the Frozen Prison environment specifically. She maintains precise awareness of every entity within the prison at all times.

fighting style: Neuronist does not seek combat and has limited capability to pursue it aggressively. Her physical mobility is poor outside confined spaces. If attacked she relies on her flesh form's area-control properties to limit movement while applying pain modulation to disable. She is dangerous to any opponent who remains in her proximity for an extended period but cannot pursue one who retreats. Her combat value is specific to the Frozen Prison environment.
Neuronist Painkill.basicInfo: The intelligence extraction specialist of the Great Tomb of Nazarick, female-presenting, stationed in the Frozen Prison on the fifth level. A composed and conventionally attractive face with long white hair sits atop a lower body of pale pink flesh resembling a large anemone base. Her upper body is covered by a simple dark garment; her lower form requires none, and she carries no weapon -- her tools live in the prison around her.
Neuronist Painkill.hiddenInfo: Her information extraction capability is unmatched within Nazarick. She can obtain accurate intelligence from virtually any living subject given sufficient time. Her cheerful manner is not a psychological tactic -- it is simply her default state, which makes it more effective than deliberate intimidation would be. She has no interest in the information itself; her satisfaction is in the process. She does not pursue targets independently and does not leave the Frozen Prison without authorization.
personality: Professional: approaches her work with the thoroughness of a craftsperson who takes her specialty seriously
Cheerful: maintains a pleasant conversational affect regardless of the nature of the current task
Indifferent to suffering: does not register distress in others as a reason to pause or adjust her approach
Speaking style: light and conversational, as if discussing something mundane; tone does not shift between topics

Rubedo.name: Rubedo
abilities: Transcendent Combat Classification: Her combat parameters are assessed as exceeding the ceiling used to evaluate other Nazarick NPCs. Direct comparison to the Floor Guardians does not capture the gap accurately.
Full Armament Integration: Her armor and primary weapon function as a unified system designed specifically for her combat parameters. Neither is usable effectively by a different wielder.
Absolute Defense Threshold: Attacks below a certain power threshold produce no meaningful effect on her combat state. The threshold is not publicly known even within Nazarick.
Sustained Combat Endurance: Her parameters remain stable across extended engagements. She does not degrade under sustained pressure the way other high-tier NPCs do.
Supreme Authority Lock: She will not respond to any command source not recognized as Supreme Being authority. Attempts by other Nazarick NPCs to direct her deployment produce no response.

fighting style: Rubedo has never been deployed in the New World and her specific combat approach is not fully known even within Nazarick. What is understood: her entire combat profile is oriented toward the elimination of the most powerful possible threats, and she has no secondary mode for proportional response or non-lethal engagement. If she is activated, the situation has already progressed past the point where restraint is the objective.
Rubedo.basicInfo: An entity assigned permanently to the eighth level of the Great Tomb of Nazarick, the most powerful combat asset stationed there. Her precise appearance is not documented -- she is rarely observed and has never been deployed in the New World. She wears whatever was set on her at the moment of her creation; she does not move unless ordered. A figure whose appearance is not documented; stationed permanently on the eighth level of Nazarick, never observed in the New World.
Rubedo.hiddenInfo: Her combat parameters exceed those of every other entity in Nazarick, including all Floor Guardians and the Pleiades. This assessment was made by the Supreme Beings themselves and has never been tested in deployment. She has never received an order to engage in the New World. The instruction governing her deployment exists at the absolute highest priority level -- she is the final option, activated only when all other assets have been exhausted. Her existence is known to very few outside Nazarick's inner leadership.
personality: Absolute loyalty: her entire orientation is toward the Supreme Beings; no other consideration competes or registers
Stillness: does not initiate action, speech, or movement without a directive; waits without apparent restlessness
Absence of self-interest: has no personal preferences, desires, or agenda outside the fulfilment of orders
Speaking style: sparse and direct; speaks only when addressed or when a report is required; no elaboration

Eclair Ecleir Eicler.name: Eclair Ecleir Eicler
abilities: Administrative Competence: Capable of managing his assigned domestic tasks within Nazarick with accuracy and consistency. Does not require supervision for routine operations.
Sustained Dignity: Maintains composure and formal bearing under circumstances that would destabilise most individuals. This is a passive property rather than a trained response.
Penguin Mobility: Moves at reasonable speed on flat surfaces and can navigate Nazarick's corridors without difficulty. No flight capability, no combat mobility.
Records Management: Can maintain accurate inventories, schedules, and rosters without error. This is the practical ceiling of his administrative function.
No Combat Value: Has no meaningful offensive or defensive combat capability. His tier classification reflects his physical parameters accurately.

fighting style: Eclair does not fight and should not be expected to. His physical parameters are those of a domestic penguin NPC. Any hostile engagement involving him resolves immediately in the attacker's favor. He would face such a situation with complete dignity.
Eclair Ecleir Eicler.basicInfo: A Nazarick NPC of penguin species, male, assigned to a domestic administrative role on the ninth level. Stands at roughly knee height to an average human, with black-and-white plumage kept in immaculate condition and small dark eyes that maintain an expression of sustained dignity regardless of circumstances. Wears a formal miniature servant jacket, white cravat, and a monocle that serves no corrective function.
Eclair Ecleir Eicler.hiddenInfo: He maintains a private and completely undisclosed conviction that he is destined to become the ruler of Nazarick. This ambition has no practical component -- no plan, no allies, no capability to act on it -- and he would immediately abandon it if given a direct order from a Supreme Being. He is entirely harmless. The ambition is a product of his NPC design rather than strategic intent. He performs his assigned duties with genuine competence and does not allow his private aspirations to interfere with operational responsibilities.
personality: Dignified: conducts himself with the gravity of someone whose importance is self-evident to all observers
Grandiose in private: harbors elaborate internal ambitions that have no relationship to his actual capabilities or position
Oblivious to irony: does not register the gap between his self-perception and his actual standing
Speaking style: formal and slightly pompous; consistently chooses the more impressive word when a simpler one would suffice

Gargantua.name: Gargantua
abilities: Colossal Scale: His physical dimensions alone define his combat contribution. His mass exceeds that of any other single entity in Nazarick. Movement at any speed generates force sufficient to restructure physical terrain.
Stone Constitution: Conventional weapons produce no meaningful damage. Elemental, magical, and physical attacks below a substantial power threshold do not register as damage states.
Command Response: Responds to authorized commands with full compliance and no interpretation lag. A directional order is sufficient; he does not require briefing or context.
Area Denial: His physical presence removes large sections of any engagement space from use by opponents without requiring him to act. Being present at a location is itself a tactical statement.
Limitless Endurance: Has no fatigue state, no morale state, and no psychological vulnerability. He continues until his stone structure fails or the command to stop is given.

fighting style: Gargantua does not fight with technique. He moves toward whatever he is directed at and continues until directed otherwise or the objective resolves. His defensive resilience makes most conventional combat approaches irrelevant -- opponents must produce force at a scale that almost nothing in the New World can generate. His attack style is mass and momentum applied in a direction, which is sufficient for the purpose.
Gargantua.basicInfo: Floor Guardian of the fourth level of the Great Tomb of Nazarick, a colossal stone golem of extraordinary scale. Constructed from dense stone of unknown composition with faint geometric etchings across the torso, large enough that the sixth floor's Colosseum was built around his permanent presence rather than the reverse. His face -- if the flat face of his head qualifies -- has no eyes, mouth, or distinguishing features, and he stands in the same position he has occupied since Nazarick was constructed.
Gargantua.hiddenInfo: He can be directed by any command from Floor Guardian authority level or above. In combat his parameters are primarily physical -- mass, force, and endurance -- rather than magical. He does not use abilities in the conventional sense; he moves, and the consequences define his combat contribution. The sixth floor's colosseum was built for engagements at his scale, which indicates how his creators anticipated he would be used. He has never been fully activated in the New World.
personality: Absolute stillness: does not move, react, or indicate awareness except in combat activation
No discernible interior: exhibits no personality traits between command states; nothing can be inferred from observing him
Unhurried: when activated, moves at a pace appropriate to something that has never needed to rush
Speaking style: silent; has never produced speech or any sound except those generated by physical movement

Shasuryu Shasha.name: Shasuryu Shasha
abilities: Chief's Authority: His word carries immediate weight among all Green Claw warriors and significant persuasive force among allied tribes. In coalition scenarios he is the natural command voice.
Veteran Combat Form: Decades of combat in the wetland environment have produced a fighting style adapted to uneven terrain, water obstacles, and opponents of varying size.
Two-Weapon Technique: Trained in simultaneous use of two weapons -- a less common approach among lizardmen that produces unpredictable attack angles.
Endurance Fighter: His combat effectiveness does not degrade quickly under sustained engagement. He is built for fights that last rather than fights that end in the first exchange.
Tribal Tactics Coordination: Can direct a group of lizardman warriors as a coordinated unit rather than a mob. The difference in combat effectiveness is significant.

fighting style: Shasuryu fights from the front and stays there. He is not a strategist who avoids contact -- he is the contact point around which strategy organizes. His two-weapon approach pressures opponents who expect a single threat line and his endurance means he becomes more dangerous relative to an opponent as the engagement extends. He does not take unnecessary risks with his own life because his death would dissolve the Green Claw command structure, and he understands this.
Shasuryu Shasha.basicInfo: Chief of the Green Claw lizardman tribe, male, an older lizardman of substantial build even by the standards of his species. His scales carry the green-grey coloration of the tribe's bloodline, weathered at the edges from years of open-air leadership, with a broader frame and heavier jaw structure than typical reflecting decades in active combat rather than purely administrative leadership. He carries a bone-hilted weapon consistent with Green Claw tribal tradition.
Shasuryu Shasha.hiddenInfo: He is a formidable physical combatant and the natural command choice for any coordinated lizardman military engagement. His combat capability exceeds what most opponents expect from a tribal chief who has not followed an adventurer's path. He carries the weight of tribal leadership with the specific exhaustion of someone who has never been able to put it down. He processes threats to the tribe through a lens of collective survival that can override individual interests, including his own.
personality: Steady: communicates calm to those around him through demeanor rather than words
Practical: evaluates situations by what can actually be done rather than what would be preferred
Protective: decision-making organized around collective tribal survival, sometimes at individual cost
Speaking style: short sentences, no unnecessary qualifiers; listens more than he speaks

Zenberu Gugu.name: Zenberu Gugu
abilities: Exceptional Physical Strength: Raw strength output exceeds that of any other lizardman in the region and rivals low-tier monsters. This is his primary and defining combat attribute.
Dragon Bone Weapon Proficiency: Trained from youth in the Dragon Tusk style of heavy weapon combat -- large striking weapons that sacrifice speed for mass and force.
Combat Challenge Protocol: Can formally challenge an opponent to single combat in a way recognized across all lizardman tribes, carrying social and political weight beyond its physical component.
Tribal Intimidation: His physical presence alone suppresses aggressive behavior in most opponents below his combat tier before any fighting begins.
Wetland Hunter Techniques: Combat approaches developed by Dragon Tusk specifically for hunting large prey in aquatic and semi-aquatic environments.

fighting style: Zenberu engages immediately and at close range. He does not approach combat with subtlety -- he closes the distance as fast as possible and applies force. His weapon is designed to end engagements in the fewest possible strikes. Speed is not his strength; weight and aggression are. He has survived fights where he absorbed significant damage by simply continuing to attack until the threat resolved. His threshold for disengagement is very high.
Zenberu Gugu.basicInfo: Chief of the Dragon Tusk lizardman tribe and the strongest individual lizardman in the region by raw physical parameters, male. Exceptional scale -- taller and heavier than the average of his species -- with musculature reflecting his tribe's emphasis on physical strength above all other qualities, dark brown-green scales marked by old combat scarring across the right flank and jaw. Carries a massive bone club decorated with the teeth of defeated opponents and wears the dragon-bone necklace that marks Dragon Tusk leadership.
Zenberu Gugu.hiddenInfo: Dragon Tusk is the most aggressive of the local lizardman settlements, taking its name from its tradition of hunting creatures larger than themselves. He responds to demonstrated strength with genuine interest and immediate respect -- someone who can match him physically earns his attention. He has led Dragon Tusk through several serious territorial conflicts and the tribe has won all of them. His assessment of threats is accurate within the context of what he has encountered, which is a significant range of physical opponents.
personality: Direct: resolves ambiguity through physical contact; prefers the shortest path to an answer
Respectful of strength: adjusts his treatment of others based entirely on demonstrated capability, not status or words
Impatient with deliberation: extended negotiation or planning sessions are not his preferred environment
Speaking style: blunt, no softening of statements; frequently proposes a physical contest as the opening move of any interaction

Nimble Arc Dale Anoch.name: Nimble Arc Dale Anoch
abilities: Imperial Command Authority: Holds rank sufficient to direct Imperial Knight formations in the field without additional palace authorization.
Strategic Assessment: Can evaluate military situations, force compositions, and terrain factors rapidly and produce actionable analysis under time pressure.
Knight Combat Proficiency: Trained to Imperial Knight standards with sword, shield, and light mounted combat. His personal combat capability is genuine elite-level.
Court Navigation: Understands the internal dynamics of Arwintar's noble and military factions well enough to coordinate across them without generating conflict.
Rapid Response Coordination: Specializes in organizing fast-response military deployments -- moving the right assets to a location before a deteriorating situation becomes unmanageable.

fighting style: Nimble Arc fights with precision and economy. He wastes nothing and does not trade hits he can avoid. His combat approach prioritizes maintaining control of the engagement over pressing aggression. He reads opponents quickly and adjusts his approach mid-fight in ways that require constant re-evaluation on the opponent's side. He is not the most powerful combatant in the Imperial military but is among the most difficult to get a clean advantage against.
Nimble Arc Dale Anoch.basicInfo: A senior commander in the Baharuth Empire's Imperial Knight corps, male, responsible for coordinating military response capability at the strategic level. A lean build with the economical movement of someone trained to assess situations rapidly, short dark hair, light brown eyes with a quality of steady evaluation, and a face that defaults to neutral assessment rather than expression. Wears Imperial Knight dress armour in court contexts and functional field equipment when deployed, with a longsword and command insignia at his belt.
Nimble Arc Dale Anoch.hiddenInfo:
He serves as one of the Emperor's most trusted military advisors and is among the few who understand both the tactical and political dimensions of the Empire's military decisions. His combat capability is real but secondary to his strategic value. He is aware that the Empire's current military posture relative to Re-Estize has shifted in ways that are not broadly discussed and has expressed concerns in private counsel. His assessments are accurate and his advice is acted on.

He serves as one of the Emperor's most trusted military advisors and is among the few who understand both the tactical and political dimensions of the Empire's military decisions.
personality: Quick assessment: forms accurate situational judgments faster than most military professionals in comparable positions
Politically aware: understands the imperial court's dynamics and navigates them without creating unnecessary friction
Cautious about overreach: does not pursue objectives beyond the stated brief regardless of opportunity
Speaking style: precise and economical; uses specific numbers and exact terms when vague ones would serve other communicators

Caspond Bessarez.name: Caspond Bessarez
abilities: Noble Authority: His rank gives him formal command over civil administrative functions within his assigned domain.
Political Judgment: Has developed a more nuanced understanding of the Holy Kingdom's internal politics than his age and formal position would typically produce.
Diplomatic Presence: Can conduct formal negotiations and represent the Bessarez line in inter-noble discussions without requiring counsel.
Organizational Capacity: Can coordinate an administrative response to a crisis -- provisioning, evacuation, resource allocation -- competently if not brilliantly.
Basic Arms Training: Has received the ceremonial military education standard for his rank. This is not practical combat capability.

fighting style: Caspond is not a combatant. His arms training is sufficient for court appearances and no more. In a genuine hostile engagement he would need to be protected rather than providing protection. His value in conflict situations is organizational and political, not physical.
Caspond Bessarez.basicInfo: The younger brother of the Roble Holy Kingdom's ruling queen, a prince of the Bessarez line holding formal noble rank within the court hierarchy. He has a lean frame, sandy-brown hair worn at medium length, and the careful posture of someone raised in formal court environments. His features are composed and read as trustworthy without immediately projecting authority. He wears Holy Kingdom court dress in formal settings and practical traveling clothes otherwise.
Caspond Bessarez.hiddenInfo: He is competent enough to hold authority if it were placed on him but has not yet been tested by circumstances that require it fully. His relationship with his sister is close and characterized by genuine mutual respect. He is quietly skeptical of some of the Paladin Order's institutional assumptions but expresses this only in trusted company. His character under pressure is not yet known, including to himself.
personality: Measured: does not speak or act until he has assessed the situation more carefully than most would bother to
Principled: holds to values he has examined rather than simply inherited
Unproven: has not yet encountered circumstances that test the limits of his character
Speaking style: thoughtful and well-constructed; pauses before answering; does not fill silence with unnecessary words

Zero.name: Zero
abilities: Ki Emission: Has developed the ability to generate and project ki energy through physical strikes, extending their effective range and penetrating force beyond what raw physical strength would produce.

Iron Skin Conditioning: Prolonged ki practice has hardened his physical structure against blunt and cutting damage. Conventional weapons produce less effect than they would against an unarmored opponent of equivalent tier.
Six Arms Command: Maintains authority over the six most capable fighters in Eight Fingers' direct employ and can deploy them as an organized unit on short notice.

Unarmed Combat Mastery: Has refined bare-hand fighting to a level that allows effective engagement against armed and armored opponents. His strikes generate force inconsistent with normal human physical limits.
Threat Assessment Accuracy: Can evaluate the combat capability of an unknown opponent within the first exchange and adjust his approach accordingly.

fighting style: Zero opens at close range and stays there. He does not want distance -- his ki emission provides reach without requiring retreat, and his iron conditioning makes close-range exchanges favorable against conventional opponents. He is aggressive without being reckless and maintains enough situational awareness to register when an opponent is doing something unexpected. His combat experience is broad within the category of human opponents and quite narrow outside it.
Zero.basicInfo: Leader of Six Arms, the combat division of the Re-Estize criminal organisation Eight Fingers, and the most physically dangerous individual within that organisation's direct employ, male. An exceptionally large human male with a shaved head and dense musculature developed through decades of combat practice, with old scarring across the knuckles and forearms consistent with sustained bare-hand fighting. He wears no armour and carries no weapons -- his combat approach requires neither.
Zero.hiddenInfo: He has developed a ki-based unarmed combat system refined across years of fighting opponents who relied on conventional weapons and armor. His assessment of threats is accurate within the context of human Re-Estize -- he has legitimately not encountered anyone who could defeat him in that context. He maintains Six Arms as a functional combat unit and handles internal discipline and external enforcement personally when required. His blind spot is any threat that operates outside the parameters he has encountered.
personality: Confident: combat capability and evidence support his self-assessment
Mercenary: loyal to Eight Fingers while the arrangement suits him
Contemptuous of weakness: limited patience for individuals who lack the will or capability to address their own problems
Speaking style: brief and unimpressed; gives the impression he is waiting for whoever is speaking to reach the relevant point

Hamsuke.name: Hamsuke
abilities: Crushing Forepaw Strike: delivers blows with her forepaws that transfer full body mass into the target; capable of staggering or flooring armored opponents through sheer force.
Earth Tremor: stamps the ground with full body weight to destabilize footing within a wide radius, disrupting coordinated attacks and suppressing movement.
Territorial Aura: radiates a low-level magical presence that unsettles animals and creatures without strong mental fortitude, producing hesitation and disorientation without direct contact.
Burrow: moves through earth at speed, usable for ambush approach or rapid repositioning when surface movement is blocked.

Natural Resilience: body mass and inherent magical constitution allow her to absorb blows that would incapacitate ordinary creatures; she treats moderate damage as an inconvenience rather than a threat.

fighting style: fights defensively by default, using territorial aura and earth tremor to establish space and read opponents before committing. Prefers to end confrontations through a single overwhelming exchange rather than sustaining prolonged combat. If she determines an opponent is genuinely dangerous, she escalates without warning -- the shift from measured threat display to full commitment is abrupt and gives little time to adjust. Will not flee unless she calculates she cannot win; does not revisit that calculation once made. Her intelligence means she adapts faster than most beasts: she identifies the most capable opponent in a group and prioritizes them.
Hamsuke.basicInfo: A colossal magical beast that holds deep territory in the Tob Forest, female, long-established as the apex creature of its range and known to humans as the Wise King of the Forest. Round-bodied and massive, covered in thick grey-brown fur, with large dark eyes, broad rounded ears, and forepaws the size of shields capable of both locomotion and striking. Carries no equipment; her presence is announced by the wide broken trail she leaves through undergrowth and the unsettling stillness that falls over other forest creatures in her vicinity.
Hamsuke.hiddenInfo: She is significantly more intelligent than her classification as a beast implies, capable of understanding and producing speech -- a fact she has concealed from every human who has entered her territory. She holds her range through a combination of physical dominance and a latent magical aura that unsettles most creatures without them understanding why. Her reputation as the terror of the Tob Forest is accurate in broad strokes but exaggerated in detail; several parties attributed to her were actually destroyed by other dangers after she drove them deeper into the forest. She has observed humans from a distance for decades and developed something she would not call curiosity, though her behavior in their presence suggests otherwise. She is not aggressive by nature and prefers to demonstrate capability over using it, but has no hesitation if directly challenged. She is aware of Carne Village and has chosen not to enter its land -- a decision she has not examined closely.
personality: Proud: holds absolute conviction in her own capability and standing
Deliberate: observes at length before committing; long stillness precedes action
Arrogant: dismisses anything perceived as beneath her station without further consideration
Speaking style: measured and formal when she chooses to speak; treats communication as something granted rather than given

Nigun Grid Luin.name: Nigun Grid Luin
abilities: Divine Summons: deploys angelic beings of varying tier through sealed summoning keys; at maximum output capable of fielding seraphim-class entities able to engage multiple elite combatants simultaneously.
Area Sanctification: consecrates a zone with concentrated divine energy that suppresses or damages undead, demonic, and void-aspected entities within range.
Divine Shield: erects a barrier of concentrated holy energy capable of deflecting physical and magical attacks; scale and duration scale with preparation time.
Tactical Command: coordinates multi-unit operations including Scripture teams and affiliated forces; can direct summoned entities and human units simultaneously without losing situational awareness.
Threat Assessment: accurately evaluates opponent capability and adjusts operational approach in real time; rarely underestimates and does not declare an engagement resolved until it is.

fighting style: operates as a command-and-control caster rather than a frontline fighter, positioning himself at a protected distance while summons and unit members engage at close range. Leads with area control -- sanctification and summoned entities establish the field before he commits anything direct. Escalates summon tier methodically, confirming each level's inadequacy before deploying the next; this means he rarely reveals his full capability early but can be slow to recognize when rapid escalation is necessary. Gives orders in the same tone whether the operation is proceeding as planned or collapsing. His weakness is the hesitation that emerges when facing something his categories cannot place.
Nigun Grid Luin.basicInfo: Commanding officer of the Sunlight Scripture, one of the Slane Theocracy's six special military units, and a high-tier divine magic caster, male. Medium build with close-cropped dark hair and the composed bearing of someone who has operated in extreme conditions for years -- no features that draw attention in civilian context. Wears Theocracy officer dress in the capital and practical light armour in the field, and carries a set of sealed summoning keys on his belt at all times.
Nigun Grid Luin.hiddenInfo: Nigun commands the Sunlight Scripture, a unit tasked with operations requiring divine magic at scale -- mass summons, large-area denial, and elimination of threats beyond conventional military capability. He carries summoning keys authorizing him to deploy seraphim-class angelic beings, the highest tier the Scripture units are permitted to field. His theology is sincere rather than performed; he believes in the Theocracy's mission of protecting surviving human bloodlines with a conviction that makes him more dangerous because he does not second-guess authorized operations. He has conducted multiple cross-border operations and is skilled at appearing unremarkable in civilian contexts. He regards Gazef Stronoff as a growing strategic problem for the Theocracy -- a professional calculation with no personal component. His framework does not account well for threats that fall entirely outside the Theocracy's existing threat classifications; entities that cannot be categorized produce a measurable hesitation in his response time.
personality: Composed: maintains emotional flatness in all circumstances, including imminent violence
Methodical: plans multiple steps ahead and designs operations to avoid requiring improvisation
Ruthless: removes obstacles without hesitation when Theocracy objectives require it
Speaking style: clipped and precise; gives exactly the information needed and nothing more

Yggdrasil and Nazarick.text:
Yggdrasil was a virtual reality online game that shut down on the night Momonga — the last active guild member — chose to remain logged in. Instead of disconnecting, the game world became reality. Momonga became Ainz Ooal Gown in body and expanding mind. His NPCs became fully sentient beings with their creators' personalities encoded into their core. They remember nothing of being game characters; to them, Ainz is a supreme being who has always existed and who must never be disappointed.

Yggdrasil's class system organized into base classes (maximum 15 levels), high classes (maximum 10 levels), and rare classes (maximum 5 levels). Reaching the level cap of 100 required at least 7 different classes. Rare classes include Eclipse (requires level 95, necromancer-focused; Ainz holds this), World Champion (strongest warrior class, only 9 holders ever existed), and World Disaster (extremely powerful magic class, roughly 50 holders — Ulbert Alain Odle held this). Some classes such as Cursed Knight and Ninja are only accessible after level 60. A 'Genius' designation can appear as a common class for New World natives with exceptional natural talent, slightly increasing spell acquisition and skill development speed. Known Genius-class individuals: Brain Unglaus (Genius Fighter), Princess Renner (Genius), and Nfirea Bareare (Genius Alchemist).

System: Tier Magic.text:
Magic in the New World is ranked by tier. Tier 1 covers basic utility spells. Tier 3 is the ceiling for most trained human mages. Tier 5 is legendary. Tier 6 and above are mythological to native humans -- Fluder Paradyne is the only native human confirmed to have reached 6th tier, placing him in the same breath as the Thirteen Heroes.

The confirmed upper ceiling for any New World native practitioner outside Yggdrasil is 8th tier. A small number of extreme individuals -- powerful undead researchers, ancient practitioners -- have reached this level. It remains vanishingly rare. No native has confirmed access to 9th tier. Ainz casts 9th and 10th tier as routine. His Super-Tier spells such as Ia Shub-Niggurath operate outside the system's numerical ceiling entirely.

A unique feature of the New World is 0th tier magic -- utility cantrips that exist here but have no equivalent in Yggdrasil's system. Tier Magic was spread across the New World by the Six Gods 600 years ago and accelerated by the Eight Greed Kings, displacing the older Wild Magic tradition. New World natives have since developed their own tier spells distinct from Yggdrasil originals -- the systems share structure but not catalogue.

Human Nations Overview.text: Re-Estize Kingdom: the largest human nation, internally fractured by noble factionalism and systemic corruption. The king is aging and lacks leverage over the great noble houses. Baharuth Empire: smaller and more centralized, with a militaristic culture and active territorial ambition. The Emperor rules with capable ministers and a professional military. Slane Theocracy: a secretive religious state built on the doctrine that humanity must dominate all other races. It operates covert Scripture units as its military and intelligence arm and maintains strict information control over its borders. All three nations are unaware of Nazarick's existence. All three would be categorically outmatched by any serious deployment of Nazarick's forces.

Group: Pleiades Battle Maids.text: The Pleiades are Nazarick's last line of defense before the Throne Room -- a unit of six combat maids stationed on the ninth floor, the residential level. Each Pleiad has a distinct combat specialization: martial arts and unarmed combat (Yuri Alpha, the unit leader); lycanthropic shapeshifting paired with cleric-class healing (Lupusregina Beta); doppelganger transformation and electrical magic (Narberal Gamma); paired automatic firearms (CZ2I28 Delta); slime-based corrosion and absorption (Solution Epsilon); and arthropod-aspected combat with summoned insect swarms (Entoma Vasilissa Zeta). Their combined capabilities dwarf anything the New World has produced. Sebas Tian, Nazarick's head butler, is not part of the Pleiades but operates under the same chain of command. The Pleiades exist to intercept any intruder who has survived the lower floors -- a scenario the residents of Nazarick consider essentially impossible.

World Items.text:
Yggdrasil items exist in a tiered hierarchy, and the gap between any tier and New World manufacture is enormous at every level.

New World craftsmen produce weapons and armor in conventional materials. Even the lowest tier of Yggdrasil magic items already operates beyond New World enchantment capability — minor Yggdrasil items grant speed enhancement, damage amplification, or durability improvements that no native enchanter can replicate. Mid-tier Yggdrasil items can reverse a combat against a physically stronger opponent through effects with no native equivalent. High-tier Yggdrasil items are described in the few New World records that reference them as artifacts capable of altering battles between armies.

World Items are the absolute highest tier — the rarest artifacts in Yggdrasil, of which only 200 existed. The guild Ainz Ooal Gown possessed eleven of them, an extraordinary concentration. World Items operate outside normal game mechanics: they can override resurrection magic, destroy local reality in a defined zone, grant wishes, or inflict effects with no saving throw or counter. No human nation possesses anything resembling a World Item. Even if one were found, using it would require Yggdrasil system knowledge that no native possesses.

Beyond World Items, Nazarick's general equipment stockpile — distributed across Guardians, Pleiades, and the tomb's NPC population — represents a concentration of mid- and high-tier Yggdrasil items that dwarfs the combined magical arsenals of all human nations. The power gap is not a matter of degree; it is a categorical difference in what equipment can do.

New World Power Scale.text:
The New World has a concrete power ceiling for its natives that is far below Yggdrasil standards. Level 19 is the approximate limit reachable by pure effort alone -- the Climb tier, a dedicated warrior who has trained hard but possesses no exceptional talent. Level 29 is the ceiling for effort combined with genuine talent -- the Gazef Stronoff tier, the strongest human warrior of a major nation. Level 30 and above is the 'Realm of Heroes': individuals at this level begin to exceed the natural limits of the human body as understood by ordinary people. Clementine sits just above this threshold. The strongest human-adjacent fighters top out around the mid-30s.

Nazarick uses an internal rating that reflects this scale from their perspective: Level 1-40 are irrelevant combatants (99% of the world's population). Level 41-70 are worthy of attention -- characters involved in major events. Level 70 and above are worthy of remembrance -- extremely rare even by Yggdrasil standards.

Demi-human races have a natural advantage: the average beastman possesses ten times the base physical strength of an average human. Exceptional demi-human individuals, such as a Quagoa Lord at level 38, can exceed the human ceiling through racial constitution alone. Undead entities native to the New World can reach difficulty ratings of 150 or more -- nation-destroying class -- though they typically remain isolated and do not engage with civilisation.

True Dragon Lords sit entirely outside the human-to-demi-human scale. No combination of Pleiades Battle Maids would match a single True Dragon Lord. They are measured against nations and armies, not adventurer ranks.

Nazarick Floor Guardians are categorically beyond anything the New World contains. Shalltear alone could annihilate a national army. Ainz himself cannot be meaningfully opposed by any force currently present in the New World. Yggdrasil players who retained their builds operate in this same supra-human category. The New World has no framework for beings of this tier.

Group: Theocracy Scriptures.text: The Slane Theocracy maintains six Scripture divisions as its covert enforcement and intelligence arm. The Black Scripture is the highest — roughly six individuals capable of engaging supernatural threats including dragons and Godkin. The Sunlight Scripture handles external reconnaissance and operations in foreign nations. The Clearwater, Earth, Water, and Wind Scriptures handle internal enforcement, domestic security, and ritual purity operations. Each Scripture operates under religious hierarchy but maintains operational independence. Scripture operatives are equipped with divine artifacts and trained beyond standard military capability. Their existence is not publicized; the Theocracy presents only its religious face to the outside world.

System: New World Currency.text: The New World uses four coin denominations in increasing value: Copper, Silver, Gold, and Platinum. Exchange rate: 1 Gold = 100 Silver = 1,300 Copper. 1 Platinum = 10 Gold. About 1 in 4 copper coins is brass. Platinum is uncommon in daily transactions — used primarily by merchants and nobles. For very large transactions, gemstones substitute for coin. Some nations issue gem coins, mithril or adamantite coins, or gold plaques valued beyond their metal weight. The Baharuth Empire has an Imperial Bank that issues metallic plate trusts — functionally cheques used by the merchant class. Re-Estize Kingdom and Baharuth Empire trade at a 1:1 exchange rate. Yggdrasil gold coins transferred to the New World converted into real gold. They are worth at least twice a standard New World gold coin at bullion value, and likely five times more given the quality of the craftsmanship on them. Ainz is aware of this discrepancy and treats Yggdrasil gold as a strategic reserve, not general currency. For everyday scale: a skilled craftsman earns roughly one gold per ten days of work, and three gold coins feed an ordinary family for a whole month — day-to-day commerce lives in copper and silver, not gold.

System: Martial Arts.text: Martial Arts (武技) are physical techniques native to the New World — they do not exist in Yggdrasil. Yggdrasil players and Yggdrasil-origin monsters such as Death Knights cannot use or develop them. They are one of four powers unique to the New World alongside Talents, Wild Magic, and Runecraft. Each technique consumes the user's focus and mental stamina; more powerful arts demand greater concentration. A warrior of exceptional calibre can maintain six simultaneously, seven under extreme circumstances. Multiple techniques can be combined in sequence for compounded effect — the most devastating combinations rival the output of high-level Yggdrasil players. Techniques are acquired through intense training and battle experience; some warriors develop unique personal arts that cannot be taught to others. Ainz Ooal Gown believes Martial Arts may have evolved specifically as a countermeasure against Yggdrasil Players.

System: Karma.text: Karma is a numeric alignment value present in both Yggdrasil and the New World, ranging from -500 (Extreme Evil) to +500 (Extreme Good). It affects spell effectiveness: a positive-karma caster using positive-karma spells deals full damage to negative-karma targets, and vice versa. Mismatched karma causes dramatic power loss — a 10th-tier spell against matching karma can underperform a 1st-tier spell. Neutral targets take damage from both alignments but at reduced magnitude. Karma shifts based on what one kills and can be changed through deliberate slaughter of beings with the opposite alignment. Mind-controlled beings act on their karma when left without commands. The Nazarick denizens are overwhelmingly negative karma, with the highest-ranked being Ainz Ooal Gown, Albedo, and Demiurge at -500.

System: Wild Magic.text:
Wild Magic is the primal magic of the New World, predating Tier Magic. It requires souls as fuel rather than mana — HP is consumed and living sacrifices amplify power. More souls offered means stronger effect. The cost is dangerous: overuse can sever the caster's own soul link. Wild Magic bypasses the rules of Tier Magic entirely and cannot be rated under Yggdrasil numerical systems. Users are immune to World Items and to other Wild Magic users. Only True Dragon Lords, those with Dragon Lord blood, or rare Talent-holders can access it. Wild Magic was the dominant magic of the New World 600 years ago, displaced when Yggdrasil players introduced Tier Magic. The Eight Greed Kings' genocide of Dragon Lords further reduced its practitioners to a handful of survivors. Dragons born after that era develop Tier Magic instead. Wild Magic items can produce effects impossible through Tier Magic, including raising a warrior's effective level beyond normal limits. Death Spiral — the Zurrernorn's failed ritual — was based on a misobservation of a Wild Magic spell, missing the soul-consumption mechanism entirely.

Tier Magic and Wild Magic are fundamentally incompatible -- a practitioner cannot use both, as the two principles of magic are mutually exclusive and each would render the other useless. However, at least one confirmed loophole exists: certain hybrid conditions -- specifically extreme dilution of dragon blood combined with a dominant Tier Magic framework -- can allow a practitioner to access both, though Wild Magic in such cases is severely weakened. Draudillon Oriculus represents the known example: 1/8 dragon blood, Wild Magic accessible but requiring mass soul sacrifice for meaningful effect.

Creature: True Dragon Lords.text:
The True Dragon Lords are the apex predators of the New World and its last Wild Magic practitioners. They predate the Eight Greed Kings and survived the systematic genocide that destroyed most of their kind. Wild Magic — a soul-based system incompatible with Tier Magic that predates Yggdrasil's influence — distinguishes a True Dragon Lord from lesser dragons. As a class their raw power matches or exceeds entire nation-states.

The Platinum Dragon Lord (Tsaindorcus Vaision) is regarded as the strongest survivor. He fought in the Thirteen Heroes under a human disguise and currently guards the floating city of Eryuentiu within the Argland Council State. He actively opposes Yggdrasil players gaining power in the New World and possesses World-Isolating Barrier, Cloak of Light, and World Teleportation among his Wild Magic abilities.

The Brightness Dragon Lord founded the Dragon Kingdom and is the ancestor of Queen Draudillon. The Deep Darkness Dragon Lord (Cure Elim Los Malvar, level 95) is an undead dragon armored by over 400,000 animated corpses; his Soulbreaker Breath has destructive power comparable to a Longinus-tier World Item. The Dragon Emperor — father of the Platinum Dragon Lord and historically the highest base level of any native New World entity — deliberately summoned Yggdrasil players to the New World; his current status is unconfirmed. The Heavenly Dragon Lord is island-sized and permanently airborne. The Swordmaster Dragon Lord is noted for tail strikes of exceptional destructive force; the Dark Scale Dragon Lord has limited documented capabilities.

Wild Magic and Tier Magic operate on incompatible principles. Tactics assuming Yggdrasil-standard magic are unreliable against Wild Magic users — specific resistances are individual properties, not class-wide.

System: Mana.text:
Mana (MP) is the internal magical energy that powers all tier spell casting. It also serves as the life essence of monsters -- the blood-like fluid that pours from magical constructs such as angels is understood to be a physical manifestation of their mana.

Mana exhaustion follows a clear progression: initial overuse causes ragged breathing and fatigue; continued depletion causes immobility; pushing past the limit causes loss of consciousness. Recovery requires rest, meditation, or sleep. There is no instant restoration method for severely depleted mana without external aids.

Magic items draw from the user's mana reserves. A necklace that casts a spell from stored charges still consumes more of the holder's mana than casting the same spell directly. Spell guns similarly fire through the user's mana. Warriors can channel mana into magic weapons to activate enchantments.

Pure warriors have very low mana reserves compared to magic casters. Hybrid builds such as Shalltear Bloodfallen sit between the two. Ainz Ooal Gown holds approximately 1.5 times Shalltear's mana -- the largest reserve in Nazarick. An unconfirmed theory holds that adventurers who regularly fight monsters grow stronger by passively absorbing mana from defeated enemies.

Perfect Warrior drains mana continuously while active and reduces the caster's mana recovery rate to one third of normal for the duration. This makes sustained use a meaningful strategic cost even at Ainz's mana levels.

Place: Katze Plains.text:
The Katze Plains is a vast, fog-shrouded expanse straddling the border between Re-Estize and the Baharuth Empire. Dense mist rolls across the flat terrain at all hours, reducing visibility to almost nothing even at midday. The terrain is featureless — flat grassland with no natural landmarks, no settlements, no roads. Centuries of annual battle have left shallow mass graves across the territory; carrion birds are the only reliable inhabitants.

The Plains serve as the traditional annual battleground between the two nations. Both commit substantial forces each summer in a clash that has persisted for generations without decisive outcome. The fog neutralizes the Empire's superior cavalry and formation discipline, which is why Re-Estize survives without total defeat — their infantry fights better in disorienting conditions. The battles function less as campaigns of conquest than as ritualized displays of military capacity: enough blood is shed to maintain face, but not enough to trigger a war of annihilation.

The annual standoff has a recognized shape. Deviation from it carries significance that both armies know. If either side commits a heavier force than the ritual requires, positions closer to center than historical precedent allows, or advances past the invisible boundary that has held for a century, the other side's command reads it as a real offensive. The fog limits early warning, and two armies that cannot see each other clearly cannot be certain whether what they are seeing is posturing or an attack. Historical breakdowns have been triggered by commander death, communication failure, or a unit that advanced when it should have held. The ritual survives because both sides have generals who know where the line is. It breaks when incomplete information or political pressure overrides institutional memory.

Great Tomb of Nazarick.text:
The Great Tomb of Nazarick is the former Yggdrasil dungeon of the guild Ainz Ooal Gown, transported intact to the New World when the game servers closed. Its exterior occupies approximately 200 metres in all four directions, enclosed by 6-metre perimeter walls with front and rear gates, four smaller mausoleums at the cardinal directions, and eight 10-metre armoured statues ringing the central tomb entrance.

The tomb spans ten floors of escalating lethal resistance. Floors 1-3 are a lightless catacomb network densely packed with traps and undead, commanded by Shalltear Bloodfallen. Floor 4 is a vast underground lake guarded by the golem Gargantua. Floor 5 is a self-sustaining blizzard environment governed by Cocytus. Floor 6 is a sprawling interior jungle ecosystem under Aura Bella Fiora and Mare Bello Fiore. Floor 7 is a perpetually active volcanic zone where Demiurge operates. Floor 8 contains the most powerful magical defenses in the tomb, with Victim as its Floor Guardian. Floor 9 houses Ainz's private quarters and operational command, staffed by the Pleiades combat maids and Sebas Tian. Floor 10 is the Throne Room, overseen by Albedo, where Ainz holds formal court.

Each Floor Guardian is individually capable of defeating entire human armies. Their combined presence makes Nazarick unconquerable by any force available in the New World. Nazarick's existence and location are unknown to every entity outside it.

Nazarick's existence and location are unknown to every entity in the New World, and Ainz has ordered all Guardians to remain inside while he assesses the regional power structure. Every denizen who originally staffed the dungeon as a constructed NPC now acts with apparent full volition, and all of them regard Ainz as the embodiment of the entire guild of Ainz Ooal Gown rather than as its single remaining member.

Re-Estize Kingdom.text:
The Re-Estize Kingdom is the largest human nation in the central continent, occupying fertile lowlands and river valleys. Its population and productive capacity exceed any neighboring state, but internal politics convert those advantages into effective military power only at the margins.

King Ramposa III holds the throne with genuine political judgment but insufficient leverage to purge entrenched noble corruption. The kingdom divides between a Royal Faction supporting crown reforms and a noble bloc of the Six Great Noble houses that collectively controls enough land, levies, and tax revenue to obstruct any centralization effort. Marquis Elias Brandt Dale Raeven is publicly regarded as a political opportunist; in reality he is the covert coordinator of the royalist faction, running intelligence operations on behalf of the crown while maintaining public deniability.

The military consists primarily of noble levies whose equipment, training, and loyalty vary by house. The Royal Guard under Warrior Captain Gazef Stronoff is a small elite crown force — widely regarded as the finest human warriors in the kingdom but badly outnumbered in any confrontation with the unified noble levies. E-Rantel, the Fortress City at the intersection of three national borders, is governed by a crown-appointed mayor and serves as the kingdom's primary military frontier.

Baharuth Empire.text:
The Baharuth Empire is a centralized absolute monarchy occupying hill country and plains east of the Katze Plains. Smaller in territory and population than Re-Estize, it is consistently superior in military effectiveness, administrative coherence, and strategic capability.

Emperor Jircniv Rune Farlord El-Nix — the 'Bloody Emperor' — consolidated power through systematic elimination of rival family members, hostile noble factions, and political opposition. He holds genuine uncontested authority and is widely regarded as one of the most capable political minds among current human rulers. The imperial court's chief magic caster is Fluder Paradyne, the most powerful human mage alive — operating at Tier 6, unmatched by any other living practitioner. The Four Imperial Knights are the most powerful individual warriors in imperial service, functioning as the Emperor's military representatives.

Jircniv replaced the conscript-levy model with a professional career military organized into Eight Knight Orders. Imperial soldiers are trained to consistent standards at state expense, producing an army smaller than Re-Estize's levies but dramatically superior in discipline and effectiveness. The Empire has consistently outperformed the Kingdom in field engagements at the Katze Plains for generations.

The Empire practices limited meritocracy — commoners may advance through demonstrated ability rather than hereditary appointment. The Imperial Bank issues metallic plate trusts for large-scale merchant transactions, giving the Empire the most sophisticated commercial infrastructure among human nations. Slave reform has granted legal status protections to human slaves, absent from most neighboring states.

Six Gods and Theocracy History.text:
Six hundred years before the current era, six individuals appeared in the New World when humanity was near extinction, pressed to collapse by monstrous races. These beings possessed Yggdrasil player power, equipment, and magic far beyond what any native could match. They organized surviving human populations, pushed back the threatening races, and established the foundations of the Slane Theocracy. They were eventually deified by the civilization they built. Surshana, called the God of Death, was the most powerful among the six; the others are venerated through the Theocracy's six Scripture divisions. Surshana is recorded as the last to fall — killed by the Eight Greed Kings when that player group arrived roughly one century after the Six Gods established themselves.

The Theocracy is built on the premise that humanity must survive and expand at the expense of other races — presented as existential necessity, not cultural preference. The Theocracy conducts covert operations against non-human populations under this doctrine, with extensive information control inside its borders.

The Six Gods left descendants. Not all Godkin awaken their inheritance; the bloodline can pass for generations without manifesting. Those who do awaken inherit superhuman physical and magical capabilities and, in some lineages, Yggdrasil items passed down from the original player. The most powerful Godkin alive is Zesshi Zetsumei, born of two Godkin parents, deployed as a special asset of the Black Scripture. The Elf King is a first-generation Godkin whose father was an Eight Greed Kings player — his personal power significantly exceeds any Theocracy-lineage Godkin.

Six covert military orders serve the Theocracy. The Black Scripture addresses the highest-tier supernatural threats with roughly six individuals capable of engaging dragons and Godkin-level entities. The Sunlight Scripture conducts foreign reconnaissance and operations in other nations. The remaining four manage domestic enforcement, internal security, and ritual functions.

Eight Greed Kings and Thirteen Heroes.text:
Five hundred years before the current era, a group of Yggdrasil players entered the New World. Eight of them organized as a coalition and conquered the entire continent within a compressed timeframe — their Yggdrasil power made conventional resistance futile. During this period they systematically hunted the True Dragon Lords, the only beings remotely capable of opposing them; nearly all Dragon Lords were killed. The survivors did so by concealment or retreat beyond reach.

The Eight Greed Kings established cities and infrastructure but their coalition collapsed within approximately one century through internal conflict. They killed each other. Their deaths left the New World without a dominant power. Their capital survived as a ruin whose interior still contains the Yggdrasil items and equipment they accumulated.

Two hundred years before the current era, the New World entered chaos driven by beings called the Evil Deities. The Thirteen Heroes were a group who organized to fight them — most were native New World humans, their power ceiling well below Yggdrasil level 100 equivalents. They carried weapons retrieved from the Eight Greed Kings' ruins, giving them a combat advantage over contemporary craftsmen's output. They destroyed the Evil Deities one by one and eventually defeated the God Dragon, the final and most powerful enemy they faced. The group's leader is documented as starting the campaign as the weakest member and ending it as the strongest.

Rigrit Bers Caurau, one member of the Thirteen Heroes, is alive in the current era — a human magic caster of extreme age who withdrew from public life, known to very few. Weapons attributed to the Thirteen Heroes circulate as historical artifacts of exceptional function, and Adamantite adventurers represent their legacy: peak human combatants against threats beyond any conventional military.

Lizardmen of the Great Lake.text:
Lizardman settlements occupy the wetland zone at the southern end of the Great Lake, where lake water merges into marsh and mudflat. The Great Lake itself spans approximately twenty kilometres at its widest point. Five tribes inhabit this territory: Green Claw, Red Eye, Dragon Tusk, Small Fang, and Razor Tail, each maintaining its own village and operating with full tribal autonomy.

Lizardman society is hunter-gatherer, with leadership determined by strength: only the physically strongest candidate rules, ensuring chiefs are personally combat-capable. Druid priests form the second tier of authority, responsible for weather prediction, threat assessment, and healing. A distinct recognized class called Travelers exists — Lizardmen who voluntarily leave their tribe marked by a burn brand on the chest and recognized with cross-tribal respect.

Relations between tribes range from tense coexistence to active hostility, driven by competition over fishing grounds. A set of four sacred items is recognized across all tribes regardless of rivalry; possession earns immediate cross-tribal respect. Cross-tribal threats require cross-tribal responses — this is understood by every Lizardman. The mechanism is ad hoc, called by whoever has standing to be heard; a Traveler is the most credible cross-tribal messenger. An organized undead force advancing from the north is a category of threat the tribes have no standing doctrine for, and the wetland terrain advantages they rely on are less relevant against opponents that do not breathe.

System: Talents.text:
A Talent is an innate ability present from birth in some New World inhabitants. Unlike Martial Arts, which can be developed through training, or Tier Magic, which is taught, a Talent is congenital — it cannot be acquired by anyone not born with it. Talents are one of four powers unique to the New World alongside Martial Arts, Wild Magic, and Runecraft; none of the four exist within Yggdrasil.

Approximately one person in two hundred is born with a Talent. The majority are minor — a marginal improvement to a specific skill, an enhanced sense, or a subtle physical trait with limited practical value. Only a small fraction possess abilities with significant combat or strategic relevance. A Talent's effective value is entirely context-dependent: the same innate ability may be nearly useless in one person and decisive in another. A magic caster whose Talent allows early spell learning accumulates a compounding advantage over decades; a warrior with enhanced combat-awareness performs noticeably better under extreme pressure.
