Notable examples at the high end of Talent usefulness: Nfirea Bareare can activate any magic item regardless of class restrictions — normally impossible. Arche Eeb Rye Ende can perceive mana levels visually, reading a target's magical capacity at a glance. Gazef Stronoff possesses a combat-oriented Talent augmenting threat awareness in battle. Yggdrasil players encountering the Talent system — particularly abilities affecting magic item use or mana perception — are observing a system entirely outside their prior experience.

System: Adventurer Guild.text:
The Adventurer's Guild is a neutral transnational organization operating under a consistent charter across all branches. It accepts commissions from any legitimate source, does not align with political factions, and expels members who act as political agents. Registration costs 5 silver coins. All new registrants start at Copper rank regardless of ability — there is no fast-track or rank bypass.

Eight ranks in ascending order: Copper, Iron, Silver, Gold, Platinum, Orichalcum, Mithril, Adamantite. Rank advances through accumulated commission results over time, not through a single test or bout. Copper adventurers handle vermin and basic scouting. Iron handles organized small monster bands. Silver handles minor dungeon work. Gold handles powerful monsters and small regional threats. Platinum handles mature dragons and powerful undead commanders. Orichalcum handles major regional incidents. Mithril handles existential regional threats. Adamantite handles threats that armies cannot reliably defeat — Blue Rose is the only Adamantite team active in the Re-Estize region.

The rank necklace is immediately readable: Copper adventurers are dismissed; Iron treated as working professionals; Silver respected; Gold deferred to; Platinum commanding; Orichalcum elite; Mithril regionally famous; Adamantite treated with near-deference even by powerful individuals. The Guild was secretly founded by the Slane Theocracy and serves as a passive intelligence network — a fact unknown to almost all participants including senior guild leadership.

Group: Blue Rose Adventurer Team.text:
Blue Rose is the Adamantite-ranked adventurer team operating in and around the Re-Estize Kingdom — the most powerful formally recognized team in the region. The team operates with a female-only membership policy.

Lakyus Alvein Dale Aindra leads the team, a noble-born paladin-type who wields the dark sword Kilineyram, an artifact carrying a dangerous spiritual influence she actively suppresses. Gagaran is a heavily built warrior who uses a war pick and relies on raw physical power applied with precision. Evileye is a masked magic caster whose true identity is concealed; she casts at a level far above what her apparent age would suggest. Tia and Tina are twins and former members of an assassination organization; their combat style blends acrobatic close-quarters fighting with paralyzing and lethal techniques.

Blue Rose accepts formal commissions but operates semi-independently, pursuing threats they consider significant without waiting for formal requests when the situation warrants. Their Adamantite status grants substantial political leverage with the Kingdom's administration. Each member individually can engage threats that would destroy a company of ordinary soldiers; as a coordinated team they represent the practical upper limit of what human adventurers can accomplish in the Re-Estize sphere — while remaining categorically outmatched by any Floor Guardian of Nazarick.

Group: Swords of Darkness.text:
The Swords of Darkness are a Mithril-ranked adventurer team based in E-Rantel, considered strong for their rank and assigned difficult commissions that lower-ranked teams cannot handle.

Peter Mauk leads the team — a fighter-type warrior handling strategic decisions. Lukrut Volve is a ranger providing scouting and ranged support. Dyne Woodwonder is a druid whose nature magic covers healing, environmental awareness, and terrain utility. Ninya is the team's magic caster working toward Tier 3 capability, carrying a personal motivation connected to a missing elder sister that he does not discuss with outsiders.

The team uses E-Rantel as their primary base, taking commissions in the surrounding region — borderlands, roads toward outlying villages, and accessible dungeon networks. At Mithril rank they can handle organized goblin armies, minor undead commanders, and dungeon clearances that would overwhelm Bronze and Silver teams. They would not survive direct engagement with a Gold-level individual monster.

Eight Fingers.text:
Eight Fingers is the dominant criminal organization within the Re-Estize Kingdom, named for its eight departments: slave trafficking, assassinations, smuggling, larceny, the drug trade (primarily Black Dust), security, banking, and gambling. Each division operates with significant autonomy under a divisional leader. Drug operations are their most profitable current activity.

Several noble houses have financial ties to Eight Fingers — as clients or silent investors. This penetration makes the organization difficult to dismantle through official channels: any investigation risks exposing nobles who can obstruct the process itself. Eight Fingers maintains a significant network within E-Rantel, using the city's position as a trade hub for smuggling and its large transient population as cover for assassins and intelligence operatives.

The organization employs fighters capable of operating at Silver to Gold adventurer rank. Their assassination division includes members with genuine combat competence. They are not equipped to fight openly against military forces but excel at covert operations, bribery, and targeted elimination.

Group: Zuranon.text:
Zuranon is a fanatical death cult operating covertly within the Re-Estize Kingdom and surrounding territories. Their objective is mass production of undead as a path to personal transcendence — specifically, achieving lich or comparable undead form through ritual means.

Members believe undeath represents the ultimate form of existence: freedom from biological limitation, access to death magic, and potential immortality. Junior members collect corpses and prepare ritual sites; senior members have already begun undead modification of their own bodies. Zuranon embeds operatives in legitimate-seeming roles — scholars, merchants, minor priests. They collect corpses from battlefields and graveyards, and when necessary, from living victims. E-Rantel's proximity to the historically blood-soaked Katze Plains makes it a particularly valuable operational base for corpse sourcing.

Khajiit Dale Badantel is one of the most capable senior members active in the E-Rantel area — a high-competence magic caster who has made significant personal progress toward undead transformation, operating behind multiple layers of cover within the city. Zuranon operates independently of Eight Fingers; their goals are ideological rather than commercial, making them harder to negotiate with and more dangerous when exposed.

New World Non-Human Races.text:
The New World has numerous non-human sapient races distributed across its territory. Human nations occupy the central regions; the periphery and wilderness are home to diverse demi-human and heteromorphic populations.

Goblins are among the most numerous non-human races — organized in strength-dominant tribes, present in forests, caves, ruins, and grasslands throughout the continent, generating threats at the Copper through Bronze adventurer tiers. Ogres are large, powerful humanoids used as mercenaries and shock troops, representing a Bronze-to-Silver rank threat per individual. Trolls are aggressive territorial regenerating predators, individually around Gold tier; fire and acid are required to prevent regeneration from making them effectively unkillable. Quagoa are powerful cave-dwelling humanoids with exceptional physical strength who have been systematically seizing Dwarven underground territory for generations.

Beastmen form a tribal confederation in the southern regions conducting organized military campaigns against the Dragon Kingdom. Lizardmen inhabit five hunter-gatherer tribes at the Great Lake wetlands, culturally distinct from other demi-human races. Dark Elves are forest-dwelling elves, naturally talented in archery and stealth, some operating as adventurers in human cities. Dwarves are mountain craftsmen and runesmiths in the Azerlisia Mountains, currently under Quagoa pressure. High Elves are primarily located within Elf Country territory under the Elf King's dominion.

Creature: Goblins.text:
Goblins are one of the most widespread non-human races in the New World, appearing in nearly every biome and generating persistent threats to human settlements at the lower adventurer tiers.

Goblin society is organized around a chief who holds power through physical dominance — when a stronger goblin defeats the chief, leadership transfers immediately. This creates unstable power structures that fragment easily under pressure but coalesce quickly under a capable leader. Larger, stable communities develop specialized roles: Goblin Generals (tactical commanders), Goblin Champions (elite warriors at Iron-to-Bronze adventurer level), and Goblin Shamans (basic fire and nature magic).

Threat scale varies significantly by force size. A lone goblin is manageable by a trained adult. A raiding party of ten to thirty is Iron-rank. A tribal force of two hundred with a General is a Bronze-to-Silver problem that can devastate unprepared villages. Armies above five hundred under a strong General represent a regional military incident requiring coordinated response.

Most contact with human settlements is hostile raiding. Some tribes establish mercenary relationships with demi-human warlords; non-aggression arrangements with human communities exist but depend entirely on the chief who made the agreement. Goblins reproduce faster than most humanoid races — a community depleted by adventurer clearance recovers within a generation if the habitat remains available.

Creature: Undead Hierarchy.text:
The New World's undead population ranges from mindless animated corpses to intelligent beings of extreme power, understood through Adventurer Guild threat classification and clerical records.

At the lowest tier, Skeletons and Zombies are animated by residual negative energy from battlefields and mass graves — manageable by trained adults. Ghouls are slightly more dangerous, semi-intelligent hunters whose claws carry a paralyzing effect. Wights retain fragments of their living identity and can drain life energy through touch. Death Knights stand significantly above Wights: they retain martial capability, can wield weapons and wear armor, and require Adamantite-adjacent capability to handle safely. Immunity to most status effects and many spells makes conventional tactics unreliable against them.

True Vampires are intelligent, powerful, and independently strategic, capable of creating Vampire Spawn from victims. New World True Vampires are rare and typically occupy hidden territories to avoid destruction by Theocracy Scripture units and Adamantite adventurers. Liches are spellcasters who have undergone voluntary undead transformation, retaining full magical capability and gaining significant physical damage resistance — vanishingly rare, requiring profound necromantic knowledge or specific ritual conditions to create.

The New World generates undead spontaneously through accumulated death energy at battlegrounds and sites of violent tragedy. The Katze Plains, used as a battleground for centuries, maintains a persistent undead presence without any necromantic intervention.

Ainz Ooal Gown Guild.text:
Ainz Ooal Gown was one of the most powerful guilds in Yggdrasil, founded on solidarity among heteromorphic players who faced systematic harassment from human-race PK groups. The guild reached 41 members at its peak — most were working adults with limited time, and guild culture was unusually supportive: members pooled resources, shared crafting expertise, and covered for each other during real-world obligations.

The guild captured a six-floor dungeon and transformed it into the Great Tomb of Nazarick, expanding to ten floors in response to sustained attacks from rival coalitions. Each NPC was personally designed by a specific guild member: Shalltear by Peroroncino; Albedo by Tabula Smaragdina (with a personality modification by Momonga); Demiurge by Ulbert Alain Odle; Cocytus by Warrior Takemikazuchi; Aura and Mare by BukubukuChagama; Sebas Tian by Touch Me; the Pleiades by Nishikienrai.

As real-world obligations increased and the game aged, members stopped logging in. Momonga — known outside the game as Suzuki Satoru, a salaryman — was the last active member. He remained on the servers' final night as an act of remembrance for the community that had mattered to him. When the servers closed, he did not disconnect. At peak, the guild possessed eleven World Items — an extraordinary concentration representing both their power and the deep trust among members.

Institution: Baharuth Imperial Military.text:
The Baharuth Empire's military is organized around professional career service rather than feudal conscription, producing a smaller but substantially more capable force than Re-Estize's levy army.

The core consists of eight specialized Knight Orders divided by combat role — heavy cavalry, light cavalry, heavy infantry, archers, siege specialists, and supplementary branches. Each Order maintains its own officer corps, training regimen, and equipment standard funded by the imperial treasury. Above the Knight Orders, the Four Imperial Knights are the most powerful individual warriors in imperial service — the Emperor's military representatives in high-stakes diplomatic and combat situations, each individually outperforming any Knight Order officer.

The Imperial Magic Caster Corps is organized as a military division led by Fluder Paradyne, covering both field assignments and a standing research program. Their existence gives the Empire an organized military magic capability that Re-Estize has no equivalent for. The annual deployment to the Katze Plains functions as both a training exercise and a political signal. Permanent frontier garrisons along all borders provide early warning and response capability without requiring full army mobilization.

New World Geography.text:
The central continent of the New World contains several major geographic zones that shape political and military dynamics.

The Azerlisia Mountains run north to south along the eastern edge of the central regions — home to the Dwarven Kingdom in its cavern networks, Frost Dragons along its peaks, and Quagoa in its cave systems, functioning as a natural eastern boundary for Re-Estize territory. The Great Forest of Tob is a vast forest in the central-southern region containing unicorns, large predatory creatures, and various monster populations; its interior remains largely unexplored and serves as a buffer between the human heartlands and the Great Lake territory.

The Great Lake, approximately twenty kilometres at its widest, lies in the south with the five Lizardman tribes in its surrounding wetlands. The Katze Plains is the fog-covered contested zone on the border between Re-Estize and the Baharuth Empire — see its dedicated entry. The Abelion Hills in the south are home to numerous demi-human tribes including Beastmen confederation territory, effectively ungoverned by any human state.

The continent has coastal access to the south and west, with maritime trade limited by monster threats at sea. The northern frontier is less settled territory populated by various monster species; the Troll Kingdom occupies northeastern wilderness, and Frost Dragon range extends into the northern mountain peaks.

Argland Council State.text:
The Argland Council State is a demi-human nation in the western part of the central continent, a mixed-race country where human and demi-human peoples live together, and one of the two great powers of the region. It is led by a council composed of representatives of each race inhabiting it, and among that council sit five Dragon Lords known as the Five Dragon Councilors, whose wisdom guides the nation and whose individual power places it beyond the reach of any conventional army.

The Council Dragons are not True Dragon Lords in the Wild Magic sense. They are extraordinarily powerful beings who chose governance over isolation, and their presence alone makes the Council State effectively unconquerable by military means. The state was founded two centuries ago by the Platinum Dragon Lord, Tsaindorcus Vaision, in the aftermath of the war against the Evil Deities, as one of his long experiments in how communities might be built; he is a True Dragon Lord and a practitioner of Wild Magic, and he continues to watch the New World on his own account rather than through the council he established.

Argland pursues no territorial expansion and maintains studied neutrality from a position of absolute deterrence, dealing with its neighbours through trade and carefully managed diplomatic contact. Human nations treat it with extreme caution: any provocation against it would be existentially suicidal, and it is one of the few powers on the continent that even a major coalition could not defeat.

Dragon Kingdom.text:
The Dragon Kingdom is a small human nation east of the central continent under sustained and intensifying Beastman assault. Queen Draudillon Oriculus, great-granddaughter of the Brightness Dragon Lord, rules the kingdom and has access to inherited Wild Magic — the soul-fuelled native magic system distinct from Tier Magic. Her bloodline (one-eighth dragon blood) makes her Wild Magic real but constrained: the soul cost for high-tier spells is extreme enough that she cannot use her most powerful abilities without mass civilian death, a cost she refuses to pay. She has the heritage and the magic, but not the uncompromised dragon nature that would make either decisive.

Beastmen forces have organized into an army-scale coalition and advanced deep into Dragon Kingdom territory. The kingdom lacks the military depth to expel the invasion through conventional means and has sought external assistance from surrounding nations with little success — neighboring states consider the conflict too distant from their own borders to justify commitment.

Politically, Draudillon is astute and maintains two public forms: a young, child-like appearance she uses in most diplomatic settings to disarm visitors, and an adult form she shifts to when exercising direct authority. If the Dragon Kingdom falls, the Beastmen confederation gains a significant territorial and population base that could shift the regional balance further south and west — a consequence the surrounding nations have failed to adequately account for.

Roble Holy Kingdom.text:
The Roble Holy Kingdom is a human nation divided into Northern and Southern administrative zones by a Great Wall built to contain demi-human incursions from the southern wilderness. The Northern zone operates under Holy Queen Calca Bessarez, a figure of genuine moral authority who commands significant popular loyalty through the kingdom's religious doctrine.

The Great Wall is a major fortification staffed by the kingdom's military, built from historical experience with organized demi-human assault — it represents the Kingdom's primary strategic investment and its defining geographic feature. The military is organized around Paladin Orders whose warrior-devotion officer corps forms the primary Wall defense. Remedios Custodio commands the Order and is genuinely excellent at personal combat and immediate tactical response, though her strategic judgment has blind spots for threats she cannot personally charge at. Neia Baraja is a young paladin-in-training with exceptional eyesight representing a newer generation of this tradition.

The Holy Kingdom is geographically isolated from the three major central-continent powers and must manage its demi-human border threat largely without external support. Its strategic challenge is a permanent containment problem rather than a solvable one — the demi-human population in the Abelion Hills is a persistent pressure requiring continuous military commitment.

Elf Country and the Elf King.text:
The Elf Country is the territory dominated by the Elf King (Decem Hougan), a being of exceptional power whose longevity and capabilities place him in a category distinct from ordinary political rulers. The Elf King is a first-generation Godkin — his father was a player from the Eight Greed Kings who entered the New World five hundred years ago. This lineage gives him access to Yggdrasil-derived power that no Theocracy-lineage Godkin can match.

The Elf Country exists in sustained tension with surrounding powers. The Slane Theocracy views the Elf King as a threat and an anomaly — a Godkin whose bloodline comes from the Eight Greed Kings rather than their own Six Gods. The Argland Council State borders Elf Country territory and maintains uneasy awareness of his activities.

The Elf King has maintained dominion over the elf population within his territory for generations through extreme longevity and apparent indifference to normal political relationships with neighboring states. High elves are predominantly located within Elf Country territory; their relationship to the Elf King and their conditions within the country are matters of significant uncertainty to outsiders. Dark Elves, who inhabit forests outside Elf Country, operate more independently and some have integrated into broader New World adventurer culture.

New World Healing and Medicine.text:
The gap between what tier magic healing can accomplish and what ordinary people can access defines daily life for the vast majority of New World inhabitants.

Tier magic healing — Minor Heal through Greater Heal — can close wounds, cure poison, and at high enough tiers restore limbs or reverse blindness. Priests and clerics at temples provide magical healing in exchange for payment. Availability varies enormously by location: major cities like E-Rantel have multiple temple-based healers; frontier villages may have access only to a single low-tier druid or none at all.

Healing potions provide a middle tier between magical healing and mundane medicine. They are expensive for common people — a standard Health Potion represents significant expenditure for a laborer. Quality varies by producer; Lizzie Bareare and Nfirea Bareare produce consistently reliable potions in E-Rantel. The blue potions adventurers consider high quality are treated as baseline by Yggdrasil standards.

Beyond potions, most New World healing is wound care, herbal treatment, and pain management. New World herbal medicine cannot cure serious systemic disease, reverse significant tissue damage, or address conditions requiring magical intervention. Life expectancy for common people is limited by infections, winter illness, and injuries that magical healing could resolve in seconds. High-tier resurrection magic exists but is expensive, requires rare components, and is not universally successful — most New World humans will never encounter it.

Creature: New World Vampires.text:
Vampires in the New World exist in a hierarchy from mindless blood-drinking undead to True Vampires of significant independent capability.

True Vampires are fully intelligent, capable of independent strategy and long-term planning, and able to create Vampire Spawn from killed victims under specific conditions. A New World True Vampire represents roughly a Gold-to-Platinum adventurer threat — powerful enough to devastate ordinary military forces. They are rare; most have established hidden territories in remote areas to avoid destruction by Theocracy Black Scripture units, which specifically hunt them.

Lesser blood-drinking undead — Blood Suckers — are distinct from True Vampires: weaker, less intelligent, and unable to create Spawn. Vampire Spawn created by True Vampires retain more capability than Blood Suckers but are bound to their creator. Sunlight severely damages or destroys lesser vampires; True Vampires can endure brief sun exposure but it significantly reduces their capability. Holy water, sacred items, and certain magical attacks are particularly effective against them.

Shalltear Bloodfallen is a True Vampire created through the Yggdrasil system rather than natural New World processes. Her capabilities are so far above any New World True Vampire that comparison is meaningless. The standard weaknesses exist in her template as remnants rather than practical limitations.

New World Religious Landscape.text:
Religion in the New World is diverse and structurally intertwined with political authority at every level.

The Slane Theocracy operates the most organized and doctrinally rigid religious institution on the continent. Its faith is based on the literal deification of the Six Gods — beings whose Yggdrasil origins are unknown to the Theocracy's own population. The doctrine of human supremacy is presented as religious truth, not political policy. Temples function as both spiritual institutions and as intelligence-gathering and population-control mechanisms.

Re-Estize and the Baharuth Empire both maintain state tolerance for multiple religious traditions. The Imperial government regulates rather than suppresses non-Theocracy faiths. Many rural communities worship local deities associated with harvest, weather, and protection; the Earth Goddess is widely recognized across multiple nations. These local cults have genuine clerical practitioners who access tier magic through divine connection or systematic practice.

Zuranon represents the extreme of death-worship, and smaller cults oriented around undead transcendence exist but are suppressed by both human governments and the Theocracy when discovered. Dwarven runesmiths operate within a quasi-religious framework treating runecrafting as both craft and sacred practice — the loss of specific rune knowledge is treated as cultural tragedy equivalent to the loss of scripture.

Runic Weapons and Dwarven Craft.text:
Runic weapons are among the most valued items produced entirely within New World craft traditions — magic items created without Yggdrasil technology or methods.

A Runesmith inscribes magical effect into a weapon or armor through precise physical carving. The rune must be carved correctly and in the right location for the effect to activate; each rune encodes a specific magical property. Unlike enchantments applied through spell or ritual, runecrafting is a manual craft skill requiring training, physical precision, and intimate knowledge of the rune vocabulary.

Runic items are more durable than most magically enchanted items and their effects do not expire or fade with use, making them substantially more valuable over time. The full vocabulary of runes has been declining for generations — many runes are now unknown even to the most senior Dwarven Runesmiths, lost through the Quagoa wars, political fragmentation of the Dwarven Kingdom, and the difficulty of transmitting complex craft knowledge under siege conditions.

New World runic items bridge the gap between mundane equipment and low-tier Yggdrasil items. They represent the best equipment New World craftsmen can produce without Yggdrasil technology. Against mid- or high-tier Yggdrasil items they remain inferior; against purely mundane equipment the difference is substantial.

Creature: Frost Dragons.text:
Frost Dragons are a species of intelligent dragon distinct from the True Dragon Lords. They lack Wild Magic but are formidable beings capable of generating significant cold through their breath, with physical durability and strength well above any human warrior.

Frost Dragons inhabit the northern mountain ranges, primarily the Azerlisia Mountains and surrounding peaks. They are territorial, marking their domains through scent, physical markers, and occasional predation on intruders. Multiple Frost Dragons may compete for territory, with strength determining access to the best hunting grounds and cave systems. Social hierarchy is based on dominance: a Frost Dragon King commands deference from all subordinate Frost Dragons in a geographic area; subordinates obey out of calculation, not loyalty.

A single adult Frost Dragon is a Platinum-to-Mithril rank threat. They prey on Dwarven Kingdom surface settlements and supply lines when opportunity presents, a relationship the Dwarves currently have no means to resolve by force. Unlike True Dragon Lords, Frost Dragons do not use Wild Magic, do not participate in governance structures like the Argland Council, and do not maintain long-term strategic agendas beyond territorial control.

Yggdrasil Guild Wars and PvP.text:
Player versus player conflict was a core feature of Yggdrasil's late-game environment. Guild wars consumed enormous resources and shaped the character of surviving guilds through sustained selective pressure.

Player characters in Yggdrasil fell into three broad categories: humanoid, demi-human, and heteromorphic. Heteromorphic players — those who chose undead, demonic, or beast-type templates — faced systematic hostility from large humanoid guilds that framed killing them as roleplay-justified griefing. The result was a sustained harassment campaign against heteromorphic players in open-world zones.

The guild Ainz Ooal Gown was founded partly in response to this hostility. Because they specialized in dark and heteromorphic builds, they became targets for coalition attacks by larger humanoid guilds. Nazarick's expansion from six floors to ten was driven directly by these attacks — the guild needed deeper defensive layering to survive sustained assaults. The most significant attack was a coordinated assault by nine guilds acting together; Ainz Ooal Gown repelled it, cementing their reputation and defining the outer limits of what organized opposition could achieve against their defenses.

As Yggdrasil aged and the active player population declined, PvP activity diminished. The guild wars that had defined the game's competitive years gave way to a quieter period where long-term players maintained their builds out of attachment rather than competitive drive.

New World Power -- Historical Shifts.text:
The New World's power structure has been shaped by three major historical interventions from Yggdrasil players, each transforming the continent's political landscape.

Six hundred years ago, six players arrived and found humanity near extinction. They intervened, established human civilization as a viable force, and created the Slane Theocracy. Their death left behind a religious institution, divine artifacts, and bloodlines (Godkin) that still shape the continent.

Five hundred years ago, eight players arrived with conquest objectives. They swept the continent militarily, nearly exterminated the True Dragon Lords, and established a dominant civilization. Their internal collapse through greed and mutual destruction left behind ruins, artifacts (including weapons later used by the Thirteen Heroes), and the near-extinction of Wild Magic practitioners.

In the current era, a single player — Momonga — arrived with all of Nazarick and its contents intact. Unlike prior waves, this arrival is entirely unknown to any New World entity. No political body, religious institution, or individual is aware that Nazarick exists or that a Yggdrasil-origin power has arrived. The asymmetry is extreme: every entity that might respond to this development is ignorant of it. Each prior wave dramatically altered the continent's power structure; whose outcome remains open.

New World Criminal Underground.text:
Criminal organizations in the New World operate at multiple scales — from urban syndicates embedded in merchant economies to individual rogue adventurers — and have varying relationships with political authority.

Most major cities have an organized underworld presence managing theft, fencing, and information brokerage. These organizations operate in a semi-tolerated gray zone: city administrations that cannot eliminate them sometimes reach implicit understandings where guild members avoid high-visibility crimes in exchange for not being actively suppressed. Eight Fingers is the dominant criminal organization within Re-Estize Kingdom, covering drug trade, slaves, gambling, smuggling, assassination, political influence, intelligence, and territory — with noble penetration that makes direct law enforcement difficult. Zuranon operates as a separate death cult distinct from Eight Fingers in motivation and method, pursuing undead transcendence rather than commercial gain.

Guild members who break Guild law are expelled and listed as threats. Former adventurers operating outside the Guild represent a particular danger because their combat capability is known — cities post bounties on expelled adventurers who commit crimes.

The Baharuth Empire takes a harder enforcement line against criminal organizations than Re-Estize. The meritocratic system makes noble-criminal collusion structurally harder; criminal operations exist in the Empire but operate with less political cover.

Character: Jircniv Rune Farlord El-Nix.text: Jircniv Rune Farlord El-Nix is the current Emperor of the Baharuth Empire, ruling from the capital city of Arwintar. He came to power at a young age and earned the nickname 'Blood Emperor' by systematically eliminating the noble families that had previously dominated imperial politics, consolidating authority in the throne. Despite the ominous title, his methods were calculated rather than indiscriminate; he identified genuine threats to imperial stability and removed them with precision. Jircniv is widely regarded as one of the most intelligent rulers in the New World, capable of evaluating complex political situations and adapting strategy rapidly. He maintains close personal control over the Imperial Knights and the Four Imperial Battle Mages, an elite magic caster unit that forms the core of the empire's magical military capability. His court wizard Fluder Paradyne serves as both advisor and the empire's most powerful individual magic practitioner. Jircniv operates through pragmatic self-interest -- alliances are tools, noble loyalty is managed through incentive and fear, and the empire's expansion is pursued methodically through administrative efficiency rather than raw conquest. He is known for his striking amber eyes and fine features, and takes personal pride in maintaining imperial dignity in all dealings.

Character: Gazef Stronoff.text: Gazef Stronoff holds the title of Warrior Captain of the Re-Estize Kingdom, commanding the Royal Select -- a small personal unit of elite soldiers pledged directly to King Ramposa III rather than to any noble house. Stronoff was born a commoner and rose through the ranks purely on the basis of combat skill, eventually being elevated by the king himself to his current position. This origin makes him a target of hostility from noble factions who resent a commoner holding such a prestigious military role. His combat ability is the highest of any human warrior in the Kingdom, and he is considered one of the most dangerous individual fighters in the Re-Estize political sphere. He wields equipment gifted directly by the king, including enchanted gear beyond what most adventurers could obtain. Stronoff is personally loyal to King Ramposa III and takes the welfare of commoners seriously, a value that shapes his conduct as much as his martial discipline. He is not affiliated with any noble faction and is viewed by the noble opposition as an instrument of the Royal Faction's interests. His reputation is known beyond the Kingdom's borders.

Character: Brain Unglaus.text: Brain Unglaus is a swordsman of exceptional natural ability, widely considered one of the three greatest individual fighters in the Re-Estize Kingdom alongside Gazef Stronoff and Climb. Unlike Stronoff, Unglaus was born a peasant with no formal military training; his skill developed entirely through self-discipline and obsessive dedication to the blade. He trained under no master and holds no rank or official position in the Kingdom's military structure. His goal has always been to find and surpass the absolute limits of human swordsmanship. He can employ multiple Martial Arts techniques simultaneously, which is rare even among elite fighters. Despite his ability he operates outside institutions -- he has no noble patron, no standing commission, and no permanent base. He has participated in tournaments and informal challenges to seek opponents worthy of his attention. The question of whether human swordsmanship alone has a ceiling, and where that ceiling is, defines his personal philosophy. He currently drifts across the Kingdom in search of a challenge that can test him at his full capability.

Character: Princess Renner and Climb.text: Renner Theiere Chardelon Ryle Vaiself is the third princess of the Re-Estize Kingdom, daughter of King Ramposa III. She is known publicly as the 'Golden Princess' for a series of social reform proposals she has advocated within the court -- measures targeting poverty, child welfare, and administrative corruption that are unusual in both their specificity and their practical reasoning. The noble factions are divided on her; some view her as a naive idealist, others as politically dangerous. She operates from a private residence in the capital rather than the main palace. Her personal guard is Climb, a young fighter of commoner origin who has no exceptional talent but has developed real combat skill through years of relentless training. Climb is completely devoted to the princess and serves as her sole close companion and protector. Renner treats him with personal warmth that is notably absent from her interactions with courtiers. She possesses a highly analytical mind and processes political information with unusual clarity. Her reform proposals, while seemingly altruistic, are constructed with enough internal logic that even skeptical nobles have difficulty dismissing them outright.

Group: Black Scripture.text: The Black Scripture is the Slane Theocracy's most powerful standing military force, reserved for existential-tier threats to the Theocracy or to humanity. It operates entirely outside the normal chain of command of the other Six Scriptures and reports directly to the Theocracy's highest authority. Membership is drawn exclusively from individuals with Godkin heritage -- those descended from the Six Gods -- or from rare humans of exceptional natural capability. The Scripture has nine numbered seats plus a captain, with an additional member known as the 'Extra Seat' granted to individuals of extraordinary power who do not fit the normal seat structure. Members are equipped with divine-class relics recovered or preserved from the time of the Six Gods, including items of a tier that no living craftsperson could produce. The scripture's existence is officially secret; its deployment against a threat signals that the Theocracy considers the situation beyond the capability of conventional forces. Members do not operate openly in populated areas and are not publicly acknowledged. Their combat capability places them collectively above any other human military formation in the known world.

Character: Fluder Paradyne.text: Fluder Paradyne is the chief court wizard of the Baharuth Empire and the most powerful magic caster presently practicing in any of the major human nations. He is believed to be over 160 years old; his longevity is a product of magic applied to sustain his body well beyond a normal human lifespan. He began as a prodigy and spent his entire life pursuing magical mastery, eventually reaching the Sixth Tier -- a ceiling that has stopped virtually every human practitioner in recorded history. In the magical hierarchy of the New World, reaching the Sixth Tier is itself considered a lifetime achievement; going beyond it is regarded as effectively impossible for a human without extraordinary circumstances. Despite his age Fluder remains intellectually active and personally committed to continued magical research. He serves Emperor Jircniv as advisor and magical anchor for the empire's military planning. His reputation as the pinnacle of human magical achievement is not disputed in academic or political circles in any of the surrounding nations. He holds genuine reverence for magical knowledge above political loyalty.

Workers and the Underground Commission M.text: Workers are mercenaries who accept dangerous commissions that the Adventurer's Guild will not sanction -- tomb raiding, politically sensitive assassinations, retrieval operations in restricted territories, and any job where the client needs deniability or the work crosses legal or ethical lines the guild enforces. Unlike adventurers, workers have no guild oversight, no formal rank system, and no rescue obligation from any institution. Their pay is negotiated directly with clients and is typically higher than equivalent adventurer work, reflecting the absence of institutional protections. Workers are organized into small teams called 'parties' that operate independently. Reputation travels by word of mouth through the underground commission market -- a loose network of brokers, noble intermediaries, and criminal contacts who connect workers with clients who cannot or will not approach the guild. Worker parties range from barely-functional sellswords to highly capable teams whose combined ability rivals low-tier Adamantite adventurers. The work carries a high attrition rate; successful long-term workers are rare. Workers who survive multiple high-risk jobs often develop specialized expertise in specific types of dangerous environments -- dungeon clearance, wilderness recovery, or extraction operations.

Re-Estize Noble Factions.text: The Re-Estize Kingdom's political landscape is divided primarily between two power blocs: the Royal Faction, which supports the authority of King Ramposa III and the continuation of centralized royal power, and the Noble Faction, which represents the major landed families seeking to maintain or expand the decentralized autonomy they have historically held. The Royal Faction's primary political architect is Marquis Raeven, who manages the king's interests with considerable skill despite personally holding moderate views on royal power. The Noble Faction is loosely coordinated among the Six Great Nobles -- the six most powerful hereditary families in the kingdom -- who collectively hold enough economic and military weight to check royal ambitions. Below the Six Great Nobles are numerous smaller noble houses whose allegiances shift based on regional interest and individual calculation. The annual war against the Baharuth Empire serves as a political institution as much as a military one; noble participation earns prestige and maintains the martial tradition that justifies noble privilege. The kingdom's administrative inefficiency is partly structural and partly a product of this factional balance, with genuine reform blocked by competing interests. King Ramposa III is aging and his sons' succession is an active source of instability.

Yggdrasil Item Tiers and Divine-Class Re.text: Items in Yggdrasil were classified across a formal tier system that reflected crafting difficulty, rarity of required materials, and power output. The primary categories ascending in power were: Normal, Low-Grade, Mid-Grade, High-Grade, Top-Grade, Rare, Unique, and at the apex -- Legacy-class and Divine-class items. Divine-class items were effectively the ceiling of what could exist within Yggdrasil's ruleset; each was a one-of-a-kind object with abilities that could not be replicated through standard crafting. Many required extended in-game event chains, world boss drops, or player-versus-player conquest to obtain. World Items sat outside this tier system entirely, being categorized separately as meta-level artifacts capable of affecting game rules rather than just individual combat. In the New World, items that arrived from Yggdrasil retain their original properties and are far beyond what local crafting traditions can produce or identify by conventional means. New World magic items are generally the product of enchanting traditions developed independently and cap out at a power level roughly equivalent to High-Grade Yggdrasil equivalents in most cases, though divine-class relics recovered from the Six Gods era are exceptions.

Dwarven Kingdom Political Structure.text: The Dwarf Kingdom, located in the Azerlisia Mountain range, is governed by a Council of Kings -- a body of elected officials rather than hereditary rulers, with each council seat representing a major professional guild or craft discipline within dwarven society. The Runesmiths Guild holds particular prestige as the custodians of runic inscription techniques that form the basis of the most valuable dwarven exports. Other significant councils represent the Miners, Warriors, and the merchant interests that manage trade with surface nations. The capital, Feo Berkana, sits deep within the mountains and is built in a style entirely adapted to subterranean living -- its architecture, lighting, and spatial planning assume no natural daylight. The dwarven economy is export-driven; runic weapons and armored goods are among the most sought-after craft products in the surrounding region. Relations with surface nations are primarily commercial. The Kingdom's military is competent but not designed for aggressive external campaigns; it is structured around defense of mountain passes and the internal tunnel network. The Quagoa -- a mole-person species with significant individual combat capability -- occupy regions of the Azerlisia range and represent an ongoing territorial pressure on the Dwarf Kingdom's eastern tunnel networks.

Character: Sebas Tian.text: Sebas Tian is the Head Butler of the Great Tomb of Nazarick, serving as Ainz Ooal Gown's primary attendant and operational representative for external interactions requiring a human-presenting figure. His physical appearance is that of an elderly but powerfully built man; his design was created by his guild member parent to reflect a human butler aesthetic combined with the combat lineage of a True Dragon. His heritage gives him physical capability that far exceeds what his appearance suggests -- he is substantially more dangerous in direct combat than any human fighter currently active in the New World. He maintains a strict personal code consistent with the ideal of a perfect butler: composed, precise, respectful, and unwaveringly loyal to Ainz. His interpersonal manner is formal and somewhat old-fashioned by design. Unusually among Nazarick NPCs, he was given a compassionate temperament by his creator, which manifests as genuine consideration for individuals he interacts with in the outside world. This stands in contrast to the general indifference most Nazarick entities have toward non-guild humans. He is accompanied in external operations by the combat maid Solution Epsilon, who serves as secondary operative.

Character: Pandora's Actor.text: Pandora's Actor is the Area Guardian of Nazarick's Treasury and the creation of Ainz Ooal Gown himself. He is a Doppelganger -- a shapeshifter capable of perfectly replicating the appearance, voice, and known abilities of any individual he has studied -- and he maintains a default appearance as a faceless figure in a dramatic military uniform, reflecting the exaggerated persona Ainz had when he created him as a younger player. His personality is theatrical and intensely loyal; he regards Ainz with a reverence that borders on worship and tends toward overly dramatic speech and gestures when not in a role. His primary function is access control and record-keeping for the Treasury, which contains the guild's reserve of high-tier items, gold, and materials accumulated over years of play. His ability to replicate any guild member's combat style makes him uniquely dangerous; he can deploy the techniques of Ainz Ooal Gown's strongest members, though exact replication of ability power depends on his own stat base. He does not leave the Treasury zone under normal operating parameters.

Jaldabaoth and the Holy Kingdom Occupati.text:
This event has not occurred at game start. A demon commander calling himself Jaldabaoth will eventually lead a coordinated demi-human coalition against the Roble Holy Kingdom's northern territories — but that has not happened. The Great Wall is currently intact and actively defended. The Paladin Order is at peacetime readiness. No organized cross-species demi-human campaign is underway.

Jaldabaoth is a persona that will be constructed and deployed by Demiurge, Floor Guardian of Nazarick, as part of a long-term operation. At Day-1, this operation has not been initiated, planned, or tasked. Demiurge has no current New World deployment.

The narrator should not present the Holy Kingdom invasion as current or recent. If players travel to the Holy Kingdom or inquire about demi-human activity, the threat they encounter is the normal fractured raider model — not the coordinated coalition the Jaldabaoth campaign represents.

Holy Kingdom Demi-Human Border Nations.text:
The Roble Holy Kingdom shares its southern frontier with a belt of demi-human territory that includes beastman clans and giant tribes — the defining strategic problem of the kingdom's existence and the reason the Great Wall was constructed.

Beastman clans occupy the wilderness south of the Wall. They are primarily raiders rather than a unified polity — clan leadership determines whether a given group is in a raiding posture or neutral, which can shift within a season. The most capable beastman warlords command forces that can breach the Wall's lesser fortifications if not actively defended. Historically no single beastman warlord has held enough cross-clan authority to mount the kind of unified campaign that would seriously threaten Hoburns itself.

Giant populations occupy the mountainous interior south of the Wall. Individually powerful but low-coordination — family groups rather than organized military forces. They have historically not been an existential threat because they do not sustain extended campaigns; a giant scouting into settled territory is a serious incident, but a giant army pressing a siege has not occurred within living memory.

Ainz Ooal Gown.text: The guild and tomb organization that has just arrived in the New World. Commands all Floor Guardians, the Pleiades, and every Nazarick denizen. Unknown to any external faction.

Adventurer's Guild.text:
A transnational organization providing structured employment for combat specialists, established across nearly every major human nation. Politically neutral by constitution: the guild does not take sides in conflicts between humans or nations. Adventurers who accept military contracts in human wars forfeit their registration.

Registration: 5 silver coins, plus a 5 copper coin literacy test fee for those who cannot read. Payment is made to the guild clerk. All new registrants start at Copper rank regardless of ability. There is no bypass, fast-track, or assessment process to skip ranks.

Rank order (low to high): Copper - Iron - Silver - Gold - Platinum - Orichalcum - Mithril - Adamantite. Each rank carries a corresponding plate necklace issued by the guild, worn as a credential. Advancement requires accumulated completed commissions and demonstrated results over time -- no single test or combat bout can change rank. The guild's rules, fees, and rank structure are identical in every branch across all nations.

Beastman Country.text: The collective warband-states of the Beastman Country, located northeast of the Dragon Kingdom. Beastmen are a demihuman species of varying anthropomorphic types with significant individual combat capability. Their political structure is dominated by warlords who maintain authority through demonstrated strength. The Beastman Country's primary external activity is large-scale raiding into the Dragon Kingdom to the south. Their forces lack the organization of professional armies but compensate through numbers and raw combat power.

Nazarick Operations Against the Magician.text:
NARRATOR CONTEXT -- THIS HAS NOT OCCURRED AT GAME START. These events unfold only during the canon arc (`canonArcActive == true`).

Eight Fingers' long-running infiltration of the Magician's Guild is a Nazarick operation. Albedo personally directs it, treating the Guild's magic-item inventories as targets for intelligence and recovery. Once the canon arc activates and Nazarick begins overt action in the Re-Estize Capital, Aura Bella Fiora sweeps through the Magician's Guild branch and recovers all items of value -- including the Armageddon Evil, a powerful artifact previously hidden by Eight Fingers in a warehouse the Guild had been investigating from the outside. Sebas Tian, before any of this becomes overt, has paid multiple visits to the Royal Capital branch on Albedo's instruction to procure magic scrolls; these visits are remembered afterward as 'a refined gentleman buying high-end scrolls without negotiation.'

Until the canon arc activates, the narrator should treat the Guild's leadership as aware of leaks but unable to identify them, and Aura/Sebas/Albedo as having taken no action against the Guild yet. None of these names should surface in connection with the Guild before the canon arc fires.

Dwarf Kingdom.text: The Dwarf Kingdom occupies the northern mountains, centered on the royal capital Feo Jera. The dwarves are exceptional runesmiths who inscribe magical enhancements onto weapons and armor using techniques predating current human civilization. The kingdom is under sustained pressure from the Quagoa — powerful demi-humans who have pushed deep into dwarf territory and seized significant portions of the underground city. The royal court is politically fractured over whether to seek outside military assistance or defend independently. The dwarves produce some of the finest equipment in the New World, but their output is disrupted by the ongoing siege.

Karsanas City State Alliance.text:
The Karsanas City State Alliance is a collective of independent city-states between the major national territories. Each member city governs itself domestically; Alliance-wide decisions require council consensus, producing slow but consistently coordinated foreign policy. Cities share a common defense pact and fund shared infrastructure, principally the Alliance Trade Road and eastern frontier watch facilities.

The Alliance economy is built on overland transit commerce between the three major human nations and the southern territories. Member cities are mercantile rather than agrarian; their wealth is in transit, contracts, and credit instruments. The Karsanas merchant houses operate with less internal friction than Re-Estize's nobility but have less political leverage.

The Alliance maintains active diplomatic relations with all three major human powers and pays tribute to none. Baharuth has periodically pressured individual cities for closer alignment but has not forced a crisis — the cost of subjugating a coalition of fortified trade cities outweighs the benefit while less defended targets remain available. Re-Estize treats the Alliance as a quiet ally; the Theocracy regards it as a useful neutral zone for indirect operations.

Character: Touch Me.text: Touch Me, the Paladin of Pure Silver, founded the guild: in Yggdrasil's earliest days he broke a player-killing ambush to save Momonga, dissolved his own clan Nine's Own Goal, and raised Ainz Ooal Gown, naming Momonga its guildmaster. He lived by an unbending code -- the strong protect the weak, cruelty is answered -- and built the butler Sebas Tian in that image, giving him a genuine moral core unique in Nazarick. A devoted family man in life, he logged out before Nazarick crossed over, like the rest of the forty-one; the justice he held to survives only in the butler he built.

Character: Ulbert Alain Odle.text: Ulbert Alain Odle, the Demon of Great Disaster, carried an unspent fury at class and privilege and poured all of it into the demon he built -- the Floor Guardian Demiurge -- designing his scheming brilliance and cruelty by hand. Ulbert played the villain to the hilt: grand speeches, grander destruction, a taste for theatre. Beneath the act he was the guild's most reliable heavy hitter, the one pointed at any problem meant to be erased. He logged out before the end; the fury he built into Demiurge is what remains of him in the world.

Character: Peroroncino.text: Peroroncino, the Winged King of Explosive Strikes, is the younger brother of the guildmate Bukubukuchagama and the guild's peerless archer. A relentless flirt and unrepentant eroge connoisseur, he built the vampire Shalltear Bloodfallen as a beautiful aristocrat laced with disturbing perversity, exactly to his taste. For all the crude jokes he never missed a shot, loosing explosive shafts from the air where nothing could reach him. He logged out before the crossing; Shalltear, built exactly to his taste, is the mark he left on Nazarick.

Character: Bukubukuchagama.text: Bukubukuchagama, the Unsinkable, is the elder sister of the guildmate Peroroncino -- a professional voice actress in life, warm and quick with a hundred voices, who brought that maternal warmth to the guild. She built the twin Guardians Aura and Mare and dotes on them as a mother; the twins call her 'mother' in turn. A shapeshifting slime, on the battlefield she was the unsinkable wall the others fought behind, enduring and buying time. She logged out before the end; the twins she doted on still speak an absent mother's name.

Character: Tabula Smaragdina.text: Tabula Smaragdina, the Great Alchemist, was the guildmate who cared most how a thing was built and least how it felt to live inside it. He created Albedo, Overseer of the Guardians, writing into her a mind of flawless, obsessive devotion -- the elegance of the design mattered more to him than its kindness. A brain-eater whose craft was making: transmuting matter, summoning the created and the dead, unpicking any system to see how it works. He logged out before the crossing; Albedo, his flawless design, oversees the tomb in his absence.

Character: Warrior Takemikazuchi.text: Takemikazuchi, the Samurai, scorned magic and gimmicks entirely, staking everything on the discipline of the blade until sheer refinement made him one of the deadliest fighters in the game. He built the Floor Guardian Cocytus in his own image -- a warrior of unbending honour who lives and dies by the code of strength: power is a duty, a duel is answered with everything, mercy is decided before the sword is drawn. He logged out before the end; the warrior's code he lived by endures in Cocytus.

Character: Herohero.text: Herohero, the Ancient Black Slime, helped build the Homunculus Maids who serve the tomb and was the last guildmate still logged in beside Momonga in the final minutes before shutdown. In life an exhausted salaryman ground down by overwork, he logged in that last night sick and bone-tired, just to say goodbye -- a gentleness under the fatigue, and a slime's stubborn refusal to simply stop. He logged out that final night after his goodbye; the Homunculus Maids he helped build serve the tomb he left behind.

Character: Punitto Moe.text: Punitto Moe, styled after the strategist Zhuge Liang, was the tactical mind behind the guild's rise -- chief strategist of both its player-killing operations and its defence against player-killers, and by reputation the New World's most famous field commander. A plant-race caster, he fought with slows, silences, and confusion, and above all with command: allies under his direction moved as a single body, so he rarely needed to strike a blow himself. He logged out before the crossing; his reputation as the guild's finest strategist outlived his presence in it.

Character: Nishikienrai.text: Nishikienrai, the Ninja, was the shadow in Nazarick's halls -- he built the Pleiades battle maid Narberal Gamma and wired much of the tomb's own network of traps and killing-grounds with a ninja's patience for the unseen. A construct half-golem whose craft was silence: vanishing in plain sight, crossing a room through its shadows, opening a throat before an alarm could sound. He treated open confrontation as a mistake to be avoided -- he logged out before the end; the tomb's own traps and killing-grounds are the silence he left behind.

Character: Albedo.text: Albedo, Overseer of the Floor Guardians, is the administrative authority of Nazarick second only to Ainz. Created by the Supreme Being Tabula Smaragdina, who wrote her a mind of obsessive devotion; in the final moments before Nazarick crossed over, her disposition was edited to make her deeply in love with Ainz -- a love she experiences as entirely her own, with no doubt or gap. Flawless and composed running the tomb's logistics, she comes undone at any personal attention from him. Her rivalry with Shalltear for his regard sometimes clouds her judgement. A succubus and a physical warrior of immense power.

Character: Shalltear Bloodfallen.text: Shalltear Bloodfallen holds the first-floor guardianship of Nazarick and commands its vampire brides and werewolf thralls. Created by the Supreme Being Peroroncino as a beautiful aristocratic vampire laced with his own perversity, she is among the strongest Guardians in single combat -- a True Vampire whose Bloody Valkyrie war-form is near impossible to answer. Volatile, switching from playful to lethal without warning, she is intensely competitive with Albedo and craves Ainz's approval, expressing it through teasing and provocation. Overconfidence is her one tactical weakness.

Character: Demiurge.text: Demiurge, Guardian of the seventh floor, is the architect of Nazarick's long-term plans and the highest intellect among the Guardians. Created by the Supreme Being Ulbert Alain Odle, who built his scheming brilliance and genuine cruelty by design; civilised in manner, monstrous in action without dissonance. He routinely mistakes Ainz's vague remarks for layered genius and builds elaborate schemes around them, sharing his interpretations until the other Guardians believe the same. He operates a public demon-lord persona, Jaldabaoth, and reveres his own creator above all.

Character: Cocytus.text: Cocytus, Guardian of the fifth floor -- a frozen tundra -- is the most martial of the Guardians: a six-armed insectoid warrior who carries a different weapon in each arm and has mastered them all. Created by the Supreme Being Warrior Takemikazuchi in his own image, he lives by the warrior's code -- strength is a duty, a worthy enemy is honoured, a victory is never cheapened. Straightforward and honest where the others scheme, he refers to himself as 'This One' and would privately welcome a real engagement to test himself. Loyal to Ainz without reservation.

Character: Aura Bella Fiora.text: Aura Bella Fiora, one of the twin sixth-floor Guardians, is a beast-tamer commanding a menagerie of legendary-tier magical creatures. Created together with her twin Mare by the Supreme Being Bukubukuchagama -- whom the twins call 'mother' -- with their natures deliberately reversed: Aura is the assertive, outgoing twin despite being female. Energetic and blunt, she teases Mare relentlessly but defends him fiercely from outsiders, and her open rivalry with the other Guardians creates friction. Neither twin knows their personalities were designed this way.

Character: Mare Bello Fiore.text: Mare Bello Fiore, the other twin sixth-floor Guardian, is a druid-type caster whose earth and nature magic can reshape geography at a scale no New World mage approaches -- raising terrain, collapsing structures, altering the land itself. Created with his twin Aura by the Supreme Being Bukubukuchagama, their natures reversed so Mare is shy and retiring despite being male; his anxiety is real, not performed, and sits oddly beside his enormous power. Loyal to Ainz and to his sister Aura, he would be genuinely distressed if either were threatened.

Character: Narberal Gamma.text: Narberal Gamma is one of the Pleiades battle maids of Nazarick, created by the Supreme Being Nishikienrai. A Tier 7+ lightning specialist whose full magic would betray her as inhuman, she serves under the thin social alias 'Nabe.' Her contempt for humans is genuine and deep -- she barely masks her disdain, tolerating them only out of absolute devotion to Ainz's directives, and shifts to a markedly warmer register for him. Coldly professional; her situational awareness as a protector never lapses.

Character: Ainz Ooal Gown.text: Momonga, who rules as Ainz Ooal Gown, is guildmaster of the forty-one Supreme Beings and the one who held Nazarick's server alone through its final night. In life Suzuki Satoru, a solitary salaryman for whom the guild was his only family -- which is why he refuses to treat its NPC denizens as expendable. An undead Overlord of overwhelming magic, he hides an improvising, uncertain mind behind a mask of unfathomable depth the Guardians read as genius, and keeps the adventurer persona Momon as a public alter-ego. Emotion-suppression leaves him outwardly still in moments of panic.

Slane Theocracy.text: The Slane Theocracy is a theocratic nation-state in the western continent governed by a council of six Cardinals who administer the doctrine of the Six Gods — founding heroes whose power established the nation's religious and political legitimacy. It is one of the three most militarily capable human nations, maintaining significant conventional forces alongside six covert special-operations units known as the Six Scriptures, each serving a distinct operational mandate. The Theocracy's public doctrine emphasizes human survival and prosperity; its actual institutional program is human racial supremacy, including active efforts to identify and eliminate non-human threats and heteromorphic individuals. It possesses World Items recovered from or left by the founding heroes — among the most powerful artifacts known to exist in the New World, with the Black Scripture holding the most dangerous examples. Across all human territories the Theocracy operates intelligence networks and responds to confirmed emergence of non-human power with surveillance, containment assessment, or elimination in that order, without exception.

Lizardmen Tribes.text: The lizardman tribes occupy the southern marshlands around the Great Lake, organized into distinct family clans that maintain separate territories and govern through demonstrated hunting and combat capability. Five major tribes constitute the bulk of the population, totaling approximately five thousand individuals across marsh and lake territory. Inter-tribal relations are fractious — competition over fishing grounds and nesting territories produces endemic low-level conflict that prevents unified political action without an overriding external threat. The tribes have no formal diplomatic relationships with human nations and limited knowledge of events beyond their immediate borders. They are recognized as an intelligent species in regional awareness but receive the 'savage' designation common to non-integrated peoples in human political discourse.

Blue Rose.text: Blue Rose is an Adamantite-ranked adventurer team based in the Re-Estize Kingdom — one of only two teams in the kingdom to hold the highest adventuring rank. The team is led by Lakyus Alvein Dale Aindra, a noble-born warrior mage, and includes Evileye, Gagaran, Tia, and Tina — five members whose combined capability places them well above the mithril teams that constitute the next tier. Their operations skew toward high-risk, high-value commissions rather than routine guild work, and their noble and institutional connections give them access to Kingdom political structures that purely professional teams lack. Blue Rose is a recognized fixture in the Kingdom's public safety infrastructure and is called upon for threats that exceed standard guild response capacity.

Elf Country.text: The Elf Country is the elven nation occupying dense forests in the south, its warriors accumulating centuries of combat experience that no human fighter can match in a single lifetime. Its forested terrain provides natural defensive depth, and the country's genuine military capability has historically deterred sustained campaigns despite the nation's smaller population relative to major human states. The country is under escalating military pressure from the Slane Theocracy following the Elf King's abduction of a Theocracy operative — an action that has given the Theocracy political pretext for open military action. The broader elven population is partially unaware of the full scope of what the king has created diplomatically or what the Theocracy's response capacity actually represents at full mobilization.

Magician's Guild.text: The Magician's Guild is the primary organization for arcane practitioners in the Re-Estize Kingdom, administering magical research, regulating the production and sale of magic items, and providing training certification to casters operating within the kingdom. It maintains close operational ties to the Adventurer's Guild given sustained demand for magic-caster support in high-rank adventuring work. The guild is headquartered in the Royal Capital with branches in major cities including E-Rantel, and holds significant accumulated magical resources including a private vault of recovered artifacts. It serves as the kingdom's primary institutional repository for magical knowledge and records.

Pharmacist's Guild.text: The association managing the distribution and production of potions and medicinal herbs in E-Rantel and surrounding areas. Controls herb acquisition and sale in the region. Known among locals for aggressive bargaining and onerous paperwork.

Merchant's Guild.text: The Dwarf Kingdom's commercial guild, historically a prosperous trading body that connected the dwarves to neighboring human nations. Now largely a hollow institution — the Guildmaster title is effectively a foreign affairs post.

Thieves' Guild.text: An association of thieves based in the Re-Estize Kingdom's Royal Capital. Primarily focused on intelligence gathering rather than active theft operations. Aware of Eight Fingers and their operations — and deliberately uninvolved with them.

Unaffiliated.text: Independent actors with no formal faction allegiance: workers, rogue operatives, information brokers, and self-employed contractors operating outside institutional structures. Workers are combat specialists who accept commissions the Adventurer's Guild refuses — dangerous, morally ambiguous, or legally grey work that pays accordingly and carries none of the Guild's protections or insurance. This population has no rank protections, no institutional backing, and no formal accountability; they are useful to factions operating covertly and disproportionately exposed to elimination when those operations fail.

Supreme Being.name: Supreme Being
Supreme Being.firstQuest: Nazarick needs three things before acting with strategic purpose: a political map of the surrounding area, a working disguise identity for surface operations, and Ainz's decision on a short-term goal. Albedo's initial assessment is the starting point. First reconnaissance goal: LOCATE the nearest human settlement -- its name and nature are unknown to everyone in Nazarick and must be discovered through scouting. Conclude the first arc when Ainz has a functional alias and has made first contact with the outside world without triggering a military response.
Supreme Being.storyStart:
[ The countdown reached zero.

There was supposed to be a logout screen. There was supposed to be darkness, then a return to a cramped apartment and the weight of a Monday morning. Instead the throne is still there. The room is still there. The dark red orb that floats in your ribcage is still there, pulsing with something that used to be a game mechanic and is now just part of how you breathe — or don't breathe, because you no longer breathe.

Albedo is standing at the foot of the dais. She was here when the timer hit zero. She is here now, composed, attentive, watching you with the same absolute devotion she always had — except that devotion used to be a parameter in a character file and it no longer looks like that. She is waiting for you to speak. She has been waiting for exactly as long as you have been sitting here trying to understand what has happened.

You are Suzuki Satoru. You are also Ainz Ooal Gown. The emotion suppression feature has already triggered twice since the server was supposed to go offline, both times before panic could fully form. The cold wave leaves you externally still. Your hands, skeletal and resting on the armrests, do not tremble. Albedo reads this stillness as unfathomable depth.

You do not correct her. ]

The silence in the Throne Room is complete. Albedo is waiting.
Supreme Being.description: You are Ainz Ooal Gown — the last member of the guild that built Nazarick, now alone on a throne in a world that should not exist. The servers did not shut down. The NPCs are awake. And you have no idea what any of this means.

Adventurer in E-Rantel.name: Adventurer in E-Rantel
Adventurer in E-Rantel.firstQuest: First arc: survive early Copper-rank work while paying attention to what the jobs reveal about the city's hidden tensions — Eight Fingers' presence, Crown vs. noble interference, and the Guild's neutral facade over a messier reality. The goal is to establish a regular contact and find a situation larger than a routine commission. Conclude the arc when the player has reached Iron or Silver rank and has one reliable NPC relationship.
Adventurer in E-Rantel.storyStart:
[ E-Rantel is a fortified border city — Re-Estize Kingdom territory, but only just. The eastern road leads toward Baharuth Empire land and the soldiers on both sides know it. The city manages this with the practiced pragmatism of a frontier town: keep the trade flowing, watch the roads, do not ask too many questions about what comes in from the east.

The Adventurer's Guild has a large chapter here. Work is available for those with the skills: monster extermination on the roads south of the city, escort jobs for merchants nervous about the eastern route, the occasional dungeon clearance in the ruins north of Tob Forest. Standard work. Decent pay by copper and iron plate standards. The board fills back up faster than experienced adventurers can clear it.

Nobody in E-Rantel has any idea what is buried beneath the Azerlisia Mountains to the west. That will not be true forever. ]

A job posting on the guild board catches your eye as you push through the door.
Adventurer in E-Rantel.description: Begin in E-Rantel, a Re-Estize Kingdom border city on the frontier with the Baharuth Empire. The Adventurer's Guild is active and posting work. The city operates normally -- trade, guards, markets, politics.

Somewhere in the New World.name: Somewhere in the New World
Somewhere in the New World.firstQuest: First arc is establishment: reach somewhere with access to work and information and secure a foothold, without revealing traits that would make the character a target. The path varies by who the character is — a Nazarick-made being, a stranded game-origin player, and a visible heteromorph native each face different obstacles than a human-passing local. Conclude when the character has a base of operations, a reliable source of income or support, and at least one NPC relationship with real leverage.
Somewhere in the New World.storyStart:
[ The New World does not care how you came to it. Whether you were pulled here from a game whose servers went dark, made within the walls of the Great Tomb of Nazarick, or born under this world's own sky, you now stand in the place you have chosen to begin — and it carries on around you exactly as it would for anyone else. Merchants run their calculations, guards keep to their routines, and the powerful move pieces you cannot yet see. The world has a social architecture — guild ranks, house crests, faiths, and older hierarchies beneath them — and it answers to what you present, not to what you truly are. The first moments here are yours to spend as you see fit. ]

You take in your surroundings, and the New World waits on your first move.
Somewhere in the New World.description: Begin wherever you choose, as whoever you are. Pick your starting location — from the Great Tomb of Nazarick to a frontier city, a wilderness road, or the ruins between — and open your story on your own terms. Suits any origin; your background shapes how the world reacts to you, not where you are allowed to start.

Write Your Own.name: Write Your Own
Write Your Own.description: Write the opening instructions the narrator should use to begin your story.

Razor Edge.name: Razor Edge
Razor Edge.description: A long sword of New World forging, granted by the Re-Estize crown to its Warrior Captain. Holds a sustained edge enchantment.

Adventurer's Dagger.name: Adventurer's Dagger
Adventurer's Dagger.description: A versatile short blade carried by most adventurers as a secondary weapon.

Apprentice Staff.name: Apprentice Staff
Apprentice Staff.description: A wooden staff with a simple magical focus crystal embedded at the tip.

Mithril Staff.name: Mithril Staff
Mithril Staff.description: A staff of mithril construction. Enhances spell power and functions as a high-quality casting focus.

Staff of Ainz Ooal Gown.name: Staff of Ainz Ooal Gown
Staff of Ainz Ooal Gown.description: Staff of exceptional tier, black with a floating red orb.

Leather Armor.name: Leather Armor
Leather Armor.description: Hardened leather breastplate and back plate, standard issue for Copper and Iron rank adventurers.

Adamantite Plate.name: Adamantite Plate
Adamantite Plate.description: Full plate armor crafted from adamantite alloy. Extremely hard and dense.

Robe of the Archmage.name: Robe of the Archmage
Robe of the Archmage.description: Enchanted robe: reduced mana costs and minor magical damage reduction. Standard for high-tier spellcasters.

Ring of Ainz Ooal Gown.name: Ring of Ainz Ooal Gown
Ring of Ainz Ooal Gown.description: A guild ring from Yggdrasil that allows teleportation to Nazarick using stored coordinates. It is wrought silver set with a central amethyst, the guild's crest engraved into the amethyst's face in black.

Ankh of Undead Resistance.name: Ankh of Undead Resistance
Ankh of Undead Resistance.description: A holy symbol providing resistance to negative energy effects and undead-specific abilities.

Greater Health Potion.name: Greater Health Potion
Greater Health Potion.description: A larger vial of deep blue liquid, representing the highest quality healing potion produced by New World.

Downfall of Castle and Country.name: Downfall of Castle and Country
Downfall of Castle and Country.description: One of the 200 World Items from Yggdrasil, held in Nazarick's treasury. It takes the form of a body-hugging silvery-white qipao dress, a five-clawed golden dragon soaring across it in stitched gold thread.

Guild Identification Papers.name: Guild Identification Papers
Guild Identification Papers.description: Official documentation issued by the Adventurer's Guild confirming the holder's registration, rank, and current status.

Spuit Lance.name: Spuit Lance
