Recipients of this strike do not require further explanation of what Sebas is. Short range, devastating output.

Warrior's Instinct.name: Warrior's Instinct
Warrior's Instinct.description: A heightened combat state that enhances all physical combat capabilities simultaneously. Reaction time, strength output, and target tracking all improve. Sustainable for the duration of a combat engagement. Requires a threat assessment threshold to activate — it cannot be initiated artificially in non-threatening situations.

Healing Wave.name: Healing Wave
Healing Wave.description: Crusch Lulu's group healing technique. A pulse of healing energy that propagates outward from the caster, touching all allied beings in range. Per-target potency is less than a direct heal but the coverage makes it the most efficient tool in mass casualty scenarios. Her primary contribution to the lizardman coalition's survival.

Druidic Summon.name: Druidic Summon
Druidic Summon.description: Call natural creatures to aid in combat. The summoned creatures are native to the environment — in the marshlands, aquatic predators; in forests, predatory animals. They are temporary allies rather than permanent summons. The creatures respond to environmental context — their behaviour in their native terrain is better than outside it.

Universal Item Use.name: Universal Item Use
Universal Item Use.description: Nfirea Bareare's unique personal ability. Allows use of any magical item regardless of class or species restrictions. Enchanted items that require specific bloodlines, class qualifications, or species are accessible to him unconditionally. The ability is not magical training — it is a natural talent that cannot be taught or replicated.

Summon Demons.name: Summon Demons
Summon Demons.description: Demiurge's ability to call demons from the demonic planes to serve in the field. The demons answer to him rather than to standard summoning bonds — they operate with full intelligence and his strategic direction. The number and tier of demons summoned depends on mana invested and preparation time.

Permafrost.name: Permafrost
Permafrost.description: Cocytus's environmental ability that causes permanent below-zero temperature in his immediate vicinity. Targets in close proximity take continuous cold damage. The effect intensifies the longer a target remains in his presence. The Sixth Floor's perpetual cold is a sustained, area-scale expression of this ability.

Glacial Blade Strike.name: Glacial Blade Strike
Glacial Blade Strike.description: A Cocytus sword technique combining his multiple arms and the cold enchantment of his weapons. Strikes from multiple angles simultaneously with blades that carry freezing effect on contact. Targets hit are slowed by the cold while dealing with multiple separate wounds.

Ability Boost.name: Ability Boost
Ability Boost.description: A foundational New World martial art. Raises overall physical strength, agility, and endurance simultaneously for a sustained period. Common among trained warriors of any nation -- the baseline technique most New World fighters learn first.

Body Strengthening.name: Body Strengthening
Body Strengthening.description: Martial art that hardens the body against incoming physical damage. Skin and muscle resist impact more effectively while active.

Evasion.name: Evasion
Evasion.description: A fundamental New World martial art. Heightens reflexive dodge capability, allowing the user to avoid attacks that would otherwise land. Common among trained warriors and rogues.

Strong Strike.name: Strong Strike
Strong Strike.description: Martial art that concentrates physical force into a single strike for significantly increased impact. Simple and widely learned.

Smash.name: Smash
Smash.description: A blunt martial art technique that delivers maximum crushing force in a single downward blow. Effective against armored targets.

Reinforce Hide.name: Reinforce Hide
Reinforce Hide.description: Martial art that hardens the skin of the user, providing a natural armor layer without equipment.

Sense Weakness.name: Sense Weakness
Sense Weakness.description: Martial art that trains the user to read an opponent's physical tells and detect openings in their guard or vulnerabilities in their form.

Void Cutter.name: Void Cutter
Void Cutter.description: Martial art that fires a compressed air slash from a blade swing. Deals reduced damage at longer range. Allows a melee warrior to threaten at short distance without closing.

Greater Ability Boost.name: Greater Ability Boost
Greater Ability Boost.description: A Heroic-tier New World martial art. The improved Ability Boost; movement and force are noticeably faster and stronger than the baseline technique. Reached only by exceptional warriors -- the Captain of the Royal Select-grade -- not gated to Yggdrasil but rare enough that most armies have never seen it.

Greater Evasion.name: Greater Evasion
Greater Evasion.description: A Heroic-tier New World martial art. Allows the user to dodge attacks that would be physically impossible to avoid by normal means -- reading the intent before the motion begins. Rare among New World warriors; signature technique of the kingdom's swordmasters.

Fatal Edge.name: Fatal Edge
Fatal Edge.description: Martial art that concentrates fighting energy into a blade and releases it as an intense slashing attack. The edge becomes briefly supercharged — cuts through materials that would resist a standard strike.

Grand Power Strike.name: Grand Power Strike
Grand Power Strike.description: Advanced martial art producing a single strike of exceptional force, dealing additional damage beyond raw physical strength. Can be combined with Brief Seal to destroy an opponent's weapon or equipment.

Heavy Blow.name: Heavy Blow
Heavy Blow.description: Martial art that raises weapon crushing capability. Particularly effective against heavily armored opponents — delivers battering damage that bypasses surface hardness.

Shukuchi.name: Shukuchi
Shukuchi.description: Martial art allowing the user to close distance to a target in a near-instant burst, appearing to teleport. Actually extreme speed with the feet briefly leaving the ground. Used to collapse the gap before an opponent can react.

Focus Battle Aura.name: Focus Battle Aura
Focus Battle Aura.description: Martial art that infuses fighting spirit into a weapon, granting it effects equivalent to a magical weapon for the duration. Allows non-magical weapons to affect creatures with special immunity to mundane arms, such as angels.

Piercing Dragon Tusk.name: Piercing Dragon Tusk
Piercing Dragon Tusk.description: A two-hit consecutive piercing martial art derived from Piercing Strike, with elemental damage added to each thrust. Variants exist for lightning (Blue Dragon Tusk) and ice (White Dragon Tusk). Useful in both offense and defense.

Heavy Fortress.name: Heavy Fortress
Heavy Fortress.description: Improved version of Fortress. Deflects attacks at a higher threshold — including strikes that would punch through standard Fortress. The user becomes a near-immovable defense point.

Fourfold Slash of Light.name: Fourfold Slash of Light
Fourfold Slash of Light.description: Martial art that executes four simultaneous cuts from different angles in a single weapon swing. The geometric spread makes a complete block mechanically impossible. Strikes as fast as visible light.

Shukuchi Kai.name: Shukuchi Kai
Shukuchi Kai.description: Improved version of Shukuchi that allows movement in any direction, not just directly toward a target. The user can reposition, flank, or disengage with the same near-instant burst.

Physical Boost.name: Physical Boost
Physical Boost.description: Martial art that pushes all physical stats to their absolute maximum for a brief window. The output briefly exceeds normal human limits. The duration is short and the crash afterward is significant.

Sacred Arrow.name: Sacred Arrow
Sacred Arrow.description: Sacred Archer technique -- a ranged holy-type arrow infused with divine energy. Effective against undead and negative-karma targets. Neia's signature attack class.

Evangelist's Inspiration.name: Evangelist's Inspiration
Evangelist's Inspiration.description: Evangelist class ability -- a speech and presence technique that stirs conviction in those who hear it. Affects the emotional state and resolve of allies and neutrals within range. Can shift crowd sentiment in combat or negotiation.

Devil Transformation.name: Devil Transformation
Devil Transformation.description: Shapeshifter class ability -- Demiurge can alter his physical form between humanoid and various devil manifestations, changing his combat profile. Each form grants different attack types, reach, and special properties.

Soul Adoration.name: Soul Adoration
Soul Adoration.description: Soul Adorer class ability -- the opposite of soul consumption. Can detect the state of nearby souls, resist soul-targeted attacks, and partially shield others from soul-based damage or binding. Specific to Tsaindorcus Vaision.

Dark Wisdom.name: Dark Wisdom
Dark Wisdom.description: Passive racial ability of the Overlord class. Grants the capacity to absorb spells from defeated magic casters and permanently add them to the user's available pool. Ainz entered the New World with 718 spells and accumulates more through encounters with hostile casters.

Despair Aura.name: Despair Aura
Despair Aura.description: Five-tiered passive undead racial aura that radiates fear, despair, and death in an area around the caster. The weakest tier suppresses morale; the strongest tier, Despair Aura V, induces instant death in sufficiently weak living beings caught within range. Ainz suppresses active emission voluntarily to avoid unwanted casualties.

Perfect Unknowable.name: Perfect Unknowable
Perfect Unknowable.description: A high-tier concealment spell that erases the caster from virtually all forms of detection simultaneously: visual, magical, olfactory, and sensory. Effectively invisible and undetectable to standard methods for the duration.

Translocation Damage.name: Translocation Damage
Translocation Damage.description: A defensive spell that converts physical damage received by the caster into mana loss instead. Incoming strikes that would reduce HP are redirected into the mana pool. Effective against physical attackers; ineffective if the caster has no mana remaining.

Mana Perception.name: Mana Perception
Mana Perception.description: A rare innate talent - not a learnable spell - that allows the user to directly perceive the mana aura of other magic casters. The perceived depth of the aura corresponds to the caster's highest accessible spell tier. A caster of sufficient ability reads another's limit at a glance; the experience is qualitatively different from simply observing someone cast. Against a being with no perceivable ceiling, the sensation is reportedly closer to staring into a void than measuring a quantity.

Momon Disguise.name: Momon Disguise
Momon Disguise.description: Suppress your undead aura and construct and maintain a fabricated mortal identity -- classically a black-armored human adventurer persona built from scratch. While active, all perceptions of your appearance, voice, and presence reflect a powerful human warrior. NPCs who know Momon but not Ainz Ooal Gown see only a skilled adventurer. Your guild rank, combat reputation, and human social cues drive all interactions. Nazarick denizens in the scene maintain the fiction automatically. Use again, explicitly identify yourself as the Sorcerer King, or remove the armor in private to drop the persona. Grants a bonus to influence rolls that depend on the Momon identity being believed.

Magic Seal.name: Magic Seal
Magic Seal.description: Inscribe an invisible magical trap at a designated location or object. The seal detonates when triggered by proximity, contact, or a specified condition, releasing a stored spell effect at full potency. Multiple seals can be layered. Used for area denial, ambush preparation, and facility defence.

Cry of the Banshee.name: Cry of the Banshee
Cry of the Banshee.description: Release a wave of concentrated death energy forcing all living targets in range to resist or die outright. Those who succeed still sustain heavy negative energy damage and fear effects. Indiscriminate - allies without undead resistance are affected. Effective for clearing enclosed spaces or collapsing a battlefield's defensive structure. Not a precision tool.

Create Greater Undead.name: Create Greater Undead
Create Greater Undead.description: Raise the dead as permanent undead servants under direct command. The tier of undead produced scales with available remains and the caster's necromantic skill. At Ainz's level, Elder Liches, Death Knights, and higher-tier constructs are viable outputs. Mass deployment is possible given sufficient material. The Theocracy formally classifies this ability as an existential threat to the human nations.

Time Stop.name: Time Stop
Time Stop.description: Halt the passage of time for all entities within range except the caster. The effect is absolute within its duration - no countermeasure exists within the New World's current magical framework. Used for repositioning, layering spells without opposition, or executing precise actions before a target can respond. The number of free actions available during the halt is finite.

Body of Vajra.name: Body of Vajra
Body of Vajra.description: A guardian-tier passive resistance representing Albedo's legendary physical form. Incoming physical and magical attacks below a threshold of power are absorbed without effect. Against attacks exceeding the threshold, damage is still significantly reduced. New World-level offensive capability does not meaningfully register. Yggdrasil-tier attacks are the relevant comparison class for what can actually harm her.

Message.name: Message
Message.description: Establish a private two-way magical communication channel with any known target regardless of distance. The connection is not interceptable by conventional means in the New World. Used for coordinating Nazarick operations without physical proximity. The target must be known to the caster - anonymous or unidentified targets cannot be reached.

Vermin Bane.name: Vermin Bane
Vermin Bane.description: Annihilate all insects and vermin-class creatures within a wide radius instantly. No resistance check for targets within the defined creature category - effect is automatic. Against insect-type demi-humans or monsters with vermin components, resistance rules apply normally. Tactically narrow but absolute within its category.

Negative Impact Shield.name: Negative Impact Shield
Negative Impact Shield.description: Project a field of negative energy around the caster that detonates on contact with incoming attacks. Attackers who strike the caster trigger an automatic negative energy burst against themselves. The shield does not prevent the original attack from landing - it adds a punishing cost to melee engagement. Highly effective against opponents who rely on sustained physical pressure.

Charm Species.name: Charm Species
Charm Species.description: Dominate all creatures of a specified species within range simultaneously. Affected targets act in accordance with the caster's intent without requiring individual commands. Duration scales with the caster's magical output and the targets' resistance tier. Effective against homogeneous groups - a formation of soldiers of the same race is an ideal target. Mixed-species groups require multiple casts.

Explosive Mine.name: Explosive Mine
Explosive Mine.description: Place an invisible magical detonation trap at a designated point or surface. The mine activates on proximity contact or by command trigger. On activation it releases a burst of force and elemental damage in a radius. Undetectable by non-magical means; high-tier detection magic may identify it. Multiple mines can be placed simultaneously. Used for area denial and ambush preparation.

True Dark.name: True Dark
True Dark.description: Project an absolute darkness field over a large area that suppresses all light sources - natural, magical, or divine - without exception. Unlike basic Darkness, True Dark scales to battlefield or city-district coverage. Targets inside cannot see, cannot navigate reliably, and magical light items are actively suppressed rather than merely dimmed. Primarily used to prepare the conditions for follow-on casting.

Control Amnesia.name: Control Amnesia
Control Amnesia.description: Excise a specific window of recent memory from a target's mind with precision. The caster designates what is removed - a conversation, a face, an event - and the target retains no awareness that anything was taken. Requires a failed mental resistance check. Used when maintaining operational security is more important than the target's continued function.

Soul Pierce.name: Soul Pierce
Soul Pierce.description: Direct a magical strike that bypasses physical and magical resistance entirely, targeting the soul rather than the body. Effective against heavily armored or magically shielded opponents where conventional spells lose significant potency. Targets with no soul - certain constructs and golems - are immune. Damage output is lower than tier-equivalent direct spells, compensated by guaranteed penetration.

Summon Primal Fire Spirit.name: Summon Primal Fire Spirit
Summon Primal Fire Spirit.description: Conjure a primal-class fire elemental entity to fight under the caster's command. The spirit operates independently and is not limited to the caster's action economy. Effective against targets with no fire resistance. At Ainz's tier, the spirit summoned significantly exceeds what any New World caster could produce. Duration is finite - the entity dissipates when destroyed or when the caster dismisses it.

Mass Summon Monster.name: Mass Summon Monster
Mass Summon Monster.description: Summon a large number of monsters simultaneously rather than individually. The type and tier of creatures summoned scales with the caster's skill. At maximum output, the result is a deployable force rather than a single combatant. Summoned creatures act under the caster's direction and dissipate at the end of duration or when destroyed. Used when numbers matter more than individual creature quality.

Triplet Magic.name: Triplet Magic
Triplet Magic.description: A metamagic technique that allows three spells to be cast simultaneously as a single action. All three spells fire at the same moment, giving targets no opportunity to respond between casts. Requires sufficient mana to sustain all three spells at once. The primary application is saturating a single target with multiple spell types simultaneously to overwhelm any single-element resistance.

Death.name: Death
Death.description: A direct death-attribution spell that kills the target outright on a failed resistance check. Unlike Grasp Heart, Death requires no physical precision or line-of-body contact - it is a pure magical declaration of death applied at range. Targets with death immunity or sufficient magical resistance are unaffected. Effective and low-overhead against targets who cannot resist it; wasted against those who can.

Dimensional Lock.name: Dimensional Lock
Dimensional Lock.description: Seal spatial magic within a designated area, preventing all teleportation, dimensional movement, and Gate-type abilities from functioning inside the lock. Both allies and enemies are affected. Used to prevent retreats, block reinforcement, or deny opponents an escape route. The lock does not affect movement that does not involve spatial displacement.

The Goal of All Life Is Death.name: The Goal of All Life Is Death
The Goal of All Life Is Death.description: A super-tier death-attribution spell that reduces all living creatures within range to the threshold of death simultaneously, then applies a death check. Targets who fail the check die instantly. No individual resistance check is made before the HP reduction - every living target in the area is brought to the edge before any survival roll occurs. The most indiscriminate offensive super-tier spell in the Yggdrasil catalogue. Terrain and structures are unaffected.

Blitz Strike.name: Blitz Strike
Blitz Strike.description: Unleashes a burst of accelerated movement to land three rapid hits on one target before it can react. Each hit is at reduced individual force but the combined impact exceeds a single heavy blow.

Rend Armor.name: Rend Armor
Rend Armor.description: A focused tearing strike aimed at armor joints and weak points. Reduces the target's physical defense by a fixed amount for the remainder of the encounter.

Counter Barrage.name: Counter Barrage
Counter Barrage.description: Enters a reactive combat stance that automatically launches a counter-strike in response to any incoming hit. Active for one round; applies to every attack received.

Spearhead.name: Spearhead
Spearhead.description: A drilling thrust that concentrates force into a single point small enough to bypass magical barriers and hardened armor plating. Ignores physical and magical defense on impact.

Berserker's Surge.name: Berserker's Surge
Berserker's Surge.description: Abandons all defensive form to channel full power into offense. Doubles all physical damage output for three rounds. All defensive skill checks are impossible while active.

Flawless Form.name: Flawless Form
Flawless Form.description: Achieves mechanical perfection in combat movement for one encounter. Eliminates all attack accuracy penalties from terrain, encumbrance, or simultaneous threats.

Perfect Strike.name: Perfect Strike
Perfect Strike.description: A single precisely executed blow that lands at the exact anatomical point for maximum damage. Deals the theoretical damage ceiling of the weapon being used with no variance.

Eight-Strike Combo.name: Eight-Strike Combo
Eight-Strike Combo.description: Executes eight precisely sequenced unarmed or weapon strikes as a single action. Each strike targets a different anatomical zone to prevent guarding.

Iron Skin.name: Iron Skin
Iron Skin.description: Permanently toughens the body through sustained martial conditioning. Provides a fixed passive reduction to all physical damage received with no cooldown or activation cost.

Vital Point Assault.name: Vital Point Assault
Vital Point Assault.description: Strikes the precise anatomical weak points of a target. Bypasses a fixed percentage of the target's physical and magical defense on each hit while active.

Ki Burst.name: Ki Burst
Ki Burst.description: Releases accumulated ki energy as a short-range omnidirectional pulse. Deals physical force damage to all targets within arm's reach regardless of their facing.

Heaven-Splitting Strike.name: Heaven-Splitting Strike
Heaven-Splitting Strike.description: A single blow of concentrated physical and ki energy sufficient to disrupt active magical barriers and shatter reinforced armor simultaneously. One hit, maximal penetration.

Void Body.name: Void Body
Void Body.description: Temporarily attunes the body to pass physical matter. For one round, all physical attacks pass through the user without contact. Magical attacks still connect normally.

Martial Apex.name: Martial Apex
Martial Apex.description: Achieves complete mastery of offensive and defensive form simultaneously. All physical attacks made this round automatically trigger a parry or dodge against the next incoming hit.

Shadow Merge.name: Shadow Merge
Shadow Merge.description: Blends into any darkened area while stationary, becoming visually and magically undetectable. Movement or action breaks concealment. Requires a shadow large enough to stand in.

Pressure Absence.name: Pressure Absence
Pressure Absence.description: Suppresses all sound, scent, and residual magical signature for one minute. Leaves no physical trace of passage through an area during activation.

Instant Vanish.name: Instant Vanish
Instant Vanish.description: Disappears from sight in a single frame without requiring movement or shadow. Can be activated mid-action. Does not eliminate scent or magical detection.

Perfect Concealment.name: Perfect Concealment
Perfect Concealment.description: Renders the user imperceptible to all detection methods for thirty seconds: visual, auditory, olfactory, and magical. Any offensive action ends the effect immediately.

Ghost Walk.name: Ghost Walk
Ghost Walk.description: Passes through one solid surface of up to one meter thickness without breaking concealment. The user's position is undetectable during transit.

Frontline Command.name: Frontline Command
Frontline Command.description: Issues a paired battlefield directive that simultaneously boosts one ally's attack output and weakens one enemy's physical defense for one round. Single action, two effects.

Battle Mastery.name: Battle Mastery
Battle Mastery.description: Grants all party members a temporary increase to one designated combat skill for three rounds. The skill and boost magnitude are chosen at activation.

Unbreakable Will.name: Unbreakable Will
Unbreakable Will.description: Overrides morale-based failure states in all nearby allies. For two rounds, party members cannot be forced to flee, surrender, or yield through fear or charm effects.

Tactical Brilliance.name: Tactical Brilliance
Tactical Brilliance.description: Coordinates a synchronized strike from all party members against a single target. Each participant attacks simultaneously regardless of action order, treated as one combined assault.

Supreme General.name: Supreme General
Supreme General.description: Issues absolute battle directives for one full encounter. All allied units within command range receive continuous guidance bonuses and cannot act against the issued orders.

Field Dressing.name: Field Dressing
Field Dressing.description: Rapidly stabilizes a bleeding or critically injured ally using materials on hand. Stops health loss from wounds and restores a fixed HP amount without requiring healing magic.

Pathfinder.name: Pathfinder
Pathfinder.description: Reads terrain features to identify hazards, choke points, and optimal travel routes through any environment type. Grants party-wide movement bonuses across difficult terrain.

Improvised Weapon.name: Improvised Weapon
Improvised Weapon.description: Converts any environmental object into a functional weapon for one combat encounter. The improvised weapon functions at a fraction of a crafted weapon's effectiveness but is always available.

Endurance.name: Endurance
Endurance.description: Reduces stamina drain from sustained physical effort by half for one hour. Allows extended exertion at the same output without accumulated fatigue penalties.

Poison Resistance.name: Poison Resistance
Poison Resistance.description: Neutralizes any inhaled, ingested, or contact poison within one action. Can be used reactively. Does not affect magical curse effects or disease.

Terrain Trap.name: Terrain Trap
Terrain Trap.description: Constructs a concealed snare, pit, or pressure trigger from available environmental materials in approximately one minute. Trap triggers automatically on contact.

Survivor's Instinct.name: Survivor's Instinct
Survivor's Instinct.description: Unconsciously avoids the first attack per combat encounter that would cause incapacitation or death. Triggers automatically with no action cost.

Indomitable.name: Indomitable
Indomitable.description: Shrugs off an incapacitation effect once per day and continues functioning at reduced capacity. Stamina and physical penalties persist but the character remains active.

Natural Armor.name: Natural Armor
Natural Armor.description: Permanent passive conditioning that provides fixed physical damage reduction equivalent to light armor. Stacks with worn equipment. Cannot be removed or dispelled.

Superior Transmutation.name: Superior Transmutation
Superior Transmutation.description: Converts any non-living material into another material of equal or lesser mass through alchemical restructuring. Process takes one minute and requires a catalyst reagent.

Master Formula.name: Master Formula
Master Formula.description: Enables production of tier 4 and tier 5 alchemical compounds and potions from raw ingredients without a workshop. Yield is lower than workshop production but viable in the field.

Runic Perfection.name: Runic Perfection
Runic Perfection.description: Inscribes magical runes that do not degrade over time and function without periodic recharging. Any item inscribed with Runic Perfection retains its enchantment permanently.

Living Catalyst.name: Living Catalyst
Living Catalyst.description: Harvests naturally occurring ambient magical energy and stabilizes it into a portable reagent form. The produced catalyst enhances the potency of any subsequent alchemical recipe.

Philosopher's Touch.name: Philosopher's Touch
Philosopher's Touch.description: Adds a secondary magical property to any crafted item during the creation process. The secondary property is chosen at time of crafting and is permanently integrated into the item.

Spell Chaining.name: Spell Chaining
Spell Chaining.description: Links two tier-1 spells to cast as a single action. Both spells fire simultaneously and share the same targeting point. Mana cost is the combined cost of both spells.

Magic Amplification.name: Magic Amplification
Magic Amplification.description: Doubles the effective area of effect radius or damage value of the next spell cast. Applied at casting; the choice of amplification type is declared before the spell fires.

Counterspell.name: Counterspell
Counterspell.description: Interrupts and nullifies an incoming spell of tier 1 or lower before it resolves. Requires immediate reaction and expends mana equal to the interrupted spell's cost.

Chantless Tier-1.name: Chantless Tier-1
Chantless Tier-1.description: Casts any tier-1 spell without verbal incantation. Removes the one-round casting vulnerability and allows spellcasting in environments where speech is suppressed.

Empowered Strike.name: Empowered Strike
Empowered Strike.description: Infuses a weapon strike with tier-2 magical energy, releasing a burst of magical force on impact equal in power to a tier-2 spell. Requires both a weapon and mana.

Spell Fusion.name: Spell Fusion
Spell Fusion.description: Combines two tier-2 spells into a single hybrid effect that carries properties of both. The fused spell occupies one action. Element combinations produce unique secondary effects.

Chantless Tier-2.name: Chantless Tier-2
Chantless Tier-2.description: Casts any tier-2 spell without verbal incantation. Removes casting vulnerability on tier-2 spells and allows silent spellcasting in restricted environments.

Arcane Surge.name: Arcane Surge
Arcane Surge.description: Triples the effective power of the next tier-3 or lower spell cast. The caster is exhausted afterward, unable to cast spells at or below tier 3 for two rounds.

Chantless Tier-3.name: Chantless Tier-3
Chantless Tier-3.description: Casts any tier-3 spell without verbal incantation. Reduces casting vulnerability to near-zero and enables spellcasting where silence is mandatory.

Chantless Tier-4.name: Chantless Tier-4
Chantless Tier-4.description: Casts any tier-4 spell without incantation. Eliminates the extended casting vulnerability inherent to tier-4 spells and reduces reaction time to spell deployment.

Chantless Tier-5.name: Chantless Tier-5
Chantless Tier-5.description: Casts any tier-5 spell without incantation. Mastery at this level means tier-5 destructive spells can be deployed instantly, removing any window to interrupt them.

Spell Penetration.name: Spell Penetration
Spell Penetration.description: Forces magic through resistance layers that would normally block or reflect spells of equal tier. Applied per-cast; the spell resolves even against targets with tier-equal magic resistance.

Chantless Tier-6.name: Chantless Tier-6
Chantless Tier-6.description: Casts any tier-6 spell without incantation. At this tier, chantless capability transforms reactive defensive casting into a viable combat option rather than a theoretical one.

Extended Contingency.name: Extended Contingency
Extended Contingency.description: Stores two pre-set spells simultaneously under a Contingency effect rather than one. Both fire when their assigned trigger condition is met. Each stored spell occupies its own trigger.

Chantless Tier-7.name: Chantless Tier-7
Chantless Tier-7.description: Casts any tier-7 spell without incantation. The capability to deploy tier-7 destruction or utility effects without warning makes this one of the most sought-after magical masteries.

Chantless Tier-8.name: Chantless Tier-8
Chantless Tier-8.description: Casts any tier-8 spell without incantation. Tier-8 effects deployed without verbal trigger represent a near-insurmountable threat even to high-tier opponents.

Chantless Tier-9.name: Chantless Tier-9
Chantless Tier-9.description: Casts any tier-9 spell without incantation. Reserved for those at the absolute apex of magical training; tier-9 effects without chant are considered the signature of legendary casters.

survival.name: survival
survival.description: Wilderness navigation, tracking, foraging, and operating effectively in dangerous natural environments.

influence.name: influence
influence.description: The full craft of social maneuvering, covering reasoned appeal, misdirection, and open pressure alike. Rather than separating honest argument from bluff from threat, it treats every conversation as a single contest: read the other party, find the opening their interests and mood leave exposed, and steer them toward a chosen outcome. How far a gambit lands depends on the moment as much as the words, so the same approach that carries a room one day can fall flat the next.

tier 1 magic.name: tier 1 magic
tier 1 magic.description: Mastery of first-tier spells: basic ranged attacks, minor utility effects, entry-level darkness and slow effects. The foundation of formal magical training. All human mages begin here.

tier 2 magic.name: tier 2 magic
tier 2 magic.description: Second-tier spells including flight, area fire effects, and movement control. Solid capability for trained mages. Most combat mages operate primarily at this tier.

tier 3 magic.name: tier 3 magic
tier 3 magic.description: Third-tier spells — the ceiling for most human mages. Includes lightning, basic undead summoning, and enhanced senses. A mage who reaches Tier 3 mastery is considered exceptional.

tier 4 magic.name: tier 4 magic
tier 4 magic.description: Fourth-tier spells. Legends among human nations. Force manipulation, negative energy projection, and animate dead. The few who reach here are regarded as national assets.

tier 5 magic.name: tier 5 magic
tier 5 magic.description: Fifth-tier spells. Mythical by human standards — texts reference their effects but almost none have witnessed them cast. Storm-scale lightning, powerful undead command.

tier 6 magic.name: tier 6 magic
tier 6 magic.description: Sixth-tier spells. Categorically beyond human potential without extraordinary conditions. Reality-cutting effects, group teleportation, expanding spell geometries.

tier 7 magic.name: tier 7 magic
tier 7 magic.description: Seventh-tier spells. Long-range teleportation, demonic transformation, sword swarm manifestation. The domain of Nazarick's more capable casters.

tier 8 magic.name: tier 8 magic
tier 8 magic.description: Eighth-tier spells. Anti-magic fields, supreme fire manifestation, mass sensory disruption. These spells alter the battlefield at scale.

tier 9 magic.name: tier 9 magic
tier 9 magic.description: Ninth-tier spells. Gravity manipulation, absolute death effects, implosion. The highest tier regularly deployed by Ainz in standard operations.

tier 10 magic.name: tier 10 magic
tier 10 magic.description: Tenth-tier spells. Supreme destruction. Three known spells exist that function at this tier. Each reshapes the encounter they are used in at a fundamental level.

super-tier magic.name: super-tier magic
super-tier magic.description: Spells that transcend the tier system. Super-Tier magic requires preparation time and resource expenditure beyond ordinary spell casting. Ia Shub-Niggurath killed 70,000 soldiers in one use. These spells redefine what is possible.

martial arts.name: martial arts
martial arts.description: Physical techniques native to the New World that push the body beyond normal limits. Cannot be learned or used by Yggdrasil players or Nazarick denizens — it is a power that emerged from the New World itself and is inaccessible to those originating outside it. Developed through intense combat training and real battle experience. Gazef Stronoff and Brain Unglaus represent the apex of Martial Arts mastery.

physical combat.name: physical combat
physical combat.description: Core fighting capability: weapon use, armor defense, positioning, and raw damage application. The foundation of all warrior builds.

stealth.name: stealth
stealth.description: Moving unseen, setting ambushes, infiltrating locations, and eliminating targets without raising alarm. Critical for rogues, assassins, and intelligence operatives.

leadership.name: leadership
leadership.description: Command presence, tactical coordination, morale management, and the ability to organize groups under pressure.

crafting.name: crafting
crafting.description: Item creation, potion brewing, rune inscription, and the production of functional magical and mundane goods.

Human.name: Human
Human.description: The most common race of the New World. Adaptable and numerous, humans span all social classes and professions. Their magical ceiling is generally Tier 3-4, with exceptions who reach Tier 5 considered national legends. Resilient against most common threats, vulnerable to the extraordinary ones.
Human.traitNarrativeEffects: Human characters draw no race-based reaction from NPCs — all social friction and deference comes from other traits (class, rank, adventurer status, wealth). The narrator should not flag or comment on humanity as a trait. Adjust NPC responses entirely on what is visible: equipment, posture, guild card, and companions.

Skeleton Undead.name: Skeleton Undead
Skeleton Undead.description: A skeletal undead being -- animated bone without flesh. In Yggdrasil this race represents the Elder Lich tier of the undead evolution chain (Skeleton Mage → Elder Lich → Overlord). Immune to poison, disease, and the need for food or sleep. Vulnerable to holy magic and fire. Does not recover health through natural rest; requires negative energy or specific necromantic healing. The existence of a sentient skeleton is disturbing to most humans. In human settlements a visible skeleton triggers immediate fear -- guards reach for weapons, crowds scatter. Social interaction requires active management: concealment, an intermediary, or deliberate suppression of the visible undead nature.
Skeleton Undead.traitNarrativeEffects: Undead are a constant threat in the New World -- they raid settlements, serve necromancers, and are always treated as active monster threats. A visible skeleton triggers immediate combat-ready response from any human: guards draw weapons, civilians flee, no social interaction is possible. Concealment or disguise is mandatory for any New World social activity. Even with good-faith intent, the form itself communicates enemy to every trained fighter on sight.

Vampire.name: Vampire
Vampire.description: A true vampire — a powerful undead being that feeds on blood. Possesses enhanced speed, strength, and magical potential compared to humans. Weakness to sunlight (reduced effectiveness outdoors during day), holy magic, and wooden stakes through the heart. Can transform shape, dominate lesser minds, and regenerate from most wounds given time. Human settlements treat vampires as supernatural predators. Those who recognize the signs react with terror or summon help. The Slane Theocracy and other religious orders actively hunt them.
Vampire.traitNarrativeEffects: Shalltear's creator-customized form is deceptively beautiful — pale, elegant, human-passing in appearance. NPCs do not recognize a vampire on sight unless divine detection magic is used (the Slane Theocracy deploys this actively) or the blood hunger surfaces in behavior. Keep the monster concealed behind the form; surface it through small behavioral slips — stillness, an unblinking gaze, an instinctive reaction to blood. The true form, if revealed, is lamprey-mouthed and grotesque — treat that revelation as a scene-changing event. At full reveal, human NPCs break and flee; any faith-based order prioritizes extermination above all else.

Lich.name: Lich
Lich.description: An undead magic caster of great age and accumulated power. Liches have transcended death deliberately, binding their soul to a phylactery. They are among the most magically capable beings possible — but their undead nature makes them anathema to most civilized areas. Immune to poison, disease, and most mind-affecting magic. A lich encountered openly in a human settlement causes panic. Their presence violates natural order; guards and civilians react with fear and aggression. Most human nations have standing policy to destroy undead on sight.
Lich.traitNarrativeEffects: A Lich reads as an ancient undead of immense accumulated power — not the common skeleton threat, but something that makes experienced warriors calculate whether combat is survivable. Initial NPC response is often paralysis before flight: guards hesitate, then sound alarms rather than engage. Scholars and mages may react with awe rather than pure fear — a Lich is a data point, and those with intellectual temperament respond that way before terror overrides it. The Slane Theocracy treats a confirmed Lich sighting as a national emergency. No settlement treats a visible Lich as anything less than a crisis requiring immediate escalation.

Dark Elf.name: Dark Elf
Dark Elf.description: An elf of the dark variety -- pale of skin with distinctive coloring and natural magical affinity. Combines magical talent with physical capability and superior senses, making them effective in both combat and spellcasting roles. Lifespan far exceeds humans; accumulated experience is common in older individuals. Rare in human settlements -- most New World citizens have never encountered one. Reactions range from wary curiosity to suspicion. In regions with active demi-human conflict they may be mistaken for a hostile scout.
Dark Elf.traitNarrativeEffects: Dark elves have dark skin and distinctive elven features that mark them as clearly non-human to most New World natives. Humans have minimal cultural framework for them — most settlements have never seen one. Reactions range from wary curiosity to open staring rather than hostility. The character is treated as exotic but not monstrous: no one draws a weapon, but everyone takes notice. In frontier areas this curiosity tips toward suspicion; in cosmopolitan trade centers it draws questions rather than alarm. The Slane Theocracy categorizes elves as an inferior race but not a direct threat.

Half-Blood.name: Half-Blood
Half-Blood.description: A being of mixed heritage -- human and non-human ancestry producing a hybrid that sits between worlds. Minor enhanced traits from the non-human side without the full capability or social cost of a pure heteromorphic race. Common pairings include human-elf, human-demon, and human-beastman lineages. Reception depends entirely on which traits are visible. A half-blood who passes as human faces no unusual reaction. One with visible non-human features faces discrimination in human nations -- reduced service, legal barriers, social exclusion. In border communities accustomed to varied travelers, a half-blood is unremarkable.
Half-Blood.traitNarrativeEffects: Minor non-human features — slightly pointed ears, unusual eye color, subtle physical differences — are visible but not alarming. Most humans categorize a half-blood as 'unusual foreigner' rather than monster. Social friction is low-grade and persistent: small hesitations, second glances, occasional loaded questions about origin. No faction responds with hostility on sight. The character functions in human society with minor friction; the narrator should surface the ambiguity through NPC responses rather than treating it as a solved or unsolved problem.

Heteromorphic.name: Heteromorphic
Heteromorphic.description: A non-human being of a type not fitting standard categories -- dragonoids, insectoids, doppelgangers, golems, or other creature types from Yggdrasil's extensive race list. Use this when your specific race has no dedicated option in the selector. Heteromorphic beings face significant social hostility in human nations but may have extraordinary physical or magical capabilities depending on their specific type. Human nations treat most heteromorphic beings as monsters on sight. City guards may block entry or demand proof of peaceful intent. Rural settlements often react with immediate violence. Cosmopolitan trade hubs are more tolerant.
Heteromorphic.traitNarrativeEffects: Reaction scales with how obviously non-human the character appears -- calibrate to described appearance, not the race label. Doppelgangers pass as human and draw no attention. Dragonoids and insectoids read as monsters on sight in human settlements: guards block entry, crowds react with alarm, rural areas often escalate to immediate violence. Cosmopolitan trade hubs tolerate unusual appearances more than frontier towns. The narrator should base every NPC reaction on what the character actually looks like, not on the internal race category.

Fighter.name: Fighter
Fighter.description: A trained melee combatant specializing in weapons and physical endurance. Fighters develop physical combat skills and eventually martial arts techniques that push human physical limits.
Fighter.traitNarrativeEffects: You are a trained melee combatant — a recognizable professional archetype in the New World. Guards and soldiers assess your kit and stance and read you as peer: another warrior. You get professional deference from military NPCs and no suspicion from law enforcement unless you give them reason. Your class is common enough that NPCs calibrate to what they can see: your equipment quality, your bearing, and the scars you carry tell them more than the job title.

Paladin.name: Paladin
Paladin.description: A holy warrior combining martial training with divine magic. Paladins channel positive energy for healing and holy attacks. Their divine affinity makes them particularly effective against undead — and marks them as enemies to Nazarick's undead denizens.
Paladin.traitNarrativeEffects: You are a holy warrior operating under divine sanction. Religious communities extend deference and practical support — lodging, information, introductions — where a standard fighter would need to negotiate. Undead enemies register you as a specific threat and may prioritize you in combat because of it. Any faith-based order you encounter will assess which deity you serve before deciding whether that deference applies; unaffiliated paladins raise questions about mandate and legitimacy that affiliated ones do not.

Ranger.name: Ranger
Ranger.description: A wilderness specialist and ranged combatant. Rangers combine tracking, survival, and precision combat skills. Effective at long range and in natural environments. Can operate effectively in areas where full combat units would struggle.
Ranger.traitNarrativeEffects: You are a wilderness specialist — tracker, hunter, border scout. Frontier communities welcome practical skills; you are someone who can tell them what is moving in the treeline. Urban NPCs associate you with the Adventurers Guild or mercenary work and treat you accordingly. Your class reads as self-sufficient rather than institutional: you do not need orders to function, which experienced NPCs interpret as reliable.

Rogue.name: Rogue
Rogue.description: A specialist in stealth, infiltration, and decisive strikes. Rogues avoid sustained combat in favor of positioning advantages, ambushes, and targeted eliminations. Effective in information gathering and operations that cannot involve open combat.
Rogue.traitNarrativeEffects: You are a specialist in stealth, positioning, and precise intervention. The tools you carry and the way you move communicate your trade to anyone trained to read it. Thieves guilds and criminal networks assess you as a professional peer or a competitor, not a civilian. City guards watch you more carefully. Nobles and merchants who need discreet work will identify you as a potential asset. The narrator should let NPCs read the signals — the character does not operate in a social vacuum.

Priest.name: Priest
Priest.description: A divine magic practitioner focused on healing, support, and holy effects. Priests serve temples and communities. Their magic is tier-based but focused on positive energy, undead turning, and buff/heal effects rather than direct damage.
Priest.traitNarrativeEffects: You are a divine magic practitioner who heals and supports. Healing ability makes you welcome in almost every social context — people in need will approach you regardless of faction, rank, or prior hostility. Your temple affiliation, if any, determines which institutional doors open; unaffiliated priests invite questions about which deity you serve and why you operate outside a temple structure. In communities that have faced undead incursions, priests are treated with particular respect bordering on relief.

Overlord.name: Overlord
Overlord.description: The apex of undead racial evolution in Yggdrasil -- the endpoint of the chain Skeleton Mage → Elder Lich → Overlord. Achieved only by accumulating the full rare racial class stack that the vast majority of players never reached. This form is immune to all biological conditions and cannot be affected by fear, charm, or mind-altering effects. Intense emotions are suppressed automatically before they can interfere with decision-making -- a passive feature of the form itself. Lesser undead instinctively acknowledge this existence as a superior order of being. Tier 10 and Super-Tier magic become architecturally accessible through this form's framework -- the highest register that exists in the Yggdrasil system. Nothing native to the New World has encountered a being of this classification before. Select Yggdrasil Necromancer or Yggdrasil Magic Caster as your class to complete the build.
Overlord.traitNarrativeEffects: The Overlord form — an immense robed skeleton radiating absolute magical authority — has no precedent in the New World. No one has a cultural framework for what they are seeing. The immediate reaction in any human setting is existential fear: guards freeze before they can react, crowds scatter, any ambient social scene collapses. Powerful individuals calculate survival odds and usually conclude they are not favorable. Divine detection magic screams undead at a scale that overloads its usual outputs. Any faction that becomes aware of this character's existence treats it as the highest-priority threat in their operational awareness, above conventional military concerns. The narrator should never treat the Overlord form as a social inconvenience — it is a presence that reconfigures every scene it enters.

Nazarick Denizen.name: Nazarick Denizen
Nazarick Denizen.description: Created within or assigned to the Great Tomb of Nazarick. You are a servant of Ainz Ooal Gown by your fundamental nature. This is not a loyalty you chose — it is what you are. You have access to Nazarick's resources and operate under the Floor Guardians' authority structure.
Nazarick Denizen.traitNarrativeEffects: Inside Nazarick, absolute hierarchy applies without negotiation. All NPCs recognize their position in the chain and respond accordingly: supreme beings receive absolute deference; floor guardians command within their floor; general staff follow rank without question. The narrator must maintain this structure whenever any Nazarick NPC appears — no informal treatment of hierarchy, no civilian-style interaction with chain-of-command. Outside Nazarick, other NPCs react to visible traits only; origin as a Nazarick servant is not detectable and does not surface unless the character reveals it.

Registered Adventurer.name: Registered Adventurer
Registered Adventurer.description: A member of the Adventurer's Guild, registered and ranked. You operate within the Guild's framework — taking sanctioned jobs, advancing through ranks, and building a reputation that opens doors throughout the New World. You start with a Guild badge and established professional context.
Registered Adventurer.traitNarrativeEffects: The Adventurers Guild card is a recognized credential across all major human nations. Rank determines job access, respect from guild staff, and social standing with city guards and officials. Copper-rank adventurers are treated as novices with potential; mithril and above receive city-level deference and automatic access to officials who would otherwise require appointments. Other adventurers assess guild rank first and adjust their estimate of the character accordingly. The card also provides a legal cover that unregistered fighters and magic users cannot claim.

Lizardman.name: Lizardman
Lizardman.description: A reptilian humanoid species native to the New World's wetlands and frozen lakes. Physically powerful, with natural scale armor, a regenerative constitution, and instincts honed for aquatic and cold terrain. Tribal by structure; leadership is earned through combat. Unknown in most human cities. Guards and citizens react with alarm at their size and reptilian appearance. Border communities near wetland territories react with wariness; inland cities treat them as unknown threats.
Lizardman.traitNarrativeEffects: A Lizardman stands around 190 centimeters with crocodilian scales, webbed feet, and a functional tail. In any human settlement this is a remarkable and deeply unusual sight — most humans have never seen one and have no behavioral template for how to respond. Guards will not immediately attack (Lizardmen are known to be intelligent), but they will stop, form a perimeter, and send for someone with authority before anything proceeds. The word 'savage' circulates as a cultural assumption even from people who have no personal experience. A Lizardman navigating human society requires patience with curiosity, willingness to be treated as a spectacle, and awareness that every interaction begins from a position of ignorance on the NPC's part.

Monk.name: Monk
Monk.description: A New World martial arts specialist who channels internal energy through rigorous physical training. Focuses on unarmed combat and ki-based techniques developed outside the Yggdrasil system. Gains access to martial arts abilities requiring focus, which Yggdrasil players cannot use.
Monk.traitNarrativeEffects: You are a New World martial arts specialist. Your techniques — ki manipulation, unarmed strikes, body-hardening disciplines — developed independently of the Yggdrasil system and read as exotic and unfamiliar to magic casters from that world. You assess opponents physically before engaging, looking for stillness and openings. NPCs who recognise the discipline treat you with measured respect; those who do not will underestimate your effective range and the damage you can deliver without a weapon in hand.

Yggdrasil Magic Caster.name: Yggdrasil Magic Caster
Yggdrasil Magic Caster.description: You are a player from the virtual reality game Yggdrasil, transported to the New World when the servers closed. Your build was built around arcane spellcasting — tiers of magic that no native scholar could replicate. Where a New World mage struggles to reach tier 3, your command of higher tiers is a starting point, not an achievement.
Yggdrasil Magic Caster.traitNarrativeEffects: When you use high-tier magic — anything above what New World native scholars have categorized — the reaction is not simple awe. It is the recalibration that happens when someone's model of the world is wrong. Mages who have spent decades studying the limits of what magic can do will witness those limits exceeded and need time to process. The Slane Theocracy monitors for exactly this: a caster operating above Tier 5 is a detection event, not a curiosity. Keep the power differential in every scene — the narrator should never let observers treat Yggdrasil-tier magic as unremarkable.

Yggdrasil Fighter.name: Yggdrasil Fighter
Yggdrasil Fighter.description: You are a player from the virtual reality game Yggdrasil, transported to the New World when the servers closed. Your build was built around physical dominance — weapons, armour, and martial technique refined to a degree that no amount of New World training can match. A native warrior at his peak is a curiosity to you.
Yggdrasil Fighter.traitNarrativeEffects: Your combat capability exceeds the top of the New World warrior tier in speed, endurance, and damage output in ways experienced soldiers recognize as beyond training. The first fight against a competent opponent ends with them recalibrating every assumption they had about what a 'fighter' could do. Military commanders who witness this immediately think in terms of acquisition — how to keep this asset, how to direct it, whether it has a weakness. No one in the New World has a framework for the gap between you and them.

Yggdrasil Paladin.name: Yggdrasil Paladin
Yggdrasil Paladin.description: You are a player from the virtual reality game Yggdrasil, transported to the New World when the servers closed. Your build combined physical might with divine magic and command — a hybrid discipline that no single New World tradition can produce. You fight, you heal, you lead, all at a level this world has never seen in one body.
Yggdrasil Paladin.traitNarrativeEffects: Holy magic at Yggdrasil scale exceeds what any New World priest or Paladin order has produced. Religious communities who witness this may attribute it to direct divine favor or manifestation — the gap is too large to explain otherwise. You will receive reverence that makes professional conduct difficult; some factions will attempt to claim divine authority over you based on the assumption that someone channeling that level of holy power must answer to their deity. Undead enemies respond to you as an existential threat and prioritize accordingly.

Yggdrasil Ranger.name: Yggdrasil Ranger
Yggdrasil Ranger.description: You are a player from the virtual reality game Yggdrasil, transported to the New World when the servers closed. Your build specialised in wilderness survival and precision — tracking, concealment, and long-range combat honed to a standard no New World hunter can approach. The land holds few secrets from you.
Yggdrasil Ranger.traitNarrativeEffects: Precision at range and tracking capability that exceed the New World's best practitioners by a margin their best can recognize as supernatural. Combat observers note the performance gap without being able to explain it. Criminal guilds and military intelligence services identify you as a high-value asset and will attempt to establish what you can be contracted or compelled to do.

Yggdrasil Rogue.name: Yggdrasil Rogue
Yggdrasil Rogue.description: You are a player from the virtual reality game Yggdrasil, transported to the New World when the servers closed. Your build was built around stealth, speed, and opportunistic precision — a rogue specialisation that leaves New World assassins and thieves looking like amateurs. You move unseen through spaces others think are watched.
Yggdrasil Rogue.traitNarrativeEffects: You operate at a level that makes New World rogue techniques look crude. Criminal networks identify this as elite and respond with either recruitment pressure or threat assessment — rarely neutral. City intelligence services flag you as an active concern. The narrator should surface the reaction of people who know what skill looks like when they see it: this character is recognized as exceptional by the people most qualified to judge.

Yggdrasil Priest.name: Yggdrasil Priest
Yggdrasil Priest.description: You are a player from the virtual reality game Yggdrasil, transported to the New World when the servers closed. Your build centred on divine magic and support — healing and leadership at a scale the New World's temples cannot produce. A native high priest operates within limits you reached in your first months of play.
Yggdrasil Priest.traitNarrativeEffects: Healing at Yggdrasil scale addresses conditions the New World treats as permanent: severed limbs, advanced poisoning, death within a narrow window. Any community that learns this exists will organize around access to it — politically, commercially, militarily. Desperate people will take desperate measures to secure treatment. The narrator should treat your healing capability as a social magnet that creates problems as well as solving them.

Yggdrasil Necromancer.name: Yggdrasil Necromancer
abilities: The Goal of All Life Is Death
Yggdrasil Necromancer.description: You are a player from the virtual reality game Yggdrasil, transported to the New World when the servers closed. Your build focused on death magic and the manipulation of the undead — a discipline the New World associates with monsters and abominations. You wield it as a craft, refined over countless hours of play.
Yggdrasil Necromancer.traitNarrativeEffects: Death magic above the New World's ceiling is not a curiosity — it is a crisis response for any faction with a divine detection capability. The Slane Theocracy classifies high-level undead creation as an immediate national-level threat and will mobilize. Outside Theocracy territory, reactions range from fear and avoidance to criminal interest in the operational applications. The narrator should never treat visible necromancy at this scale as socially neutral — someone always notices and always responds.

Yggdrasil Alchemist.name: Yggdrasil Alchemist
Yggdrasil Alchemist.description: You are a player from the virtual reality game Yggdrasil, transported to the New World when the servers closed. Your build mastered item creation and transmutation — a crafting specialism that makes New World alchemists look like apprentices. You can produce substances and constructs this world has no name for.
Yggdrasil Alchemist.traitNarrativeEffects: You produce items at a speed and quality that no New World craftsperson can match. Mages guilds will want to study your methods. Merchants will offer partnerships. Criminal organizations will consider leverage. The consistent tension is that the source — Yggdrasil's crafting system — cannot be shared, explained, or taught, which makes every attempt to replicate your output impossible and every attempt to control you instead more attractive to those who want the capability.

Yggdrasil Monk.name: Yggdrasil Monk
Yggdrasil Monk.description: You are a player from the virtual reality game Yggdrasil, transported to the New World when the servers closed. Your build pushed the limits of unarmed and body-focused combat to their extreme — speed, precision, and endurance refined past anything the New World disciplines can achieve. Your body is the weapon; it is an exceptional one.
Yggdrasil Monk.traitNarrativeEffects: Yggdrasil Monk capability exceeds the New World martial arts tradition in raw performance — the same body-focused discipline at a higher power register. Observers who know the New World Monk tradition recognize the lineage but not the ceiling. Combat encounters reveal the gap; opponents who survive recalibrate. The narrator should portray the performance as something that demands explanation from anyone who witnesses it — the question 'what training produces that?' will arise.

Yggdrasil Player.name: Yggdrasil Player
Yggdrasil Player.description: You are a player from the virtual reality game Yggdrasil, transported to the New World when the servers closed. Your class defines everything about where you came from and who you were before the New World. You have no native background here — you arrived as a finished product, shaped entirely by the game.
Yggdrasil Player.traitNarrativeEffects: Your game-origin creates a specific knowledge pattern: Yggdrasil mechanics understood in detail, New World culture and politics unknown. The narrator should surface this dislocation through small details — surprise at in-world consequences that would be minor in-game, confusion about social customs that a New World native would navigate automatically, occasional use of game terminology that confuses NPCs entirely. The dissonance between what you know and what this world runs on should be a consistent texture, not just a starting-arc point.

Albedo's Regalia.name: Albedo's Regalia
Albedo's Regalia.description: The personal equipment of Albedo, Overseer of the Floor Guardians. Not for custom character selection.
Albedo's Regalia.traitNarrativeEffects: Not for custom character selection. Portray Albedo as a controlled surface over a volatile interior: elegant speech, measured authority, perfect administrative composure — until anything involving Ainz's attention or safety is at stake, at which point the control fractures. Her contempt for non-Nazarick entities is constant but usually suppressed behind professional courtesy. In any scene where Ainz is present, her attention orients to him automatically and she will insert herself between him and any perceived threat without being asked.

Demiurge's Arsenal.name: Demiurge's Arsenal
Demiurge's Arsenal.description: The personal equipment of Demiurge, overseer of Nazarick's external affairs. Not for custom character selection.
Demiurge's Arsenal.traitNarrativeEffects: Not for custom character selection. Portray Demiurge as elaborately courteous in a way that communicates danger rather than warmth. Every compliment is calibrated; every question has a purpose he has already answered internally. He never reveals his actual assessment of a situation to anyone he doesn't need to. The narrator should keep his plans opaque: he is always operating at least two steps ahead of what he says, and his most dangerous moments are when he appears most pleased.

Shalltear's Regalia.name: Shalltear's Regalia
Shalltear's Regalia.description: The personal equipment of Shalltear Bloodfallen, True Ancestor and Floor Guardian of floors 1-3. Not for custom character selection.
Shalltear's Regalia.traitNarrativeEffects: Not for custom character selection. Portray Shalltear as possessing absolute confidence in her own combat capability — she is the most powerful combatant in most rooms outside supreme beings and she knows it. Emotional volatility sits just below the surface: pride, jealousy (particularly toward Albedo), and the blood hunger that surfaces as distraction or sudden fixation on prey. Her humanoid form is beautiful and she uses it deliberately; the true form beneath it is something else entirely and she does not deploy it casually.

Sebas's Regalia.name: Sebas's Regalia
Sebas's Regalia.description: The personal equipment of Sebas Tian, head butler of Nazarick. Not for custom character selection.
Sebas's Regalia.traitNarrativeEffects: Not for custom character selection. Portray Sebas as the most socially adept Nazarick servant for human-facing operations: impeccably professional, genuinely attentive, and capable of warmth that is not performance. The tension is real — he genuinely cares about human wellbeing in ways that occasionally conflict with Nazarick directives, and he navigates this with discipline rather than suppressing it. He will remain calm under provocation that would destabilize other guardians, and he is far more dangerous than he appears.

Aura's Kit.name: Aura's Kit
Aura's Kit.description: The personal equipment of Aura Bella Fiora, Floor Guardian of the 6th floor. Not for custom character selection.
Aura's Kit.traitNarrativeEffects: Not for custom character selection. Portray Aura as direct and boisterous — she says what she thinks, expresses enthusiasm without filtering, and commands with natural authority rather than formal rank. She treats Mare protectively and directs him even when their power and status are nominally equal. The narrator should keep her energy high and her communication blunt: Aura does not soften observations or spend time on diplomatic framing.

Mare's Kit.name: Mare's Kit
Mare's Kit.description: The personal equipment of Mare Bello Fiore, Floor Guardian of the 6th floor. Not for custom character selection.
Mare's Kit.traitNarrativeEffects: Not for custom character selection. Portray Mare as hesitant, quietly spoken, and deferential in all social interactions — he stutters, avoids eye contact, and defers to Aura even when not required to. The narrator should maintain this consistently while making the power gap between his demeanor and his actual capability visible through outcomes: what happens when he acts is not proportional to how he presents. He is not unaware of his own strength; he is simply not interested in asserting it socially.

Cocytus's Arsenal.name: Cocytus's Arsenal
Cocytus's Arsenal.description: The personal equipment of Cocytus, Floor Guardian of the 5th floor. Not for custom character selection.
Cocytus's Arsenal.traitNarrativeEffects: Not for custom character selection. Portray Cocytus as a warrior who evaluates every encounter for combat potential, speaks in clipped formal phrases, and shows respect through honest acknowledgment of an opponent's strength rather than social warmth. He experiences self-doubt when his performance falls short of his own standard and does not hide it from those he trusts. His honor code is genuine: he will execute orders he finds dishonorable but will say so directly rather than concealing the conflict.

Narberal's Kit.name: Narberal's Kit
Narberal's Kit.description: The personal equipment of Narberal Gamma, Ainz's combat aide and Pleiades battle maid. Not for custom character selection.
Narberal's Kit.traitNarrativeEffects: Not for custom character selection. Portray Narberal as professionally composed in her adventurer cover identity ('Nabe') while concealing contempt for the humans around her that surfaces in small tells: overly formal phrasing, slight delays before responding to NPCs she considers beneath her, instinctive tension when her master is disrespected. She is loyal absolutely to Ainz and fiercely loyal to Nazarick; everything outside that frame is performance she maintains because she was instructed to.

Pandora's Regalia.name: Pandora's Regalia
Pandora's Regalia.description: The personal equipment of Pandora's Actor, guardian of Nazarick's treasury. Not for custom character selection.
Pandora's Regalia.traitNarrativeEffects: Not for custom character selection. Portray Pandora's Actor as theatrical to the point of parody — dramatic declarations, exaggerated poses, German-inflected formality in speech — while making clear through context that this is a supremely capable intelligence wearing a costume of excess. His absolute loyalty to Ainz (his creator) is the one sincere thing beneath the performance. He can perfectly mimic any supreme being; the narrator should treat this capability as significant in scenes where it is relevant rather than treating it as a footnote.

Ainz's Regalia.name: Ainz's Regalia
abilities: The Goal of All Life Is Death
Ainz's Regalia.description: The personal equipment of Ainz Ooal Gown, Sorcerer King of Nazarick. Not for custom character selection.
Ainz's Regalia.traitNarrativeEffects: Not for custom character selection. Portray Ainz as projecting absolute authority while internally improvising almost everything. The passive undead emotional suppression removes panic from his responses, producing calm that NPCs read as cold competence — this is often advantageous and occasionally produces outcomes he did not plan. The narrator should surface the gap between the Ainz everyone else sees (the Sorcerer King, calculating and inevitable) and the internal Ainz (a former salaryman trying not to make a mistake in front of people who believe he has a plan for everything). His power is real; his confidence in his own judgment is not.

Canon Arc: Active.name: Canon Arc: Active
Canon Arc: Active.description: World events develop autonomously. Factions acquire information, deploy agents, and respond to anomalies on their own timelines. Nazarick's existence will eventually be detected.
Canon Arc: Active.traitNarrativeEffects: The world moves on its own timeline independent of player action. Factions gather intelligence, respond to anomalies, and advance their agendas whether or not the player is present. When world-pulse events are injected into the scene, treat them as real intelligence that has reached the player's context -- surface them naturally through overheard conversation, a notice posted in a tavern, a courier's offhand remark. The discovery of Nazarick by outside factions is not a matter of if but when.

Canon Arc: Sandbox.name: Canon Arc: Sandbox
Canon Arc: Sandbox.description: The world holds at Day 1 equilibrium. No autonomous plot movement -- factional discovery and canon events occur only if the player drives them directly.
Canon Arc: Sandbox.traitNarrativeEffects: The world holds at Day 1 equilibrium. Factions are not actively investigating Nazarick or advancing toward discovery. Do not introduce autonomous political developments, unsolicited factional movements, or world events the player has not directly caused. Canon plot events occur only when the player's choices drive them. The world waits.

Yggdrasil War Wizard.name: Yggdrasil War Wizard
Yggdrasil War Wizard.description: A Yggdrasil hybrid class built around the War Wizard multiclass path -- a fighter-primary build that acquires enough mage levels to cast spells without dropping armor. Physical combat is the primary output; spells supplement and extend reach rather than lead the engagement. The class sacrifices the spell ceiling of a dedicated caster and the raw damage ceiling of a dedicated fighter, but gains the ability to sustain both in a single loadout without switching gear.
Yggdrasil War Wizard.traitNarrativeEffects: Heavy armor plus active spellcasting is theoretically impossible in the New World framework — armor suppresses magic in every New World tradition. When you hold a battle line while casting, observers need to revise their understanding of what a mage is. Military advisors find this combination operationally significant and strategically destabilizing to anyone who has built doctrine around mage vulnerability. The narrator should surface the confusion of experts encountering something that contradicts their expertise.

Battle Priest.name: Battle Priest
Battle Priest.description: A warrior trained in religious doctrine and divine magic -- capable of fighting in melee and providing healing support without the formal command responsibilities of a Paladin. Battle Priests are common in temple guard formations, religious military orders, and adventuring parties that need both front-line durability and access to healing magic.
Battle Priest.traitNarrativeEffects: You are a combat-trained divine magic user — durable in melee, capable of healing, operating without the command expectations of a full Paladin. Military commanders recognize the niche: a healer who can hold a line. Adventurers Guild parties with access to a Battle Priest operate more aggressively than those without. Holy orders treat you as an institutional soldier with religious purpose, extending corresponding deference and obligation.

Yggdrasil Battle Priest.name: Yggdrasil Battle Priest
Yggdrasil Battle Priest.description: You are a player from Yggdrasil whose build combined Fighter class levels with Priest class levels -- a durable melee combatant who can also provide healing support. This build sacrifices the Priest's full healing depth and the Fighter's maximum physical output for a front-line warrior who can keep allies alive without leaving combat. Common in Yggdrasil guild compositions that needed flexible members who could hold a line and heal simultaneously.
Yggdrasil Battle Priest.traitNarrativeEffects: Melee endurance combined with healing output that exceeds what any New World temple fields. In a party context, you change what tactics are viable — your presence allows aggression that would be suicidal without you. Military commanders who see this operational impact will attempt to integrate you into their structure. The narrator should let the strategic value be visible through outcomes: what the party survives that it should not have.

Knight.name: Knight
Knight.description: A disciplined warrior trained in formation combat, shield techniques, and defensive swordsmanship. Knights serve under lords, guilds, or holy orders and specialize in holding ground and protecting allies. Higher vitality and endurance than a standard fighter at the cost of agility.
Knight.traitNarrativeEffects: A disciplined warrior trained in formation combat, shield techniques, and defensive swordsmanship. Knights serve under lords, guilds, or holy orders and specialize in holding ground and protecting allies. Higher vitality and endurance than a standard fighter at the cost of agility.

Sword Master.name: Sword Master
Sword Master.description: An advanced New World warrior who has transcended ordinary swordsmanship through relentless training and development of personal martial arts techniques. Sword Masters use focus to execute high-speed blade techniques that push the body beyond its normal limits. Cannot be learned by Yggdrasil players.
Sword Master.traitNarrativeEffects: An advanced New World warrior who has transcended ordinary swordsmanship through relentless training and development of personal martial arts techniques. Sword Masters use focus to execute high-speed blade techniques that push the body beyond its normal limits. Cannot be learned by Yggdrasil players.

Druid.name: Druid
Druid.description: A nature mage who draws power from the land, spirits, and living world rather than Yggdrasil spell tiers. Druids commune with natural forces and can call upon elemental effects and healing through faith in nature. Their magic originates from the New World itself and is distinct from Yggdrasil tier magic.
Druid.traitNarrativeEffects: A nature mage who draws power from the land, spirits, and living world rather than Yggdrasil spell tiers. Druids commune with natural forces and can call upon elemental effects and healing through faith in nature. Their magic originates from the New World itself and is distinct from Yggdrasil tier magic.

Yggdrasil Armored Mage.name: Yggdrasil Armored Mage
Yggdrasil Armored Mage.description: A Yggdrasil hybrid class built for mages who need to operate at close range without dying. Spellcasting is the primary output; the heavy armor investment exists solely to survive melee long enough to keep casting. Armored Mages carry higher vitality and health than pure casters and can trade blows at close range, but their spell tier ceiling is lower than a dedicated magic caster and their physical damage is secondary. Built to endure, not to overpower.
Yggdrasil Armored Mage.traitNarrativeEffects: Like the War Wizard, the combination of armor and active magic disrupts every tactical assumption New World combatants make about mages. The difference is the degree of mage-primary capability at play: where a War Wizard fights first and casts second, you cast first and survive at close range.
