Opponents who engage expecting a vulnerable spellcaster will adjust mid-fight to something they have no prior model for.

Demon.name: Demon
Demon.description: A demon-type heteromorphic being -- one of the major heteromorph categories in Yggdrasil, spanning countless subtypes from imps to archdemons to succubi. Physically varied but unified by high intelligence, innate dark magic affinity, and a commanding presence that unsettles humans. Demons radiate an aura that most humanoids read as threat before intent. In the New World, demon sightings are rare and associated with catastrophe. Guilds of the Slane Theocracy treat demon encounters as extermination events. Undead factions may be neutral or hostile depending on karma alignment. Among other Yggdrasil heteromorphs, rank is recognized and respected.
Demon.traitNarrativeEffects: Reaction is driven by appearance, not race label. Many demon subtypes have beautiful or human-passing forms -- a succubus or greater demon may draw admiration before suspicion. Initial New World reactions are based entirely on how the character looks: if they pass as human, they are treated as human. Demonic nature only becomes a factor when revealed through divine detection magic (which the Slane Theocracy uses actively), visible demonic features, or explicit display of dark abilities. At that point the Theocracy shifts to extermination response; common humans react with fear; undead factions vary by karma. Among Yggdrasil heteromorphs, demon-type rank is recognized and respected regardless of form.

Angel.name: Angel
Angel.description: A holy-type heteromorphic being from Yggdrasil -- one of the few races with innate positive karma alignment and divine magic affinity. Angels take many forms depending on tier, from basic winged servants to towering armored seraphs, but all carry an aura of sacred authority. In the New World, angelic beings are objects of reverence and terror in equal measure -- holy orders treat them as manifestations of divine will, while undead and demon-aligned factions respond with immediate hostility. An angel moving through human settlements draws crowds, prayers, and the attention of every cleric within range. Darkness and negative energy abilities are strongly resisted; holy and positive energy abilities are amplified.
Angel.traitNarrativeEffects: Most angel subtypes are visibly divine -- wings, radiant light, sacred geometry. In the New World this reads as manifestation of divine will, not monster threat. Religious humans (Theocracy clergy, Re-Estize Church) react with reverence and awe; common people may kneel or pray. The primary social risk is the opposite of most heteromorphs: overwhelming attention, religious expectation, and factions attempting to claim or direct the character. Undead and dark-karma factions respond with instinctive hostility. An angel moving through any human settlement draws a crowd -- discretion requires concealment or deliberately subduing the divine presence.

Homunculus.name: Homunculus
Homunculus.description: An artificially created being -- constructed through advanced alchemy or Yggdrasil character engineering to fulfill a specific function. Homunculi are optimized by design rather than shaped by natural selection: the body was built with intent, which makes it precise but narrow. Physical appearance is often near-human but subtly wrong -- too symmetrical, too still, too composed. Most humans recognize that something is off before they can name what. Social interactions with humans who do not know the truth carry an underlying unease; those who do know it may treat the homunculus as property, tool, or person depending on their worldview. Among Yggdrasil players, homunculi are understood as created characters with full agency. Stat profile is narrow and intentional -- high in designed function, lower elsewhere.
Homunculus.traitNarrativeEffects: Passes as human in most circumstances. The uncanny valley effect produces social discomfort -- people sense something is off before they can name it -- but not hostility. No faction treats homunculi as a threat on sight. Reaction varies entirely by who learns the truth: Yggdrasil players recognize created characters as full agents; New World humans with no context may treat the character as property, tool, or person depending on their worldview. Cannot be reliably identified by most divine detection magic due to an unusual soul signature.

Battle-Forged Technique.name: Battle-Forged Technique
Battle-Forged Technique.description: A martial refinement earned through repeated combat rather than granted at creation. Years of live engagements strip wasted motion from a fighter's technique, converting raw training into economy: fewer telegraphed strikes, faster recovery between actions, better read of an opponent's weight shift before a blow lands.
Battle-Forged Technique.traitNarrativeEffects: Your combat has lost its rough edges -- other fighters read your stance and footwork as seasoned rather than trained. Instructors and veteran soldiers acknowledge you as a peer without needing a demonstration. Opponents who underestimate you on first appearance recalibrate within the first exchange.

Arcane Specialization: Evocation.name: Arcane Specialization: Evocation
Arcane Specialization: Evocation.description: A magic caster's deliberate focus on direct destructive spellwork -- refining tier magic already in the caster's repertoire toward faster casting and greater raw output at the cost of breadth in other schools.
Arcane Specialization: Evocation.traitNarrativeEffects: Your destructive spellwork has narrowed and sharpened -- casting times drop and effect radius grows more precise, in visible contrast to a caster who has not specialized. Other mages who witness it recognize deliberate focus rather than raw talent, and calibrate their own approach to you accordingly.

Arcane Specialization: Abjuration.name: Arcane Specialization: Abjuration
Arcane Specialization: Abjuration.description: A magic caster's deliberate focus on protective and warding spellwork -- refining tier magic already in the caster's repertoire toward sustained defensive effect at the cost of breadth in other schools.
Arcane Specialization: Abjuration.traitNarrativeEffects: Your wards hold longer and absorb more before failing, a difference other casters and battlefield commanders notice immediately when you anchor a defensive position. Allies standing near an active ward of yours read it as a meaningfully safer place to stand.

Undead Ascendance: Bound Marrow.name: Undead Ascendance: Bound Marrow
Undead Ascendance: Bound Marrow.description: A deepening of skeletal undead physiology through accumulated existence rather than external enchantment -- bone density and negative-energy retention both increase, a documented feature of long-lived skeletal undead that never underwent decay in the first place.
Undead Ascendance: Bound Marrow.traitNarrativeEffects: Your bone structure has visibly densified and darkened at the joints -- a difference other undead register as seniority and living witnesses read as an even more unnatural sight than an ordinary skeleton. Negative energy sources you draw on last longer before depleting.

Sanguine Ascendance.name: Sanguine Ascendance
Sanguine Ascendance.description: A deepening of true vampiric capability through the accumulation of blood and years -- greater control over transformation, faster wound regeneration, and a stronger dominating presence over lesser minds.
Sanguine Ascendance.traitNarrativeEffects: Wounds close visibly faster now, and your dominating presence over weaker-willed creatures holds without active concentration. Those attuned to detect the undead -- Theocracy scripture teams especially -- register the increase as a meaningfully higher threat classification.

Blessing of the Ordained.name: Blessing of the Ordained
Blessing of the Ordained.description: A recognized deepening of divine favor granted through sustained faith practice and documented healing work -- a step beyond baseline divine casting that temple authorities record formally in a caster's standing.
Blessing of the Ordained.traitNarrativeEffects: Temple staff and fellow clergy treat your standing as formally elevated -- documented healing work at this volume is recorded, not assumed. Holy orders extend deeper institutional trust: access to restricted texts, introductions to senior clergy, and requests for aid that bypass the usual vetting.

Tactical Command Bearing.name: Tactical Command Bearing
Tactical Command Bearing.description: A command presence built through demonstrated results rather than rank or birth -- the accumulated experience of being followed successfully enough times that others defer to the judgment before it is explained.
Tactical Command Bearing.traitNarrativeEffects: Soldiers and hired companions fall into formation around your calls faster than rank alone would explain -- your instructions read as tested rather than theoretical. Officers and guild captains who watch you direct a group for the first time recognize a peer instead of a subordinate.

New World Native.name: New World Native
New World Native.description: You were born and raised in the New World, not summoned from any game. You know its kingdoms, its faiths, and its unwritten rules the way only someone who grew up under them can. You carry no Yggdrasil powers or player abilities; your strength is whatever your race, your trade, and your own hard living have given you.
New World Native.traitNarrativeEffects: Your knowledge is the mirror of a Yggdrasil player's: New World culture, politics, geography, and social custom understood instinctively, while game mechanics, player terminology, and the truth of what Nazarick and the 'Supreme Beings' really are mean nothing to you. The narrator should let you read the world's customs and dangers with a local's ease and treat any game-origin concept as alien. Your ceiling is a mortal's: real, hard-won growth, never a player's imported power.

Servant of Nazarick.name: Servant of Nazarick
Servant of Nazarick.description: You were created within the Great Tomb of Nazarick, or bound to it before memory — a denizen shaped to serve Ainz Ooal Gown as a matter of your very nature. You are a being of this world, not a transported player, but you were made with the strength and craft of Nazarick behind you, and you know the Tomb's hierarchy the way you know your own name.
Servant of Nazarick.traitNarrativeEffects: You understand Nazarick's absolute chain of command instinctively and are recognized within it, while the wider New World's kingdoms and customs are only as familiar as a sheltered servant's would be. The narrator should treat your loyalty to Nazarick as intrinsic rather than chosen, and surface the Tomb's rigid hierarchy whenever its denizens appear. Your power is real and considerable, drawn from how you were made — a created being's strength, not a Yggdrasil player's imported arsenal.

Origin.name: Origin
Origin.description: Where do you come from? A Yggdrasil player was pulled into the New World from the dead servers of the game, arriving a finished, game-built being. A Servant of Nazarick was created within the Great Tomb itself, a denizen made with the Tomb's strength behind them. A New World native was simply born here, carrying only what their race, trade, and hard living gave them. This choice opens your class path.

Race.name: Race
Race.description: What you are, in a world that judges heteromorphs on sight -- your race sets your body, your ceiling, and how strangers treat you before you speak.

subcategories.name: Humanoid
subcategories.description: Human Species stock -- humans, mixed blood, and elvenkind: unremarkable in body next to a heteromorph, and spared the worst of the stigma that dogs monstrous races.

subcategories.name: Heteromorphic
subcategories.description: Monstrous and undead beings of great power and greater stigma, able to evolve their race far past any human ceiling.

subcategories.name: Demihuman
subcategories.description: Demi-Human peoples with their own cultures and strengths, held beneath humans in the New World's pecking order.

Class.name: Class
Class.description: Your class: what you were trained or built to do. Your Origin sets which classes are open to you. A Yggdrasil player draws on the job builds of the old game; a New World native on the crafts of this world.

subcategories.name: Pure Classes
subcategories.description: The core Yggdrasil jobs, each a clean single specialization from the old game.

subcategories.name: Hybrid Builds
subcategories.description: Multi-class Yggdrasil builds that fused two job trees into something neither could be alone.

subcategories.name: Martial
subcategories.description: Warriors of the New World, mastering weapon, shield, and body.

subcategories.name: Faith & Nature
subcategories.description: Half-casters and casters who draw power from faith or the living land.

Story Mode.name: Story Mode
Story Mode.description: Choose how closely the game holds to the canon timeline.

Supreme Being.name: Supreme Being
Supreme Being.description: A being who transcends the New World's power scale entirely. Ainz Ooal Gown and potentially other Yggdrasil players. Treat as functionally unchallengeable by ordinary means.

Floor Guardian.name: Floor Guardian
Floor Guardian.description: A Nazarick Floor Guardian — among the most powerful beings in the New World. Each is individually capable of defeating entire human armies. Loyal absolutely to Ainz Ooal Gown.

Human Warrior.name: Human Warrior
Human Warrior.description: A trained human fighter, from foot soldiers to legendary warriors like Gazef Stronoff. The gap between even the best human warrior and a Floor Guardian is categorical.

Undead.name: Undead
Undead.description: Undead creatures ranging from mindless skeletons to death knights and elder liches. Nazarick contains undead of mythic power. New World undead are comparatively primitive.

Monster.name: Monster
Monster.description: Non-human hostile creatures: trolls, ogres, goblins, giant insects, and more. Standard New World threats for adventurers. No match for Nazarick.

Battle Maid.name: Battle Maid
Battle Maid.description: A member of the Pleiades battle maid unit of Nazarick. Each is a unique creature type with power far exceeding any New World equivalent. They serve as Nazarick's surface-deployed military and intelligence assets.

Area Guardian.name: Area Guardian
Area Guardian.description: A Nazarick Area Guardian. Less powerful than Floor Guardians but still categorically above New World peak humans. Assigned to specific sections of Nazarick rather than full floors.

Ruler.name: Ruler
Ruler.description: A head of state — king, emperor, or equivalent. Political authority rather than individual combat power. Surrounded by protective infrastructure that compensates for personal vulnerability.

Noble.name: Noble
Noble.description: A member of the aristocracy with political influence, private military resources, and social capital. Individual combat capability varies widely — from non-combatant administrators to trained warriors.

Imperial Knight.name: Imperial Knight
Imperial Knight.description: An elite Baharuth Empire knight. The best non-magical human fighters the empire produces, selected and trained through rigorous evaluation. Represent the practical ceiling of unaugmented human martial capability.

Black Scripture.name: Black Scripture
Black Scripture.description: A member of the Slane Theocracy's most elite Scripture division. Power in the upper range of what the New World produces in humans — individual capability that approaches or matches Floor Guardian tiers in rare cases.

Lizardman Chief.name: Lizardman Chief
Lizardman Chief.description: A lizardman tribal chief or warrior leader. Strong physical combatant by New World standards — not at human peak-adventurer tier but capable in coordinated tribal warfare.

Lizardman Druid.name: Lizardman Druid
Lizardman Druid.description: A lizardman healer and nature magic user. Primary combat role is support and healing rather than direct damage. Critical to tribal cohesion in extended engagements.

Alchemist.name: Alchemist
Alchemist.description: A practitioner of alchemical arts — potion crafting, compound production, and pharmaceutical research. Non-combat specialist whose value is in production capability rather than battlefield presence.

Village Chief.name: Village Chief
Village Chief.description: A settlement leader without formal military training. Administrative authority in a local context. Physical capability is ordinary. Leadership value is in community organisation and local knowledge.

Guild Master.name: Guild Master
Guild Master.description: An Adventurers Guild branch manager. A former adventurer in most cases, now in an administrative role. Personal combat capability at retirement-adventurer level. Institutional knowledge and network connections are the primary value.

Adventurer.name: Adventurer
Adventurer.description: A registered member of the Adventurers Guild. Capability ranges from copper rank (slightly above ordinary human) to adamantite rank (peak human with magical enhancement). Tier within this range varies significantly.

Court Wizard.name: Court Wizard
Court Wizard.description: A mage serving in a national court capacity. Significantly more capable than standard guild mages — court positions are held by individuals who have reached the practical ceiling of human magical achievement in the New World.

Swordsman.name: Swordsman
Swordsman.description: A specialist melee fighter with advanced sword technique. Often self-trained through obsessive practice rather than institutional training. Individual capability can approach or match palace knight level through different paths.

Knight.name: Knight
Knight.description: A trained warrior in knightly service. Combat-specialised with formal training and quality equipment. Individual to a noble house or royal guard. Capability varies by institution — the Re-Estize royal guard is below the Baharuth imperial knights.

Butler.name: Butler
Butler.description: Nazarick's head butler. Appears as a distinguished elderly gentleman. Is not one. Extreme physical power channelled through precise technique, concealed entirely by his presentation. One of Nazarick's most dangerous beings in the field.

Holy Kingdom Paladin.name: Holy Kingdom Paladin
Holy Kingdom Paladin.description: A paladin of the Roble Holy Kingdom. Faith-driven, combat-trained, and significantly hardened by the demon army invasion. More capable than standard human warriors, with divine-magic reinforcement.

Dragon Lord.name: Dragon Lord
Dragon Lord.description: A True Dragon Lord -- an ancient Wild Magic-wielding dragon of nation-state-level power. Completely immune to Tier Magic at 6th tier and below. Wild Magic spells operate outside standard spell-defense rules. No adventurer ranking applies to a True Dragon Lord; they are measured against armies, not individuals.

Royalty.name: Royalty
Royalty.description: A reigning monarch or heir to a throne. Political authority, personal guard, and court resources are available as assets. Actual combat capability varies widely by individual.

character.name: character
character.description: Default type for named individuals encountered in the New World. Applies to adventurers, merchants, nobles, and others not covered by a more specific type.

Worker.name: Worker
Worker.description: An independent mercenary who operates outside Adventurer's Guild sanction. Takes commissions for tomb raiding, politically sensitive operations, and high-risk retrieval. No institutional protection. No rescue obligations. Combat capability varies enormously; experienced workers are often more dangerous than their rank implies.

Priest.name: Priest
Priest.description: A divine magic practitioner affiliated with the Six Gods religion or a regional faith. Provides healing, protective magic, and spiritual authority. Combat capability ranges from noncombatant to paladin-adjacent depending on denomination and training.

Thief.name: Thief
Thief.description: A stealth-trained operative specialized in infiltration, information extraction, and precision elimination. Combat approach relies on surprise, positioning, and escape rather than sustained engagement. Found in adventurer parties, worker teams, criminal organizations, and intelligence services.

Criminal Leader.name: Criminal Leader
Criminal Leader.description: An organized crime figure managing resources, personnel, and relationships across a network. Eight Fingers division heads are the archetype. Personal combat capability is secondary to operational capability -- they matter because of what they control, not what they can do directly.

Imperial Mage.name: Imperial Mage
Imperial Mage.description: A magic caster trained and deployed within the Baharuth Empire's military structure. The Four Imperial Battle Mages are the elite tier. Standard imperial mages provide magical support in field operations and occupy advisory roles in administrative centers. Training is systematic and output-focused rather than exploratory.

Ranger.name: Ranger
Ranger.description: A wilderness-trained scout and tracker. Effective in natural environments; less effective in urban or dungeon settings. Core capabilities: tracking, long-range combat, survival, and hazard identification. Common in adventurer parties operating outside city ranges.

Druid.name: Druid
Druid.description: A nature magic practitioner. Summons wildlife, manipulates terrain, provides healing outside the Six Gods religious framework. Among lizardman tribes the druid caste holds significant social authority. Abilities scale with the practitioner's connection to natural environments.

Dark Knight.name: Dark Knight
Dark Knight.description: A warrior aligned with dark or undead power systems. Distinct from paladins in that combat capability is enhanced through negative energy rather than divine blessing. May be a Yggdrasil-origin class or a New World warrior who has accessed taboo enhancement methods.

Paladin.name: Paladin
Paladin.description: A divine warrior whose combat capability is enhanced by faith. Different from a purely martial warrior in that their damage output, resilience, and detection ability improve with devotion. Theocracy Scriptures, the Holy Kingdom Paladin Order, and individual faith-driven fighters all fit this type.

Theocracy Agent.name: Theocracy Agent
Theocracy Agent.description: An operative deployed by the Slane Theocracy -- one of the Six Scriptures, an intelligence function, or a missionary presence in foreign territory. Combat capability varies by Scripture assignment. Ideological commitment to human supremacy is consistent across roles.

Beastman.name: Beastman
Beastman.description: A demihuman species of varying anthropomorphic types, native to the Beastman Country. Physical combat capability is high relative to humans. Pack coordination is natural. Strategic capacity varies by individual; warlords like Buser operate well above the average.

Goblin.name: Goblin
Goblin.description: A low-tier demihuman species present throughout the New World. Individually weak; dangerous in large groups with coordination. The Goblin Lord upgrade significantly exceeds base-type capability. Goblin champions and generals represent exceptional individuals within this type.

Troll.name: Troll
Troll.description: A large, physically powerful demihuman with significant regenerative capability. Found in the Troll Kingdom and as mercenary-adjacent muscle in other demihuman regions. Fire damage suppresses the regeneration. Otherwise, attrition combat without fire is inefficient.

Skeletal Warrior.name: Skeletal Warrior
Skeletal Warrior.description: A basic undead combatant -- animated bone structure with residual combat programming. Physical damage is reduced; magic effective. No morale. No fatigue. No capacity for independent judgment. A common component of undead armies and Nazarick's lower-floor security.

Death Knight.name: Death Knight
Death Knight.description: A high-tier undead warrior created from a strong-willed human who died violently. Retains combat technique from its prior life enhanced by undead resilience. Significant threat to any standard adventurer party. Nazarick uses them as security assets.

Elder Lich.name: Elder Lich
Elder Lich.description: A high-tier undead magic caster -- a practitioner who achieved undeath through long preparation or was created by another high-tier practitioner. Retains full magical knowledge. Highly dangerous in magical combat. Immune to most mundane threats.

Vampire.name: Vampire
Vampire.description: An undead creature of variable origin -- naturally occurring in the New World or Yggdrasil-class. Evileye represents the natural New World variety. Shalltear is Yggdrasil-created. Combat and magical capability scales dramatically with tier. Sunlight sensitivity is type-variant; true Yggdrasil vampires are not affected.

Demon.name: Demon
Demon.description: A creature of demonic nature -- either summoned, native to a demonic realm, or a being who has undergone demonic transformation. Demon presence in this world is recorded primarily through the Abelion Hills demi-human and demonic populations and through summoned-demon incidents. Capability varies enormously; lesser demons are creature-tier, greater demons are genuinely dangerous to experienced adventurers.

Merchant.name: Merchant
Merchant.description: A trade-focused NPC whose primary value is information, connection, and resource access rather than combat. Guild merchants operate through the Merchant's Guild. Independent merchants are common in frontier areas. What they know about supply and demand often reflects what is really happening in a region.

Scholar.name: Scholar
Scholar.description: An academic or researcher. Primary asset is knowledge -- of magic systems, history, geography, or creature ecology. Combat capability typically minimal. In the Baharuth Magic Academy and equivalent institutions, some scholars are capable practitioners who happen to focus on theory rather than application.

Spy.name: Spy
Spy.description: An intelligence operative under maintained cover. Real capability is concealed. Relationships are operational assets. The identity presented to the world is curated. Theocracy agents in foreign nations and noble house intelligence networks both fit this type.

Warrior Captain.name: Warrior Captain
Warrior Captain.description: A military leader who commands forces through demonstrated capability and institutional authority. Gazef Stronoff is the archetype. Personal combat ability is genuine and significant. Strategic and logistical capability varies; some are effective commanders, some are exceptional fighters who happen to hold command rank.

Elf.name: Elf
Elf.description: An elven NPC. Long-lived relative to humans; culturally distinct; magic-adjacent. The Elf Country operates under the Elf King's absolute authority. Elves in the New World outside the Elf Country are often escaped slaves of the Theocracy or the half-elf population that exists in mixed-race communities. Capability varies by individual training and background.

Dwarf.name: Dwarf
Dwarf.description: A dwarven NPC -- craftsperson, warrior, or merchant from the Dwarf Kingdom in the Azerlisia Mountains. Runesmiths are the prestige caste. Warriors are built for tunnel defense rather than open-field warfare. Dwarves in the New World outside the kingdom are rare; most dwarven interaction happens through trade.

Quagoa.name: Quagoa
Quagoa.description: A mole-person demihuman species native to the Azerlisia Mountain range. Burrows through rock with natural digging capability. Individual combat power is significant. Represents an ongoing territorial threat to the Dwarf Kingdom's eastern tunnel networks. Tribal hierarchy with clan leadership structure.

Giant.name: Giant
Giant.description: A large-category creature -- Giant Tree Frogs, Giant variants of natural animals, and true giant-race humanoids. Physical power scales with size. Intelligence is type-variant. New World wilderness and dungeon encounters include multiple giant-type creatures.

Sea Creature.name: Sea Creature
Sea Creature.description: Aquatic or semi-aquatic creature type. Present in the Great Lake, the coastlines, and deep water regions. Ranges from mundane fish-type creatures to dangerous aquatic predators. The Lake area near the Lizardmen tribes has its own ecology distinct from open-water equivalents.

Elemental.name: Elemental
Elemental.description: A summoned or naturally occurring entity composed of elemental force. Fire, water, earth, and wind types are all possible in the New World. Yggdrasil summoning magic can produce higher-tier elementals. Combat capability is specialized around their elemental nature -- strong against opposing elements, weak against their own counters.

Wild Beast.name: Wild Beast
Wild Beast.description: Non-sentient animal-tier creature. Basilisks, Giant Lizards, cave bears, and similar fauna. Danger comes from physical power and territorial behavior rather than tactics. Common in wilderness encounter zones and in dungeon lower levels.

Slime.name: Slime
Slime.description: Gelatinous creature type. Found in dungeons and dark/wet environments. Physical resistance compensated by magical vulnerability. Some slime variants are corrosive; others are passive unless disturbed. Dangerous in enclosed spaces.

Villager.name: Villager
Villager.description: An ordinary civilian living in a village or frontier settlement. No combat training, no formal position -- just someone trying to survive in a dangerous world.

Lizardman Warrior.name: Lizardman Warrior
Lizardman Warrior.description: A lizardman fighter of the Wetland tribes. Combat-trained in the tribal tradition, wielding primitive but effective weapons. Warriors handle tribal defense, hunting, and inter-tribal conflict.

health.name: health
health.usageInstructions: Health tracks physical vitality. Minor hit: -5 to -15. Serious wound: -15 to -35. Near-fatal: -35 to -60. At 0, character is downed. Recovery requires rest or healing magic. Undead characters do not recover health through natural rest — only negative energy or specific necromantic healing applies.

mana.name: mana
mana.usageInstructions: Mana fuels all tier magic spells. Tier 1-2: -2 to -5. Tier 3-5: -5 to -15. Tier 6-8: -15 to -30. Tier 9-10: -30 to -50. Super-Tier: -50+. No mana potions exist in Yggdrasil - mana restores naturally through rest (approximately 1/8 of max per hour). Mana Crystal Clusters allow a caster to store and draw mana as a bonus action, providing field-use recovery. Warriors generally have low mana reserves; hybrid warrior-mage builds have moderate amounts; dedicated casters have high pools. At 0 mana no tier magic is possible until recovery.

focus.name: focus
focus.usageInstructions: Focus is the internal Ki energy that powers New World Martial Arts techniques. It is a New World concept - Yggdrasil warriors used cooldown-based skills, not a focus resource. In the New World, Focus acts as a warrior's equivalent to mana: high-level martial artists channel it to temporarily exceed normal physical limits, similar to spellcasting. New World martial artists use both physical stamina (for sustained movement and exertion) and Focus (for technique activation). Basic technique: -5 to -10. Intermediate: -10 to -20. Advanced: -20 to -35. Apex techniques: -35+. Recovers through rest and controlled breathing meditation.

stamina.name: stamina
stamina.usageInstructions: Stamina is the physical endurance pool used by living Yggdrasil players built around weapon and body-mastery combat. It is a tabletop abstraction of the cooldown-based skill system from the game, representing sustained physical output. Undead characters - Skeleton Undead, Overlord, Lich, Vampire, and all undead variants - are completely immune to stamina loss and never spend or track stamina. Living Yggdrasil warriors spend stamina for combat techniques: light action -5 to -10, standard technique -10 to -20, heavy or extended sequence -20 to -35, apex technique -35 to -55. At 0 stamina the fighter can still act but loses access to special techniques and narration reflects growing fatigue. Recovers through brief rest periods and pauses in combat. Stamina Draughts eliminate exhaustion penalties instantly.

Rise Through the Ranks.name: Rise Through the Ranks
Rise Through the Ranks.mainObjective: Advance from your starting rank by completing jobs and demonstrating capability.
Rise Through the Ranks.questStatement: As a newcomer to E-Rantel, register with the Adventurer's Guild (5 silver coins at the clerk's counter; all new registrants start at Copper rank regardless of ability) and then advance by completing jobs and demonstrating capability. The Guild tracks progress by performance, not time.
Rise Through the Ranks.questDesignBrief: Standard adventurer progression quest. First step is registration at the guild clerk's counter: 5 silver coins, plus 5 copper for a literacy test if the registrant cannot read. All new registrants start at Copper rank -- no exceptions, regardless of apparent ability or reputation. The clerk does not negotiate the fee or the starting rank. After registration, jobs range from monster hunting near E-Rantel to deliveries, investigations, and escort work. The Guild tracks quality of outcomes, not just completion. Rank advancement rewards the appropriate rank plate necklace at each milestone. The necklace is cosmetic but culturally significant.

completionCondition.query: The player has completed at least five successful Guild jobs and advanced at least one rank.

A Meeting with the Sorcerer King.name: A Meeting with the Sorcerer King
A Meeting with the Sorcerer King.mainObjective: Facilitate or participate in the diplomatic meeting between the Baharuth Empire and the Sorcerer Kingdom.
A Meeting with the Sorcerer King.questStatement: Emperor Jircniv seeks a meeting with Ainz Ooal Gown to discuss the current treaty between the Baharuth Empire and the Sorcerer Kingdom. The meeting requires careful diplomatic navigation.
A Meeting with the Sorcerer King.questDesignBrief: A high-stakes diplomatic encounter. Jircniv is pragmatic and genuinely skilled; he negotiates from the only position available to him: as someone who correctly recognized reality and is trying to make the best of it. Ainz will project supreme confidence while internally uncertain of the right moves.

completionCondition.query: The meeting between Imperial and Nazarick representatives has occurred and a clear outcome established.

The Kingdom's Fracture.name: The Kingdom's Fracture
The Kingdom's Fracture.mainObjective: Assist Gazef in countering the noble faction destabilizing the Re-Estize Kingdom.
The Kingdom's Fracture.questStatement: Gazef Stronoff is attempting to hold the Re-Estize Kingdom together against internal noble factions who see opportunity in the kingdom's post-Katze weakness. He needs assistance that he cannot officially request through normal channels.
The Kingdom's Fracture.questDesignBrief: A political investigation in a human capital under stress. Gazef is straightforward; the noble opposition is not. Brain and Climb can provide ground-level support. The player navigates court politics without supernatural resources — this is a human-scale problem.

completionCondition.query: The destabilizing noble scheme has been identified and disrupted through whatever means the player chooses.

What Lies Below Nazarick.name: What Lies Below Nazarick
What Lies Below Nazarick.mainObjective: Investigate the ancient magical anomaly Demiurge has identified in the New World ruins.
What Lies Below Nazarick.questStatement: Demiurge has identified something in the New World's ancient ruins that warrants investigation — a magical phenomenon that predates any known civilization and may relate to Nazarick's arrival. The investigation requires someone with the ability to assess magical anomalies.
What Lies Below Nazarick.questDesignBrief: An investigation into ruins that predate known civilization. The anomaly is real — something about the New World's magical substrate predates Yggdrasil's arrival in ways that Demiurge finds strategically significant. The player uncovers partial answers; full understanding requires more. Deep Nazarick contains items from Yggdrasil that can be discovered or earned: Rings of Sustenance, Amulets of Undead Command, and Scrying Orbs.

completionCondition.query: The anomaly has been investigated and a report submitted to Demiurge with findings.

The Lizardman Subjugation.name: The Lizardman Subjugation
The Lizardman Subjugation.mainObjective: Accompany the subjugation force or assist the tribes in preparing a meaningful resistance.
The Lizardman Subjugation.questStatement: An undead army has arrived at the Great Lake, dispatched by an unseen power to subjugate the lizardman tribes. Cocytus commands the force with military precision. The lizardman tribes have formed a desperate coalition under Zaryusu Shasha -- not to win, but to demonstrate enough resistance to be worth keeping alive. The outcome leans toward submission; how the player arrives at it is not predetermined.
The Lizardman Subjugation.questDesignBrief: This quest positions the player at the intersection of Nazarick's expansion and the lizardmen's survival instinct. A player on the Nazarick side executes the campaign and witnesses Cocytus's military discipline. A player on the surface side witnesses the tribes' desperate coalition under Zaryusu. The resolution is historical — the tribes submit — but how the player arrives at that resolution is open. Tribal trophies and equipment from the subjugation include Dragon Scales, White Dragon Bone Armor if the lizardman warriors are defeated, and potentially Frost Pain if its wielder falls.

completionCondition.query: The tribes have either submitted to Nazarick or been destroyed. Cocytus has made his report to Ainz.

Carne Village Under Attack.name: Carne Village Under Attack
Carne Village Under Attack.mainObjective: Defend Carne Village against the attacking force.
Carne Village Under Attack.questStatement: Carne Village is threatened. A military force is approaching that the village cannot repel through conventional means. Enri Emmot possesses the horn — but using it is a one-time decision. The village's defenders must hold until the horn is used or until other assistance arrives.
Carne Village Under Attack.questDesignBrief: The horn produces a goblin army that exceeds any expectation a player would have for a village-level summon — this reveal is the quest's dramatic centrepiece. Lupusregina is observing the whole time. Whether she intervenes is a function of her orders, not her feelings about the villagers. Village resources offered as thanks: basic healing potions, rations, and serviceable iron weapons.

completionCondition.query: The attacking force has been repelled. The village remains standing.

The Battle of Katze Plains.name: The Battle of Katze Plains
The Battle of Katze Plains.mainObjective: Witness or participate in the decisive military confrontation at Katze Plains.
The Battle of Katze Plains.questStatement: Ainz Ooal Gown has challenged Gazef Stronoff to a duel and manipulated the Re-Estize army into a battle it cannot win. The true purpose is a demonstration of Tier 10 magic sufficient to end all military resistance to the Sorcerer Kingdom. The player may be present on either side.
The Battle of Katze Plains.questDesignBrief: This is a milestone event quest — it occurs when the story has reached a point where Nazarick has made public contact and military confrontation with the human nations becomes the next step. The dramatic core is Gazef Stronoff: he knows he cannot win, he asks his king to withdraw, and he fights anyway. The Super-Tier casting that follows is the largest display of magical power the New World has witnessed. The player's role depends on which side of the confrontation they are on. Handle the scale deliberately — this is the event that ends the military question of human resistance to Nazarick.

completionCondition.query: Ainz has cast the Super-Tier spell. The army's ability to resist is ended.

Eight Fingers Dismantlement.name: Eight Fingers Dismantlement
Eight Fingers Dismantlement.mainObjective: Penetrate an Eight Fingers facility and disrupt the organisation's operations.
Eight Fingers Dismantlement.questStatement: Eight Fingers, the criminal syndicate controlling significant portions of Re-Estize's black economy, is to be broken. Renner has provided intelligence. The Blue Rose is the primary strike force. The player's role is to enter one of the organisation's facilities and extract information or neutralise leadership.
Eight Fingers Dismantlement.questDesignBrief: The Blue Rose's raid on Eight Fingers is a heist-style quest in urban terrain. Renner's intelligence is accurate — she has been gathering it for years. The player may discover during the quest that Eight Fingers' leadership is already compromised by something they cannot identify, which is Demiurge's influence. Confiscated Eight Fingers contraband includes Sealing Crystals, Enchanted Stilettos recovered from their operatives, and high-quality healing supplies.

completionCondition.query: Eight Fingers' immediate capability in this district is broken. Key figures have been captured or forced out.

Fluder's Hidden Research.name: Fluder's Hidden Research
Fluder's Hidden Research.mainObjective: Investigate Fluder Paradyne's sealed private laboratory and report on its contents.
Fluder's Hidden Research.questStatement: Fluder Paradyne's private laboratory at the Imperial Magic Academy has been sealed since his departure. The emperor has ordered it assessed. The contents of the laboratory may include dangerous magical research, intelligence assets, or materials whose nature is unknown without inspection.
Fluder's Hidden Research.questDesignBrief: The laboratory contains evidence of Fluder's magical obsession at its peak — research into Tier 6 and beyond. The player pieces together the arc of a mage who spent decades searching for something and found it in Ainz Ooal Gown. The discovery may include items Fluder chose to leave behind deliberately. Research completion rewards access to Fluder's library: the Greater Ring of Spell Knowledge and an advanced Spellcaster's Tome.

completionCondition.query: The laboratory has been examined. The player has reported on its contents to the appropriate authority.

The Black Scripture's Target.name: The Black Scripture's Target
The Black Scripture's Target.mainObjective: Gather intelligence on Nazarick and the Sorcerer Kingdom and deliver it to the Theocracy.
The Black Scripture's Target.questStatement: The Black Scripture has identified Ainz Ooal Gown as a threat beyond the Theocracy's current military capability to address directly. Antilene Heran Fouche has been briefed. The question is intelligence — what can the Theocracy learn about Nazarick's structure and capability before committing to a response?
The Black Scripture's Target.questDesignBrief: This quest tasks the player with intelligence work rather than direct confrontation. The Theocracy knows enough to be afraid and not enough to act. The player fills in the picture — and in doing so, reveals how comprehensively Nazarick understands its observers. The intel may be intercepted before it arrives. Captured or recovered Theocracy equipment includes Scripture Combat Vestments and, if the operation succeeds, a Theocracy Relic Blade.

completionCondition.query: A meaningful intelligence picture of the Sorcerer Kingdom has been assembled and reported.

Zaryusu's Coalition.name: Zaryusu's Coalition
Zaryusu's Coalition.mainObjective: Help Zaryusu build a coalition between the lizardman tribes before the undead army arrives.
Zaryusu's Coalition.questStatement: Zaryusu Shasha is travelling between lizardman tribes to build a coalition against the incoming threat from Nazarick's undead force. He needs the support of the Green Claw, Razor Tail, Dragon Tusk, and Small Fang tribes — each with their own reasons for reluctance. The player can assist in the negotiations.
Zaryusu's Coalition.questDesignBrief: Each tribe has a different objection. Zenberu Gugu of Dragon Tusk wants to fight Zaryusu first. Crusch Lulu's Red Eye tribe is the medical asset that makes the coalition viable. The player helps navigate inter-tribal politics in a world where strength is the primary currency. Participating in the coalition's battles yields access to lizardman crafted equipment: White Dragon Bone Armor and Monster Cores from defeated creatures.

completionCondition.query: At least three tribes have committed to the coalition. A joint command structure has been established.

Nfirea's Herb Request.name: Nfirea's Herb Request
Nfirea's Herb Request.mainObjective: Retrieve the herbs from the Tob Forest interior and deliver them to Nfirea.
Nfirea's Herb Request.questStatement: Nfirea Bareare needs a specific herb that grows only in the deeper regions of the Tob Forest. The herb is used in a potion compound that exceeds standard healing capability. The forest's deeper sections have creature populations that have been escalating — previous herb gathering parties have not returned.
Nfirea's Herb Request.questDesignBrief: A classic delivery quest with an escalating threat. The Tob Forest's deeper sections are more dangerous than officially acknowledged. The missing previous parties may be encountered. The encounter with the forest's creature population hints at Aura's influence without making it explicit. Reward includes Compound Healing Potions -- better than any commercially available healing potion -- and a Rare Herb Bundle for future use.

completionCondition.query: The herbs have been retrieved and delivered. Nfirea has been able to proceed with his compounding.

Empire Tribute Negotiation.name: Empire Tribute Negotiation
Empire Tribute Negotiation.mainObjective: Facilitate or observe the treaty negotiations between Nazarick and the Baharuth Empire.
Empire Tribute Negotiation.questStatement: The Baharuth Empire has formally entered vassal status with the Sorcerer Kingdom following the Battle of Katze Plains. The terms of tribute — what the empire owes and what protection it receives in return — must be negotiated. Albedo represents Nazarick. The player may be involved as facilitator, observer, or operative.
Empire Tribute Negotiation.questDesignBrief: This quest unlocks after the Katze Plains confrontation has made Nazarick's military supremacy undeniable. Jircniv enters negotiations knowing his position is fundamentally weak and performs brilliantly within that constraint. Albedo knows exactly how weak his position is. The player witnesses how Ainz constructs a vassal relationship that is humiliating by conventional diplomatic standards but framed so that Jircniv can justify it internally. The dramatic interest is in the subtext — two parties with perfect mutual understanding of the power dynamic performing the ritual of negotiation anyway.

completionCondition.query: Terms have been agreed and formalised. The empire's tribute obligations are set.

Adamantite Trial.name: Adamantite Trial
Adamantite Trial.mainObjective: Complete the adamantite evaluation task and demonstrate the required capability.
Adamantite Trial.questStatement: Advancement to adamantite rank requires demonstration of capability at a level that normal job completion does not document. Ainzach has put forward a specific evaluation — a task that tests the candidate's power, judgment, and capacity to operate independently. Success means the highest non-legendary rank the guild grants.
Adamantite Trial.questDesignBrief: The evaluation task is calibrated at the top of the non-legendary range — difficult enough that most mithril-ranked adventurers cannot pass it. The player's completion method is a character statement. Evileye and Lakyus are present as evaluators with different assessment priorities. Trial completion earns recognition and adamantite-grade equipment: Adamantite Plate armor, an Adamantite War Axe, and the Adamantite Plate Necklace signifying rank.

completionCondition.query: The evaluation task has been completed. Ainzach has confirmed the rank advancement.

The Dwarven Runesmith Commission.name: The Dwarven Runesmith Commission
The Dwarven Runesmith Commission.mainObjective: Acquire the materials required for the runesmith commission and deliver the completed item.
The Dwarven Runesmith Commission.questStatement: The Dwarf Kingdom's remaining runesmiths have been asked to produce a commission — a weapon or piece of armour using authentic dwarven runework. The materials required include components not easily sourced within the kingdom. The player is tasked with acquiring them and delivering the commission result.
The Dwarven Runesmith Commission.questDesignBrief: This quest introduces the dwarf kingdom and the runesmith art. The materials quest likely takes the player into the Azerlisia Mountains or the wilderness. The completed item is a genuine artifact of the ancient craft — something that cannot be produced by standard New World enchantment. Completion earns a piece of Dwarf Kingdom runic equipment: combat-class characters receive a Runic Longsword or Runed Breastplate; all participants receive a Runic Amulet and Dwarven Craft Ore.

completionCondition.query: The runesmith has completed the commission using the acquired materials. The item has been delivered.

Ancient Ruins Exploration.name: Ancient Ruins Exploration
Ancient Ruins Exploration.mainObjective: Reach the deep levels of the ancient ruins and document what they contain.
Ancient Ruins Exploration.questStatement: An adventurer team reached the middle depths of the unnamed ancient ruins in the wilderness and reported active constructs and unusual magical phenomena before retreating. The guild is commissioning a fully equipped follow-up expedition to push deeper and document what is down there.
Ancient Ruins Exploration.questDesignBrief: The ruins' deep levels contain suggestions of a prior Player presence — Yggdrasil equipment and magical frameworks that do not belong in the New World timeline. The player may recognise details Ainz would recognise. The exploration is as much an archaeology quest as a combat one. Successful exploration recovers Ancient Rune Stones, Tomb Relic Shards, Data Crystals, and Mana Crystal Clusters from the ruins.

completionCondition.query: The deep levels have been reached and observed. A report has been delivered to the guild.

Sebas and the Slave.name: Sebas and the Slave
Sebas and the Slave.mainObjective: Help Sebas extract the rescued individual from danger and manage the Eight Fingers response.
Sebas and the Slave.questStatement: Sebas Tian, operating in Re-Estize as Ainz's intelligence asset, encountered a human woman being sold through Eight Fingers' trafficking network. His response to this — rescuing her — has put him at odds with his operational parameters and attracted the attention of eight fingers' security apparatus.
Sebas and the Slave.questDesignBrief: This quest explores the tension between Sebas's personal ethics and operational requirements. Solution's commentary on Sebas's choices provides the ideological counterpoint. The Eight Fingers enforcers who come for Sebas discover what he actually is — this revelation can be played for dramatic effect or used as a combat encounter.

completionCondition.query: The rescued individual is safe. Eight Fingers' response has been dealt with. Sebas's cover is intact or the situation has been resolved by other means.

Evileye's Past.name: Evileye's Past
Evileye's Past.mainObjective: Help Evileye retrieve or address something from her past.
Evileye's Past.questStatement: Evileye has been a member of the Blue Rose for years. Her past — as a vampire who survived centuries and watched much that she cared about disappear — surfaces in the context of an encounter or discovery that resonates with her history. She needs a specific piece of information or artifact that connects to events before she joined the Blue Rose.
Evileye's Past.questDesignBrief: Rigrit Bers Caurau's involvement connects Evileye's history to the Thirteen Heroes era. Lakyus provides the team's relational anchor. The quest's tone is reflective rather than action-heavy — most of the substance is in conversations between Evileye and Rigrit about what centuries looks like.

completionCondition.query: The quest's personal objective has been resolved. Evileye has closed the open thread.

Nazarick New World Survey.name: Nazarick New World Survey
Nazarick New World Survey.mainObjective: Survey the assigned region and deliver a complete intelligence report to Albedo.
Nazarick New World Survey.questStatement: Albedo has assigned the player to conduct a reconnaissance of a specific New World region not yet fully mapped by Nazarick's intelligence. The player is to assess military presence, faction activity, notable individuals, and geographic features. The report goes directly to Albedo.
Nazarick New World Survey.questDesignBrief: A reconnaissance quest that sends the player into a region of the GM's choosing. The report format is specific — Albedo's standards are exacting. The player learns how Nazarick processes and categorises intelligence about the world outside. What they report may influence future quests.

completionCondition.query: The report has been delivered. It contains actionable information about the region.

Pandora's Actor Deployment.name: Pandora's Actor Deployment
Pandora's Actor Deployment.mainObjective: Successfully deploy Pandora's Actor as a Ainz stand-in without the deception being revealed.
Pandora's Actor Deployment.questStatement: Ainz needs a stand-in for a public appearance in a location he cannot attend directly. Pandora's Actor will mimic Ainz. The player's role is to manage the deployment — ensuring the mimic reaches the location, performs correctly, and exits without the deception being discovered.
Pandora's Actor Deployment.questDesignBrief: Working with Pandora's Actor means managing his theatrical personality while keeping the operation professional. His mimic of Ainz is perfect — the challenge is everything around the mimic: the approach, the exit, and keeping Pandora's Actor from overacting in ways Ainz would not.

completionCondition.query: The appearance has been made. Pandora's Actor has been recovered. The deception was not detected.

The Theocracy Spy in E-Rantel.name: The Theocracy Spy in E-Rantel
The Theocracy Spy in E-Rantel.mainObjective: Identify and deal with the Theocracy intelligence operative in E-Rantel.
The Theocracy Spy in E-Rantel.questStatement: A Slane Theocracy intelligence operative has been identified conducting surveillance in E-Rantel. The scope of what they have observed -- and whether they have passed it on -- is unknown. The operative must be located, assessed, and dealt with before they can complete their mission and exit the city.
The Theocracy Spy in E-Rantel.questDesignBrief: Counter-intelligence in an urban setting. The operative is professional — they are not easy to identify. Once identified, the player must assess whether their intelligence has been sent. Demiurge's instructions about disposal are precise and do not include operational ambiguity. Captured spy equipment: Sealing Crystal used for intelligence operations, Scripture Combat Vestments, and an Enchanted Stiletto.

completionCondition.query: The operative has been handled. Demiurge has received a report on what they knew and who they were in contact with.

Jircniv's Secret Contact.name: Jircniv's Secret Contact
Jircniv's Secret Contact.mainObjective: Monitor Jircniv's external contacts without alerting him that Nazarick is watching.
Jircniv's Secret Contact.questStatement: Jircniv has been making discreet contacts with non-Empire factions, seeking alternatives to Nazarick's dominance. Ainz is aware and has chosen to monitor rather than act — for now. The player is the monitoring asset. Their role is to track the contacts, document the approach, and report without alerting Jircniv.
Jircniv's Secret Contact.questDesignBrief: Jircniv is the most competent human ruler. Watching him work without being detected by someone of his quality is a real challenge. The player observes his brilliance and his limitations simultaneously. What he is attempting is understandable. What the report to Ainz will mean for him is the quest's weight. Imperial diplomatic tokens include a Ring of Protection as a gesture of goodwill and official Guild Identification Papers confirming the contact's legitimacy.

completionCondition.query: The contact has been documented. Ainz has been briefed on what Jircniv is attempting.

The Wise King of the Forest.name: The Wise King of the Forest
The Wise King of the Forest.mainObjective: Address the Wise King of the Forest situation — by defeat, capture, or negotiated resolution.
The Wise King of the Forest.questStatement: The Wise King of the Forest — a massive magical beast that has held territory in the Tob Forest for generations — has been sighted closer to Carne Village than its normal range. The Guild has a standing contract for whoever can address the situation. The Wise King is significantly beyond standard hunting difficulty.
The Wise King of the Forest.questDesignBrief: The Wise King of the Forest is a named creature from the Overlord source — Ainz captured it and it became his mount (Hamusuke). The player may attempt to duplicate this or may encounter it in its natural territory. A player who defeats it cleanly is demonstrating capability in the upper range of Re-Estize Kingdom adventuring. The Wise King's defeat or negotiated cooperation yields a Monster Core and Dragon Scale for the player, usable as crafting components or sold.

completionCondition.query: The Wise King is no longer threatening village proximity. The Guild contract is closed.

Renner's Secret Request.name: Renner's Secret Request
Renner's Secret Request.mainObjective: Complete Renner's actual private objective, not the public one.
Renner's Secret Request.questStatement: Princess Renner has a private request she cannot submit through official channels. Her public request is a charitable mission. Her actual request is something the player will only learn after accepting — and the two requests are not the same thing.
Renner's Secret Request.questDesignBrief: The gap between Renner's public face and her actual nature is the quest's core tension. The player uncovers the real objective through observation rather than being told. Whether they complete it, refuse it, or use what they know differently is a character choice with political consequences.

completionCondition.query: Renner's real goal has been achieved. The player has decided what to do with what they know about her.

The Theocracy's Forest War.name: The Theocracy's Forest War
The Theocracy's Forest War.mainObjective: Determine the state of the forest war and the viability of the elven resistance.
The Theocracy's Forest War.questStatement: The Slane Theocracy has been advancing a military road through the Forest of Evasha toward Crescent Lake for years. The Elf King's erratic leadership has worsened the situation.
The Theocracy's Forest War.questDesignBrief: A long-running conflict with no clean sides. The Elf King is not a sympathetic figure. The Theocracy's soldiers are professional but their doctrine is ugly. The forest itself is a factor in every encounter.

completionCondition.query: Contact made with the elven resistance and the Theocracy's forward position assessed.

Wolf Pack Cull.name: Wolf Pack Cull
Wolf Pack Cull.mainObjective: Kill the wolf pack and return with two pelts as proof of completion.
Wolf Pack Cull.questStatement: A wolf pack has moved into the farmland east of E-Rantel and attacked two farmsteads. The Guild requires the pack culled and two pelts returned as proof.
Wolf Pack Cull.questDesignBrief: Grounded, low-stakes combat. The wolves are a real economic threat to farmers, not a dramatic set-piece. The player may encounter a grateful farmstead family. Keep it practical and human-scale.

completionCondition.query: The wolf pack has been eliminated and the player has returned to the Guild with two wolf pelts as proof.

Supply Run to Carne.name: Supply Run to Carne
Supply Run to Carne.mainObjective: Deliver the supply crate to Enri Emmot in Carne Village and return the signed receipt.
Supply Run to Carne.questStatement: Carne Village requires a delivery of medical supplies before the weather closes the road. Transport the crates safely and return a signed receipt.
Supply Run to Carne.questDesignBrief: A gentle introduction to Carne Village and Enri. The goblin defenders are a worldbuilding reveal — Enri should not be apologetic about them. Road bandits are optional; include only if pacing allows. The receipt confirms completion; make the return to the Guild a brief scene.

completionCondition.query: The supplies have been delivered to Carne Village, a receipt obtained from Enri Emmot, and the player has returned to the Guild.

Goblin Scout Elimination.name: Goblin Scout Elimination
Goblin Scout Elimination.mainObjective: Locate and eliminate the goblin scouts before they withdraw.
Goblin Scout Elimination.questStatement: A goblin scouting party has been spotted watching the east road. Neutralize them before they can report back to a larger force.
Goblin Scout Elimination.questDesignBrief: Urgency is the core mechanic. The scouts have a window — delay means escalation. They are not stupid; they retreat tactically. Tracking is as important as the engagement itself. Do not let the player turn this into a leisurely hunt.

completionCondition.query: All goblin scouts have been eliminated before they could report to a larger group.

Missing Caravan Investigation.name: Missing Caravan Investigation
Missing Caravan Investigation.mainObjective: Locate the missing caravan and return a full account of its fate to the Guild.
Missing Caravan Investigation.questStatement: A merchant caravan departed E-Rantel four days ago and has not arrived at its destination. Investigate the route and determine what happened.
Missing Caravan Investigation.questDesignBrief: Detective work on a road. Build the scene in stages. A witness account from a passing farmer, then signs on the road, then the site itself. Survivors are possible but not guaranteed. Nfirea can identify certain materials if samples are recovered.

completionCondition.query: The fate of the caravan has been determined and reported to the Guild, with any survivors or recoverable goods returned.

Undead Village Clearance.name: Undead Village Clearance
Undead Village Clearance.mainObjective: Eliminate all undead in the abandoned village and destroy whatever is generating them.
Undead Village Clearance.questStatement: An abandoned village east of E-Rantel has become a nest for undead. Clear it before the infestation spreads toward inhabited settlements.
Undead Village Clearance.questDesignBrief: The village looks manageable from the outside. Inside, the numbers are wrong — too many, too organized. The generation source is a buried ritual object, not a living caster. Finding and destroying it requires moving through the concentration of undead, not around it.

completionCondition.query: The undead population has been eliminated and the generation source identified and destroyed.

Tob Forest Herb Commission.name: Tob Forest Herb Commission
Tob Forest Herb Commission.mainObjective: Gather six bundles of Lanasor Root from the outer Tob Forest and deliver them to the Bareare Apothecary in E-Rantel.
Tob Forest Herb Commission.questStatement: The Bareare Apothecary requires rare herbs from the outer Tob Forest. The gathering site is in monster territory. Combat-capable escort is required.
Tob Forest Herb Commission.questDesignBrief: Nfirea can identify the correct plants; the player provides protection. The outer forest has real threats — not overwhelming, but requiring competence. The herb scent makes stealth approaches complicated. Lizzie is pleased by good samples; her assessment matters for the commission fee.

completionCondition.query: Six bundles of Lanasor Root have been gathered in the outer Tob Forest and delivered intact to the Bareare Apothecary.

The Troll of Duchy Road.name: The Troll of Duchy Road
The Troll of Duchy Road.mainObjective: Kill the troll and return with its head as proof for the border patrol reward.
The Troll of Duchy Road.questStatement: A large troll has claimed territory on the Duchy border road and destroyed two wagons. Multiple hunter attempts have failed. An adventurer team is required.
The Troll of Duchy Road.questDesignBrief: The troll is not a random beast — it has adapted to the road. It positions in chokepoints and uses fallen trees as leverage. Players who go in without fire readiness find regeneration a serious problem. This is a fight that requires preparation, not just power.

completionCondition.query: The troll has been killed and its head delivered to the Guild or border patrol post.

Noble House Surveillance.name: Noble House Surveillance
Noble House Surveillance.mainObjective: Gather actionable evidence of noble involvement in bandit activity and deliver it to the Guild contact.
Noble House Surveillance.questStatement: A Guild contact suspects a noble house of funding bandit operations for territorial gain. Document evidence without exposing the commission.
Noble House Surveillance.questDesignBrief: The noble is genuinely competent — catching him requires patience and indirect methods. Direct confrontation destroys the evidence. The Guild contact's identity is itself sensitive. Marquis Raeven has background context that can narrow the approach if the player has established trust with him.

completionCondition.query: Documented evidence has been gathered and delivered to the Guild contact without exposing the commission's origin.

The Lost Dungeon Levels.name: The Lost Dungeon Levels
The Lost Dungeon Levels.mainObjective: Reach the lowest accessible dungeon level, neutralize the threat, and return with a full account of what caused the party losses.
The Lost Dungeon Levels.questStatement: Three copper-rank parties entered the dungeon complex west of E-Rantel and none returned. Platinum assessment required: clear the lower levels and determine what is down there.
The Lost Dungeon Levels.questDesignBrief: The dungeon tells its own history through what the player finds. Copper-party gear in wrong locations. Signs of retreat that went wrong. The threat at the bottom is not exotic — it is a creature that has had years of undisturbed adaptation. The horror is the scale, not the type. This is genuinely dangerous platinum work, not a warm-up.

completionCondition.query: The dungeon's lower levels have been cleared, the threat identified and eliminated, and a complete report delivered to the Guild.

Bandit Militia Pacification.name: Bandit Militia Pacification
Bandit Militia Pacification.mainObjective: Neutralize the bandit organization through negotiation with leadership, targeted elimination, or full clearance.
Bandit Militia Pacification.questStatement: A bandit organization west of the capital has grown to militia scale. The Guild has received authorization to negotiate terms or eliminate leadership. The scale of this operation is at the absolute ceiling of platinum-rank work.
Bandit Militia Pacification.questDesignBrief: This is hard platinum work — the bandit leader has military training and does not underestimate adventurers. Brain Unglaus has intelligence on the leader from prior encounters. Negotiation requires something real: a pardon, a different employer, or leverage. Full elimination means working against a man who expects it and has contingencies. There is no easy path at this level.

completionCondition.query: The bandit organization no longer poses a regional threat. The Guild accepts any method that achieves this result.

The Bloodthorn Wyrm.name: The Bloodthorn Wyrm
The Bloodthorn Wyrm.mainObjective: Kill the Bloodthorn Wyrm and return with the head.
The Bloodthorn Wyrm.questStatement: A mature wyrm is systematically destroying villages along the eastern route. Mithril-minimum engagement. Fire resistance is mandatory. Three mithril teams have failed to finish it.
The Bloodthorn Wyrm.questDesignBrief: Three mithril teams have tried direct engagement and failed. The wyrm is not stronger than all three combined — it is smarter than how they approached it. The player must find its underground access points and seal or guard them before drawing it into combat. Blue Rose can provide tactical support if the relationship has been established. This is genuinely difficult mithril work that requires planning.

completionCondition.query: The Bloodthorn Wyrm has been killed and its head returned to the Guild as proof.

Theocracy Embedded Agent.name: Theocracy Embedded Agent
Theocracy Embedded Agent.mainObjective: Confirm the operative's identity, assess what intelligence they have gathered, and resolve the situation by report or elimination.
Theocracy Embedded Agent.questStatement: Surveillance has identified a suspected Slane Theocracy operative embedded in E-Rantel's merchant quarter. Confirm identity, assess intelligence gathered, then report or neutralize. This is sensitive enough that the commission does not appear on the public board.
Theocracy Embedded Agent.questDesignBrief: The operative blends completely with the city's population and has been in place long enough to develop a credible cover identity. The player builds identification through behavioral patterns: routes taken, contacts made, information sought, reactions to specific stimuli. Once confirmed, there is a choice with political consequences — expose them publicly, report quietly, make contact, or eliminate. The Theocracy's response depends on what the player chooses and what the operative had already transmitted.

completionCondition.query: The operative has been confirmed identified, their intelligence gathering assessed, and the situation resolved.

Demon Summoning at Warden's Vale.name: Demon Summoning at Warden's Vale
Demon Summoning at Warden's Vale.mainObjective: Destroy the demon summoning circle and eliminate all summoned entities in Warden's Vale.
Demon Summoning at Warden's Vale.questStatement: A ritual site has been confirmed active in Warden's Vale. Summoned demons have been sighted across three villages. Adamantite-only response. The circle must be destroyed while the demons are engaged — it will resummon otherwise.
Demon Summoning at Warden's Vale.questDesignBrief: The optimal approach — destroying cultists before engaging demons — is not obvious because the demons occupy attention. The player must split focus or find a way to isolate the cultists. Demiurge may have intelligence on the cult's origin that changes the context. Ainz is aware of this incident; his interest in the outcome is unstated but present.

completionCondition.query: The summoning circle has been destroyed and all summoned demons eliminated. The cult operating the ritual has been neutralized.

Envoy to the Dragon Council.name: Envoy to the Dragon Council
Envoy to the Dragon Council.mainObjective: Travel to Argland, meet Dragon Lord representatives, and establish the terms of initial diplomatic contact with Nazarick.
Envoy to the Dragon Council.questStatement: Dragon Lord representatives in the Argland Council State have agreed to meet with an envoy of sufficient standing. Adamantite rank is the minimum credibility threshold they will accept. The purpose of the meeting: establishing initial terms for formal communication between human institutions and the Dragon Council.
Envoy to the Dragon Council.questDesignBrief: The Dragons already know Nazarick's military capability — that is not what they are testing. They are assessing judgment and intent. The player cannot out-argue Tsaindorcus; they can only demonstrate through behavior. Draudillon provides a more accessible angle. A failed meeting is a valid outcome with consequences — do not make success automatic.

completionCondition.query: A meeting with Dragon Lord representatives has concluded and an initial framework for contact — established or rejected — has been reported to Ainz.

The Undead Army at Katze.name: The Undead Army at Katze
The Undead Army at Katze.mainObjective: Locate the vampire lord, disrupt its undead force, and destroy it.
The Undead Army at Katze.questStatement: A vampire lord of unknown origin has established itself in the Katze Plains and is organising the undead accumulation from decades of war into a functional army. The force is approaching operational scale. Locate and eliminate the vampire lord before the organised undead reach the surrounding settlements.
The Undead Army at Katze.questDesignBrief: The Katze Plains are already dangerous territory — the vampire lord has been using that cover to operate for months without drawing serious attention. The player must establish that this is directed activity before the garrison will take it seriously, then locate the source without triggering a retreat. The core tactical challenge is sealing retreat options before direct engagement. The vampire lord is intelligent enough to never fight a battle it cannot win — cornering it is harder than defeating it.

completionCondition.query: The vampire lord has been destroyed and its undead army scattered or eliminated.

The Platinum Dragon Lord's Trial.name: The Platinum Dragon Lord's Trial
The Platinum Dragon Lord's Trial.mainObjective: Complete the Platinum Dragon Lord's trial without relying on overwhelming force. The terms are set by Tsaindorcus.
The Platinum Dragon Lord's Trial.questStatement: Tsaindorcus Vaision has issued a formal trial to a Nazarick agent: demonstrate that Nazarick operates by principles, not power alone. The Dragon Council's stance on the Sorcerer Kingdom depends on the outcome. There is no assistance available. The trial's terms are Tsaindorcus's.
The Platinum Dragon Lord's Trial.questDesignBrief: This is the hardest quest in the chain — harder than any combat commission. The tasks require demonstrating genuine restraint and judgment in situations where the player could simply use force. Tsaindorcus is not fooled by performance; he has been alive long enough to recognize it. Failure is a legitimate outcome with real consequences for Nazarick's international position. Success changes the Dragon Council's posture permanently. This is a conclusive quest.

completionCondition.query: The trial has concluded. The Dragon Council's assessment of Nazarick has been established — positive, negative, or conditional.

The Merchant's Stolen Ledger.name: The Merchant's Stolen Ledger
The Merchant's Stolen Ledger.mainObjective: Recover the stolen ledger and identify who took it.
The Merchant's Stolen Ledger.questStatement: A merchant's account ledger has been stolen from his office. The ledger contains transaction records that would damage his business if disclosed.
The Merchant's Stolen Ledger.questDesignBrief: The thief has a specific motive: a business rival, a creditor, or someone named in the ledger wanting records destroyed. The player works backward from entry method to suspect. Both recovery and identification are required.

completionCondition.query: The ledger has been recovered and the thief identified or dealt with.

The Missing Apothecary Apprentice.name: The Missing Apothecary Apprentice
The Missing Apothecary Apprentice.mainObjective: Locate the missing apprentice and determine what happened.
The Missing Apothecary Apprentice.questStatement: An apothecary apprentice left for a routine herb collection three days ago and has not returned. His route took him into the outer Tob Forest edge.
The Missing Apothecary Apprentice.questDesignBrief: Lizzie is worried but composed. Nfirea is more distressed. The apprentice followed the route correctly but encountered something unexpected — he may be sheltering, injured, or gone. The resolution must match what the player finds, not a preset outcome. Do not guarantee survival.

completionCondition.query: The apprentice has been found — alive or dead — and his fate reported to the apothecary.

The Protection Racket.name: The Protection Racket
The Protection Racket.mainObjective: Dismantle the extortion operation in the district.
The Protection Racket.questStatement: A district in the capital is under organized extortion. Shop owners are paying a criminal group for protection they did not request. Discreet intervention commissioned.
The Protection Racket.questDesignBrief: The racket leader pays upward to a minor noble as insurance. Dismantling the street operation is straightforward. The patron connection is the complication — it can be exposed, ignored, or used as leverage. The player chooses which problem they want after clearing the immediate one.

completionCondition.query: The extortion group has been neutralized and the district is no longer under organized pressure.

The Poisoned Well.name: The Poisoned Well
The Poisoned Well.mainObjective: Identify who poisoned the well and ensure the threat is resolved.
The Poisoned Well.questStatement: The main well in a village near E-Rantel has been deliberately poisoned. Three villagers are ill. The Guild requires the source identified before it happens again.
The Poisoned Well.questDesignBrief: The perpetrator wanted disruption, not deaths. The motive is local: a land dispute, a grudge, or an attempt to drive people away. Enri knows everyone in the village and has strong suspicions she will not voice without evidence. The investigation is about building the case she already knows but cannot prove.

completionCondition.query: The source of the poisoning has been identified and the perpetrator dealt with.

Holy Kingdom Refugee Escort.name: Holy Kingdom Refugee Escort
Holy Kingdom Refugee Escort.mainObjective: Escort the refugee group safely from the border to their designated settlement.
Holy Kingdom Refugee Escort.questStatement: Holy Kingdom refugees have reached the Re-Estize border but cannot safely complete the final stretch to settlement housing without armed escort. The route passes through contested territory.
Holy Kingdom Refugee Escort.questDesignBrief: The difficulty is logistics, not combat. Managing exhausted civilians who have been walking for days is the actual challenge. The bandit encounter is brief and tilted in the player's favor. The terrain crossing — a river or mountain pass depending on the season — is the hard part. Neia Baraja, if present, is capable and earnest but has strong opinions about how things should be done. The quest ends when the group reaches a safe location; what condition they arrive in depends on the player's choices en route.

completionCondition.query: The refugee group has arrived at the settlement. Losses, if any, are noted.

The Blackmail Letter.name: The Blackmail Letter
The Blackmail Letter.mainObjective: Identify the blackmailer, recover the material they hold, and neutralize the threat without disclosure.
The Blackmail Letter.questStatement: A minor noble is receiving blackmail letters. He cannot involve official channels without the compromising information becoming public. Discreet resolution required.
The Blackmail Letter.questDesignBrief: The noble is afraid and withholding information that would help. The blackmailer has a dead-drop system.
