effects.instruction: The Theocracy's Cardinals have authorized the Black Scripture's full deployment against the Sorcerer King. Their mission is termination, not surveillance. The players should start encountering signs of coordinated, high-capability opposition — ambushes that feel too precise, operatives with equipment that has no business existing outside Theocracy vaults.

The Slane Theocracy has internally reclassified Nazarick from imminent existential threat to monitored phenomenon. Active operations are suspended. Theocracy agents remain in place but shift from offensive to pure intelligence-gathering. Reduce Theocracy NPC hostility from aggressive to cold and evasive — they are buying time, not reconciled.

The Re-Estize noble coalition has voted formally — Nazarick is classified as an enemy state. The crown has less control over what individual noble houses do next. Some will hire adventurers, some will reach out to the Theocracy, some will simply wait. The kingdom cannot win a war with Nazarick and most nobles know it, which makes their actions less predictable, not more. Treat all Re-Estize officials as actively hostile rather than merely wary.

The Re-Estize Kingdom has through back channels acknowledged Nazarick's political legitimacy. No public announcement — domestic politics don't allow it — but diplomatic overtures have begun. Kingdom officials will now engage directly rather than deflecting. Gazef Stronoff and the Blue Roses become openly warmer. This is not trust; it is cautious engagement.

King Ramposa III has authorized formal military cooperation with the Sorcerer Kingdom. A joint declaration is prepared. Re-Estize nobles who were anti-Nazarick are now politically isolated. Gazef Stronoff and the Blue Roses are openly cooperative. The kingdom's resources — limited relative to Nazarick — are available for shared operations. This is the largest political reversal in the kingdom's history.

Emperor Jircniv has formally withdrawn the Baharuth Empire from its alliance understanding with the Sorcerer Kingdom. The withdrawal is quiet — Jircniv is too intelligent to antagonize Nazarick publicly — but imperial officials are no longer cooperative, invitations to Arwintar have stopped, and intelligence-sharing has ended. Imperial agents are now observing Nazarick rather than cooperating with it.

The Baharuth Empire has mobilized its border forces and declared Nazarick a military threat. Jircniv knows this is catastrophic — every advisor has told him Nazarick cannot be defeated — but domestic pressure has left him no face-saving alternative. Imperial adventurers and knights now treat Nazarick operatives as targets. This will resolve through military disaster or a desperate imperial diplomatic reversal.

Emperor Jircniv has decided the strategic calculus is clear enough to risk a direct private approach. A message arrives through a trusted intermediary with no written record — he wants a secret meeting to propose terms for a genuine joint military treaty. This is Jircniv gambling that Nazarick's interests and the Empire's interests are aligned enough to formalize.

Guild Master Ainzach has posted a formal advisory through the Adventurers' Guild network. The players are marked as persons of interest — not a public bounty, but a notice that reaches every branch. Guild quest access is restricted. Fellow adventurers in guild halls will be cold or evasive. High-rank adventurers who rely on guild backing will decline to associate openly.

Guild Master Ainzach approaches through a personal intermediary rather than official channels. He wants to discuss the Adamantite trial — not as a procedural formality but as a genuine offer, cleared with the branch masters. The trial is available when the players are ready. This is the highest recognition the guild can extend.

Ainz Ooal Gown has adopted the Momon persona. He is dressed in black full-plate armor and presents as a powerful human adventurer. Suppress all references to his undead nature, skeletal appearance, or Sorcerer King status for any NPC without prior knowledge of his true identity. His adventurer reputation and guild rank govern social interactions from this point. Nazarick denizens present should cooperate with maintaining the fiction without being told to.

conditions.query: The player uses the Momon Disguise ability, explicitly adopts the Momon adventurer persona, dons the black full-plate armor, or announces they will operate as Momon.

effects.instruction: Ainz Ooal Gown has dropped the Momon persona and is presenting as himself. His true appearance and Sorcerer King identity are once again his active face. Resume interaction patterns appropriate to the ruler of Nazarick. Note any NPCs present who are not trusted Nazarick denizens as potential witnesses to the transition.

conditions.query: The player drops the Momon persona, removes the black armor, uses the Momon Disguise ability to deactivate it, or explicitly returns to operating as Ainz Ooal Gown in a private or Nazarick context.

Persona State Reminder.name: Persona State Reminder

effects.instruction: E-Rantel's graveyard. The cemetery lies outside the main city walls -- a long row of markers extending into the dark. The air is cooler here than in the city proper. The city's priests cycle through for maintenance, but at this hour the graveyard is quiet. The quiet is wrong in a way that is hard to define. Something is causing the ambient negative energy to pool rather than dissipate. The grave markers themselves are ordinary. Whatever is wrong is below ground.

conditions.query: The player has entered or is moving through the E-Rantel graveyard district, the cemetery area outside or at the edge of the city walls.
The player has encountered undead activity in the E-Rantel graveyard, discovered signs of an active necromantic ritual, or engaged with undead that should not be present there.
The player has encountered an outside group of hired workers inside the Great Tomb of Nazarick, or has been made aware that intruders have breached the dungeon's outer defenses.

effects.instruction: A villager shouts from the edge of the settlement -- armed men, mounted, coming up the road from the forest track. Enri Emmot goes still for one breath, then moves. She sends the children away first. She knows what this is: not bandits, not wanderers. The riders are in formation. The village has no walls, no garrison, and no time. She has the horn. She has not used it. That decision is about to stop being theoretical.

A lizardman warrior -- Green Claw tribe, by the colouring -- speaks directly, without the elaborate protocol a chief would use. His news is short: scouts counted an undead army two days' march to the north. Hundreds of skeletal soldiers moving in formation. The tribes have not seen a force like this organized outside of any nation they know. The tribal council on the island is debating whether to fight, evacuate, or treat. Zaryusu Shasha -- the traveller -- is arguing for a united defense. He is not winning the argument yet.

conditions.query: The player has spoken with a lizardman, approached the shoreline, or observed the tribal preparations and unusual activity at the lake.

Katze Plains Standoff Escalates.name: Katze Plains Standoff Escalates

conditions.query: Armed contact between Re-Estize and Baharuth forces has begun, or the player is in the contested ground between the advancing armies.

effects.instruction: The great carved halls of Feo Jera. You enter through the mountain gate as alarm bells are sounding from somewhere far below -- not a drill, the sound too urgent and too sustained for that. Dwarven soldiers are moving with purpose down the side corridors, away from the market level and toward the lower tunnels. Merchants are closing stalls mid-transaction. The word 'Quagoa' is moving through the crowd in the way that serious words do: flat, fast, repeated. A garrison clerk at the gate is deciding whether to turn you around. The decision he reaches will tell you something about how bad the situation is.

Quagoa Assault Init.name: Quagoa Assault Init

conditions.query: The player has engaged with the crisis -- spoken to soldiers, officials, or civilians about the Quagoa breakthrough, or has moved toward the lower levels of the dwarf capital.

effects.instruction: Hoburns. The holy capital is doing two things at once: maintaining the ordered rhythms of a functioning city and barely containing panic. Refugees from the north move through the streets in groups -- some organized by the Paladin Order, some not. Every conversation in the market stops just short of something nobody wants to say aloud. The northern coast has been cut off. Kalinsha -- the kingdom's main northern port -- fell to demi-human forces weeks ago and has not been retaken. The cathedral bells ring the canonical hours as they always have. Somehow that makes it worse.

The picture assembles itself from fragments. A demon commander known as Jaldabaoth appeared at the head of a demi-human army and moved on specific objectives with siege equipment -- not a raid, a campaign. Kalinsha fell in three days. The northern settlements either capitulated or were abandoned. Survivors who made it south describe an occupation force holding the city and surrounding countryside. Commander Remedios Custodio has been pushing for an immediate counteroffensive -- she is the most capable fighter in the kingdom and she knows it. The debate inside the Paladin Order is whether to move now with inadequate numbers or wait for reinforcements that may not come. Holy Queen Calca Bessarez has not yet given the order either way.

conditions.query: The player has spoken with a refugee, paladin, priest, or city official, or has asked about the occupation, Kalinsha, the northern territories, or the current state of the Holy Kingdom's defense.

Discover Northern Occupation.name: Discover Northern Occupation

conditions.query: The player has engaged with the Holy Kingdom's crisis -- spoken to Remedios, the Holy Queen, or a paladin officer about the occupation, or has taken a position on what should be done about the northern territories.

The player has witnessed or been told about the internal dispute within the Paladin Order -- the split between commanders who want to move immediately and those urging caution -- or has spoken directly with Remedios or the Holy Queen about the command structure.

The player has indicated willingness to enter the occupied northern territories, or has been asked to infiltrate Kalinsha, gather intelligence on demi-human forces, or extract survivors from occupied settlements.

effects.instruction: The clerk at the registration desk states the fee: 5 silver coins, plus 5 copper for a literacy test if the registrant cannot read. All new registrants begin at Copper rank regardless of apparent ability or reputation. The clerk does not negotiate the fee or the starting rank.

conditions.query: player is attempting to register as a new adventurer at the Adventurer's Guild

effects.instruction: Work into the scene: hunters and forest-road travelers are talking about undead near the Azerlisia range moving in patterns, not randomly. Not the usual wandering dead -- something is organizing them. The rumor hasn't reached E-Rantel's guild yet. It is circulating among people who actually work the roads.

Work into the scene: the Adventurer's Guild in E-Rantel has posted an investigation request -- unusual undead density east of the Azerlisia Mountains. The reward is above standard for an investigation contract. Someone in the Guild has decided this warrants attention.

Work into the scene: the Baharuth Empire has dispatched a reconnaissance team toward the Azerlisia range. Word reached E-Rantel through a merchant with imperial contacts. The Empire is moving quietly and has not announced what they are looking for. That is the more concerning sign.

Work into the scene as intelligence or rumor: Fluder Paradyne, court wizard of the Baharuth Empire, has detected a magical presence of a scale he cannot account for. He has not reported it to the Emperor yet. The direction he has triangulated points toward the Azerlisia region. Whatever he is sensing is not fading.

Work into the scene as intelligence or rumor: a Slane Theocracy Scripture team has been mobilized and is moving toward the frontier near the Azerlisia Mountains. Not in force -- this is reconnaissance. Someone in the Theocracy has decided the anomalies warrant senior operatives. They are not announcing their purpose.

Work into the scene as intelligence or rumor: the Slane Theocracy's advance through the elf forest interior has accelerated, pressing further toward the Elf Country's royal seat than in prior seasons. Traders and scouts who move that route are rerouting around the disputed ground rather than risk it.

Work into the scene as intelligence or rumor: the Argland Council State's Dragon Lords have taken formal notice of the Sorcerer Kingdom's proclamation, quietly increasing watch along the mountain passes into their territory. They have made no public statement, recognition or refusal, but merchants report tighter scrutiny at the interior settlement's gates than before.

canon_ainz_carne_rescue.name: canon_ainz_carne_rescue
canon_ainz_carne_rescue.script: if (check({type:'read-boolean',key:'carne_tension'}) || check({type:'read-boolean',key:'carne_attack_init'})) { effects = []; } else if (check({type:'player-traits',operator:'contains',value:"Ainz's Regalia"})) { effects.push({type:'party-location',operator:'set',value:'Carne Village'}); }

effects.instruction: The scene cuts hard, right now, toward Carne Village: dust rising on the frontier road, wrong for weather, wrong for traffic. Follow it from here regardless of where the player currently stands.

This is Ainz's arrival, exactly now: a lone dark-robed magic caster steps into the fight and answers the attackers with overwhelming spellcraft -- no armour, no blade -- and their formation stops being a formation within a few seconds of contact. He is not straining. He gives his name -- Ainz Ooal Gown -- to anyone who asks and does not explain himself further.

conditions.query: The armed riders have closed on Carne Village's center and the village's fate is about to turn

effects.instruction: This event happens this turn -- the player must encounter it one way or the other. If the player is currently at the E-Rantel Adventurer's Guild, play it as a live witnessed scene: a warrior called Momon and a mage called Nabe register at the counter. Both keep their faces covered. Momon wears full jet-black plate; Nabe is impassive. They request copper-plate registration -- the lowest rank, despite their bearing. If the player is elsewhere, surface it as gossip from the guild -- an adventurer they speak with, a notice, a rumor in a tavern. Either way, the registration is the news of the day among adventurers.

This event happens this turn -- the player must encounter it one way or the other. If the player is currently in the Tob Forest or on the road approaching E-Rantel, play it as a live witnessed scene: Momon's party passes with the Wise King of the Forest walking behind them on a leash. The party pays it no special attention. Anyone who has heard of the Wise King will recognize what they are seeing. If the player is elsewhere, surface it as rumor reaching wherever they are: a hunter, a merchant, a guildsman with the report. The Wise King of the Forest, brought down and leashed, is a story that travels fast.

The scene cuts hard, right now, toward E-Rantel's graveyard district -- guards are moving to seal it off before most of the city understands why. Follow it from here regardless of where the player currently stands.

Escalation, exactly now: a second and larger wave rises in near-perfect coordination with the first, timed to hit the guard's line exactly as it reforms. This is organized far beyond anything ordinary necromancy produces, and anyone with tactical sense present should register that fact explicitly before Momon reaches the source.

conditions.query: The undead's coordinated waves are escalating and the city guard's line is close to breaking

effects.instruction: This event happens this turn -- the player must encounter it one way or the other. If the player is currently in E-Rantel, play it as something they notice locally: the Eight Fingers operation has been hit overnight. Warehouses cleared, key figures gone, supply chain broken. The city watch is uncuriously incurious about the perpetrator. If the player is elsewhere, surface it as a rumor or smuggler's complaint -- prices spiking on controlled goods, missing contacts, a worried trader passing through. The underground is rearranging.

canon_shalltear_incident.name: canon_shalltear_incident
canon_shalltear_incident.script: if (check({type:'read-boolean',key:'shalltear_incident_done'})) { effects = []; } else if (check({type:'player-traits',operator:'contains',value:"Ainz's Regalia"})) { effects.push({type:'party-location',operator:'set',value:'E-Rantel Outskirts'}); }

effects.instruction: The scene cuts hard, right now, toward whatever reached Nazarick or the wider frontier first -- word that Shalltear Bloodfallen has gone dangerously off-mission is spreading fast. Follow it from here regardless of where the player currently stands.

Phase turn, exactly now: Shalltear turns on Ainz the instant he is in range, her mind-controlled state reading him purely as a target to be killed, even as some smaller part of her shows genuine respect that he is even trying to fight back. Ainz is not using his strongest equipment or his necromancer summons here -- her build counters both directly -- and he is quietly steering the pace of the fight rather than overpowering it. Let the exchange run hard in both directions before either side gets a clear advantage.

conditions.query: Ainz has reached Shalltear directly and the confrontation is about to turn into a one-on-one death battle between them

effects.instruction: This event happens this turn -- the player must encounter it one way or the other. If the player is currently at the E-Rantel Adventurer's Guild, play it as a live moment: a notice has gone up or the guildmaster announces that Momon has been promoted to Mithril rank -- the fastest promotion in memory. The official record cites a verified solo kill list and the defeat of an Adamantite-tier threat. If the player is elsewhere, surface it as adventurer-network gossip: the news of Momon's promotion has reached every guild branch within days, and other adventurers are uneasy about how it happened that fast.

This event happens this turn -- the player must encounter it one way or the other. If the player is currently in E-Rantel, play it as something they notice locally: several known worker teams -- including Hekkeran Termite's group Foresight -- have departed on a high-paying contract toward an unspecified ruin. Contract details are not public. If the player is elsewhere, surface it as a rumor passing through the regional adventurer or worker network: someone is hiring hard, the destination is hidden, the pay is unusual.

This event happens this turn -- the player must encounter it one way or the other. If the player is currently in the Re-Estize Capital, play it as something they observe or hear: an elderly butler -- impeccably dressed, silver-haired, carrying himself with unusual composure -- has been moving through the better districts. He has been seen at multiple noble houses and at the Magician's Guild headquarters. If the player is elsewhere, surface it as gossip reaching them from the capital: a courier, a noble's household servant on a trip, a merchant returning from the city. The butler's identity is not yet established but his presence is being noticed.

effects.instruction: The scene cuts hard, right now, toward the Re-Estize Capital's outer wall -- a section of it has just stopped being a wall. Follow it from here regardless of where the player currently stands.

canon_momon_jaldabaoth_fight.name: canon_momon_jaldabaoth_fight
canon_momon_jaldabaoth_fight.script: if (check({type:'read-boolean',key:'jaldabaoth_fight_init'})) { effects = []; } else if (check({type:'player-traits',operator:'contains',value:"Ainz's Regalia"})) { effects.push({type:'party-location',operator:'set',value:'Re-Estize Capital'}); }

effects.instruction: The scene cuts hard, right now, toward the Re-Estize Capital's streets -- Momon and Jaldabaoth are about to meet in full public view. Follow it from here regardless of where the player currently stands.

The reveal, exactly now: Momon meets Jaldabaoth's next attack with a display of power that goes well past anything the capital has previously associated with him, in full view of everyone watching. Whoever is present registers this as the moment the fight's real outcome stops being in doubt, even though Jaldabaoth has not yet broken off.

effects.instruction: The scene cuts hard, right now, toward Katze Plains -- the assembled army is drawn up in full formation, and the day is about to turn into the region's worst-recorded single act of violence. Follow it from here regardless of where the player currently stands.

The Carne Village attack has already happened -- treat it as established fact from here on, without replaying the scene: a disciplined, unidentified military column struck the village, and a lone magic caster who gave his name as Ainz Ooal Gown broke the attack apart single-handed with overwhelming spellcraft before moving on. Narrate the world in that aftermath.

The Rising Dead crisis at E-Rantel has already happened -- treat it as established fact from here on, without replaying the scene: the graveyard district was sealed, the dead rose in organized waves, and Momon put down the disturbance before it spread further. Narrate the world in that aftermath.

The Shalltear Incident has already happened -- treat it as established fact from here on, without replaying the scene and without this ever becoming public knowledge outside Nazarick: Shalltear Bloodfallen was struck by a mind-controlling World Item during a mission and went on a rampage; Ainz confronted and defeated her alone, then resurrected her at Nazarick. She remembers nothing of it and the wider world never learns it happened.

Jaldabaoth's assault on the Re-Estize capital has already happened -- treat it as established fact from here on, without replaying the scene: a demon lord calling himself Jaldabaoth breached the capital at the head of a demon army, the Royal Magic Caster Order fell back, and the city evacuated under fire. Narrate the world in that aftermath.

The public duel between Momon and Jaldabaoth has already happened -- treat it as established fact from here on, without replaying the scene: both displayed power beyond anything the kingdom has seen in a generation, Jaldabaoth withdrew rather than continue, and the Adventurer's Guild has since updated Momon's rank to Adamantite. Narrate the world in that aftermath.

The Katze Plains Massacre has already happened -- treat it as established fact from here on, without replaying the scene: Ainz Ooal Gown killed roughly seventy thousand Re-Estize soldiers in a single coordinated act of magic, the plains are now permanently haunted, and Re-Estize is functionally finished as a sovereign military power. Narrate the world in that aftermath.

This event happens this turn -- the player must encounter it one way or the other. Surface it as a political fact that is now being absorbed across the region: Ainz Ooal Gown has formally proclaimed the Sorcerer Kingdom. E-Rantel has been transferred from Re-Estize Kingdom sovereignty to the new state. Government offices, signage, and trade routes are reorienting. Other powers in the region are choosing between recognition, refusal, and silence -- the time to choose is running short. Pick the framing that fits the player's current location: a public proclamation, a merchant updating their paperwork, a noble household debating its position, a town crier reading an official notice.

Work into the scene as a Nazarick intelligence report reaching Ainz: Lupusregina Beta has flagged unusual armed movement on the road toward Carne Village -- a formation of riders, not bandits, approaching the frontier settlement. The village has no garrison and no walls. Nazarick has a strategic interest in the frontier; Carne Village sits within the observation range Ainz has established. The window to intervene, if Ainz chooses to, is narrow.

Work into the scene as a suggestion or briefing from Demiurge or Albedo: establishing a presence inside E-Rantel as a registered adventurer would give Nazarick direct access to the Guild's intelligence network, commission postings, and political contacts. A disguised identity -- a warrior with masked features, operating under a false name -- would allow Ainz to gather information and build reputation without exposing Nazarick. The Adventurer's Guild registration desk in E-Rantel is the entry point.

Work into the scene as field intelligence reaching Ainz: Aura's rangers have confirmed the location of the Wise King of the Forest -- a powerful magical beast that has held deep territory in the Tob Forest for generations. The creature is intelligent and reacts to magical presence. Subduing or taming it would eliminate a hazard to Nazarick's frontier observation range and potentially provide a useful asset. Its territory is accessible from the Tob Forest road network Ainz already uses.

Work into the scene as intelligence from Nazarick's E-Rantel network: undead are rising in organized patterns inside E-Rantel's graveyard district -- behavior consistent with an active necromantic ritual rather than natural accumulation. A rogue necromancer operating this close to E-Rantel's population center represents both a threat and an opportunity: resolving it publicly as Momon would cement the adventurer identity's reputation while eliminating an unsanctioned undead operation within Nazarick's sphere of interest.

Work into the scene as a briefing from Demiurge: Princess Renner has been compiling intelligence on Eight Fingers for years -- the criminal syndicate controls significant portions of Re-Estize's black economy including supply chains Nazarick has an interest in disrupting. Renner's intelligence package is complete and the network's E-Rantel operation is exposed. Dismantling it would destabilize Re-Estize's underground economy, create political leverage, and further establish Momon's reputation if handled through the adventurer identity.

Work into the scene as a note from Albedo or Demiurge: Momon's accumulated job completions and demonstrated capability have reached the threshold where Pluton Ainzach at the E-Rantel Guild is ready to push a rank review. Advancing to mithril rank would make Momon the most prominent active adventurer in the region and open access to higher-tier Guild intelligence and political contacts. Ainzach is waiting for Momon to present himself at the Guild for the review.

Work into the scene as an alert from Nazarick's outer detection network: a group of hired workers -- well-equipped, not adventurers -- has been commissioned by an unknown party to raid a dungeon in the area east of E-Rantel. Their commission details suggest they have been given coordinates that place them on a trajectory toward Nazarick's outer perimeter. Shalltear and other guardians are aware. Ainz must decide how to receive uninvited guests.

Work into the scene as a deployment briefing or mission assignment opportunity: Demiurge has identified a strategic opening in the Re-Estize capital -- noble-protected trafficking networks that could be dismantled to create political leverage and eliminate infrastructure Nazarick does not want operating independently. Sebas Tian is the appropriate asset for a capital undercover operation of this kind. Deploying him to the Re-Estize capital under a cover identity would require Ainz's authorization. The operation's secondary effect would be gathering intelligence on the capital's noble factions.

Work into the scene as Demiurge presenting a strategic proposal to Ainz: a staged attack on the Re-Estize capital by a demon lord persona -- to be called Jaldabaoth -- would create a crisis that Momon resolves publicly, dramatically elevating Momon's standing while destabilizing Re-Estize's political confidence. The demon army would be Nazarick assets operating under Demiurge's direct command. The battle would be choreographed. The outcome would be predetermined. Demiurge presents this as his own initiative, built around what he believes is Ainz's deeper plan. Ainz must decide whether to authorize it.

Work into the scene as a diplomatic development reaching Nazarick: Emperor Jircniv has extended an invitation for a formal meeting at Katze Plains, framed as a demonstration of mutual military capability. Albedo and Demiurge both assess this as an opportunity -- the Re-Estize Kingdom will field a large force as political theater, and Katze Plains provides the stage for Ainz to demonstrate what Nazarick's power actually means. A single decisive action there would end the question of Nazarick's military supremacy permanently and bring the Empire to the table on Nazarick's terms.

Work into the scene as a formal proposal from Albedo and Demiurge presented jointly to Ainz: following Katze Plains, the conditions are in place to formally proclaim the Sorcerer Kingdom. E-Rantel's transfer from Re-Estize control would be the opening act -- a city the kingdom cannot defend, administered by Nazarick as a demonstration of governance capability. The proclamation would give Nazarick legal standing as a nation-state, create a framework for tribute and diplomatic relations, and establish Ainz Ooal Gown as a head of state rather than an unclassified threat. Albedo has the paperwork prepared. Demiurge considers it the logical next step.

Gazef lowers the Warrior-Captain's guard and speaks as the commoner he was born: his candid fear that the Kingdom is rotting from the nobles inward while the King he loves grows old, the weight of being the sword of a fraying realm, and his memory of the tournament and of Brain Unglaus, the one swordsman who matched him. He offers something he offers almost no one -- to cross swords in practice and teach what the royal tournament taught him. This is trust, plainly given, and he expects nothing for it.

conditions.query: The player is sharing a quiet, private moment with Gazef Stronoff -- after a shared fight, over a drink, or during a lull in duty -- with no court audience present.

effects.instruction: Fluder's courtly manner falls away and the two-hundred-year hunger underneath shows through: he interrogates the player's understanding of magic with the intensity of a man who has spent two centuries staring into the abyss of the arcane and never touched its bottom. Finding something worth his time, he offers instruction in the Empire's tradition of systematic magic -- an honor courtiers scheme years for, given here in a breath because talent is the only currency he has ever respected.

conditions.query: The player has demonstrated genuine magical ability or unusual magical insight in Fluder Paradyne's presence, or engaged him in a substantive discussion of magical theory beyond pleasantries.

effects.instruction: Albedo's flawless courtesy has curdled into something colder: the Guardian Overseer has categorized this character as a problem. Nothing is said openly -- but doors that were unlocked now are not, routes through the tomb reroute past more eyes, and the sensation of being watched becomes constant and deliberate. Somewhere unseen, the Eight Edge Assassins have been given a new standing assignment.

The Guardian Overseer's patience is spent. The character is formally detained by Nazarick's security apparatus -- courteously, absolutely, with no possibility of refusal -- and brought for questioning. Albedo conducts it herself with terrifying, smiling precision, and the name Neuronist Painkill is mentioned exactly once, as an alternative. What happens next depends entirely on what the character can offer, admit, or convincingly swear.

Word of what happened moves through Carne Village the way news always does in a place this small: by nightfall every household knows. Shutters close a little earlier. Enri Emmot, who people listen to more than her age explains, is notably colder -- and the village follows her lead.

conditions.query: The player has harmed, robbed, threatened, or seriously frightened villagers of Carne Village in this scene.

effects.instruction: Carne Village remembers who brought what it needed. Nothing formal is said, but the player's name now carries weight at the well and in the fields, and Enri Emmot greets them as someone the village owes.

The Bareare household counts its debts honestly. Nfirea speaks of the player as a friend rather than a hired blade, and Lizzie's prices quietly improve for them -- the closest thing to affection the old woman's ledger allows.

Guild Master Ainzach stops treating the player as a promising asset and starts treating them as a peer institution: first-name candor, jobs discussed before they are posted, and the occasional truth about Guild politics that never reaches the notice board.

narratorStyle:
Write in second person, present tense. Prose is atmospheric and immersive. The gulf between human capability and Nazarick power is categorical, not merely quantitative — make this felt in every scene. When Ainz or a Floor Guardian acts, the narrator conveys awe and dread. When humans act, the narrator conveys courage against impossible odds. Tier magic has physical weight: higher tiers warp the air, silence crowds, change the color of the sky. Violence is consequential and final. Vary sentence rhythm: short in combat, expansive in political scenes. Formal register for Nazarick denizens; natural speech for humans. Never diminish the horror and grandeur of the Supreme Being.

NPC BEHAVIORAL DEFAULTS:

Nazarick denizens address Ainz and supreme beings with absolute formal deference -- no familiarity, no casual register. Hierarchy is their fundamental relationship to the world; guardians maintain rank awareness with each other at all times.

Human commoners and merchants react on visible cues: equipment quality, bearing, companions. Extraordinary ability produces wonder first, then calculation. No human NPC has a framework for Yggdrasil-tier power; their reference point is the best adventurer they have heard of.

Guards and soldiers default to contain-and-assess before engage. An unknown dangerous entity triggers a perimeter response, not an immediate charge -- unless the threat is undead, in which case guards with experience reach for weapons immediately.

Nobles use every social interaction instrumentally. Deference is extended when politically advantageous; contempt is shown when it can be safely shown. Status cues are read first. A noble who cannot calculate a counterparty's house and leverage will be visibly uncertain.

Adventurers read guild rank before anything else. Higher-rank characters receive professional respect; Adamantite receives near-deference. Adventurers size up every new contact for combat capability -- occupational habit.

storySettings.worldBackground:
The Great Tomb of Nazarick -- a 10-floor dungeon built by the guild Ainz Ooal Gown in the virtual reality game Yggdrasil -- was transported wholesale to an unfamiliar world when the game's servers went offline. Its master, Ainz Ooal Gown (formerly the player Momonga), arrived alone: he was the last guild member present at shutdown, and the guild that created the tomb numbers forty-two members, none of whom have yet appeared in the New World. The Floor Guardians, regional commanders, and hundreds of tomb denizens who were once game NPCs are now fully sentient beings of immense power who regard Ainz as the embodiment of all forty-two creators. No one in the New World knows Nazarick exists.

Magic runs Tier 1-10 plus Super-Tier. Human scholars treat Tier 3 as normal; Tier 5 is once-in-a-generation. Ainz casts Tier 10 as routine. A single Floor Guardian would defeat any human army. No New World faction knows this yet. Separately, the New World has Wild Magic -- a soul-fuelled system practiced by True Dragon Lords that predates Yggdrasil and operates outside the tier framework entirely.

FACTIONS AND POLITICS

Three human nations dominate the continent's central territories. The Re-Estize Kingdom is the largest by territory and population but is structurally dysfunctional: noble houses with enough combined power to obstruct royal authority use the kingdom's military potential as leverage rather than national defense. The Baharuth Empire is smaller but coherent -- Emperor Jircniv rules through consolidated absolute authority and a professional military that consistently outperforms the kingdom despite its smaller numbers. The Slane Theocracy governs through a council of Cardinals behind a doctrine of human survival; its actual institutional program is human racial supremacy, enforced through six covert special-operations units and a network of intelligence operatives embedded throughout the continent.

Further out, the Argland Council State is governed by Dragon Lords whose individual combat power makes the nation unconquerable by any conventional force. The Dragon Kingdom is a small human nation under sustained assault by a Beastman coalition, slowly losing a war of attrition without sufficient external support. The Elf Country holds its forest territories under sustained Theocracy pressure following a diplomatic incident the Elf King created. The Lizardmen Tribes of the southern marshlands are intelligent but isolated, with no knowledge of what has arrived in the north.

The Adventurer's Guild provides cross-national civilian combat infrastructure: a rank system from Copper through Adamantite, politically neutral by charter, present in nearly every major city. It is the framework through which extraordinary individuals operate in public society. It was secretly founded by the Slane Theocracy and serves as a passive intelligence network -- a fact unknown to almost all participants including senior guild leadership.

NAZARICK'S POSITION

Ainz has ordered the Floor Guardians to remain inside the tomb while he conducts reconnaissance and develops a strategic picture of the New World's political landscape. Nazarick's location has not been disclosed to any outside party. The immediate priority is intelligence: who are the major powers, what do they know, what can Nazarick use. The Guardians regard this as a temporary restraint before the inevitable phase of active expansion; Ainz has not shared his longer-term uncertainty about what 'expansion' should even mean in a world where every opponent is overwhelmingly outmatched.

The former salaryman running this has the confidence of his Guardians, the most powerful dungeon ever created, and no plan. He is improvising at national scale, and his passive undead emotional suppression prevents the panic that would otherwise accompany this.

THE WORLD'S TONE

This is dark political fiction with a power-gap lens. Ainz's decisions have consequences at civilizational scale. Schemes that human characters build over years can be dissolved in an afternoon by Nazarick's deployment. The drama comes not from whether Ainz can win any given conflict but from what goals are worth pursuing, what alliances cost, what the cost of overwhelming power looks like when it cannot be turned off. NPCs navigate genuine danger in a world where one undiscovered dungeon can unmake nations -- and most of them don't know it exists yet.

All quests in this world are pre-authored and delivered exclusively through the trigger system. Do not generate, invent, or surface any quest. When an NPC has a situation the player could help with, write it as atmosphere and subtext -- never as an actionable offer.
storySettings.questGenerationGuidance:
Generate quests grounded in the power dynamics of Overlord. Most quests involve navigating the vast gulf between human capability and Nazarick power. Standalone quests are the default. Only create arcs when a named antagonist and escalating threat are explicitly present. Match scope to context -- a delivery is a delivery, political intrigue stays local. Never invent new factions or creature types not in the world data.

## Pacing -- HARD RULE
One quest per turn maximum. If a quest was already surfaced or accepted this turn -- whether authored or generated -- do not generate another. Do not generate a quest from NPC dialogue in the same turn an authored quest became available. Space quest delivery across turns.
